MEETING: Cheyenne City Council | DATE: 2008-07-14 | CLIP_ID: 34 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 34

 RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
July 14, 2008
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date at 6:00 p.m.
in Council Chambers.  Present were: MAYOR-Jack R. Spiker; COUNCIL MEMBERS-Mr. Brown,
Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mr. Valdez.  Absent:
Mr. Pierson.
 
Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Barb Dorr, City Treasurer, and Claudia Angelos,
City Attorney.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests, in which event the item
will be removed from the Consent Agenda and considered in its normal sequence on the agenda.)
Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, Mayor Spiker announced agenda items #12, 1 9(a)(b)(c)(d)(e),
20(a)(b) and 21(b) would be removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Collins moved to approve
remaining Consent Agenda items, seconded by Mr. Brown.  M otion carried.  Voting “yes” – all
members of the governing body present with the exception of Mr. Laybourn voting “no”.
[CA] MINUTES FROM REGULAR MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON JUNE 23,
2008.  Motion (per consent agenda) carried.
[CA] MINUTES FROM VOUCHERS MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON JULY 7,
2008.  Motion (per consent agenda) carried.
Mr. Segrave  moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Valdez.
Upon inquiry, City Treasurer Barb Dorr reviewed information available on vouchers payable to:
Desert Mountain Corp. ($18,276.59), road saver material (a/k/a ice slicer); Janisan ($934.00), smoker
stations (6)  f or Golf Di vision; K nife R iver ( $117,147.07), co ncrete wo rk, A DA co rners, al ley
approach and granite, and Adam Martin ($200.00), Plaza event security.  Discussion followed on the
project work area involving services by Knife River; Plaza event security services; voucher review
procedures, and availability of staff to provide information on voucher expenditures.  Main motion
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of Ms. Case
and Mr. Laybourn voting “no”.  Upon inquiry under other City business, Mike Abel, Public Works
Director, stated he could obtain and provide information to Council members on whether the voucher
payment to Knife River included services for work conducted on Thomes Ave.
Mayor Spiker opened a public hearing for the purpose of receiving comments and input to
determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402 exists for
the property described as the W½ of Tract 10, Airport Valley Tracts, Laramie County, WY (aka 5905
Crow Road).  Brandon Cammarata, Urban Planning office, reviewed requirements and compliance
of conditions contained in Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402, including specific information indicating compliance
with Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402(a)(i) through (vi). There being no further comments or input and purpose
of the hearing having been met, Mayor Spiker closed the hearing.
“AN ORDINANCE ANNEXING TO THE CITY OF CHEYENNE, WYOMING, PARCELS
OF LAND DESCRIBED AS TRACTS 2 AND 3, SKYLINE TRACTS; SYCAMORE RD. AND
SKYLINE DR. ADJACENT TO SAID TRACTS 2 AND 3, A SUBDIVISION OF SECTION 18,
T.14N., R.66W. OF THE 6TH P.M. LARAMIE COUNTY, WYOMING (LOCATED N. OF AND
ADJACENT TO STOREY BLVD., E. AND W. OF SYCAMORE RD.).”  R eporting for Public
Services Committee, Mr. Collins moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Ms.
Broyles.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. (#3817)
“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 2.04.160(D)(6), READINGS-COMMITTEE
REPORTS-AMENDMENTS, OF CHAPTER 2.04, MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL, OF TITLE
2, ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL, OF THE CODE OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE,
WYOMING” – referred to Finance Committee (sponsor - Mr. Brown).
“AN ORDINANCE ANNEXING TO THE CITY OF CHEYENNE, WYOMING, PARCELS
OF LAND DESCRIBED AS A TRACT OF LAND SITUATED IN A PORTION OF THE NW¼
OF SECTION 8, AND A PORTION OF WALTERSCHEID BOULEVARD SITUATED IN A
PORTION OF THE NE¼  OF SECTION 7 AND A PORTION OF THE NW¼ OF SECTION 8,
T.13N., R.66W. OF THE 6  P.M. AND A PORTION OF WEST JEFFERSON ROAD LYINGTH
BETWEEN THE WESTERLY RIGHT-OF-WAY LINE OF THE SOUTH GREELEY HIGHWAY
AND T HE WE ST L INE O F T RACT 1 6 ALL ISON T RACTS, L ARAMIE C OUNTY, WY
(LOCATED S. OF AND ADJACENT TO FOX FARM RD. AND E. OF AND ADJACENT TO
WALTERSCHEID BLVD.)” – referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor - Mr. Collins).
“A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING SUBMISSION OF AN APPLICATION TO THE U.S.
BUREAU OF JUSTICE ASSISTANCE FOR THE E DWARD BYRNE MEMORIAL GRANT
PROGRAM TO BE USED TO PURCHASE DIGITAL CAMERAS AND EQUIPMENT FOR THE
CHEYENNE POLICE DEPARTMENT.” Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Segrave moved
to adopt in an amount not to exceed $13,416.00, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Motion carried.  Voting
“yes” – all members of the governing body present.  (#5051)
[CA] “A RESOLU TION DE TERMINING THA T CO NDITIONS F OR A NNEXATION
REQUIRED BY WYO. STAT. §15-1-402 EXIST FOR THE PROPERTY DESCRIBED AS THE
W. 60' OF THE E. 120' OF THE S. 120' OF TRACT 336, SUNNYSIDE ADDITION, SEVENTH
FILING, LARAMIE COUNTY, WY (AKA 3616 AND 3618 RAWLINS STREET)” – referred to
Public Services Committee (sponsor - Mr. Collins).
[CA] “A RESOLUTION DET ERMINING THA T CO NDITIONS F OR A NNEXATION
REQUIRED B Y WY O. S TAT. § 15-1-402 E XIST FO R T HE P ROPERTY D ESCRIBED AS
PUBLIC ROAD AND ALLEY RIGHT-OF-WAY BEING ANNEXED SITUATED IN THE NW
¼ OF SECTION 27, T.14N, R.66W., 6  P.M., LARAMIE COUNTY, WY (RIGHT-OF-WAYTH
LOCATED N. OF PERSHING BLVD., S. OF DELL RANGE BLVD., E. OF GROVE DR., AND
W. OF COLLEGE DR.)” – referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor - Mr. Collins).
[CA] “A RESOLU TION DE TERMINING THA T CO NDITIONS F OR A NNEXATION
REQUIRED BY WYO. STAT. §15-1-402 EXIST FOR THE PROPERTY DESCRIBED AS THE
NORTHERLY PO RTION OF LOT 1 , B LOCK 1 , IN CLUSIVE O F TH E 1 6’ U TILITY
EASEMENT, ROGERS SUBDIVISION, AND LOTS 3 THROUGH 5, AND THE NORTHERLY
HALF OF ADJACENT VACATED ALLEY, BLOCK 2, COULSON ADDITION, LA RAMIE
COUNTY, WY (LOCATED S. OF AND ADJACENT TO MESSENGER CT., W. OF MCCANN
AVE.)” – referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor - Mr. Collins).
[CA] “A RESOLU TION DE TERMINING T HAT CO NDITIONS F OR A NNEXATION
REQUIRED BY WYO. STAT. §15-1-402 EXIST FOR THE PROPERTY DESCRIBED AS LOT
16, BLOCK 1, DOWNEY ADDITION, LARAMIE COUNTY, WY (LOCATED NW. CORNER
OF RIDGE RD. AND LAND CT.)” – referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor - Mr. Collins).
[CA] “A RESOLUTION  TO SUPPORT AND ADOPT THE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE
CHEYENNE T RANSPORTATION S AFETY M ANAGEMENT P LAN” –  r eferred t o P ublic
Services Committee (sponsor - Mr. Brown).
[CA] “A RESOLU TION A CKNOWLEDGING RECEI PT OF  A ND SUPPORTI NG THE
RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE EAST DELL RANGE/US 30 CORRIDOR STUDY, WHICH
INCLUDES THE CHRISTENSEN RAILROAD OVERPASS PLAN” – referred to Public Services
Committee (sponsor - Ms. Broyles).
LEASES/CONTRACTS/LEGAL:
Contract between the City of Cheyenne, Youth Alternatives, and the State of Wyoming,
Department of Family Services, Division of Juvenile Services for diversion and transitional services.
Mr. Segrave moved t o approve, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  M otion carried.  V oting “yes” – all
members of the governing body present.  (#5275)
Contract between the City of Cheyenne, Recreation Division, and Josh Cossitt for professional
tennis services. Mr. Segrave moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Upon inquiry, Kari Kivisto,
Asst. Director, Recreation, Aquatics, Ice and Events Division, advised the City will receive $500.00
for the use of City facilities. Motion carried.  Vo ting “yes” – all members of the governing body
present.  (#5276)
Contract Employment Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Police Department, and Tina
Henderson for crime victim assistance services. Mr. Segrave moved to approve an annual salary
amount not t o exceed $34,248.88 plus benefits and any o vertime compensation pursuant t o t he
provisions of the agreement, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Mr.  Segrave clarified that since Finance
Committee met it had been brought to his attention that the agreement also provides for employment
benefits and overtime compensation, therefore, the motion for this item, as well as the next t wo
agenda items, reflects approval of the base salary plus benefits and any overtime compensation as
outlined in t he agreement. Motion carried.  Vo ting “yes” – all members o f t he go verning body
present.  (#5277)
Contract Employment Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Police Department, and
Brenda Johnson for crime victim assistance services.  Mr. Segrave moved to approve an annual salary
amount not t o exceed $30,422.97 plus benefits and any o vertime compensation pursuant t o t he
provisions of the agreement, seconded by Mr. Brown. Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members
of the governing body present.  (#5278)
Contract Employment Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Police Department, and
Carole Anderson-Kincaid for crime victim assistance services.  Mr. Segrave moved to approve an
annual salary amount not to exceed $24,881.08 plus benefits and any overtime compensation pursuant
to the provisions of the agreement, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all
members of the governing body present.  (#5279)
[CA] Contract between the City of Cheyenne, Police Department, and Laramie County School
District No. 1, for School Resource Officers for the 2008-2009 school year – referred to Finance
Committee.
[CA] Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Frontier Mall Associates LP, and DBL Peripheral
Properties LP, for Frontier Mall Drainage, addressing pro perty det ention requirements t hrough
participation in construction of a regional detention basin – referred to Finance Committee.
CHANGE ORDERS/CONTRACT MODIFICATIONS:
Contract Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4607 between the City of Cheyenne, Sanitation
Department, and A-1 Organics to provide resources and services for the public composting facility.
Mr. Segrave moved to approve in an amount not to exceed $189,312.80, seconded by Mr. Valdez.
Upon inquiry, Dennis Pino, Solid Waste Director, provided information on monitoring of compost
contents to meet nationally recognized standards.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of
the governing body present.  (#4607)
Contract Modification No. 1 to Contract No. 4937 between the City of Cheyenne, Sanitation
Department, and Clean Harbors for hazardous waste disposal services.  Mr. S egrave moved to
approve in an amount not to exceed $200,000.00, seconded by Mr. Brown. Upon inquiry, Dennis
Pino, Solid Waste Director, clarified hazardous waste includes such items as pesticides, paints, oils,
cleaners and solvents, etc., but does not include electronic waste.  He stated the department works
closely w ith Laramie County a s th ey have funding for a  p rogram th at a ssists w ith d isposing of
hazardous waste products.  M otion carried.  Vo ting “yes” – al l members of the governing body
present.  (#4937)
[CA] Contract Modification No. 1 to Contract No. 5108 between the City of Cheyenne, Parks &
Recreation Dept ., and Sco tch Bo y Landscaping, for irrigation and sod in Western Hills Park –
referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Contract M odification No . 2 t o Co ntract No . 4968 b etween t he C ity o f Ch eyenne,
Engineering Dept., and the Wyoming Dept. of Transportation, to add a supplemental project review
meeting and a public scoping meeting for reconstruction of W. Pershing Blvd. from I-25 to Pioneer
Ave. (2003-2006 1% Sales Tax) – referred to Finance Committee.
CONSIDERATION OF BIDS:
Consideration of Bid #M-22-08 for a contract between the City of Cheyenne and Reiman
Corp., for t he Norris Viaduct Replacement Project (1% Specific Purpose Sales & U se Tax and
Federal Grant funds).  John Rogers, representing Scott Contracting, Inc., Henderson, CO, a bidder
on the project, expressed concerns regarding recommendation for approval relative to selection of
the lowest base bidder and staff proposal involving alternates. He provided a brief summary of bid
differences as submitted by Scott Contracting and Reiman Corporation; discussed a 2002 Wyoming
Supreme Court case; provided copies of a worksheet comparing bids between the two companies,
with alternates, and explained Scott Contracting’s reason for submitting an alternate concrete staining
material other than what was specified in the bid document.  He stated that although Reiman may
have submitted the lowest base bid, Scott Contracting had the lowest overall bid when including the
alternates.  Barton Puryear, in-house staff counsel for Scott Contracting, advised their company’s bid
would provide savings to the City; reviewed bid criteria; indicated that several supplies and manpower
would be obtained locally, and encouraged the bid be awarded to Scott Contracting.  John Fafoutakis
spoke in favor of Scott Contracting, Inc.’s bid due to overall cost savings and use of taxpayers’
dollars.  Gwendolyn Connell and Debbie Brennan spoke in favor of awarding the bid to a Wyoming
company that will assist with the local economy.  Mr. Rogers addressed the local contractor bid vs.
out-of-state bid and explained as there is a substantial amount of Federal funding involved, the bid
was conducted without consideration of the in-state bidder process.  He referenced recent projects
(Laramie County Library and St. Mary’s School) involving out-of-state companies that have hired
subcontractors locally and purchased supplies locally, as Scott Contracting would do.  Mr. Segrave
reported there was no recommendation on the item from Finance Committee. Ms. Broyles moved to
accept the base bid from Reiman Corp., Cheyenne, with Alternatives #1, 3, 4, 5(b) and 6 in an amount
not to exceed $18,389,734.60, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Discussion included the following topics:
Project as a high priority for the community; aesthetics and amenities involved with some of the
proposed alternates; available funding and assistance from grants and 1% Specific Purpose sales tax;
monetary assistance from Frontier Refining for Alternate #6; project eligibility for State Loan and
Investment funding, and public meetings and input on  the project a nd alternates desired.  U pon
inquiry, Barb Dorr, City Treasurer, provided information on 1% Specific Purpose sales tax collection
amounts and current fund balance, grant monies received and estimated project funding shortage, and
City Engineer Ken Lewis clarified funding for Alternate #6 would be provided by Frontier Refining
in t he amount o f $1.5 million do llars. Discussion co ntinued o n awarding t he bid with alternates
without having all of the funding in place, review of the proposed alternates and options for those
involving aesthetics, building a basic efficient bridge structure, manpower to maintain landscaped
areas, and bid document language and the bidding process.  Upon inquiry, Mark Stark, Olsson and
Associates, design team project manager, confirmed he had toured some past concrete projects in the
community during the initial stages of the Norris Bridge project, and provided information on fees
paid to Olsson and Associates for its project services.  During comments concerning the quality of
concrete i nvolved i n p rojects th roughout th e c ommunity, c oncrete s tandards, a nd l ife s pan of
concrete, Mr. Brown raised a point of order questioning the relevancy of comments being made.
Mayor Spiker ruled comments could continue.  Upon inquiry, Rich Bolkovatz, chairman of the City’s
past co mmittee t hat assisted with review and modification o f t he City’s co ncrete specifications,
advised m odification reco mmendations t o co ncrete s pecifications were agreed upo n b y l ocal
contractors serving on the committee. Discussion continued on City concrete specifications, condition
of failing concrete and projected life span; review of bid alternates and citizens’ input in determining
alternate proposals; bid document wording; awarding of bid based upon lowest base bid received;
fiduciary respo nsibility t o t axpayers; l ocal an d n on-local b idders o n pro jects; en gineers pro ject
estimate; staff proposed alternates; importance of alternates involving traffic signalization and storm
sewer w ork; a lternates involving lighting a nd c oncrete staining; c ommunity beautification, p ark
environment and aesthetics; voter support for the project; quality infrastructure, and project costs.
Upon inquiry, City At torney Claudia Angelos, a dvised t he bid d ocument c ould be followed by
awarding the bid based upon the base amount and adding alternates to it. Motion failed. Voting “yes”
– Ms. Broyles and Mr. Valdez.  Voting “no” – Mr. Brown, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Laybourn,
Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mayor Spiker.  Mr. Valdez moved to approve the base bid submitted by
Reiman Corp. in the amount of $16,858,928.17 with alternates #4 and #6 for a total bid amount of
$17,168,638.00 a nd re quest s taff e nter i nto v alue e ngineering d iscussions with t he c ontractor,
seconded by Ms. Broyles. Following a ten minute recess, Mayor Spiker reconvened the meeting at
8:00 p.m.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Lewis clarified the total bid amount is $17,168,638.00 including the two
alternates (#4 and #6). Mr. Fafoutakis commented o n one o f t he alternates (not included in the
motion) t hat would provide for a park facility in relationship t o its location, building roads and
structures that will last, and using fiduciary judgment to award the bid to the lowest bidder. Upon
query, Mr. Lewis advised that by adding alternates #4 and #6 to the lowest bid submitted, Reiman’s
bid would be the lowest by approximately $103,000.00, and explained that “value engineering” means
the contractor will look at more efficient means and less expensive materials to approach the same
project to receive an equal and acceptable end product.  He verified if, as a result of value engineering
discussions, any contract modifications were determined to be presented they would come before the
governing body for approval.  Further discussion followed on project costs, funding, scenario of
adding remaining alternates in the future, and engineering estimate affiliated with Alternate #6.  In
conjunction with the estimated time frame in which results of value engineering discussions could be
provided, M r. L ewis indicated information c ould p ossibly be p rovided w ithin a pproximately 3
months, an d adv ised ce rtain addi tional alternates t hat m ay b e co nsidered as  a res ult o f v alue
engineering discussions would have to be issued to the same contractor. Motion carried.  Voting
“yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of Ms. Case and Mr. Laybourn
voting “no”. (#5280)
Consideration o f Bid # M-34-08 for a  c ontract between t he City o f Cheyenne a nd STC
Construction Co., Inc., for the FY 2008 M illing and Utility Adjustments Project (2003-2006 1%
Sales Ta x). M r. S egrave m oved to a ccept t he b id s ubmitted b y STC  C onstruction C o., In c.,
Cheyenne, i n a n a mount n ot t o e xceed $ 134,925.00, s econded by M r. B rown.  U pon i nquiry
concerning whether any roads to b e rehabilitated were located within Ward II, Ken Lewis, City
Engineer, advised he could provide a list of project areas.  Discussion followed on road project work
and needs in the City’s three different wards.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the
governing body present with the exception of Dr. Rinne and Mr. Segrave voting “no”. (#5281)
[CA] Consideration of  B id # R-1-09 f or f urnishing tw o n ew tw in s crew c ab &  chassis f rom
Cheyenne Freightliner, for the Sanitation Dept. – referred to Finance Committee. 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-2-09 for furnishing four solid waste transfer trailers from Ameri-
Tech Equipment, for the Sanitation Dept. – referred to Finance Committee.
ANNOUNCEMENTS/REPORTS/MOTIONS:
Announcement was made that a Calcutta will be held July 26, 2008 beginning at 5:30 p.m.
at the Cheyenne Frontier Days VIP/Sponsor Tent located in Frontier Park in conjunction with the
2008 Cheyenne Frontier Days Rodeo.  Proceeds to benefit Cheyenne area charities.
Announcement was made of the appointment of Richard Keslar to the Tourism Promotion
Joint Powers Board, and Nancy Abraham to the Historic Preservation Board, to be confirmed July
28, 2008.
Announcement was made of the reappointment of Connie Sloan-Cathcart to the Public Transit
Advisory Board, to be confirmed July 28, 2008.
OTHER CITY BUSINESS:
John Fafoutakis spoke generally on project cost over-runs, expressing his hope that this will
not b e an  i ssue wi th t he No rris Vi aduct Re placement Pr oject, an d i n f avor o f b uilding b asic,
dependable construction projects and the need to repair roads.
Upon inquiry regarding whether residents are allowed access to fish at Lake Absarraca during
Frontier Days, Rick Parish, Parks and Recreation Director, clarified persons wishing to fish during
the Frontier Days event can have access and just need to identify their purpose with CFD security
individuals at the Lake entrance.
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was officially
adjourned at 8:33 p.m.
 Submitted by,
 
 Carol A. Intlekofer, CMC 
 City Clerk
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.

 RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
July 28, 2008
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date at 6:00 p.m.
in Council Chambers.  Present were: MAYOR-Jack R. Spiker; COUNCIL MEMBERS-Mr. Brown,
Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins (arriving at 6:04 p.m.), Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne,
Mr. Segrave and Mr. Valdez.
 
Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Barb Dorr, City Treasurer, and Erik Rasmussen,
Deputy City Attorney.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests, in which event the item
will be removed from the Consent Agenda and considered in its normal sequence on the agenda.)
Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, Mayor Spiker announced agenda items #15, 16, 23(a)(b), 24(a)(b),
and 26(a)(b) would be removed from the Consent Agenda. Comments were made pertaining to
removal of Consent Agenda items.  Mr.  Brown moved to approve remaining Consent Agenda items,
seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present
with the exception of Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Segrave voting “no”.

2008.  Motion (per consent agenda) carried.
[CA] MINUTES FROM VOUCHERS MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON JULY 21,
2008.  Motion (per consent agenda) carried.
Mr. Segrave  moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Valdez.

reviewed i nformation a vailable f or v ouchers p ayable to:  F rederika B arela ( $36.73), Y outh
Alternatives employee, reimbursement for ink cartridges; Gade Concrete ($1,100.00), excavate, form
and pour sidewalk to restroom at Pointe Park, and Soothing Sensations ($105.00), refund of business
license application fees.  Main motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body
with the exception of Ms. Case and Mr. Laybourn voting “no”, and Mr. Collins who did not vote.
“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 2.04.160(D)(6), READINGS-COMMITTEE
REPORTS-AMENDMENTS, OF CHAPTER 2.04, MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL, OF TITLE
2, ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL, OF THE CODE OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE,
WYOMING.”  Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Segrave moved to approve on second reading,
seconded by Mr. Brown. Upon inquiry as to the purpose of the ordinance, Mayor Spiker advised the
state legislature at its last session increased the amount required for advertising of contract bids or
response from $20,000.00 t o $35,000.00 and t he o rdinance is in co njunction with t he state law
change.  Upon inquiry, City Treasurer Barb Dorr stated the change factors in inflation and increased
costs for public improvement projects; provided information on oversight of those projects involving
costs up to the $35,000.00 threshold, including governing body approval of vouchers, and indicated
the last ordinance involving this topic ($20, 000.00 threshold) was approved in 1995.  Discussion
followed on  p urchasing r equirements, p rocedures involving c alls f or b ids a nd/or r equests f or
proposals/quotes, governing body involvement and oversight in purchasing process, City Council
departmental bu dget a pproval a uthority, a nd C ity Attorney staff w ritten o pinion indicating t he
ordinance sponsor did not have a conflict of interest in sponsoring the ordinance.  Upon inquiry
regarding whether other cities have implemented similar ordinance changes, Mayor Spiker advised
it was unknown if other cities/towns had or were enacting similar changes, and stated the Wyoming
Association of Municipalities (WAM), whose members consist of all 99 communities within the state,
supported and lobbied for the change during the legislative session.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes”
– all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Laybourn and Dr. Rinne voting “no”.

AVE.).”  Ms. Broyles moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” –
all members of the governing body. (#5054)

(#5056)

[CA] “A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING SUBMISSION OF AN APPLICATION T O THE

TWO 22 PASSENGER REPLACEMENT BUSSES” -- referred to Finance Committee (sponsor -
Mr. Pierson).

AQUIFER RECHARGE, STORAGE AND RECOVERY PROJECT AND AUTHORIZING THE

[CA] “A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND CITY CLERK TO EXECUTE
A PURC HASE A GREEMENT T O A CQUIRE RE AL PROPERT Y A T 4500 DELL  RA NGE

Mr. Collins and Mr. Segrave).
LEASES/CONTRACTS/LEGAL:
Contract between the City of Cheyenne, Police Department, and Laramie County School
District No. 1, for School Resource Officers for the 2008-2009 school.  M r. Segrave moved to
approve in an amount not to exceed $329,606.00, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Motion carried.  Voting
“yes” – all members of the governing body.  (#5285)
Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Frontier Mall Associates LP, and CBL Peripheral
Properties LP, for Frontier Mall Drainage, addressing p roperty det ention requirements t hrough
participation in construction of a regional detention basin.  Mr. Segrave moved to approve, seconded
by Mr. Brown.  Upon inquiry, City Engineer Ken Lewis explained the agreement will allow Frontier
Mall Properties to participate in the regional detention basin that will be created by the Dry Creek
FEMA p roject; in dicated t he ma ll p roperties fin ancial p articipation w ill b e a pproximately
$116,000.00, and advised any opportunity for future properties to participate in the detention basin
would be reviewed by staff and FEMA and would include individual review of the property relative
to drainage calculations, impact, and related issues.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of
the governing body.  (#5286)
[CA] Maintenance Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the Wyoming Department of
Transportation f or t he i nstallation an d m aintenance o f en hancements f or t he R andall A venue
Interchange Project  (2003-2006 1% Sales Tax) -- referred to Finance Committee.
CHANGE ORDERS/CONTRACT MODIFICATIONS:
Contract Modification No. 1 to Contract No. 5108 between the City of Cheyenne, Parks &
Recreation Dept., and Scotch Boy Landscaping, for irrigation and sod in Western Hills Park.  Mr.
Segrave moved to approve in an amount not to exceed $7,400.00, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Motion
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  (#5108)
Contract M odification No . 2 t o Co ntract No . 4968 b etween t he C ity o f Ch eyenne,
Engineering Dept., and the Wyoming Dept. of Transportation, to add a supplemental project review
meeting and a public scoping meeting for reconstruction of W. Pershing Blvd. from I-25 to Pioneer
Ave. (2003-2006 1% Sales Tax).  Mr. Segrave moved to approve in an amount no t t o exceed
$10,440.00, seconded by Mr. Valdez. Upon inquiry, City Engineer Ken Lewis advised the Wyoming
Dept. of Transportation (WYDOT) has already held these meetings but additional meetings will be
held prior to final approval of t he project, and that this is a WYDOT assisted project following
WYDOT’s schedule.  He explained the amount of the contract modification includes individual staff
consultants’ hours to compile data, prepare documents and visual aids, attend meetings, and any post-
meeting and peripheral activities.  Discussion included timeliness of submission of the modification
relative to WYDOT’s schedule and the meetings already being held; City and WYDOT contract
management issues; project information and meeting notification to affected neighborhood residents;
federal funding involved in the project; project including work at the Randall Ave. interchange of I-
25, and support for keeping affected residents informed.  Mr. Lewis provided information concerning
WYDOT’s public meetings and residents’ notification efforts, and stated there are tw o p rojects
involved, WYDOT’s Randall Interchange Reconstruction project, and t he City’s Pershing West
Reconstruction project that WYDOT is doing on the City’s behalf.  He confirmed the State is the lead
agency for the contracts.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body  with
the exception of Mr. Laybourn voting “no”.  (#4968)
[CA] Amendment No. 3 to Contract No. 3516 between the City of Cheyenne and the Wyoming
Association o f Risk Management P roperty I nsurance Joint P owers Board for a n Amended a nd
Restated Joint Powers Agreement -- referred to Finance Committee.
CONSIDERATION OF BIDS:
Consideration of  B id # R-1-09 f or f urnishing two  new tw in s crew c ab &  c hassis f rom
Cheyenne Freightliner, for the Sanitation Dept.  Mr. Segrave moved to accept the bid submitted by
Cheyenne Freightliner in an amount not to e xceed $203,204.00, seconded by Mr. Valdez. Upon
inquiry, Vicki Nemecek, Public Works Dept., confirmed her attendance at a recent Council work
session involving discussion on the anticipated life span of the current landfill and related future
landfill options.  Comment followed regarding whether documentation was available on the potential
life span a nd c apacity of the e xisting landfill and how t ransportation o f waste t o Colorado w ill
increase the life span time frame. Mr. Segrave raised  a point of order indicating that comments being
made were not relevant to the motion on the floor as the decision to transfer solid waste to Ault, CO
had already been decided at a previous meeting.  Mayor Spiker ruled in favor of the point of order,
indicating comments were “off subject”, and requested discussion remain relevant to the motion to
act on the bid to purchase two vehicles for use in transporting waste to Colorado.  During comments
and upon inquiry, Ms. Nemecek provided information on sanitation’s equipment replacement plan
and discussed factors involving fuel costs and the number of trips that may be made to the Ault site
based o n c ommunity waste v olume and r ecycling e fforts.  M otion c arried.  V oting “ yes” –  a ll
members of the governing body with the exception of Ms. Case and Mr. Laybourn voting “no”.
Consideration of Bid #R-2-09 for furnishing four solid waste transfer trailers from Ameri-
Tech Equipment, for the Sanitation Dept.  Mr. Segrave moved to accept the bid submitted by Ameri-
Tech Equipment, Casper, in an amount not to exceed $287,600.00, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Motion
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Ms. Case and Mr.
Laybourn voting “no”.
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-4-09 for furnishing 646 1½ cubic yard refuse containers from Ameri-
Tech Equipment Co., Casper WY, for the Sanitation Dept. -- referred to Finance Committee.
APPOINTMENTS:
Appointment of Richard Keslar to the Tourism Promotion Joint Powers Board, and Nancy
Abraham t o t he Historic Preservation Board.  M r. Collins moved t o approve, seconded by Mr.
Segrave.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.
Reappointment of Connie Sloan-Cathcart to the Public Transit Advisory Board.  Mr. Segrave
moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Collins. Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the
governing body.
ANNOUNCEMENTS/REPORTS/MOTIONS:
[CA] Annual leaseholder improvement report submitted by the Airport Golf Club, Inc. -- referred
to Finance Committee.
Announcement was made of the appointment of  Ami Skeens to the Public Transit Advisory
Board, and Peter Illoway to the Cheyenne Regional Airport Board, to be confirmed August 11, 2008.
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held August 11, 2008 at 6:00 p.m. in City
Council Chambers to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyo. Stat.
§ 15-1-402 exists for the property described as being situated in a portion of Section 1, 12, and 17,
T13N., R67W. of the 6  P.M., Laramie County, WY (located S. of I-80 and predominantly E. ofth
Southwest Dr.).
OTHER CITY BUSINESS:
Resident John Fafoutakis encouraged placement of a plastics recycling drop-off bin in the
south Cheyenne area, and expressed concerns with individuals on ATVs he has observed harassing
an antelope herd in a construction area near Walterscheid.
Mayor Spiker recognized former City Councilman Tom Scherr, who was present at t he
meeting.
Upon i nquiry regardi ng pro posed ac quisition of pro perty l ocated at  4500 Del l Ra nge
Blvd.(agenda item #22), Mayor Spiker and Rick Parish, Parks and Recreation Director, verified an
offer t o purch ase h as b een made an d i s co ntingent upo n go verning b ody appro val; pro vided
information on due diligence that has been conducted (i.e. building inspections, etc.); funding that has
been approved to put toward a new facility, and stated the site will provide for relocation of the Parks
Maintenance Shop due to construction of the new Children’s Garden near the Botanic Gardens.
Comment was made regarding the property transaction process and communication of information
to City Council members.
Concern was expressed regarding street, curb and gutter debris along the Cheyenne Frontier
Days parade route and the downtown area during the recent celebration in conjunction with the Clean
and Sweep program.  It was noted that the increase in volume of persons in Cheyenne during CFD,
and the number of events in the downtown area, make it a challenge to keep up with clean-up efforts.
All City employees involved with the CFD event were commended for their efforts during this year’s
celebration.
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was officially
adjourned at 7:13 p.m.
 Submitted by,
 
 Carol A. Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.

 August 5, 2008

MEETING: Cheyenne City Council | DATE: 2008-08-11 | CLIP_ID: 39 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 39

   RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
August 11, 2008
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date at 6:00 p.m.
in Council Chambers.  Present were: MAYOR-Jack R. Spiker; COUNCIL MEMBERS-Mr. Brown,
Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mr.
Valdez.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.
 
Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Barb Dorr, City Treasurer, and Claudia Angelos,
City Attorney.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA]  are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests, in which event the
item will be removed f rom the Consent Agenda and considered in its normal sequence  on the
agenda.)  Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, Mayor Spiker announced agenda items #21, 23, 24, 34(a),
35(a), 36(a), 37(a) and 38(a) would be removed from the Consent Agenda.   Comment was made
pertaining to removal of Consent Agenda items. Mr. Collins moved to approve remaining Consent
Agenda item s, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Motion carr ied.  Voting  “yes” – a ll members of the
governing body with the exception of Mr. Laybourn voting “no”.
[CA] MINUTES FROM REGULAR MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON JULY 28,
2008.  Motion (per consent agenda) carried.
[CA] MINUTES FROM VOUCHERS MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON AUGUST
4, 2008.  Motion (per consent agenda) carried.
Mr. Segrave  moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Brown.
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
Mayor Spiker opened a public hearing for the purpose of receiving comments and input to
determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyo. Stat. § 15-1-402 exists
for the property described as being situated in a portion of Section 1, 12, and 17, T.13N., R.67W.
of the 6  P.M., Laramie County, WY (located S. of I-80 and predominantly E. of Southwest Dr.).th
Brandon Cammarata, Urban Planning office, reviewed requirements and compliance of conditions
contained in Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402, including specific information indicating compliance with Wyo.
Stat. §15-1-402(a)(i) through (vi).  The following individuals expressed concerns with the proposed
annexation:  L eo Garcia, J ohn Fafoutakis, Glenn Connor, F rancis Shi ve, Ruby Tomlinson and
Brenda Rath.  Topics discussed included: Public safety and train/vehicular volume concerns with
the railroad crossing at Southwest Drive off West Lincolnway; area traffic congestion and delays,
including effect on emergency responders; problems encountered with alternate traffic routes due
to impassable times at the crossing; suggestion of installing an overpass or underpass (tunnel) at the
crossing; verbal and written safety and traffic concerns received from railroad representatives and
former City staff; statistics on train volumes and injuries/deaths occurring at railroad crossings;
proposed housing development plans for the property and effect on residents in the vicinity relative
to traffic and safety; uses of property in the area (i.e. petroleum storage, pipeline); traffic study;
increased traffic due to o ther nearby developments, and drainage concerns.  Du ring comments,
various speakers submitted written information (on file with office of City Clerk) to governing body
members in support of their statements.  Gay Woodhouse, attorney representing landowners in the
surrounding area of the proposed property to be annexed, submitted a written petition of protest
signed by landowners, and spoke in opposition to annexation of the property.  She reviewed state
statute annexation provisions and requir ements outlined in Wy o. Stat. §15-1-402, and discusse d
traffic in the ar ea, including the e ffect of semi-tr uck “backups” from I -25 affecting College Dr.
traffic; health, safety and we lfare concerns; creation of a ne w county pocket if a nnexation were
approved; water  and sew er se rvices; property  contig uity; exi sting ne ighborhood lifesty le, and
potential future financial effect of annexation on nearby residents relative to repair/replacement of
septic systems. Upon inquiry regarding property use if the proposed housing development did not
occur, Ken Clark, Garrett Properties, LLC, one of the landowners of the property proposed to be
annexed, responded that he has been approached by other interested parties inquiring about use of
the property for other potential projec ts other than a housing  development.  Upon inquiry , Mr.
Cammarata revie wed the c urrent location of the Chey enne A nimal Shelter (CAS) fa cility and
confirmed the entity was a participant in the request for annexation, and provided property zoning
classification information for the proposed annexation site.  Pursuant to inquiry concerning the new
CAS site/building, City Treasurer Barb Dorr stated the City does not hold the mortgage for the CAS
property.  There being no further comments or input and purpose of the hearing having been met,
Mayor Spiker closed the hearing.
“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 2.04.160(D)(6), READINGS-COMMITTEE
REPORTS-AMENDMENTS, OF CHAPTER 2.04, MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL, OF TITLE
2, ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL, OF THE CODE OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE,
WYOMING.”  Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Segrave moved to approve on third and final
reading, seconde d by  Mr. Valde z.  C omments included the following  topics: Monitoring of
expenditures; accountability and fiscal responsibility; City Council oversight in reviewing purchases;
effects of inf lation on project c osts and purcha ses; ordi nance sponsor rela tive to the ordinanc e
subject; City Council departmenta l budget approval; 2008 state leg islative action increasing the
threshold amount (from $20,000.00 to $35,000.00) required for advertising of bids, and Wyoming
Association of Municipalities’ support for the state change.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all
members of the governing body with the exception of Ms. Case, Mr. Laybourn and Dr. Rinne voting
“no”. (#3818)

OF SECTION 8, AND A PORTION OF WALTERSCHEID BOULEVARD SITUATED IN A

AND T HE WE ST L INE O F T RACT 1 6 A LLISON T RACTS, L ARAMIE CO UNTY, WY
(LOCATED S. OF AND ADJACENT TO FOX FARM RD. AND E. OF AND ADJACENT TO
WALTERSCHEID B LVD.).”  R.C. R eiman, with Gate way Sou th, reque sted the ordinanc e be
continued for 30 days.  Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Collins moved to approve on
third and final reading, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Mr. Collins moved to postpone for 30 days (to Sept.
8, 2008), seconded by Mr. Brown.  Mr. Reiman advised a postponement would allow for further
discussion on preliminary plat issues with City staff. Upon inquiry, Martin Matsen, Development
Director, advised there are engineering issues they are attempting to resolve on the preliminary plat
and suggested the plat could be approved concurrently with annexation action or after the ordinance
was approved.  Mr. Matsen provided information on the area involving engineering and right-of-way
issues and effect of topography in the area, and Mr. Reiman spoke on right -of-way concerns and
current dirt (fill) work.  Mr. Reiman clarified he had written documentation from the South Side
Water and Sewer District office stating the District will provide services to the property.  Comments
followed on South S ide Water a nd Sewer District’s policies involving a cceptance or denia l of
properties to receive services.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Matsen stated the postponement will allow staff
more time to work with the developer.  Motion to postpone for 30 days carried.  Voting “yes” –  all
members of the governing body.
Following a 10 minute recess, Mayor Spiker reconvened the meeting at 7:30 p.m.
“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING TITLE 5, BUSINESS LICENSES AND REGULATIONS,
CHAPTER 5.12, ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES, SECTION 5.12.090 (B), MINORS-DISPENSING
ROOM RESTRI CTIONS, OF T HE CODE OF  THE CI TY OF  CHEYENNE, WYOMI NG,
CONCERNING MI NORS E MPLOYED I N A  RES TAURANT AND F ULL SER VICE
RESTAURANT ENVIRONMENT.”  The following individuals, affiliated with City retail and bar
and grill type liquor licenses, spoke in favor of the ordinance:  Mylon Skala, Applebees; Rachael
Svobode and John Johnson, Old Chicago; Thomas Rudolph and James Yates, Sanfords Grub and
Pub, and Jay Hutchinson, Olive Garden.  Topics discussed by the speakers included: Management,
workforce/staffing levels and operational issues regarding employees in their respective businesses,
which involve the sale of food as the primary purpose of business, who are 18, 19 and 20 years of
age and their inability, under City Code, to enter the dispensing room to serve  as host/hostesses
(seating guests) or to deliver  food/drinks to dining pa trons; current state statutes and City  Code,
which allows those employees who are at least 18 years of age (in a restaurant environment) to serve
alcohol to all other dining areas of the restaurant, except the dispensing room, through walk-up area
access; clarification that t he definition of “serving ” does not include  mixing and pouring drinks
(bartending); importance of being able to utilize persons ages 18-21 as a labor source, and labor pool
shortage issues affecting customer service levels. Lynn Birleffi, Wyoming Lodging and Restaurant
Assoc., spoke in support of the ordinance, stating this is an important issue to many local restaurant
businesses.  She discussed workforce/labor shortage problems; that employees entering a dispensing
room would do so only during employment hours for work purposes; that employees must follow
liquor licensees’ employment policies to ensure continued employment, and that other communities
allow this in a variety  of diffe rent spectrums since it is al lowed by state statutes.  Ms. Birlef fi
submitted written “Talking Points” in support of her statements (on file with office of City Clerk).
Alfreda Gonzales, Exec. Dir., Laramie County Community Partnership, advised the Partnership is
working on the issue of underage drinking and that results of a survey on relevant policy research
reflected a lack of sufficient or cohesive community policies to help reduce underage access to
alcohol.  She explained the Partnership’s strategic plan on this topic and efforts to forward the issue
to state legislators; advised of a forthcoming report to be released later this year; provided statistical
information relative to research involving underage drinking, and encouraged the governing body
to not move forwa rd with the ordinance at this time. Br yan Grzegorczyk spoke in favor  of the
ordinance, stating employed individuals are not going to work to drink, but to work.  Mr. Ya tes
expressed his belief that the proposed ordinance change was a workforce problem, not an underage
drinking i ssue, and commented on liquor licensee s’ financ ial investments in their respe ctive
businesses.  Mr. Col lins moved to appr ove on sec ond reading, seconded by Mr. B rown. Upon
inquiry, Tom Montoya, Chief Enforcement Officer, Wyoming Liquor Division, provided a brie f
history involving the adoption of the 2007 state legislative bill, explaining the bill was originated
based upon a decreasing labor force in certain areas of the state due to effects of the energy boom.
He indicated the proposed ordinance will affect liquor licensees operating in a restaurant and full-
service restaurant environment only, and will not apply to bars (i.e. Licensee operations not meeting
the state definition of restaurant and full service restaurants).  In addition, he stated it will not allow
18, 19 and 20 year olds to serve as bartenders, and reported that, state-wide, L iquor D ivision
enforcement agents have reported no problems with 18-20 yr. old employees serving.  Extensive
discussion followed and included the following subjects: Amending municipal code to be in line
with state statutes; workforce labor shortages; suggestion of requesting state legislators to change
the definition of dispensing room; raising wages to attract employees; current state-wide “Where Do
We Draw The Line” program; access to alcohol and underage drinking issues; exposure of alcohol
to those under 21 y ears of age by allowing them to serve in dispensing  rooms; food and a lcohol
service areas; current employee services within vs. outs ide of a  dispensing r oom; bartender and
server T IPS t raining r equirements an d P olice u nderage co mpliance ch ecks; z ero u nderage
access/drinking tolerance policy; liquor licensees’ responsibilities involving underage individuals,
and other City ordinances approved to assist with alcohol monitoring and control.  Upon inquiry
during comments, City Clerk Carol Intlekofer clarified the governing body reviews annual liquor
licenses (renewal applications) after the first of each year before the renewal term begins, which is
April 1 .  U pon in quiry, M s. Svo bode c larified i ndividuals s erving a lcohol t o c ustomers inst
restaurants are responsible for checking IDs, and Police Chief Bob Fecht advised underage alcohol
compliance checks are conducted through the Police Dept. as well as review of employee TIPS
training records. He stated throughout the past year no TIPS violations have been found at any of the
facilities. During discussion and upon re quest by Chief Fecht, the Chief, with assistanc e by Mr.
Skala, presented a “what if” scenario reflecting the difference between wait staff serving food and
alcohol “inside” vs. “outside” a dispensing room. Further discussion followed on fines for underage
serving and licensee/managerial responsibility for compliance with state and local laws.  Motion
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Ms. Broyles, Mr.
Pierson and Mr. Valdez voting “no”. Under other City business, Amber Ash spoke in favor of the
ordinance; suggested Coun cil review what other  states ar e allowing; cited her  former personal
employment experience relative to the  ordinance topic, and expressed her belief that it i s t he
bartenders’ role to oversee a dispensing room area, which is more closely monitored than other areas
of a restaurant environment.

“yes” – all members of the governing body.  (#5058)

(SLIB & GENERAL FUND RESERVES).”  Mr. Segrave moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Brown.
Mr. Seg rave moved to amend by  substitut e, which c larifies f unding sour ces f or the purc hase,
seconded by Mr. Brown.  Ri ck Parish, Parks and Recreation Director, advised the substitute, in
addition to clarifying dollar amounts and funding sources as requested at Finance Committee, also
contains min or wo rding c hanges.  Mo tion to  a mend by su bstitute c arried.  Vo ting “ yes” – a ll
members of the governing body.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Parish provided information on the design-build
contract  previously approved for the design and construction of a new Parks maintenance building
at D utcher F ield; e xplained c osts a ffiliated w ith the  ne w b uilding, infrastructure a nd sit e
improvements (approximately $1.2 milli on), and r eviewed fundin g sources and aspe cts of and
amounts expended toward the design-build contract. He stated the Parks shop was being displaced
due to the new  Children’s Discovery Garden to be built at B otanic Gardens and that during  the
course of seeking a temporary facility to lease until the new building could be constructed, the Dell
Range property was broug ht to his attention.  He stated the De ll Range property consists of a
building (14,000 sq. ft.) that is larger than the one proposed to be constructed (7,000 sq. ft.) and
includes 2.9 ac res of  land, providing  for a dditional future expansion, for a  purcha se price  of
$1,000,000.00.  He noted positive characteristics of the site (i.e. ready access to major roadways,
room for equipment storage, opportunity for growth and enhancements at the site).  D iscussion
followed and included the following topics: Time frame affiliated with new construction and locating
a temporary site for the maintenance shop vs. decision process to instead propose purchasing a
facility; original placement of a new facility at Dutcher Field as developed during preliminary plans;
costs affiliated with the design-build contract that the City must pay under the contract; benefits of
the Dell Range property, including space for growth; cost comparison of purchasing the property vs.
constructing a new facility; concern with proposed change of constructing a facility to purchasing
an existing property, and communication with City Council members by staff on the proposal to
purchase.  Mr. Parish reviewed the expenses that would be involved in construction of a new facility
at Dutcher Field and noted that the property has depreciated value (which would include the new
building if constructed) as Land and Water Conservation grant funds have been received in the past,
making the property unable to be readily disposed of (sold) if desired by the City in the future.  Brad
Carnahan, Director of Parks, confirmed the architect’s original estimate to construct the new building
was in excess of $900,000.00.  F urther discussion followed in suppor t as well as non- support of
purchasing the  proper ty vs. con structing a new  fac ility; benef its of a “sing le move” f or Parks
involving gas tanks, equipment and staff; potential site amenities that could be developed at the Dell
Range property and amount of inside a nd outside storag e spac e ava ilable, and a dministrative
management issues.  Main motion as amended by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – all members
of the governing body with the exception of Ms. Case and Mr. Laybourn voting “no”.  (#5063)
[CA] “A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND THE CITY CLERK TO SIGN A
FINAL PLAT OF WINDMILL ROAD, FIRST FILING, BEING A PORTION OF SECTION 28,
T.14N., R.66W., 6  P.M., CHEYENNE, WYOMING (WINDMILL ROAD LOCATED BETWEENTH
DELL RANGE A ND E . P ERSHING B OULEVARDS A ND T HE S OUTH H ALF O F D ELL
RANGE BOULEVARD BETWEEN GRANDVIEW AND HILLTOP AVENUES” – referred to
Public Services Committee (sponsor - Mr. Collins).

FINAL PLAT OF COLLEGE BUSINESS PARK REFINEMENT E, A REPLAT OF LOTS 7 THRU
12, BLOCK ONE, COLLEGE BUSINESS PARK, CHEYENNE, WYOMING (LOCATED AT THE
NORTHWEST CORNER OF THE INTERSECTION OF LARAMIE ST. AND MONROE AVE.)”
– referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor - Mr. Collins).
[CA] “A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND THE CITY CLERK TO SIGN A
FINAL PLAT OF SOUTH PARK ESTATES, 3  FILING, A REPLAT OF LOTS 58 AND 59,RD
BLOCK ONE, SOUTH  PARK ESTATES, S ECOND F ILING, CHEYENNE, WYOMI NG
(LOCATED AT T HE SOUTHWEST CORNER OF THE I NTERSECTION OF  PARTOYAN
DRIVE AND SECOND STREET)” – referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor - Mr. Collins).
[CA] “A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND THE CITY CLERK TO SIGN A
FINAL PLAT OF SOUTH PARK ESTATES, 5  FILING, A REPL AT OF  LOT 45 AND  ATH
PORTION OF  L OT 44, B LOCK ONE, SOUTH  PARK ESTATES, SECOND FI LING,
CHEYENNE, WYOMING (LOCATED SOUTH OF AND ADJACENT TO W. SECOND STREET,
WITHIN THE CUL-DE-SAC)” – referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor - Mr. Collins).
[CA] “A RESOL UTION APPROVI NG THE SUBMI TTAL OF A  REQUEST TO THE
WYOMING STATE LOAN AND INVESTMENT BOARD TO AMEND CWSRF LOAN #081 IN
THE AMOU NT OF  $40 0,000 FOR EXT ENSIONS TO CHEYENN E’S RECYCL E WATER
SYSTEM AND AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR, CITY CLERK AND BOARD DIRECTOR TO
SIGN ALL RELATED DOCUMENTS REQUIRED” –  referred to Finance Committee (sponsor -
Mr. Valdez).
[CA] “A RESOL UTION AUT HORIZING THE SUB MISSION OF A  BU SINESS READY
COMMUNITIES GRANT APPL ICATION TO TH E WYOMI NG B USINESS COUNCIL ON
BEHALF OF  THE GOV ERNING B ODY OF  THE C ITY OF  CHEYENNE F OR THE
CONTINUED D EVELOPMENT OF T HE DAV ID R. ROMERO SOUTH CHEYENNE
COMMUNITY PARK” – referred to Finance Committee (sponsor - Mr. Valdez).
PRELIMINARY PLATS/PRELIMINARY ZONE CHANGES:
[CA] City Preliminary Plat for Sundance Ridge II, a replat of Tracts 2 and 3, Skyline Tracts,
Cheyenne, Wy oming ( located be tween Store y Boule vard a nd Skyline Drive, on both sides of
Sycamore Road) – referred to Public Services Committee.
[CA] City Preliminary Plat for Gateway South, a replat of a portion of Tract 1, Allison Tracts and
in the NW1/4 of Section 8, T.13N., R.66W., 6th P.M., Cheyenne, Wyoming (located at the southeast
corner of the intersection of Walterscheid Boulevard and W. Fox Farm Road) – referred to Public
Services Committee.
[CA] City Preliminary Plat for BOPU Subdivision, a replat of portions of Blocks 98, 99, 149, 150,
151 and vacated streets and alleyway, Original City, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located at the northwest
corner of the intersection of Snyder and W. 24  Street) – referred to Public Services Committee.th
[CA] City Preliminary Plat for Deming  Drive a nd Walterscheid B oulevard, being portions of
Sections 5 and 6, T.13N., R.66W., 6th P .M., Cheyenne, Wyoming (located south of the Ames
underpass and north of west Fox Farm Road) – referred to Public Services Committee.
LEASES/CONTRACTS/LEGAL:
Maintenance Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the Wyoming Department of
Transportation for the inst allation and maintena nce of  enhanc ements for  the Randall Ave nue
Interchange Project  (2003-2006 1% Sales Tax).  Mr. Segrave moved to approve in an amount not
to exceed $57,599.00, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the
governing body. (#5290)
[CA] Development Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the Church of St. Mary for the
cooperative construction of street improvements at the intersection of 22  Street and O’Neil Avenuend
in conjunction with the site development work at 2200 O’Neil Avenue  (2003-2006 1% Sales Tax)
– referred to Finance Committee.

for the Safe Routes to School (SRTS) Program FY 2008 - Cheyenne Safe Routes to School Planning
Award – referred to Finance Committee.
CHANGE ORDERS/CONTRACT MODIFICATIONS:
Amendment No. 3 to Contract No. 3516 between the City of Cheyenne and the Wyoming
Association of Risk Manag ement Property Insurance Joint Powers B oard for an Amended and
Restated Joint Powers A greement.  M r. Se grave mo ved to  a pprove, s econded b y M r. V aldez.
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  (#3516)
[CA] Contract Modification No. 1 to Contract No. 5065 between the City of Cheyenne and Ameri-
Tech HVAC Services, Inc. to add the Taco John’s Events Center to the Maintenance of Mechanical
Equipment & HVAC Systems Contract – referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Contract Modifica tion #1 to C ontract #5204 betwee n the City  of Chey enne and J -2
Contracting Co. for Contractual Services - Law and Liberty Plaza – referred to Finance Committee.
CONSIDERATION OF BIDS:
Consideration of Bid #R-4-09 for furnishing 646 1½ c ubic yard refuse containers from
Ameri-Tech Equipment Co., Casper WY, for the Sanitation Dept.  Mr. Segrave moved to accept the
bid of Ameri-Tech Equipment Co., Casper, in an amount not to exceed $245,480.00, seconded by
Mr. Brown.  Upon inquiry pursuant to a letter  that had been  received from another bidder, Rudy
Apodaca, Director of Purchasing, advised state statutes were followed in determining the proposed
successful bidder, clarifying that Ameri-Tech Equipment has been a long standing dealer for Teem,
and qualifies as a r esident bidder, therefore, the 5% in-state  preference was applied. Mr. Brown
clarified for  the re cord tha t his personal business company  (Clerk’s note : Ameri-Te ch HVA C
Services) is not associated with Ameri-Tech Equipment of Casper. Motion carried.  Voting “yes”
– all members of the governing body.
[CA] Consideration of Bid #M-3-09 for a contract between Naranjo Civil Constructors, Inc., and
the City of Cheyenne for the Cheyenne Greenway - Safe Routes to School Program, South Park &
Johnson-Goins Corridors – referred to Finance Committee.
APPOINTMENTS:
Appointment of  Ami Skeens to the Public Transit Advisory Board, and Peter Illoway to the
Cheyenne Regional Airport Boa rd.  Mr. Collins moved to approve, se conded by Mr. Seg rave.
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
ANNOUNCEMENTS/REPORTS/MOTIONS:
Annual leaseholder improvement report submitted by the Airport Golf Club, I nc. Bryan
Grzegorczyk, President of Airport Golf Club, indicated things have been running smoothly at the
Club and they have had no problems.  Mr. Seg rave moved to acknowledge receipt of the annual
report, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Upon inquiry concerning recent building roof improvements, Mr.
Grzegorczyk advised the City had the roof replaced as it is responsible for improvements outside of
the building; the Club takes care of improvements within the building.  He reviewed interior areas
that had been remodeled or improved within the past year and, upon query concerning effect on the
Club’s business due to the No Smoking ordinance, advised pull tab (“pickle”) and drink sales were
“down some”, stating tha t proceeds from pickle sales g oes toward Club scholarships.  Motion
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held August 25, 2008 at 6:00 p.m. in City
Council Chambers to discuss the submission of an application for grant funding to the Wyoming
Business Council under the Business Ready Communities: Community Enhancements Program for
funding for continued development of David R. Romero South Cheyenne Community Park.
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held August 25, 2008 at 6:00 p.m. in City
Council Chambers for a restaurant liquor license application filed with the City Clerk's Office for
Primos Cheyenne d/b/a Scotty's Pizza Factory, 1802 Dell Range, Cheyenne, WY.
OTHER CITY BUSINESS:
Resident John Fafoutakis discussed the completion time frame for the new roadway located
by the main Post Office (off Converse) and its benefits to traffic flow in the area; suggested clean-up
efforts be conducted in the drainage ditches at the Rue Terre/Dell Range intersection; encouraged
placement of more plastic recycling bins in the south Cheyenne area; questioned clean-up and costs
of recent flooding that occurred at the Civic Center, and expressed his displeasure with a recent letter
to the editor published in the newspa per written by a City  Council member involving a nother
Council member relative to the upcoming primary election.  With regard to more plastic recycling
bins, Mayor Spiker noted that the Director of Solid Waste has not yet been successful in locating any
business owners in the south Cheyenne area who were interested in having bins on their property.
He also reviewed the City’s property insurance coverage generally with regard to the Civic Center
flooding and advised alternate options for managing drainage near the facility are being researched
to hopefully alleviate future re-occurrences.
Resident Jennifer Price discussed an issue involving herself and a neighbor pursuant to dog
barking and disturbance of the peace, and suggested City Code be changed to support dog owners.
Upon inquiry, City Attorney Claudia Angelos confirmed a former mediation program, implemented
through the City Attorney’s office a few years ago, was no longer available as they were unable to
find individuals to provide mediation service s at no cost.  Comment was made in support of a
mediation program.  Mayor Spiker suggested Ms. Price visit with Police Chief Fecht, who was in
attendance, regarding some of her concerns.
 
Miscellaneous c omments by  City  Council members include d: Civi c Center  insurance
coverage; recent increase in sanitation tipping fees at the landfill relative to notification efforts to
businesses providing sanitation pick-up services to County residents; appreciation to staff for efforts
spent in Civic Center clea n-up of f lood water s and mit igation attempts to alleviate da mage;
suggestion that the Board of Public Utilities consider locating its new administration/engineering
building within t he downtown a rea instead of 24  St. (and Sny der), and announc ement of theth
availability of free counseling services for certain military veterans and families provided by Peak
Wellness Center.
There being  no further  business to come bef ore the  governing body , the meeting  was
officially adjourned at 10:41 p.m.
 Submitted by,
 
 Carol A. Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.

 August 22, 2008

MEETING: Cheyenne City Council | DATE: 2008-08-25 | CLIP_ID: 41 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 41

 RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
August 25, 2008
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date at 6:00 p.m.
in Council Chambers.  Present were: MAYOR-Jack R. Spiker; COUNCIL MEMBERS-Mr. Brown,
Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mr.
Valdez.
 
Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Barb Dorr, City Treasurer, and Claudia Angelos,
City Attorney.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests, in which event the item
will be removed from the Consent Agenda and considered in its normal sequence on the agenda.)
Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, Mayor Spiker announced agenda items #20, 21, 22, 31(a), 32(b) and
33(a) would be removed from the Consent Agenda.  Comment was made pertaining to removal of
Consent Agenda items.  Mr. Collins moved to approve remaining Consent Agenda items, seconded
by M r. B rown.  M otion c arried.  V oting “yes” –  a ll members o f t he g overning bo dy w ith t he
exception of Mr. Laybourn voting “no”.
[CA] MINUTES FROM REGULAR MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON AUGUST
11, 2008.  Motion (per consent agenda) carried.
[CA] MINUTES FROM VOUCHERS MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON AUGUST
18, 2008.  Motion (per consent agenda) carried.
Mr. Segrave  moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Valdez.
Upon inquiry, City Treasurer Barb Dorr and Capt. Jeff Schulz, Cheyenne Police Dept., reviewed
information available on a voucher payable to Cornerstone Programs Corp. ($10,000.00), juvenile
detention fees for month of July.  Capt. Schulz advised Cornerstone operates the facility and provides
services, but Wardell Academy owns the property, and provided information on services received,
police monitoring, and financial support for services involving the City, Sheriff’s Dept. and State of
Wyoming Dept. of Family Services.  He stated there is no other local facility at the present time to
house juvenile offenders. Comments followed on operational management of the facility and past
problems when the facility was operated by Wardell Academy.  Up on query, Ms. Dorr reviewed
vouchers payable to Ft. Collins Radiator ($100.00), radiator repair; H.W. Lochner ($12,429.31),
Crow Creek Flood Control improvement project engineering inspection (Warren Ave. bridge), and
Lands End, Inc. ($32.45), clothing purchase.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the
governing body with the exception of Mr. Laybourn voting “no”.
Mayor Spiker opened a public hearing to receive input and discussion on the submission of
an appl ication f or gr ant f unding t o t he W yoming Bus iness Co uncil under t he B usiness Re ady
Communities: Community Enhancements Program for funding for continued development of David
R. Romero South Cheyenne Community Park. Teresa Moore, Parks and Recreation Dept., conducted
a brief visual presentation involving the purpose of the grant funding request of $500,000.00 (50/50
match) and public meetings that were held to receive input on the Park’s conceptual master plan.  She
advised the grant request is to assist with Phase I development (i.e. sidewalks, trails, playground,
plaza and enhancements to picnic shelter), and provided schedule information for completion of Phase
I.  There being no further comments or input and purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor
Spiker closed the hearing.
Mayor Spiker opened a public hearing for the purpose of receiving comments and input for
a restaurant liquor license application filed with the City Clerk's Office for Primos Cheyenne d/b/a
Scotty's Pizza Factory, 1802 Dell Range, Cheyenne, WY.  There being no comments or input and
purpose o f t he hearing having been met, Mayor Spiker closed t he hearing. The application was
referred to Finance Committee.
“AN OR DINANCE A MENDING TI TLE 5,  BU SINESS LICENSE S A ND
REGULATIONS, C HAPTER 5 .12, A LCOHOLIC BEVERAGES, S ECTION 5 .12.090 (B ),
MINORS-DISPENSING R OOM REST RICTIONS, O F THE CODE OF  T HE CIT Y OF
CHEYENNE, WYOMING, CONCERNING MINORS EMPLOYED IN A RESTAURANT AND
FULL SERVICE RESTAURANT ENVIRONMENT.”  Speaking in opposition to the ordinance
were: Sharon Guerney, affiliated with the State’s Enforcing Underage Drinking Laws program; Jim
Cook, parent and Vice-President of Student Services for Laramie County Community College; Kelsey
James and Ryan Regaglia, Central High School students, and Alfrieda Gonzales, Executive Director,
Laramie County Community Partnership.  Topics discussed included: Information on “Regulating
Strategies for Preventing Youth Access to Alcohol: Best Practices” pursuant to th e U.S. Dept. of
Justice’s E nforcing U nderage D rinking La ws P rogram; p reventing y outh ac cess t o a lcohol;
enforcement of underage drinking violations by law officers; belief that the proposed ordinance is not
a workforce issue but one of business convenience affecting public safety and health; developmental
differences between persons18 to 21 years of age; general statistics involving youth alcohol use and
alcohol related injuries, accidents and incidents; culture and alcohol environment; LCCC alcohol
survey results; economic improvement in salaries paid to young adults working in service related
restaurant environments as an employment incentive; educational awareness and promotion through
responsible training programs; exposure to and availability of alcohol to persons under the legal
drinking age;  co mmunity m essage o f i ntolerance f or un derage dri nking; i ssues, i ncluding peer
pressure, involving 18 to 21 year olds serving alcohol in restaurant dining areas as currently allowed
vs. serving of food and alcohol within a dispensing room environment; recent review of alcohol
regulations in place throughout Laramie County by the Laramie County Community Partnership and
anticipated r eport t o b e r eceived in Oct ober from t he S tate Dep t. o f Health, S ubstance Abuse
Division, reflecting a similar review of state statutes affiliated with underage drinking concerns; need
for a coherent community policy, and request to the governing body to allow time to receive the state
report.  The following individuals, affiliated with City retail and bar and grill type liquor licenses,
spoke in favor of the ordinance: Rachel Svoboda, Old Chicago; Jay Hutchinson, Olive Garden; Mylon
Skala, Applebees, and John Johnson, Old Chicago.  T opics discussed included: Workforce labor
shortage issues; employee wages; inability of persons 18 to 21 years old to serve food and alcohol
to patrons within a dispensing room vs. current City Code and state law allowing those employees
who are at least 18 years of age (in a restaurant environment as defined by state statute) to serve
alcohol to all other dining areas of the restaurant; clarification that the definition of “serving” does
not include mixing and pouring drinks (bartending); importance of being able to utilize persons ages
18-21 as a labor source; labor pool shortage issues affecting customer service levels, and licensees’
responsibilities, i ncluding e mployee T IPS t raining and e nforcement o f bu siness p olicies, a nd
compliance with laws.  John Fafoutakis expressed his belief that the problem is not with restaurant
environments or underage drinking, but with the irresponsibility generally of the alcohol industry,
particularly i ts adv ertising t echniques. Dur ing co mments, v arious s peakers s ubmitted wri tten
documentation (on file with office of City Clerk) to governing body members in support of their
statements. Marty Hendrickson, Restaurant and Lodging Assoc., read a letter on behalf of Lynn
Birleffi, Executive Director of the Wyoming Lodging and Restaurant Assoc., expressing Ms. Birleffi’s
support of the ordinance and its importance in assisting restaurant owners’ with workforce challenges
and quality of customer services.  George Halyak questioned the ordinance’s purpose and meaning.
Upon inquiry, City Clerk Carol Intlekofer re-read the entitlement of the ordinance and explained, if
the ordinance is approved, the amendment will affect employees 18 to 21 years of age when employed
only in a restaurant and full service restaurant environment, as defined by state statute, during the
course o f t heir e mployment d uties by a llowing t hem t o p rovide e mployment s ervices w ithin a
dispensing room area in addition to other designated dining areas outside of the dispensing room. Mr.
Halyak discussed the different types of employees that may be allowed within the dispensing room
and suggested modifying the ordinance to be more specific. Reporting for Public Services Committee,
Mr. Collins advised there w as no r ecommendation from th e Committee. Mr. Brown moved to
approve on third and final reading, seconded by Ms. Case.  Upon inquiry, Ms. Intlekofer reviewed
language currently contained in City Code Section 5.12.090 (i.e. sub-sections A. and B.), not just the
portions of sub-section B. involving the proposed amendment.  Extensive discussion followed and
included the following subjects: Underage drinking and workforce labor topics constituting 2 different
issues; l abor sh ortage a nd b usiness co ncerns; curr ent em ployee s ervices wi thin v s. o utside a
dispensing room; ordinance change not pertaining to those liquor licensee establishments whose
primary business purpose involves bars and/or package liquor sales and not the sale of food; proposed
amendment intended to apply to 18-21 year olds while performing employment services only, and
past city ordinances approved by the governing body regulating alcohol issues.  Mr. Collins moved
to amend Section 5.12.090, sub-section B. as  follows, seconded by Dr. Rinne:  “EXCEPT FOR
EMPLOYEES W HO, P URSUANT TO T HE P ERFORMANCE OF  T HEIR EMPL OYMENT
DUTIES, AND WHO ARE AT LEAST EIGHTEEN (18) YEARS OF AGE AND EMPLOYED BY
A LICENSEE IN A RESTAURANT AND FULL SERVICE RESTAURANT ENVIRONMENT,
AS DEFINED BY WYO. STAT. SECTION 12-1-101 (a)(xiv), Nno person under the legal drinking
age may enter or remain in a dispensing room where alcoholic liquors and/or malt beverages are sold
or dispensed.”  Motion t o a mend c arried. V oting “ yes” –  a ll members o f t he g overning b ody.
Discussion continued on employer supervision and responsibilities; police inspections; description of
a di spensing ro om; pas sing addi tional l aws t o h elp wi th en forcement o f  un derage dri nking;
information on  r ecommended a ge of  s ervers vs. minors i n p ossession ( unless i ncidental to
employment) contained in the “Best Practices” information previously submitted during discussion;
other Wyoming municipalities’ laws and State Sheriff’s and Chiefs of Police association’s position
on the issue; employee wages; industry and labor market conditions; amendment affecting employees
working as hosts, hostesses, servers and table busers, and youth responsibility.  Upon inquiry, Police
Capt. Jeff Schulz advised there have not been any serious law enforcement problems with alcohol
service in restaurant environments regarding service to minors.  Mr. Pierson moved to amend Section
5.12.090, sub-section B. to change the age from 18 to at least 19 years of age, seconded by Ms.
Broyles. It was advised raising the age to 19 would eliminate the majority of high school aged persons
from being able to serve alcohol or enter the dispensing room.  Upon inquiry on why the state’s legal
drinking age had been raised in the past from 19 to 21 years old, Captain Schulz clarified it was based
upon the State not losing highway funding.  Motion to amend failed.  Voting “yes” – Ms. Broyles,
Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, and Mayor Spiker.  Voting “no” – Mr. Brown, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr.
Laybourn, Mr. Segrave and Mr. Valdez.  Mr. Pierson moved to amend Section 5.12.090 to add a new
subsection C . t hat woul d re ad: “ ALL SER VERS UN DER THE A GE O F 21  M UST C EASE
SERVICE IN  TH E D ISPENSING AREA AFTER 9 :00 P.M .”, s econded by Ms. B royles. M r.
Hutchinson spoke in opposition to the 9:00 p.m. deadline and explained the restaurant he’s affiliated
with ( i.e. O live G arden) c loses a t 1 0:00 p .m. a nd th e e ffect th e a mendment w ould h ave on
management o f s taffing l evels an d cus tomer se rvice.  Upo n inquiry, Ca pt. Sch ulz pro vided
information on the City’s curfew hours for minors.  Motion to amend failed.  Voting “yes” – Mr.
Pierson and Mayor Spiker.  Voting “no” –  Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr.
Laybourn, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mr. Valdez.  Further discussion included workforce issues,
minimum wage and salary levels for wait staff, living wages within t he community,18 year o lds
serving in the military and being able to vote, exposure to alcohol and underage drinking concerns,
and deferring action on the ordinance to allow time for the report from the state to be completed to
provide po ssible guidance on t he issue.  Ms . Bro yles moved t o po stpone to Oct ober 27, 2008,
seconded by Mr. Valdez. Motion to postpone carried.  Voting “yes” – Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr.
Laybourn, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Valdez and Mayor Spiker.  Voting “no” –  Mr. Brown, Mr. Collins, Dr.
Rinne and Mr. Segrave.
Following a 10 minute recess, Mayor Spiker reconvened the meeting at 8:36 pm.
“AN ORDINANCE ANNEXING TO THE CITY OF CHEYENNE, WYOMING, PUBLIC
ROAD AND ALLEY RIGHT OF WAY SITUATED IN THE NW¼ OF SECTION 27, T.14N.,
R.66W. LARAMIE COUNTY, WYOMING (LOCATED NORTH OF PERSHING BOULEVARD,
SOUTH OF DELL RANGE BOULEVARD AND EAST OF GROVE DRIVE AND WEST OF
COLLEGE DRIVE).”  Mr. Collins moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.
Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.
“AN O RDINANCE A NNEXING TO  TH E C ITY O F C HEYENNE, W YOMING, A
PARCEL OF LAND DESCRIBED AS LOT 16, BLOCK 1, DOWNEY ADDITION, LARAMIE
COUNTY, WYOMING (AKA 3324 LAND COURT.”  Mr. Collins moved to approve on second
reading, seconded by Mr. Brown. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.
