Development Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the Church of St. Mary for the
cooperative construction of street improvements at the intersection of 22  Street and O’Neil Avenuend
in conjunction with the site development work at 2200 O’Neil Avenue  (2003-2006 1% Sales Tax).
Tony Lucero, qu estioned use of 1% Sales Tax funds for the project. Ken Lewis, City Engineer,
responded to the inquiry by reviewing 1% projects and providing information on maintenance work
required in the area due to the road’s high crown, which poses vehicular problems and which will
eventually require an overlay.  He indicated the agreement is fiscally cost efficient by partnering with
St. Mary’s to achieve the work the City needs to do during the time frame that St. Mary’s is installing
its required infrastructure in the street in conjunction with its new school.  Mr. Lucero questioned
whether lo wering t he c rown w ill d ivert w ater a nd a ffect flo oding c onditions w ith M r. L ewis
explaining that lowering the crown will assist with lessening water capacity in the gutters and will not
significantly alter the water flow around the school.  Randy Byers, architect for St. Mary’s School
project, provided further information on the street crown, which is currently a challenge to individuals
with disabilities, and stated the Church’s support of partnering with the City on the project.  George
Halyak expressed concerns with the proposed construction and discussed the following issues he felt
should be resolved in association with the project: Street drainage; increased traffic at the school’s
drop-off/pick-up area, traffic flow/volume generally and turning area; possible alley closure; whether
a bump-out design is needed, and the Church’s future school project would request vacation of 22nd
St. in the future.  Mr. Byers reviewed construction improvements proposed, including the bump-out
design (pedestrian safety), and stated access plans to and from the school have not changed, and the
alley will not be closed or impeded.  Mr. Segrave moved to approve in an amount not to exceed
$86,946.50, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Upon inquiry regarding whether a traffic flow study had been
conducted, Mr. Byers advised a traffic study had been completed and approved as part of the site plan
review process and provided further information on the street  improvements and reviewing agencies
providing c omments d uring t he site p lan review a s w ell a s o ther a gencies a nd businesses being
contacted during the project.  Upon inquiry, Capt. Jeff Schulz advised the police department did not
have any issues with the site plan. In response to inquiry  regarding use of 1% funds for the project,
Vicki Nemecek, Assistant Public Works Director, clarified the City’s funding for the project will be
from t he 1%  st reet r enovation l ine i tem an d wi ll n ot t ake f unding aw ay f rom o ther pr ojects.
Discussion followed on the opportunity to partner with St. Mary’s for reduced costs to the City, use
of funds from the 1% street renovation line item, repair of the street crown and effect of reducing
street water volume, street crowning conditions on other streets, concern with bump-outs, site plan
design for t he s chool, a nd p ortion of the project involving t he C ity’s financial investment a nd
maintenance.  M r. Lewis c larified a pproval o f t he site p lan is a n administrative a ction, a nd t he
drawing before City Council is part of the site plan.  Further discussion followed on the site plan in
conjunction with the roadway, and any future changes to the plans, including whether there will be
a street vacation request by the Church in the future. Mr. Byers advised he could not speak on behalf
of St. Mary’s concerning any future property acquisition and development plans, nor was it germane
to the agenda topic; stated the project will improve handicap and pedestrian access and reviewed the

Announcement was made that due to the Labor Day holiday on Monday, September 1, 2008,
the following meetings have been rescheduled for Tuesday, September 2, 2008: Finance Committee
at 11:00 a.m., Room 122; regular Vouchers meeting of the Governing Body at Noon, City Council
Chambers, and Public Services Committee at 12:15 p. m., Room 122, Municipal Building, 2101
O’Neil Ave., Cheyenne, WY.
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held September 8, 2008 at 6:00 p.m. in
City Council Chambers for a transfer of ownership for a retail liquor license application filed with the
City Clerk’s Office for ENI, Inc. d/b/a Eagle’s Nest, 1101 W. Lincolnway, Cheyenne, WY (License
currently held by Eagle’s Nest, Inc. d/b/a Eagle’s Nest, 1101 W. Lincolnway, Cheyenne, WY).
Announcement was made of the appointment of Nicole Lindner to the Mayor’s Council for
People with Disabilities, to be confirmed September 8, 2008.
OTHER CITY BUSINESS:
John Fafoutakis discussed vandalism that had occurred recently at Botanic Gardens, and
commended Police Officer John Gay for his efforts in educating youth of Internet dangers involving
predators.
Wyoming House Representative Mary Throne, District 11, which is part of Ward I and Ward
III, a dvised a  g roup o f interested r esidents has been w orking d iligently to save several historic
residential structures located near the historic Governors’ mansion and expressed concerns that plans
by the property owner t o remove the structures from the area will have irreparable harm on the
Governors’ mansion as an historic site.  She reviewed the recent denial of a City demolition permit
through the Historic Preservation Board’s process and subsequent appeal to the Building Code Board
of Appeals, which upheld the denial; stated the Governors’ mansion neighborhood is a specially
protected historic area and stated her concerns with issuance of a City moving permit to relocate a
structure and urged the governing body to “slow down” the process to allow time for the group to
come up with options or solutions.  Speaking in support of the City intervening in the moving process
were:  J an Nelson Schroll, who read a letter received from former U.S. Senator Alan Simpson,
requesting  properties in the area be saved to preserve the history of Cheyenne; Nancy Abraham, who
requested dedicated historic districts receive respect and urged the City Council to use its power to
stop the moving of structures to maintain the integrity of the neighborhood, and Mary Ann Taliaferro,
who reviewed the area’s history and prominent individuals that had resided in the homes.  Speakers
requested the governing body intervene in the pending moving of a building within the historic area
to provide time to research options or alternatives; further requested that the governing body revisit
its regulations concerning moving permits relative to historic districts, and also discussed the historic
Governors’ Mansion neighborhood relative to possible sale of property in the area to the hospital that
purportedly may utilize the land for a parking lot.  Comments followed on the intention of the City’s
ordinance designating the Governors’ Mansion as an historic area; property owners’ rights; potential
hospital involvement; significance of area; interpretation of City Code permit requirements, a nd
Mayor and City Council authority to halt moving of a structure following issuance of a moving permit
through the Building Department. Mayor Spiker provided information available on moving permit
application procedures and status of the application that had been filed.  He explained the process a
moving permit applicant has to follow and compliance areas that have to be met.  Discussion included
whether the Mayor or City has legal authority to stop or intervene, either directly or through order
to the Police Chief, the moving process; moving permit application reviews and approvals required;
seeking a written legal review to determine Mayoral and City Council authority and options; process
utilized to review and approve demolition permits for designated historic areas vs. moving permits;
protection of the historic Governors’ Mansion area, and demolishing buildings vs. moving buildings
and effect of each on the historic integrity of the district.  City Attorney Claudia Angelos, stated her
concerns with mayoral and governing body authority to act upon the issue, and commented on state
statute and City Code provisions, which she indicated does not allow for the Mayor to stop the
issuance o f t he m oving p ermit o nce a pplication r equirements ha ve been met a nd a pproved by
necessary departments and the permit is issued.  U pon inquiry on whether there is a time frame
involved in issuing of moving permits, Ken Lewis, City Engineer, advised he was not aware of any
for moving permits. Ms. Throne referenced a section of City Code Chapter 15.50, Historic Design
Guideline (specific to the Governors’ Mansion protective area), regarding relevancy of a certificate
of appropriateness requirement for the property owner.  In conjunction with a question posed on
whether the City could file an injunction (with the court), Ms. Angelos advised if discussion continued
into issues that may involve potential litigation then the governing body needs to move into executive
session.  Following brief comments, Mr. Pierson moved to meet in executive session to discuss a
matter of potential litigation, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members
of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Laybourn voting “no”.  Mayor Spiker announced
the motion carried and members would meet in executive session, not open to the public, in Council
Chambers following a 10 minute recess;  that there may or not be any action taken by the governing
body as a result of the executive session, therefore, the meeting would reconvene and be open to the
public following closure of the executive session. He requested the City Attorney, City Clerk,  City
Engineer and Deputy City Attorney be present at the executive session. (Clerk’s Note: Executive
session began at 12:45 a.m.) Following conclusion of the executive session, Mayor Spiker reconvened
the meeting, open to the public at 1:10 a.m.  Mayor Spiker advised no action would be taken by the
governing body as a res ult of the executive session, but a s pecial meeting of the governing body
would be scheduled for Wed., August 27, 2008 at 12:00 p.m. (Noon) in City Council Chambers to
further review the concerns raised regarding removal of homes in the Governor’s historic district.
The meeting was officially adjourned at 1:13 a.m.
 Submitted by,
 
 Carol A. Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.

discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests, in which event the item

LEASES/CONTRACTS/LEGAL:
Professional Services Contract between the City of Cheyenne, Office of Youth Alternatives,
and the State of Wyoming, Department of Family Services, for intensive support mentoring for youth
in the Municipal Court System.  M r. Segrave moved to approve ($63,000.00), seconded by Mr.
Brown.  Upon inquiry, Dick Berry, Youth Alternatives Director, provided information on use of the
funding, purpose of the program and services provided.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members
of the governing body.  (#5297)
Contract between the City of Cheyenne, Police Department, Victim Witness Program, and
the State of Wyoming, Division of Victim Services, for services to victims of crime.  Mr. Segrave
moved to approve in the amount of $69,129.00, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Upon inquiry, Lt. Monti
Allsop, Police Department, advised at the current time the program is adequately funded and includes
grant funds, and briefly explained program services.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of
the governing body.  (#5298)
Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, and Cheyenne Regional Medical
Center for the purpose of creating an Emergency Medical Service Delivery System Joint Powers
Board.  Mr. Segrave moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Upon inquiry, Chief Guy
Cameron, Cheyenne Fire and Rescue Dept., clarified approval of the agreement will create a joint
powers board (JPB) and advised the consultant cost relative to the review and evaluation of the
current delivery system was approximately $89,000.00.  Comments followed on a JPB vs. governing
body oversight of the agreement with the provider of emergency medical delivery system services;
transparency; number o f City J PBs an d o ther b oards, an d improvements t o s ystem s ervices as
recommended by the consultant, which included the formation of a JPB. Chief Cameron stated the
overall goal is to improve the system and meet community needs, and explained overlapping service
areas under the current delivery system structure, citing, as an example, utilization of three different
medical directors that could be consolidated into one director to provide more uniformity and less
duplication.  He indicated the investment in improving the system will help “pull areas together” to
achieve economies of scale, eliminate or reduce fragmentation of services, improve costs and correct
inefficiencies.  During discussion, Chief Cameron spoke further on the purpose and role of the JPB,
which will serve as the foundation for implementing service delivery improvements, and commented
on streamlining the administrative process by having the service provider answer to only “one body”,
JPB’s responsibility to evaluate and select the emergency medical service provider, and positive
partnering of the agencies involved.  He noted that Laramie County Commissioners and  Cheyenne
Regional Medical Center have approved the proposed agreement to create the JPB and discussed the
board’s d uties a nd a ccountability; s tate l aw p rovisions c oncerning J PBs; s cenario o f B oard
dissolution, if it is determined to do so in the future; agreement section addressing whether a party
to the agreement wishes to withdraw from the JPB in the future, and advised an RFP (request for
proposals) f or e mergency m edical d elivery s ervices has been i ssued.  D iscussion i ncluded t he
following topics with additional information provided by Chief Cameron: Meetings held with the
consultant and consultant’s knowledge of delivery service issues; professionalizing emergency medical
system delivery services; improving e mergency medical pre-hospital services t o t he c ommunity;
medical di rector ro le; opt-out c lause i n t he a greement; de signation i n t he a greement o f J PB
membership positions, and specific identification of members and their qualifications; opportunity to
work together with the county to provide quality services to the community; utilization of public
funds and diffusion o f e lected o fficials’ respo nsibility, and JPB accountability.  M otion carried.
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Ms. Case and Mr. Laybourn
voting “no”.  (#5299)
[CA] Agreement between Laramie County School District No. 1 and the City of Cheyenne, Office
of Youth Alternatives, for counseling services to elementary and secondary age children who are
attending the PEP/TRC Center -- referred to Finance Committee. 
[CA] Agreement between Laramie County School District No. 1 and the City of Cheyenne, Office

[CA] Agreement between Laramie County School District No. 1 and the City of Cheyenne, Office

CHANGE ORDERS/CONTRACT MODIFICATIONS:
Following a five minute recess, Mayor Spiker reconvened the meeting at 8:20 p.m.
Contract Modification No. 1 to Contract No. 5280 (Norris Viaduct) to include bid alternates
#1, 2, 3, and 5.  Speaking in favor of financial investment through contract modification to provide
aesthetic improvements were:  Frank Cole, Cole Shopping Center; Sara Burlingame; Carol Matteson
Pascal; Doran Lummis; Jason Thomas, President, Historic South Side Improvement Association
(HSSIA); Mary Ramirez; Manuel Gallegos and Armand Gallegos.  Topics presented and discussed
included:  G reenway a ccess a nd a rea/community c onnectivity; p roject s upport g enerally;
beautification efforts; community involvement through public input at Norris viaduct project planning
meetings; green areas and amenities; maintaining voters’ trust; creating safe neighborhoods; residents
who have been displaced due to the project; elements of the HSSIA’s neighborhood revitalization
plan (pamphlet submitted and on file with office of City Clerk), and the project’s importance on the
neighborhood.  Mr. Segrave moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Comment followed in
support of the Norris bridge realignment project.  Ms. Broyles moved to amend by striking alternates
#1, 2, 3 and 5 and approving contract modification #1 from Reiman Corp. to include revised bid
alternate #1, aesthetic lighting, in the amount of $329,300.00 and alternate #5[b], color staining of
MSE walls and viaduct, in the amount of $84,219.40 for a total modification amount of $413,519.40;
project to be included in the City’s application to the State Loan and Investment Board (SLIB) in the
next funding cycle, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Upon inquiry by Mr. Thomas and Ms. Pascal, it was
clarified that alternates #2, aesthetic railing on viaduct approaches, and #3, additional landscaping,
were not included in the motion to amend, but as it is a two year project additional landscaping may
be p roposed t oward t he e nd of the project. I t w as a lso no ted t hat t he p roposed a mendment
incorporates value engineering savings that has resulted due to discussions with the contractor.  Upon
request Jeff Fanning, Engineering Services Director, reviewed drawings o f the proposed railing
included in the base bid vs. a depiction of aesthetic railings, and drawings showing the lighting that
will be provided through the base bid vs. proposed aesthetic lighting.  Ms. Pascal commented on
safety concerns for pedestrians relative to lighting.  Mr. Fanning advised the same lighting effect will
be achieved through the value engineering proposal; described decorative items (i.e. railing a nd
concrete, with stamped pattern, design) already included in the base bid, and advised the base bid
provides f or s ome l andscaping.  D iscussion i ncluded: B asic b id i tems a lready i ncluding m ore
attractive design elements than other projects; stone pilasters being included in the decorative lighting;
concrete staining and stamped pattern; unavailability of decorative railing; estimated project cost
when voters approved t he project vs. t oday’s construction and supply costs; SLIB funding and
correlation to upcoming Council work session to discuss potential SLIB funding requests for various
City pro jects; f iscal res ponsibility; i rrigation i nfrastructure t o s upport an y f uture addi tional
landscaping; o ther p otential f unding m echanisms, i ncluding i nvestment o f p roject f unds, a nd
suggestion that a budget analysis for the entire project be prepared.  Mr. Collins raised a point of
order to clarify discussion earlier in the day at an Investment Committee meeting involved a monetary
estimate as an example of investment funds, not an actual dollar amount.  Comments continued on
bid alternates as initially listed on the agenda; site plan issues; neighborhood meeting t o review
alternates proposed in the motion to amend; support for alternates proposed with the initial approval
of the construction contract, and project management.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Fanning further reviewed
lighting differences in the base bid vs. aesthetic lighting.  Mr. Segrave moved to call for the question
to limit debate, seconded by Mr. Collins.  M otion failed (due to a tie vote).  V oting “yes” – Mr.
Brown, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Segrave and Mayor Spiker. Voting “no” – Ms. Broyles, Ms.
Case, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Valdez.  Following further comment on quality project
components, motion to amend failed (due to a tie vote).  Voting “yes” – Ms. Broyles, Mr. Brown,
Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson and Mayor Spiker.  Voting “no” – Ms. Case, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne, Mr.
Segrave and Mr. Valdez.  Mr. Laybourn moved to postpone for two weeks (to Sept. 22 ), secondednd
by M r. V aldez.  M r. T homas, M s. P ascal a nd M r. Manuel G allegos s poke i n f avor o f t he
postponement to allow for public involvement, clarification of proposed alternates, and budgetary and
maintenance issues.  Discussion followed on the purpose of postponement and what would transpire
during the postponement time frame.  Mr. Laybourn raised a point of order that comments being
made were not relevant to the motion on the floor.  Comments continued on postponement.  Mr.
Laybourn moved to call the question to limit debate, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Mo tion failed.
Voting “yes” – Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mayor Spiker.  Voting “no” – Mr. Brown,
Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson and Mr. Valdez.  During further discussion on the
motion to p ostpone, a point of information was raised for clarification of procedures relating to
potential amendments to the main motion.  John Fafoutakis commented on the length of discussion
time on the item, and Ms. Pascal and Mr. Manuel Gallegos made statements relative to the motion
to postpone. Comments were made on postponing the item relative to the Council’s work session
scheduled later in the week to r eview proposed projects to s ubmit for SLIB funding.  M otion to
postpone failed.  Voting “yes” – Ms. Case, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Valdez.  Voting “no”
– Mr. Collins, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Brown, Mr. Segrave and Mayor Spiker.  Mr. Collins
moved t o amend by deleting alternates #1, 2, 3 an d 5 an d substituting alternate #5b, as revised
through value engineering, to add stained concrete in the amount of $84,219.40, seconded by Mr.
Pierson.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Fanning confirmed that under the value engineering proposal for alternate
#5, the concrete staining w ould be  t he s ame q uality a nd c ontent a s t he bi d, j ust a  d ifferent
manufacturer a s t he p rovider.  Ke n Lewis, C ity E ngineer, r equested if t he a mendment, o r a ny
additional a mendments, a re a pproved a s bid a lternates t hat t he M ayor be  d irected t o s ign t he
appropriate contract change order pursuant to any amendment(s). Mr. Collins, with concurrence by
Mr. Pierson as second to the motion, agreed to include Mr. Lewis’ request in the motion to amend.
Brief discussion followed on the procedural process involving the original main motion v s. t he
proposed amendment(s).  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms.
Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Valdez and Mayor Spiker.  Voting “no” – Mr. Laybourn, Dr.
Rinne and Mr. Segrave.  Mr. Collins moved to amend to include bid alternate #1, revised through
value engineering, in the amount of $329,300.00 for aesthetic lighting, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  It
was noted the alternate includes the pedestrian lighting feature.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – Mr.
Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Valdez and Mayor Spiker.
Voting “no” – Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Segrave voting “no”.  Main motion as twice amended carried.
Voting “yes” – Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Valdez and Mayor
Spiker.  Voting “no” – Mr.  Laybourn, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Segrave.
CONSIDERATION OF BIDS:

Restaurant liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Primos Cheyenne

Request to extend the time period for one additional year in which retail liquor licensee HEJE,
Inc., d/b/a Outlaw Saloon, 3839 East Lincolnway, Cheyenne, WY, is required to become operational
or open for business pursuant to Wyo. Stat. §12-4-103(a)(iv).  Mayor Spiker advised the item was
being wi thdrawn f rom t he age nda an d reques ted C ity Cl erk Caro l In tlekofer provide f urther
explanation.  Ms. Intlekofer advised that, subsequent to Finance Committee meeting discussion, the
Wyoming Liquor Division was contacted regarding when the initial 2 year time frame for “parking”
the license would expire and it was agreed the initial time frame should not expire until March 31,
2009, therefore, the agenda item (requesting one additional year) at this time is a moot point.  She
advised when the licensee’s application comes before the governing body for the next renewal period,
the licensee will need to show good cause for extending the “parked” time period for the license for
one additional year if they are not operational by then.  She clarified the City Attorney and herself had
contacted the attorney representing HEJE, Inc. to advise the initial two year “parked” expiration date
would not be until March 31, 2009, and it was agreed the licensee’s attorney, City Attorney and City
Clerk would request the item be withdrawn from the agenda.

OTHER CITY BUSINESS:
John Fafoutakis made statements on the following topics: Timing of a traffic light at 9  St.th
and Hwy 85; private attorney firm expenses for a legal opinion involving moving of buildings within
the historic Governors’ Mansion area, and the City Council’s civility ordinance and comments made
when items are removed from the Consent Agenda.  City Engineer Ken Lewis advised the traffic light
referenced by Mr. Fafoutakis was controlled by the State, but he would ask the traffic engineer to
review the matter with WYDOT to ensure the signal was functioning properly.
Jan Nelson Schroll commented on a private attorney firm’s research on case law involving
moving permits issued for buildings within the historic Governors’ Mansion area and submitted a
copy o f City Co de C hapter 2. 64 pert aining t o t he Historic Prese rvation Bo ard.  Sh e rev iewed

Responding t o statements p reviously made u nder o ther City business by Mr. Fafoutakis
concerning removal of consent agenda items, Mr. Segrave commented on his advocacy for efficient
government and his support for a Consent Agenda format; and that he will exercise his rights to
promote efficient government and use of the public’s time.
Mr. Segrave moved to adjourn, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” –
all members of the governing body with the exception of Ms. Case and Mr. Laybourn voting “no”.
The meeting was officially adjourned at 10:30 p.m.

 RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
September 22, 2008
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date at 6:00 p.m.
in Council Chambers.  Present were: MAYOR-Jack R. Spiker; COUNCIL MEMBERS-Mr. Brown,
Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne (arriving at 6:25 p.m.), Mr. Segrave
and Mr. Valdez.  Absent: Mr. Pierson.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.
 
Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Barb Dorr, City Treasurer, and Erik Rasmussen,
Deputy City Attorney.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA]  are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests, in which event the
item will be removed f rom the Consent Agenda and considered in its normal sequence  on the
agenda.)  Upon request by Mr. Collins and Mr. Laybourn, Mayor Spiker announced agenda items
#6, 7, 25(a)(b)(c)(d), 27(b) and 29(a) and (b) would be removed from the Consent Ag enda.  Mr.
Collins moved t o approve remaining Consent Ag enda items, sec onded by Mr. B rown.  Motion
carried.  Voting  “yes” – a ll members of the g overning body present with the exception of Mr.
Laybourn voting “no”.
Mayor Spiker recognized the Chey enne Board of Public Utili ties, and spec ifically Clint
Bassett, BOPU Water Conservation Specialist, for receiving the national WateReuse Association
2008 Public Education Program of the year award for the Cheyenne Water Reuse Program.  Mayor
Spiker presented Mr. Bassett with the award plaque, and noted plaque wording indicating BOPU’s
dedication to the water r euse c ommunity throug h educa tion programs that enhanc e better
appreciation of water resources, management and conservation.
 MINUTES FROM REGUL AR MEETI NG OF  THE GOV ERNING B ODY ON
SEPTEMBER 8, 2008.  Mr. Collins moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Motion  carried.
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.
 MINUTES FROM VOUCHERS MEETI NG OF  THE GOV ERNING B ODY ON
SEPTEMBER 15, 2008.  Mr. Brown moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion carried.
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.
Mr. Segrave moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Valdez.
Upon inquiry, City Treasurer Barb Dorr provided information available on the following vouchers
payable to: Chamber of Commerce ($4,617.00), annual City membership dues renewal; Habitat for
Humanity ($60,899.78), reimbursements for Messenger Court infrastructure project ($51,732.64)
and Katrina project ($9,167.14); JM Rodent Control ($3,149.30), rodent control by Weed & Pest at
several facilities and grounds, and Douglas Selby ($6,832.57), concept design for Cheyenne Depot
Plaza (building) project (current fiscal year budget and proposed State Loan and Investment Board
consensus grant funds).  During inquiry, Mayor Spiker provided additional information on Chamber
of Commerce membership benefits, and professional preliminary design services for the Depot Plaza
building.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.
Mayor Spiker opened a public meeting for the purpose of receiving comments and input to
discuss the use of 2003-2006 1% Optional Sales Tax Overage Funds in the amount of $147,280.00
for the pur pose of r eimbursing approved expenditures from the 2007-2010 Par ks & Rec reation
Department’s 1% Optional Sales Tax All ocation.  Todd F eezer, Parks and Rec reation Dept.,
provided information on the purpose of re-allocating the funds due to expenditures affiliated with
the new Parks Shop property recently purchased by the City.  There being no further comments or
input and purpose of the public meeting having been met, Mayor Spiker closed the public meeting.
“AN ORDINANCE VACATING MCCOMB AVENUE BETWEEN W. LINCOLNWAY
AND W. 17  STREET AND THE 16-FOOT ALLEY WITHIN BLOCK 401, ORIGINAL CITY,TH
CHEYENNE, WYOMING (LOCATED BETWEEN MISSILE DRIVE AND MCCOMB AVENUE
AND BETWEEN W. LINCOLNWAY AND W. 17  STREET).”  Hu Wang, property owner in theTH
near vicinity, spoke in opposition to the vacation; questioned  the vacation process, and expressed
concerns with not rec eiving notice of the proposed action and va cation procedures. He provided
information on the number of tenants who rent property from him in the area and commented that
closing the street would affect the tenants, citing access and safety concerns, particularly during
inclement we ather.  (Clerk’s note :  Dr. Rinne joined the mee ting dur ing comments.) Fur ther
comments from Mr. Wang included the topics of traffic and traffic routes, graffiti and garbage-type
waste disposal in the area, and property values (information and photos distributed and referenced
by Mr. Wang on file with office of City Clerk).  John Rogers, attorney representing applicants
requesting vacation (Robert Smith and Jim Hancock with Wyoming Grand, LLC (involved in the
Microtel hotel project)), addressed notification procedures to adjacent property owners as required
in the vacation application instructions, and stated Mr. Wang  did not receive the mailed wr itten
notification as the Laramie County Assessor’s office inadvertently had an inappropriate address,
utilized by  the ag ent issuing notifica tion notices, on file for Mr . Wang.  H e cla rified notice
concerning the proposed va cation wa s posted on the property  and wa s also adver tised in the
newspaper, and noted Mr. Wang’s presence and participation involving the proposed vacation action
at recent City Council and committee mee tings.  He  spok e in favor of the va cation; reviewed
beneficial aspects surrounding the street vacation; provided a diagram (on file with office of City
Clerk) of the property reflecting the area and access points; discussed street and internal property
lighting, and responded to concerns raised by Mr. Wang involving street lighting, drainage, and
neighboring property values due to the hotel project. Robert Smith, co-owner, Microtel hotel project,
reviewed a brief history of the site involving the  former Frontier Motel and spoke in favor of the
vacation, stating it will help with traffic control in the area and allow for better, safer access to the
property.  Larry Perry, Terrestrial Surveying and Mapping, spoke regarding Mr. Wang’s notification
concern, a dvising L aramie Cou nty’s GI S system us ed f or loc ating p roperty inf ormation h as a
disclaimer on its websit e that it is not liable for the a ccuracy and complete ness of system data.
Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Collins advised there was no recommendation on the
item. Mr. Br own moved to appr ove on third and f inal reading, seconded by Mr. Collins. Upon
inquiry regarding the storm sewer system, City Engineer Ken Lewis provided information generally
on the Public Works Dept. ma intenance prog ram, a nd Mr. Rog ers state d the storm sewe r
infrastructure ha d r ecently be en in spected b y the  City and is o n th e sc hedule fo r p eriodic
maintenance and commented that the existing inlets may be replaced during the hotel construction
project.  Discussion included the following topics: Drainage; storm sewer maintenance schedule;
location of paving of Taco John’s Ice and Events Center parking lot and curb tie-ins (information
provided by Todd Feezer, Parks a nd Recre ation Dept.); a rea development improve ments and
maintenance re sponsibilities; raising  of stree t “cr own” on W. 17  St.; s afety; proposed re -th
development of the area (i.e. new hotel project); access and ligh ting issues; street encroachment
involving Mr. Smith’s residence, and snow plowing of streets during winter months to maintain
accessibility. During discussion and upon inquiry, Larry Gallagher, Summit Engineering, reviewed
drainage development plans for the Microtel property; Mr. Lewis provided information concerning
the stree t encr oachment, and Martin Matsen, D evelopment Di rector, revie wed c urrent zoni ng
designation (CB) a nd allowable use s for prope rty located nor th of the Microte l hotel site.  J ohn

changes within the City that have not been approved.  John Fafoutakis requested that certain types
of businesses be prevented from operating in the area with Mayor Spiker clarifying that regulations

moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Discussion included the following
topics: Spot z oning; de finition of neig hborhood; neig hborhood businesses; propose d future
development ( townhomes) north of t he ar ea; pr otecting exis ting ne ighborhoods; future a rea
development t hat ma y inc lude re sidential a nd c ommercial us es, a nd Pla nCheyenne g uidelines.
Motion failed (due to a tie vote).  Voting “yes” – Mr. Brown, Mr. Segrave, Mr. Valdez and Mayor

of Youth Alternatives, for family counseling for school referred students who are in I.E.P.s.  Mr.
Segrave moved to approve in an amount not to exceed $8,740.00, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Motion
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.  (#5303)

of Youth Alternatives, f or family counseling for sc hool referred students/families.  Mr. Seg rave
moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the

Clune Design for the “Cheyenne Wayfinding Plan Phase II”.  Mr. Segrave moved to approve in an

see if any comments had been receive d pertaining to product concerns.  Motion carr ied.  Voting
“yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of Ms. Case and Mr. Laybourn

Eagle’s Nest, Inc. d/b/a Eagle’s Nest, 1101 W. Lincolnway, Cheyenne, WY). Motion (per consent

APPOINTMENTS:
Reappointment of Paul Frauendienst to the Building Code Board of Appeals and Elizabeth
Davis to the Greater Cheyenne Arts Advisory Council.  Mr. Collins moved to approve, seconded by
Mr. Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.
Appointment of Richard Shanor to the Community Action of Laramie County Board, Robert
Kanard to the Greenway Advisory Committee, Carrisa Pollard to the Planning Commission, Nicole
Novotny to t he Board of Adjustments, Jackie Smith to the Personnel Commission, and Phyllis
Sherard to t he Housing and Community Development Advisory Board.  M r. Collins moved to
approve, seconded by Mr. Brown.  April Brimmer Kunz commented on the appointment of Mr.
Shanor.  Concern was expressed with approving all of the propose d appointees en masse as one
agenda item with Mayor Spiker advising a motion to divide the question could be offered.  Motion
carried.  Voting  “yes” – a ll members of the g overning body present with the exception of Mr.
Laybourn voting “no”.
Following inquiry, no other City business was presented by the public.  Mr. Brown moved
to adjourn, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing
body present with the exception of Ms. Broy les, Ms. Case and Mr . Laybourn voting “no”.  T he
meeting was officially adjourned at 9:34 p.m.
 Submitted by,
 
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk

Ms. B royles indicated she had voted on the prevailing side on an ordinance acted u pon

“no”.  Following announcement of the vote, Dr. Rinne returned to Council Chambers.
Mr. V aldez, indicating he had voted on  th e p revailing side on  a n or dinance a cted u pon
(approved o n 3  reading) at t he September 22, 2008 meeting concerning vacation of McCombrd

Carol Intlekofer read the following agenda t itle o f t he o rdinance pro posed t o be reco nsidered:
“AN ORDINANCE ON THIRD READING VACATING MCCOMB AVENUE BETWEEN W.

ORIGINAL CITY, CHEYENNE, WYOMING (LOCATED BETWEEN MISSILE DRIVE AND
MCCOMB AVENUE A ND BETWEEN W. L INCOLNWAY A ND W. 17  ST REET).”  HuTH

questioned the vacation process and procedures, and extensively discussed various concerns he

Mayor Spiker o pened a pub lic hearing for t he purpo se o f receiving co mments and input

previous us es o f 5  penny 1% sales t ax m onies, M r. Segrav e rai sed a po int o f o rder t hatth
comments were n ot germane t o t he purpo se o f t he hearing with Mayor S piker co ncurring t hat
discussion should remain on-topic.  There being no further comments or input and purpose of the
public meeting having been met, Mayor Spiker closed the public meeting.
“AN ORDINANCE A MENDING SEC TION 2 .64.090, D EMOLITION PER MIT
REVIEW, OF  CH APTER 2.64,  HIS TORIC PRES ERVATION BOA RD, OF  TITLE 2,
ADMINISTRATION AND PERSONNEL, OF THE CHEYENNE CITY CODE, PERTAINING

CERTAIN BUILDINGS AND STRUCTURES.”  Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr.

the extensive time frame involved to acquire permit approval, indicating a reasonable time frame

expressed her belief that the Historic Preservation board should not control a personal p roperty
owner’s r ights, but should assist and g uide what can be do ne with an historic pr operty. Ho use
District 11 Representative Mary Throne spoke in favor of the ordinance and expressed the intent

allowing historical structures to be moved o ut o f a d istrict d efeats t he p urpose o f the H istoric
Preservation b oard a nd d esignation of a  s pecially p rotected d istrict.  M r. C ollins m oved to

“AN O RDINANCE D ELETING A ND R ECREATING S ECTION 2 .04.142 ( C),

Following a 10 minute recess to enable copies of the proposed substitute be provided to

substitute carried.  Vo ting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Ms.

“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 6.12.020, RABIES TAGS, OF CH APTER

Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Valdez and Mayor Spiker.  Voting “no”

“AN ORDINANCE A MENDING TI TLE 5,  BU SINESS LICENSE S A ND

MINORS-DISPENSING ROOM  REST RICTIONS, OF  T HE CODE OF  T HE CIT Y OF

“AN OR DINANCE A MENDING TI TLE 17,  Z ONING, CH APTER 17.08,  Z ONING

2, S KYLINE T RACTS, C HEYENNE, W YOMING ( LOCATED A T T HE N ORTHEAST

Announcement was made o f t he re-appo intment o f Mal Burnside, Al Cassidy, and Dan
Edeen to the Contractor Licensing Board, to be confirmed December 8, 2008.

John Fafoutakis expressed his concerns with the signal t iming rotation for a t raffic light
located at Forest D r. and Pershing; current a nd future tra ffic volume at Walterscheid and West
Allison Road; loud music from vehicle sound systems, and irresponsible pet ow ners who do not
spay and neuter pets.
Ms. Case referenced a letter Mayor Spiker recently sent t o Go vernor Dave Freudenthal
requesting co nsideration o f addi tional f unding f or m unicipalities duri ng t he s tate’s b udget
process to assist with ongoing expenses and revenue shortfalls, and questioned the state’s fiscal
responsibilities t o he lp f und c ities a nd towns.  M ayor S piker p rovided i nformation o n t he
purpose of the letter, noted the effect of reduced m onies to municipalities due t o the food sales
tax exemption, and advised the Wyoming Association of Municipalities had adopted resolutions
at i ts s tate convention i n s upport o f pursui ng addi tional s tate f unding t o m ake m unicipalities
“whole” with regard to food sales tax backfill.
There b eing n o f urther b usiness t o co me b efore the go verning b ody, t he m eeting was
officially adjourned at 9:12 p.m.

“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 6.12.020, RAB IES TAGS, OF CHAPTER

REQUIRED, OF CHA PTER 6.16, RABI ES CONTROL , OF T ITLE 6, ANIMALS, OF THE
CODE OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE, WYOMING.”  John Fafoutakis spoke in support of the
ordinance.  Reporting  for Public Service s Committee, Mr. Seg rave moved to approve  on third
and fina l rea ding, se conded by Mr. Pierson.  Mr. Seg rave moved to amend by  substitut e,
seconded by Mr. Pierson.  I t was advised the  substitu te addresses r egistration concerns. Karon
Volk spoke in favor of the substitute.  Upon inquiry , Bob Ma son, City Staff Attorne y, clarified
that lang uage conta ined in Section 6.12.020(A), r eferring to animal  registration for
Cheyenne/Laramie County, meant that registration acquired through local veterinary offices will
pertain to both city  and county residents.  Discussion topics included: County  Board of Health’s
approval of t he ra bies vac cination being  administered e very 3 y ears as an option; curr ent
ordinance history; input on proposed ordinanc e changes from local veterinarians, dog breeders
and the Dir ector of the Chey enne A nimal Control/S helter; ra bies vac cination, registration and
regulation; due diligence efforts to provide notification of proposed changes to the community;
concern with potential rabie s outbreak in the c ommunity, and purpose  of the ordina nce.  John
Rogers expressed support for  the ordinanc e change, and indica ted his belief that, due to local
media cove rage, ade quate publicity  on the proposed or dinance had bee n provided. Mr.
Fafoutakis commented in support of the proposed substitute, and Ms. Volk advised the proposed
ordinance doesn’ t chang e re porting or animal re gistration require ments.  Further discussion
continued o n pet owners’ r equirement t o u pdate inf ormation f or yearly re gistration w ith the ir
veterinarian’s office, and language pertaining to Section 6.12.020(A) previously referenced, with

the inclusion of L aramie Count y was more  for infor mational purposes, not a ma ndatory
requirement, and, during discussion, Attorney Mason provided further information relative to the
reference to Laramie County.  Discussion followed on the pr oposed amendment.  It was advised
that currently the County provides pet owners the option  of three year vs. annual vaccinations.
Motion to amend failed (due to a tie vote).  Voting “yes” – Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins,
Dr. Rinne and Mr . Segrave.  Voting “ no” – Ms. Case, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Pierson, Mr. V aldez
and Mayor Spiker. Discussion continued on the proposed substitute and included: Purpose of the
ordinance; review committee composition and involvement during ordinance compilation; public
representation; involvement by local veterinarians, and content areas of the ordinance applicable
to vaccinations, reporting and registration.  Upon inquiry,  Mr. Mason prov ided vaccination and
registration information.  Motion to amend by  substitute carried.  Voting “ yes” - all members of
the governing body with the exception of Ms. Case voting “no”.  Discussion continued on the
main motion as amended a nd included: Vaccination certification time frames; yearly registration
requirement an d any  aff iliated fee s that may  be asse ssed by  veter inarians; Animal Shelter’ s
involvement with registration, and concerns with wild animals within the City that may be rabies
carriers.  Mr. Mason explained information contained on rabies/registration animal tags as issued
by loc al ve terinarians.  M ain m otion a s a mended b y su bstitute c arried. Vo ting “ yes” – a ll
members of the governing body with the exception of Ms. Cas e and Mr. Laybourn voting “no”.

Chambers.

discuss the sale of the City-owned real property located at 700 West Fox  Farm Road, Cheyenne,

Announcement was made of a public hearing to be held December 22, 2008 at 3:00 p.m.
in City Council Chambers fo r a restaurant liquor lice nse application filed with the City  Clerk’s
Office for Yu Zheng d/b/a Golden House Restaurant, 1651 Carey Ave., Ste. 8, Cheyenne, WY.
Announcement was made of the a ppointment of Tony  Adams to the Personne l
Commission, Mark Har dee to the F ire Civil Service Commissi on, Michael L emke to the
Housing and Community Development Advisory Council and Jody Malm and B everly Bowman
to the Board of Adjustment, to be confirmed December 22, 2008.
OTHER CITY BUSINESS:
John Fa foutakis expressed his conc erns with the volume of  state-wide  alcohol re lated
offenses and affiliated law enforcement time and expense.
City Councilwoman-elect Amber Ash commented on inaudible portions of City Council
meeting streaming video a rchives, due to persons not spea king directly into microphones, and
suggested a reminder be made at meetings to assist in improving the sound quality.
There b eing no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was
officially adjourned at 7:51 p.m.

 Carol Intlekofer, MMC

   RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
 
Office of City Clerk
 
January 5, 2009
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne assembled for its first regular 2009 meeting on
this date at 6:30 p.m. in the Cheyenne Civic Center.  Purpose of the first regular meeting was to
recognize and administer oaths of office to those individuals who were elected, or re-elected, at the
most r ecent g eneral e lection t o s erve a s mu nicipal o fficials, a s w ell a s p rovide f or c ertain
administrative functions.  Ms. Mona Pearl served as mistress of ceremonies prior to the meeting being
officially convened.
Posting of Colors was provided by members of the Wyoming National Guard Joint Color
Guard, and a musical selection was performed by Ms. Patrice Pilivant with assistance by members of
Hands in Harmony.  Father Gary Ruzicka, St. Mary’s Cathedral, delivered the invocation.
The Honorable William U. Hill, Justice of the Wyoming Supreme Court, administered the oath
of elected office to Mayor-elect Richard L. Kaysen,  followed by administration of oaths of elected
office for the following newly elected and re-elected City Council members:  Amber Ash and Jimmy
Valdez, Ward I; Patrick Collins and Jack Spiker, Ward II, and Jim Brown and Don Pierson, Ward
III.
Mayor Kaysen officially called the first regular meeting to order at 6:50 p.m.  Those present
were: MAYOR - Richard L. Kaysen; COUNCIL MEMBERS - Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles,
Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Spiker and Mr. Valdez.  Also present were Carol
Intlekofer, City Clerk, and Bob Nicholas, Acting City Attorney.  Following the pledge of allegiance,
Mayor Kaysen welcomed those present and provided comments on the community’s progress and
his vision for the City’s future.
ELECTION OF  CO UNCIL PRESI DENT F OR 2009.   M ayor Kaysen an nounced t hat
pursuant to City code, he would not be participating in voting for the election of Council President
and Vice President officers.  Mr. Brown moved to nominate and elect Mr. Collins as City Council
President for 2009, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Dr. Rinne moved that nominations cease, seconded
by Mr. Valdez.  Motion to cease nominations carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing
body with the exception of Ms. Case voting “no” and Mayor Kaysen who did not vote.  Motion to
nominate and elect Mr. Collins carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the
exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not vote.
ELECTION OF COUNCIL VICE PRESIDENT FOR 2009.  Mr. Pierson moved to nominate
and elect Ms. Broyles, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Dr. Rinne moved that nominations cease, seconded
by Mr. Pierson.  Motion to cease nominations carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing
body with the exception of Ms. Case voting “no” and Mayor Kaysen who did not vote.  Motion to
nominate and elect Ms. Broyles carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the
exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not vote.
APPROVAL OF APPOINTMENT OF CITY OFFICIALS (pursuant to Title 2 of the Code
of the City of Cheyenne) as follows: Guy E. Cameron, Chief of Fire and Rescue Department; Barbara
E. Dorr,  City Treasurer; Robert D. Fecht, Chief of Police Department; Paul S. Galeotos, Municipal
Court Judge; Randy K. Hays, Assistant City Treasurer; Carol A. Intlekofer, City Clerk/Assistant City
Treasurer; Ronnald J. Jeffrey, Juvenile Court Judge; Mark T. Moran, Municipal Court Judge; Rick
L. Parish, Parks and Recreation Director, and Daniel E. White, City Attorney.  Mr. Collins moved
to approve the appointments “en masse”, seconded by Mr. Spiker.  Motion  carried.  Voting “yes”
– all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not vote (mayoral
appointments).  Justice Hill administered oaths of appointment to the above listed city officials.
Following a musical selection performed by Dr. Joe Harrell, with assistance by members of
Hands in Harmony, City Clerk Intlekofer announced that refreshments would be served in the Civic
Center lobby immediately following the meeting.
There being no further business for t he first r egular meeting, t he meeting w as o fficially
adjourned at 7:15 p.m.
 Submitted by,
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY

January 5, 2009
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in “Sine Die” session at 6:00 p.m. in the

Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mr. Valdez.

Attorney. 
Following the pledge of allegiance, Mayor Spiker welcomed those in attendance and stated the
purpose of the session was to c eremonially recognize outgoing Council members for their years of
service on City Council.  He commented generally on governing body and staff achievements a nd
community leadership, and expressed appreciation to outgoing Council members for their time, effort
and dedication to the community, and recognized the support role of families, friends and co-workers.

honoring o utgoing Co uncil m ember Mr.  Segrav e en titled as  f ollows:  “ A CEREMON IAL

DEDICATION AND OUTSTANDING CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE CITY OF CHEYENNE AND
ITS CITIZENS.”  Mayor Spiker presented a framed copy of the resolution to Mr. Segrave and an item
of appreciation on behalf of City Council.  (#5093)
Mayor Spiker expressed appreciation on behalf of the governing body to Mr. Pierson, immediate
past president of City Council, and presented Mr. Pierson with a gavel plaque of appreciation.
Mayor Spiker relinquished duties of the chair to Council President Pierson.  At Council President
Pierson’s request, City Clerk Intlekofer read a ceremonial resolution in its entirety honoring Mayor

provided resulting in a $5,000 incr ease (from $16,574.00 to $21,574.00) to the City ’s contribution
toward the project.  Doug  Vetter, City Engineer, concurred the cost to the city  will be $21,574.00
pursuant to lim ited federal ARRA funding a llowed, and state d a minor cha nge to rig ht-of-way
wording within the ag reement is also included in the cor rection.  Moti on to rec onsider ca rried.

order on whether  a past ordina nce be fore the g overning body  which  pertained to rec onsideration
procedures ha d been a pproved.  U pon reque st, Ci ty Clerk Carol I ntlekofer advised the pr evious
ordinance, wh ich would have c hanged City Code reg arding the re consideration process to provide
that items brought up and appr oved for reconsideration at the next reg ular meeting of the governing
body would be postponed with the item re ferred back to a Council standing committee for r eview
prior to a ction, had failed.  She  stated although the ordinance received an affirmative majority vote
of those pre sent, it failed as the r equired six votes to approve  an ordina nce on 3  and fina l readingrd
was not attaine d.  Upon inqu iry, Mr. Vetter  provided infor mation contained within the Coopera tive
Agreement involving the City’s maintenance responsibilities.  Com ment was made in opposition to
the process being followed to reconsider and amend previously approved agenda items without prior
notification to th e public.  Motion to amend ca rried.  V oting “yes” – a ll members of the g overning
body present with the exception of Ms. C ase voting “no”.  Ma in motion as amended by  substitute,
including a substitute Exhibit B, carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the g overning body present
13
with the exception of Ms. Case voting  “no”.  U pon request, Ms. Intlekofer provided information on
votes ca st on the ordinance  that fa iled pursuant to Dr. Rinne’ s point of order r aised during
discussion.  (#5318)
Ms. Ash advised the City’s On-Track newsletter will be issued in this month’s water bills and
requested the public conta ct her (e-mail) with their comments and to advise whethe r they find the
information useful.
City Attorney Dan White requested the governing body meet in executive session to d iscuss

present.  Mayor Kaysen announced members would meet in executive session in Council Chambers,
not open t o the public; requested the City  Attorney, City Clerk, and other  staff a s requested by the
City Attorney, be pre sent at the executive se ssion, and stated there  would be no ac tion taken by the
governing body as a result of the executive session, and that the regular City Council meeting would
officially conclude at the close  of the e xecutive session.  (Clerk’s Note: Executive session conve ned
at 9:15 p.m.)
 There being  no further  business to come bef ore the  g overning body  prior to executive
session, the meeting  was o fficially adjourne d at 10:26 p.m. following c losure of the  executive
session.

 Carol Intlekofer, MMC

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
June 8, 2009
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil C hambers.  Pr esent w ere: M AYOR - Richard L . K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS - Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson,  Mr. Spiker
and Mr. Valdez. Absent: Dr. Rinne.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.
 
Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Barb Dorr, City Treasurer, and Dan White, City
Attorney.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA]  are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal s equence o n t he a genda.)  M ayor Ka ysen a nnounced Ag enda I tem # 38(e) w as be ing
withdrawn fr om t he meeting a genda a t t he r equest o f s taff. U pon r equest by M r. C ollins, a nd
pursuant to support received by Mr. Brown and Ms. Ash, agenda item #38(c) was removed from the
Consent Agenda. Mr. Collins moved to approve remaining Consent Agenda items, seconded by Mr.
Brown.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.
[CA] MINUTES FROM REGULAR MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON May 26,
2009.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
 [CA] MINUTES FROM VOUCHERS MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON JUNE 1,
2009.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Collins moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Valdez.
Ms. Broyles disclosed that a voucher payable to Lew Broyles and Son, Inc. did not involve any
current family connections or conflict of interest.  Upon inquiry regarding a voucher payable to
Cheyenne Regional Medical Center ($9,441.90), Lt. Mark Munari, Police Dept., advised t he
expenditure is for S ANE h ospital medical ex am kits, and  Ba rb Do rr, City T reasurer, pro vided
information regarding a v oucher payable t o George K. Baum & Co. ($10, 831.00), pro fessional
services fee involving lease/option to purchase agreement for sanitation equipment. Motion carried.
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.
Mayor Kaysen opened a public hearing to receive comments on a pro posed trade of real
property owned by the City of Cheyenne to Cheyenne Hotel Investors, LLC, and Cheyenne Hotel
Investors II, LLC, described as a parcel of land situated in a portion of the Replat of Westland
Subdivision, said subdivision being further described as a portion of Lot 1 of Block One, a portion
of Lot 1 of Block Two and a portion of vacated County Road 51, consisting of approximately 51,423
square feet (estimated appraised value $97,703.70), for real property owned by Cheyenne Hotel
Investors, LLC, and Cheyenne Hotel Investors II, LLC, to the City of Cheyenne, described as a
parcel of land situated in a portion of Lot 4, Block Two, Griffin Addition; and an adjoining portion
of Government Lot 5 of Section 36, T. 14 N., R. 67 W., 6  P.M., Laramie County, lying generallyth
south and west of said Lot 4, all consisting of approximately 75,682 square feet (estimated appraised
value $75,901.45), plus the sum of $21,802.25 which represents the difference between the value
of the land to be exchanged between the parties, said funds to be used for design and construction
of amenities for Pat Griffin Park, (generally located west of Westland Road and east of I-25).  Rick
Parish, Parks and Recreation Director, stated the property involves a portion of land previously
approved for trade between the parties by the governing body, but that the amount of land being
traded has changed since it was last reviewed.  He explained the location of parcels involved in the
proposed t rade and indicated development o f t he pro perty will allow for a f uture gr een s pace
corridor a long Crow Creek, a nd ho tel p roject for t he Cheyenne Hotel I nvestors g roup.  D onn
Edmunds questioned whether a public park would be built at the location with Mr. Parish responding
that the project will allow for future potential development of a park and Greenway access.  Upon
inquiry regarding deed restrictions on the property currently owned by the City, Mr. Parish advised
city staff has spoken with a representative of the previous owners who deeded the property to the
City and that the City has received written agreement to the proposed land trade.  There being no
further comments or discussion and purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Kaysen closed
the hearing.  
Mayor Kaysen opened a public hearing to receive comments on a bar and grill liquor license
application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Suite 1901 CLLC d/b/a Suite 1901, 1901 Central
Avenue, Cheyenne, WY.  U pon inquiry, City Clerk Carol Intlekofer clarified if the application is
approved, this is the City’s last bar and grill liquor license available through the City based upon the
state law population formula. There being no further comments or discussion and purpose of the
hearing having been met, Mayor Kaysen closed the hearing and referred the application to Finance

Mayor Kaysen opened a public hearing to receive comments on a winery permit application
filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Suite 1901 C LLC d/b/a The Winery at 1901, 1901 Ce ntral
Avenue, Cheyenne, WY.  Upo n inquiry, John Harrison, CEO an d representative o f Suite 1901,
spoke in favor of the application and briefly explained the proposed renovation of the Frontier hotel
facility which will result in several multi-business uses, including a bar and grill liquor environment,
restaurant, winery, and meeting rooms.  There being no further comments or discussion and purpose
of the hearing having been met, Mayor Kaysen closed the hearing and referred the application to
Finance Committee.
“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING VARIOUS CHAPTER SECTIONS OF TITLE 5,
BUSINESS LICENSES AND REGULATIONS, OF THE CODE OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
PERTAINING TO BUSINE SS LICENSE A ND PE RMIT F EES.” R eporting f or F inance

Broyles moved to amend the restaurant liquor license fee from $1,025.00 to $1,050.00, seconded

Intlekofer clarified the fee was initially proposed to be increased by $25.00 but since the ordinance
was introduced she learned that the County’s fee was $1,050.00 and, therefore, brought it to the

“yes” – al l members of the governing body present with the exception of Ms. Ash voting “no”.

(#3844)

EXTINGUISHERS AND HOSE STATION EQUIPMENT BUSINESS LICENSES; FOOD AND

OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE PERTAINING TO CEMETERY FEES.” Mr. Valdez moved to
approve o n t hird an d f inal readi ng, s econded b y M r. Co llins.  Upo n i nquiry, J ason San chez,
Cemetery Division Director, advised proposed increases include opening and closing and perpetual

been increased prior to that time since 1997.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the
governing body present with the exception of Ms. Case voting “no”. (#3847)
“AN ORDINANCE ANNEXING TO THE CITY OF CHEYENNE, WYOMING, TRACTS
249, 2 50, 2 51, 2 52, SU NNYSIDE A DDITION 6  FILING, EX CEPT N ORTH 2 40 F EETTH
THEREOF, I NCLUDING PO RTIONS O F C HARLES S TREET A ND A RTHUR STR EET.”

seconded by Mr. P ierson.  M s. Broyles d eclared a  c onflict o f interest ( family r elationship) a nd
vacated Council Chambers.  Mo tion carried.  Vo ting “yes” – all members of the governing body
present i n C ouncil Chambers.  F ollowing a nnouncement of  th e v ote, M s. B royles r eturned to
Council Chambers. (#3848)

DeHoff to the Greenway Advisory Committee for fiscal year 2010.  Mr. Collins moved to approve,
seconded by Mr. Bro wn.  A ppreciation was expressed for t he services pro vided by co mmittee
members.  M ayor Kaysen advised as these were mayoral re-appointments, pursuant to Wyoming
Statute he would not be voting.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body

with the exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not vote.
ANNOUNCEMENTS/REPORTS/MOTIONS:

in City Council Chambers for p roposed budgets for t he City of Cheyenne a nd Board o f Public
Utilities for fiscal year 2010.
Announcement was made of a Special Session of the Governing Body to be held Tuesday,
June 16, 2009 at 5:15 p.m. in City Council Chambers for proposed budgets for the City of Cheyenne
and Board of Public Utilities for fiscal year 2010.
Announcement was made of a calcutta to be held Saturday, July 25, 2009 beginning at 5:30
p.m. a t t he V IP/Sponsor T ent located in Frontier P ark in c onjunction with t he 2 009 Cheyenne
Frontier Days Rodeo.  Proceeds to benefit Cheyenne area charities.
OTHER CITY BUSINESS:
Rick Parish, Director of Parks and Recreation, announced due to pending inclement weather
the first Movies in the Park series scheduled for June 9th in Lions Park at the Amphitheater would
be moved to the Taco John’s Events Center (TJEC). He noted TJEC will be the site for future
movies to be shown during this year’s series based upon inclement weather.
There b eing n o f urther b usiness t o co me b efore t he go verning b ody, t he m eeting was
officially adjourned at 11:02 p.m.
 Submitted by,
 
 
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
June 22, 2009
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil Chambers.  P resent w ere: M AYOR -  R ichard L.  K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS - Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr.
Spiker and Mr. Valdez.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.
 
Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Barb Dorr, City Treasurer, and Dan White, City
Attorney.
In c onjunction w ith the  recent a nnual Wyoming As sociation o f M unicipalities (WA M)
convention, M ayor Kaysen r ecognized a nd pr esented 1 5 WA M I nnovation A wards to
representatives of the f ollowing City departments: Planning, Parks and Rec reation, Engineering,
Metropolitan Planning Organization, and Public Works.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA]  are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda.)  Upon request by Ms. Case, and pursuant to support received by
Mr.  Collins and Mr. Pierson, agenda item #7 was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Collins
moved to approve  remaining Consent Agenda items, seconded by Mr. B rown.  Motion car ried.

Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.
“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CERTAIN CHAPTERS AND SECTIONS OF TITLE 17,
ZONING, OF THE CHEYENNE CITY CODE BY C HANGING THE DEFINITION OF OFF-
PREMISE S IGN IN SECTI ON 17.04.040, DEF INITIONS, SI GNAGE, AND B Y ADDI NG
ADDITIONAL LANGUAGE TO SECTION 17.128.090 G., OFF-PREMISE SIGNS.”  Mr. Collins
and Mr. Va ldez each de clared a  conflict of inter est (prope rty owner ship involvi ng leasing  of
billboards) for this as well as the next agenda item, and vacated Council Chambers. Ed Strader spoke
in oppositi on to the ordinance, expressed c oncerns with a billboard locate d near an apa rtment
dwelling, commenting on light pollution and effect on tenants due to the lighted billboard; distance
of billboards from streets, rights-of-way and greenway paths, and suggested removal of certain
billboards.  Frank Cole expressed his opinion that street rig hts-of-way should be excluded in the
distance measurement for placement of billboards, and commented on concerns with billboards near
any type of residential use zones.  Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Brown stated there
was no recommendation on the item from Committee.  Mr. Brown moved to approve on third and
final reading, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Upon inquiry , Matt Ashby, Planning Services Director,
stated the current draft of the proposed Unified Development Code does not address a section on
billboards and that whatever is decided by the governing body will be incorporated, and Pat Crank,
attorney with Speight, McCue and Crank law firm, representing NextMedia, advised decisions have
not yet been made regarding placement sites of digital vs. paper billboards. Discussion followed
regarding placement of billboards in proximity to apartments/residential use areas, and purpose of
the ordinance amendment, which is to correct language pertaining to the definition of off-premise
signs due to a 2006 amendment.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body
present in Council Chambers with the exception of Ms. Case and Dr. Rinne voting “no”. (#3858)
“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTERS 17.04 INTRODUCTORY PROVISIONS
AND DEFINITIONS AND 17.128 SIGNS OF TITLE 17, ZONING, OF THE CHEYENNE CITY
CODE 2002.”  Mr. Brown moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Pierson.
Upon inquiry, Martin Matsen, Development Director, provided information on the 150 linear ft.
distance for placement of billboards from single family residential properties as proposed in Sec.
17.128.010, G., stating if someone applied for a sign permit a plot plan would be required to reflect
the distance from the property line of the closest residence to the proposed sign pillar, and explained
the use is different than for a multi-family residence.  He confirmed that duplexes and townhomes
are not considered single family residences and if a single family residence is located within a CB
(commercial business) zone and billboards are allowed, the residence would not be afforded the 150
ft. distance protection.  Upon inquiry, Pat Crank, attorney with Speight, McCue and Crank law firm,
representing Ne xtMedia, a dvised N extMedia wo uld c onsider a nd a nalyze a ny re quest f rom a
neighbor involving night time light pollution.  He stated digital billboards are less likely to present
light pollution issues.  Comments followed on neighborhood light pollution concerns, and extending
the 150 ft. distance protection to those zones containing residential housing uses.  Dr. Rinne moved
to amend Sec. 17.128.010, G. to include duplexes and townhouses, seconded by Ms. Ash.  Upon
inquiry reg arding the amendme nt, Mr. Crank cla rified his client would be  ac ceptable to t he
amendment, a nd stated that duplexes and townhouses ar e spec ifically defined in city  code.
Comments followed in support of the amendment.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all
members of the governing body present in Council Chambers.  Upon inquiry regarding placement
of billboards near apartment buildings, Mr. Crank responded with information concerning limited
viable commercial billboard locations relative to the 150 ft. buffer zone restriction and desired high
volume visibility of signs for the benefit of sign advertisers and for public safety messages.  He also
discussed the net reduction in the number of his client’s billboards if the ordina nce is approved.
Main motion as amended carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present in
Council Chambers.  Following announcement of the vote, Mr. Collins and Mr. Valdez returned to
Council Chambers. (#3859)
“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING ORDINANCE NO. 3814 DEFINING THE TERMS AND
CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT FOR NON-UNIFORMED EMPLOYEES OF THE CITY OF
CHEYENNE.”  Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Valdez moved to approve on third and final
reading, seconded by Ms. Ash.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.
(#3860)

Broyles.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#3861)

to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all
members of the governing body. (#3862)

THE MEMBERSHIP AND MEETINGS OF THE CONTRACTOR LICENSING BOARD.”  Mr.
Brown moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Ms. Case.  Mr. Brown moved to
amend by substitute, seconded by Mr. Collins. I t was advised the  substitute removes the words
“inefficiency, such as”; strikes the sentence “The governing body may investigate and recommend
removal if a member misses two consecutive regular meetings”, and strikes the sentence “Meeting
expenses will be paid by the City.”.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the
governing body.  Main motion as amended by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the

final re ading, seconde d by Mr. Pierson.  Motion carr ied.  Voting  “yes” – all members of  the
governing body. (#3865)

(LOCATED WEST OF THE INTERSECTION OF MISSILE DRIVE AND WESTLAND ROAD).”
Mr. Brown moved to approve on second reading with staff recommendations #1 through 4, seconded
by Mr. Collins.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
“AN O RDINANCE ANNEXING TO TH E CI TY OF  CHEYENNE, WYOMI NG, A
PORTION OF NORTHWEST QUARTER OF THE SOUTHWEST QUARTER (NW 1/4 SW 1/4)
OF SECTION 20, TOWNSHIP 14 NORTH, RANGE 66 WEST OF THE 6  P.M., LARAMIETH
COUNTY, WYOMING  (GENERALLY DESCRIBED AS FOL LOWS: A TRACT OF L AND
LOCATED EAST OF POWDERHOUSE ROAD, NORTH OF AND ADJACENT TO LIFE CARE

“A RESOLUTION RE-APPROPRIATING THE FISCAL YEAR 2009 BUDGET OF THE
CITY OF CHEYENNE ACCORDING TO THE PROVISIONS OF W.S. §16-4-112 AND §16-4-
113.”  Mr. Va ldez moved to adopt, seconde d by Ms. Broyles.  Mr. Valdez moved to amend by
allocating $25,000.00 from FY2009 City Council professional services fund to FY2010 Art in Public
Places fund, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Upon inquiry, City Treasurer Barb Dorr advised as of May
31, 2009, the balance in t he Art in Public Places (AIPP) account was $51,312.00.  Pur suant to
discussion on the remaining balance in the AIPP fund, Rick Parish, Parks and Recreation Director,
clarified the most recent piece of art has been commissioned and the funding will come out of the
remaining AIPP fund balance.  Comments included FY2010 budget reduction areas; other types of
art media ns that could be utiliz ed in the community , other than sc ulptures, which ar e not as
expensive; lack of  FY2010 f unding f or AIPP and effe ct on the AI PP C ommittee, a nd the re -
appropriation of funding from the current fiscal year to the next budget year.  Upon inquiry, Ms.
Dorr a dvised as of Ma y 31, 2009, t he Council’s profe ssional service s fund balanc e wa s
approximately $6,765.00, and Kris Jones, Executive Assistant to City Council, advised that a recent
communication with Acc ounting reflected an estimated bal ance of $39,000.00 in the Council’s
professional services line item.  Comm ents followed on the difference in balance amounts in the
professional services line item as reported by Ms. Dorr and Ms. Jones.  During ensuing discussion,
Ms. Dorr offered to provide a review of the line item to ascertain the correct amount of the fund’s
balance prior to the end of the evening’s meeting.  She suggested the funding source could instead
come from the FY2009 general contingency fund.  Mr. Collins moved to amend the amendment to
allocate $2 5,000.00 ou t of  F Y2009 g eneral c ontingency fu nds in stead o f t he City Cou ncil
professional services account, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Upon request, Ms. Dorr advised estimated
funds to be submitted by  departments at budget year-end will be minim al, and r eviewed the re -
appropriation process.  In conjunction with comments regarding the status of the AIPP Committee
if funding is n ot received for the next fi scal year, Mayor Kaysen clarified the Committee will
continue to meet to plan for artwork contributions in the community, and stated he had visited with
the Committee chair regarding lack of funding for the next fiscal year due to budgetary restrictions.
Further discussion followed.  Motion to amend the amendment carried.  Voting “yes” – Mr. Brown,
Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Valdez and Mayor Kaysen.  Voting “no” – Ms.
Ash, Mr. Pierson and Mr. Spiker.  Discussion continued on support for the AIPP program, funding
cut-backs made during FY2010 budget preparation, and the City’s overall financial picture.   During
comments, Ms. Dorr clarified that during the FY2010 budget preparation, the following areas were
affected by the elimination of funding: Allocation to Parks infrastructure fund; Jeff Ziebart contract;
employee bonuses, and the AIPP.  Ms. Broyles raised a point of clarification questioning the motion
on the floor with Mayor Kaysen advising the pending motion is to approve the initial amendment
as amended to reflect allocation of $25,000.00 from the FY2009 general contingency fund, instead
of from the Council’s professional services line item, to FY 2010 Art in Public Places line item.  Ms.
Broyles moved to amend to allocate $25,000.00 from Council’s FY2009 professional services line
item and requested verification of an accurate balance amount in the Council’s professional services
fund.  To allow Ms. Dorr and Ms. Jones time to research and determine the actual balance amount,
Mayor Kaysen advised the agenda item would be tabled until the end of the meeting agenda, prior
to other City business.  Mayor Kaysen removed the item from the ta ble following reading of the
announcements section on the meeting agenda.  Ms. Dorr clarified there is $6,000.00 currently in
Council’s professional services account and that the balance amount recently provided to Ms. Jones
was in error.  Ms. Broyles withdrew her motion to amend.  Motion to amend as ame nded failed.
Voting “yes” – Ms. Broyles and Mr. Collins.  Voting “no” - Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Case, Mr.
Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Spiker, Mr. Valdez and Mayor Kaysen.  Upon further query on notable
items contained in the re -appropriation, Ms . Dorr advised a r ecently rec eived invoice  for the
Downtown De velopment Author ity’s 2008 TI F ( tax i ncrement financ ing) in the amount of
$477,156.00 was included, which will leave a general fund reserve balance of about $7,000,000.00,
and provided an explanation of how the TIF payment affects reserves.  Main motion carried.  Voting

traffic data that were studied relative to modern roundabout vs. standard intersection designs.  Pacomio

and s uggested t he i tem be  p ostponed a nd t hat C ouncil m embers travel t o R awlins t o vi ew t he

followed on a modern roundabout concept, widening of the roadway and working with residents who
may be affected, West Pershing Blvd. issues, and non-feasibility, due to cost, of the City purchasing
several properties in the area.  Upon inquiry, Mr. MacDonald advised the design plan is 35% complete

times has multiple changes from the preliminary design.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members
