RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
December 28, 2009
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning at
6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers.  Present were: MAYOR - Richard L. Kaysen; COUNCIL MEMBERS:
Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Spiker and Mr.
Valdez.  Also present: Kristy Anderson, Deputy City Clerk; Tammy Fossen, City Treasurer’s Office,
and Dan White, City Attorney.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.
Nominations an d e lection o f Ci ty Co uncil Pr esident f or 2010.  M ayor K aysen an nounced,
pursuant to City Code, Title 2, the Mayor conducts the elections for City Council President and Vice-
President but may not v ote, therefore, he would not b e participating in voting for the elections of
Council President and Vice-President.  M r. Collins moved to n ominate and elect Dr. Rinne as City
Council President for 2010, seconded by Ms. Ash. Mr. Spiker moved to nominate and elect Ms. Broyles
as City Council President for 2010, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  There being no further nominations, Mr.
Collins moved that nominations cease, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Motion to cease nominations carried.
Voting “yes” – all members o f City Council. Comments followed regarding an informal straw poll
conducted by council members each year prior to the election of Council President and Vice-President,
and the role of Council President.  Upon request, Dr. Rinne and Ms. Broyles provided comments on
their experience serving o n City Council and how each felt t hey could best represent t he Council.
Motion t o elect Dr. Rinne did not carry. Voting “yes” - M s. Ash, Mr. Collins, Dr. Rinne and Mr.
Valdez.  Voting “no”- Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Pierson and Mr. Spiker with Ms. Case “passing”.
Motion to elect Ms. Broyles did not carry.  Voting “yes” - Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Pierson and
Mr. Spiker. Voting “no” - Ms. Ash, Mr. Collins, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Valdez with Ms. Case “passing”.
Mr. Pierson moved to reopen nominations, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Ms. Case raised a point of order
regarding her option to pass during voting, advising she did not abstain but wished to vote later. Mr.
Pierson withdrew his motion to reopen nominations, with concurrence by Mr. Collins as second to the
motion.  Upo n request regarding a r uling on breaking a t ie relative to passage of a motion to elect
officers, City Attorney Dan White requested a brief recess in order to research Roberts Rule of Order
further before making a ruling.  Following a 15 minute recess, Mayor Kaysen reconvened the meeting
at 6:40 p.m.  M r. White advised after reviewing Robert’s Rules of Order the option to pass is only
allowed when there is a roll call vote; the “pass” procedure doesn’t apply in this situation as it is a voice
vote, th erefore a  “ pass” c ould b e d etermined a s a n a bstention or  a  n egative v ote m aking b oth
nominations a 4-5 vote with neither candidate prevailing.  He further clarified pursuant to City Code,
the Mayor conducts the elections, but does not cast a vote.  Upon inquiry on whether it was in order
to make a new motion, Mr. White clarified per Robert’s Rules of Order, council continues voting until
a c andidate i s e lected s o n ominations w ould n eed to b e r eopened. M ayor K aysen c alled f or
nominations. Mr. Pierson moved to nominate Ms. Broyles as City Council President for 2010, seconded
by Mr. Brown.  Mr. Collins moved to nominate Dr. Rinne as City Council President for 2010, seconded
by Ms. Ash. Mr. Collins moved to  cease nominations, seconded by Mr. Brown.  M otion to  cease
nominations carried, with all Council members voting “yes”. Mr. Spiker raised a point of order on
whether a f ailed motion co uld be re-introduced at t he same meeting with Mr. White advising per
Robert’s Rules of Order nominations could continue, even for the same candidates, until someone was
elected.  He also clarified “pass” could not be used in this type of vote.   Motion to elect Dr. Rinne did
not carry by a majority vote.  Voting “yes” - Ms. Ash, Mr. Collins, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Valdez.  Voting
“no” - Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Pierson and Mr. Spiker.  Motion to elect Ms. Broyles
carried by a majority vote.  Voting “yes” - Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Pierson and Mr.
Spiker.  Voting “no” - Ms. Ash, Mr. Collins, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Valdez.
Nominations a nd e lection of  City Council V ice P resident for 2 010.  M r. Collins moved to
nominate and elect Mr. Pierson, seconded by Mr. Spiker.  Th ere being no further nominations, Mr.
Brown moved that nominations cease, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Motion to cease nominations carried.
Voting “yes” – all members of City Council.  Upon inquiry regarding whether a straw poll had been
held for Vice President, it was advised it had not.  Upon further inquiry on how Mr. Pierson had come
to be nominated, it was advised he was nominated for his past experience serving on City Council.
Motion to nominate and elect Mr. Pierson carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of City Council.  
Mayor Kaysen announced that individuals in attendance in the audience that may be present for
the two agenda items introducing an ordinance regarding terms and conditions of employment for non-
uniformed employees and sworn officers would only be referred to Finance Committee at this meeting
with no discussion at this time on either ordinance.  He advised the Finance Committee would meet in
Room 122 on January 4, 2010 beginning at 11:00 a.m.  However, he stated if those employees present
wished to speak under other business at the meeting they were welcome to stay and provide comments
at that time. 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA]  are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  T here will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two other
members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its normal
sequence on the agenda.) Upon request by Mr. Collins, and pursuant to support received by Mr. Brown
and Ms. Ash , agenda item #23(e) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon request by Mr. Brown,
and pursuant to support received by Mr. Collins and Mr. Pierson, agenda item #23(b) was removed
from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Collins moved to approve remaining Consent Agenda items, seconded
by Mr. Brown.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.
[CA] MINUTES FROM REGULAR MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON DECEMBER
14, 2009.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
[CA] MINUTES FROM VOUCHERS MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON DECEMBER
21, 2009.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Brown moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Mr.
Valdez declared a conflict of interest due to a voucher payable to radio station KYOY ($250.00), for
advertising, a nd va cated C ouncil C hambers.  Motion c arried.  V oting “yes” -  a ll members o f t he
governing b ody prese nt in Co uncil Chambers.  F ollowing an nouncement o f t he v ote, Mr.  Valdez
returned to Council Chambers. 
Mayor Kaysen opened a public hearing for a transfer of ownership for a restaurant liquor license
application f iled w ith t he Ci ty Cl erk’s Of fice f or Wei Sheng Qi u d /b/a Go lden Ho use Ch inese
Restaurant, 1651 Carey Ave., Ste. 8, Cheyenne, WY (License currently held by Yu Zheng d/b/a Golden
House Restaurant, 1651 Carey Ave., Ste. 8, Cheyenne, WY).    There being no comments or discussion
and purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Kaysen closed the public hearing and referred the
application to Finance Committee.
Mayor Kaysen op ened a  p ublic h earing to d etermine w hether c ompliance of  a nnexation
conditions required by Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402 exists for the parcels commonly known as So uthwest
Properties, situated in a portion of Sections 12 and 13, T. 13N., R. 67W., of the 6  P.M. Laramieth
County, WY. (Ge nerally located e ast o f So uthwest Drive, So uth o f Interstate 80 , West o f BNSF
Railroad, and North of Woodenshoe Road, including Cheyenne Animal Shelter and associated rights-
of-way).  Don Threewit, Planning Services Dept., reviewed requirements and compliance of conditions
contained in Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402, including specific information indicating compliance with Wyo.
Stat. §15-1-402(a)(i) through (vi).  Deb Roden, attorney with Woodhouse Roden Law Of fice,
representing county residents residing in the area proposed for annexation, advised they had the same
objections to this annexation action as they did regarding the Swan Ranch annexation.  M s. Roden
raised concerns with traffic congestion and egress/ingress to the development; geographical a nd
physical isolation of the area from the city and contiguity issues.  M ike Basom, attorney with Dray,
Thompson and Dyekman, representing the developer, advised these issues have been raised before with
other a nnexations w ith t he same platting, p lanning a nd d esign issues.  H e a dvised t his p roperty is
referred to as a natural growth property in the PlanCheyenne document and stated issues could be
worked out within the platting phase of the development. Leo Garcia, spoke in opposition to annexation
based on traffic concerns and commented he does not feel this is for the health, safety and welfare of
the individuals that live in this area. There being no further comments or input and purpose of the
hearing having been met, Mayor Kaysen closed the hearing.

BELVOIR R ANCH P ROPERTY.” M r. V aldez moved to a dopt, s econded by M r. C ollins. U pon
inquiry, Don Threewitt, Planning Services Dept., advised the total survey cost is $25,626.00, which
includes the following funding: City hard cash match of $5,000.00 through the Urban Planning Small
Grant Match fund, the award of a grant from the State Historic Preservation Office (SHPO) in the
amount of $15,000.000, an in-kind local match of $2,160.00 and staff time (150 hours) and materials
match of $3,466.00 included in the Planning Department budget.  Discussion followed on the survey
providing the opportunity to develop the ranch in the future, deadline time frame for grant application
and c ouncil approval. U pon inquiry, M r. T hreewit a dvised a n e xtension for t he a pplication t o be
submitted had been applied for and received to Jan. 31, 2010.  He further clarified $5,000 had been

was time sensitive, Mr. Threewit reiterated the deadline to submit acceptance of the grant was Jan. 31,
2010.  Discussion followed on time frame for submittal of grant acceptance and allowing enough time
for staff to negotiate survey provisions to meet the deadline, occurrence of SHPO grants being awarded,
and concerns with taking on more financial responsibilities during a budget crisis. Upon inquiry, Mr.
Threewitt advised SHPO grants have been awarded annually, however t he City has not previously
turned down a grant, stating he was unsure whether non-acceptance could effect future awards.  He
further reviewed soft match provisions involving volunteer time and staff time, and hard cash aspects
involving the project.  Motion to amend failed.  Voting “yes” - Ms. Ash, Ms. Broyles, Dr. Rinne and
Mr. Valdez.  Voting “no” - Mr. Brown, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Spiker and Mayor
Kaysen.  Discussion continued on future opportunities to apply for grants for the ranch.  Upon inquiry,
Mr. Threewitt, provided information on state grant funding available and the City’s share of awarded
funding.  Main motion failed.   Voting “yes” - Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Valdez and Mayor Kaysen.

Motion carried.  Voting “yes” - all members of the governing body.

Cheyenne, Public Works Department, purchased with funds from U.S. Department of H omeland

(#5496)

Marble Avenue (2003-2006 1% Sales Tax) -- referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Contract Modification No. 1 to Contract No. 5477 between the City of Cheyenne and Recco,
Inc. d/b/a Five-R-Co. to lower the power lines to the Transfer Station gas pumps -- referred to Finance
Committee.  
[CA] Contract Modification No. 1 to Contract No. 5045 between t he City o f Cheyenne and J-R
Engineering, L LC fo r d esign s ervices o n t he 2009 Bus S top U pgrades P roject  ( Federal T ransit
Authority & American Reinvestment and Recovery Act) -- referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Contract Modification No. 4 to Contract No. 4968 between the City of Cheyenne and Wyoming
Department of Transportation for the reconstruction of Pershing Blvd from I-25 to Pioneer Avenue
(2003-2006 1% Sales Tax) -- referred to Finance Committee.
CONSIDERATION OF BIDS:
Consideration o f Bi d #M -12-10 f or a co ntract b etween t he C ity o f Ch eyenne an d A ztec
Construction Co., Inc., of Cheyenne, for the Transfer Station Fire Main Loop Project (State Loan &
Investment Board).  M r. Valdez moved to accept the bid in an amount not to exceed $113,724.00,
seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Upon inquiry, Jim Elias, Public Works Director, explained that use of the
miscellaneous force account would allow immediate action, if necessary, for any unknown problems
that may occur during the project.  Concerns were expressed regarding completion of other projects on
the SLIB list.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Elias explained that projects for solid waste use would go unfinished
if this is paid for out of the solid waste fund.  He further advised this project is part of the single stream
recycling project that was approved under SLIB funding, and provided information on project costs and
funding. Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#5498)
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-3-10 for one new 2011 cab & chassis truck with dump body, spreader,
snow plow and tarpaulin from Peterbilt of Wyoming for the Street and Alley Department (2003-2006
& 2007-2010 1 % S ales T ax).  M otion ( per Consent A genda) c arried ( approved in the a mount of
$171,952.00). 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-5-10 for two 2010 4x4 Utility Vehicles from Greiner Ford, Casper,
WY for t he Pu blic W orks D ept a nd C onstruction En gineering D ept. (2 007-2010 1 % S ales Ta x).
Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (approved in the amount of $39,304.00).
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-7-10 for furnishing and installing one new single ram baler and one
new roller c hain c onveyor from JDM Eq uipment, L LC o f Arvada, C O for the Tra nsfer S tation --
referred to Finance Committee.
APP OINTM ENT S:
 Appointment of Philip Griggs to the Public Transit Advisory Board and Kurt Zunker to the Fire
Civil Service Commission.  Mr. Collins moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Motion carried.
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not
vote (Mayoral appointments).
ANNOUNCEMENTS/ REP ORTS /MOTIONS :
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held January 11, 2010 at 6:00 p.m. in City
Council Chambers to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyo. Stat.
§15-1-402 exists for a parcel of land being situated in the  SW ¼ NW ¼ of Section 21 T. 14N., R.
66W., of the 6  P. M., Laramie County, WY (located south of Plain View Road, west of Point Bluff,th
and north of Apache Street).
Announcement was made of the appointment of Brian N. Kozak as Chief of Police for the City
of Cheyenne, to be confirmed January 11, 2010.
OTHER CIT Y BUSINESS:
Claus Johnson, Cheyenne Public Employees Association (CPEA) President, commended Mr.
Harris for coming forth with the lease agreement of the Pride Park Softball Complex, but advised he
does not support the agreement that went through tonight with Post 1881 due t o the city’s financial
concerns.  He advised he feels employees should come first and this could have saved the city $20,000.
He no ted he w as speaking on behalf of c o-workers, stated he d oesn’t feel e mployees c reated t he
financial situation the city is in, but they are part of it, and commented that employees should have been
made a ware of the situation sooner a nd g iven a n op portunity to p rovide input.  U pon inquiry for
clarification on cost saving ideas for the city,  Mr. Johnson provided some cost saving measures the
Parks and Recreation Department has implemented, and suggested a change to the city vehicle take-
home policy. He advised CPEA is in opposition to employees losing longevity pay.
Also s peaking in re gard t o t he C ity’s financial s ituation, Stev e Pe nnock, Sa nitation B oard
representative, discussed cost saving measures that have already been implemented in the Sanitation
Department.  He advised they are willing to do their part, but expressed concerns with loss of longevity
pay. Hawk Leal, Sanitation Department employee, also expressed concerns with losing longevity pay,
stating f urlough d ays a re u nderstandable, a nd p rovided s uggestions f or cost saving m easures f or
Sanitation Department operations. He also expressed concerns over citizens lack of participation in
Sanitation Department programs.  John Palmer, Sanitation Department employee, expressed concerns
on reducing employees pay and discussed wages for Sanitation Department employees.  He  requested
the City look at cutting projects before cutting pay.
Upon inquiry regarding clarification of certain part-time employees in the Public Works Dept.
and Treasurer’s Office, Jim Elias, Public Works Director, explained that the Department is looking at
combining and/or eliminating part-time positions.  Mayor Kaysen explained the part-time position in
the T reasurer’s o ffice had been a  full-time position a nd c hanging t o p art-time status w ill r esult in
savings to the city.
Mayor Kaysen addressed the city employee vehicle policy and clarified department heads had
been asked to evaluate and assess all employees who have vehicles assigned with regard to  “on call”
responsibilities, discussed proposed longevity and deferred compensation reductions, and encouraged
employees to bring cost saving ideas and concerns to him. 
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was officially
adjourned at 10:05 p.m.
 Submitted by,
 
 
 
 Kristy B. Anderson, CMC
 Deputy City Clerk
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle
 January 11, 2010

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
January 11, 2010
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil C hambers.  Pr esent w ere: M AYOR - Richard L . K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS:  Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr.
Spiker and Mr. Valdez.  Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Barb Dorr, City Treasurer, and
Dan White, City Attorney.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA]  are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda.) Upon request by Ms. Ash, and pursuant to support received by Mr.
Collins and Dr. Rinne, agenda item #22(c) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Collins
moved to approve remaining Consent Agenda items, seconded by Mr. Brown.  M otion carried.
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.
[CA] MINUTES F ROM REGUL AR M EETING OF  T HE GOVE RNING BODY  ON
DECEMBER 28, 2009.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
[CA] MINUTES FROM VOUCHERS MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON JANUARY
4, 2010.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Brown moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Spiker.
Upon inquiry, City Treasurer Barb Dorr reviewed information available for vouchers payable to
Express Services, Inc.($505.83), temporary clerical services; McGee, Hearne & Paiz ($20,100.00),
final bill for annual auditing services, and Dept . o f Family Services ($120. 00), pre- employment
background checks.  Rich Wiederspahn, Human Resources Director, provided further information
on the voucher for Dept. of Family Services.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the
governing body.
Mayor Kaysen op ened a  p ublic hearing to determine w hether c ompliance of a nnexation
conditions required by Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402 exists for a parcel of land being situated in the  SW ¼
NW ¼ of Section 21, T. 4N., R.66W., of the 6  P. M., Laramie County, WY (located south of Plainth
View Road, west of Point Bluff, and north of Apache Street). Don Threewitt, Planning Services
Dept., reviewed requirements and compliance of conditions contained in Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402,
including specific information indicating compliance with Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402(a)(i) through (vi).
Upon inquiry, Mr. Threewitt clarified the area is different from a previous annexation request that
had come before City Council.  T here being no  further c omments o r input a nd p urpose o f t he
hearing having been met, Mayor Kaysen closed the hearing.
“AN OR DINANCE A MENDING TI TLE 17,  Z ONING, CH APTER 17.08,  Z ONING
DISTRICTS E STABLISHED A ND S ECTION 1 7.08.040 C HEYENNE C ITY M AP O F T HE
CHEYENNE CITY CODE, BY CHANGING THE ZONING CLASSIFICATION FROM MR-2
MEDIUM D ENSITY R ESIDENTIAL-DEVELOPING A ND PU D PL ANNED U NIT
DEVELOPMENT DIS TRICTS T O HR -2 HI GH DENSI TY R ESIDENTIAL-DEVELOPING
DISTRICT FOR A REPLAT OF LOTS 1 AND 2, BLOCK ONE, FARSON ADDITION AND ALL
OF BLOCK ONE, DRY CREEK TWIN HOMES, ALSO TO BE KNOWN AS WOODHAVEN
SUBDIVISION, CHEYENNE, WYOMING (LOCATED EAST OF AND ADJACENT TO WILLS
ROAD, SOUTH OF THE DRY CREEK CHANNEL AND PARKVIEW DRIVE).”  Mayor Kaysen
advised the item was being withdrawn from the agenda pursuant to written request of the developer.
“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING ORDINANCE NO. 3860 DEFINING THE TERMS AND
CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT FOR NON-UNIFORMED EMPLOYEES OF THE CITY OF
CHEYENNE.”  E ric H ardgrave, C heyenne P ublic E mployees A ssociation ( CPEA) P resident,
discussed  job loyalty by City employees, cost savings ideas that had been submitted to the Mayor
for consideration, opposition to reduction in workforce, and concern with proposed employee loss
of benefits, particularly longevity pay.  The following individuals expressed concerns regarding the
proposed ordinance amendments:  Nathan Maine, Parks Division; Mark Pollard, Golf Division; John
Palmer, San itation De pt.; Kelly K enworthy, 1% Co nstruction E ngineering; Dav e Spo rts, 1%
Construction Engineering; Steve Pennock, Sanitation; Donn Edmunds, citizen; Ron Conard, Golf
Division, and Dick Mason, Building Dept.  Topics discussed included: Dividing the p roposed
ordinance amendments to allow for separate discussion; researching and reviewing various areas
for cost savings, including energy savings options, solar/wind energy, energy grants, land sales, fuel
usage, and cell phone usage and plans; voluntary time off by higher paid employees; hiring freeze,
furlough days; opposition to removal of longevity pay program; review areas involving revenue;
employee survey to be generated by the 2009 Leadership class with the support of CPEA to acquire
input and suggestions from employees on cost savings or revenue generation; support for furlough
days before implementing a reduction in workforce or other options involving wages; suggestion
of bringing BOPU “into the fold”; concern with recent softball field agreement with VFW relative
to c osts; r estoration ti me frame for a ny b enefits w hich may b e lost; e mployees’ c oncerns w ith
communication is sues r egarding t heir in put, s uggestions a nd t he a nticipated b udget s hortfall;
allowing t ime f or a reas i nvolving c ost r eductions/efficiencies by  d epartments t o d etermine
effectiveness; review of police vehicle policy;  reducing construction and materials costs; statement
that furloughs and reductions in workforce doesn’t reduce employee workloads, and suggestion of
possible reduction in pay option predicated o n reassurance monies would be restored when the
financial situation improves.  R eporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Brown stated there was no
recommendation on the item from the Committee. Mr. Collins moved to approve on second reading,
seconded by Mr. Brown.  Mr. Collins moved to amend Section 4 and Exhibit B to restore longevity
pay pro visions, s econded b y M s. Bro yles.  Upo n i nquiry, City T reasurer Barb Do rr rev iewed
anticipated budget shortfall amounts for the current fiscal year and potential shortfall for next fiscal
year, stating the amount will depend on upcoming state legislative decisions.  She also provided
information on the City’s use of 5th penny sales tax dollars.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes”
– all members of the governing body.  Discussion followed on concerns with the next fiscal year
budget a nd s tate f unding a ssistance to m unicipalities; employee c ost s avings i deas ( submit to
Mayor); e nergy e fficiency e fforts a nd lack o f p ast d ue d iligence in r esearching and c onserving
savings; past employee pay increases; City reserves; cell phone plan review to ascertain savings;
energy savings and wind generation options, staff overtime costs, potential early retirement offering,
and r eview o f a ll bu dget a reas i n c onjunction w ith e mployee i deas f or cost savings.  D uring
discussion City Attorney Dan White confirmed there presently is no single cell phone contract plan
and Mayor Kaysen advised a city-wide review of cell phone usage was conducted in June of 2009
and that a point of control is now being utilized and a competitive provider for services process is
underway.  Upon inquiry regarding a possible early retirement offering, Ms. Dorr advised a review
of  employees eligible for retirement under the Rule of 85, pursuant to the state retirement program,
reflects that if all of the qualified individuals were to retire, $2,000,000 would be saved during the
year. S he s tated a  p ossible e arly r etirement p lan i s c urrently b eing r eviewed.  U pon i nquiry
regarding re venue e nhancement a reas t o a ssist with the an ticipated b udget s hortfall, M s. D orr
advised all departments reviewed areas during last spring’s budget preparation and many fee areas
had been increased.  She advised the City is limited in its ability to generate revenue with regard to
the amount o f property t ax assessed and o ther areas restricted by law.  U pon inquiry regarding
possible furlough days and the closing of City offices, Mayor Kaysen advised the issue involving
furlough d ays a ffiliated w ith c losure o f City offices t o t he p ublic h ad b een lo oked a t c losely
regarding potential energy/utility savings, but there may not be a lot of savings to be realized due
to the demand on utilities to “power back up”.  He explained furlough time on a flexible schedule
basis p er d epartment ( with offices r emaining o pen) w ould save money w hile still c ontinuing to
provide services to the community.  Mayor Kaysen indicated work would continue on a possible
early retirement program and noted there are federal laws that must be reviewed and complied with
relative to timing issues and notification to eligible employees.  With regard to revenue generation,
Mayor Kaysen clarified leases a re a lso being r eviewed involving u se o f City a thletic fields a nd
programs and provided information on a “pay for play” program that is being considered for a more
balanced approach for users as well as for City maintenance and operation costs.  Upon inquiry
regarding the status of debts/fees owed to the City, Ms. Dorr indicated there is money in arrears
owed by customers.  Discussion followed on employee cost savings ideas, with input provided by
Mr. Hardgrave (CPEA) upon request; developing an early retirement option that would determine
the greatest incentive to employees to retire at the lowest cost to the City; percentage of general fund
monies involving employee costs and benefits; monetary furlough effect on employees and potential
financial “crippling”of the workforce; statement that reduction in workforce may be necessary, and
energy efficiency savings. Upon inquiry, Vicki Nemecek, Public Works Dept., provided information
on the current energy efficiency program, indicating an energy audit had been conducted and the
program is moving forward with grant applications.  She explained award of grant funding has very
recently been received in the amount of $547,800.00, which will be used for l ighting r etrofits,
sensors, an energy education element, and a high efficiency boiler, which should result in proposed
savings of at least $168,000 a y ear.  Sh e indicated two other grants have been applied for ,and
advised i t w ill ta ke s ome y ears f or th e p ayback on  s ome s avings to b e realized.  D iscussion
continued on state legislative funding to municipalities; information on state funding provided by
a recent Wyoming Association of Municipalities publication, and whether the state can provide any
“wiggle ro om” relative t o t he t iming o f reduced f unds t o be received within t he state’s biennial
budget. U pon inquiry, Ms. Dorr advised she w as not a ware of a ny scenario in w hich th e state
delayed funding reductions to the second year of a biennial budget instead of implementing within
the f irst budget year.  Main motion as amended carried.  Voting “yes” – all members o f t he
governing body.
Mr. Pierson moved to change the order of agenda business to bring forward Item #25(a) as
the next item of business, seconded by Ms. Broyles. Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members
of the governing body.  Mayor Kaysen stated the item, entitled Appointment of Brian N. Kozak as
Chief of Police for the City of Cheyenne,  wo uld be brought forward for action.  M ayor Kaysen
introduced M r. K ozak, wh o i ntroduced f amily an d f riends in attendance, pr ovided a b rief
background of  h is l aw e nforcement c areer a nd e xperience, a nd c ommented on  h is p riority of
working with and gaining t he t rust o f t he community, and working with department staff.  M r.
Spiker moved to approve the appointment, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes”
– a ll m embers of  t he governing b ody w ith th e e xception of  M ayor K aysen w ho d id n ot v ote
(Mayoral appointment). Mayor Kaysen advised Mr. Kozak’s first official day of work would be
March 1 , when he will be sworn in at a ceremony to be held at 8:30 a.m. t hat day in Councilst
Chambers.
Following a ten minute recess, Mayor Kaysen reconvened the meeting at 8:10 p.m.
“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING ORDINANCE NO. 3861 DEFINING THE TERMS AND
CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT FOR SWORN OFFICERS OF THE CHEYENNE POLICE
DEPARTMENT.”  Paul Bulman, Police Protective Association President, expressed support for the
same amendment as approved for the prior agenda item, involving non-uniformed City employees,
as well as a potential early retirement proposal for police officers.  John Palmer, Sanitation Dept.,
questioned t he F ire em ployees un ion wi llingness t o discuss budget i ssues wi th M ayor K aysen
advising a meeting has been scheduled for tomorrow (Jan. 12 .  Mr. Brown reported there was noth)
recommendation on the item from Finance Committee.  Mr. Brown moved to approve on second
reading, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Mr. Collins moved to amend Section 5 and Exhibit B to restore
longevity pay provisions, s econded b y Mr. S piker.  U pon inquiry concerning w hether an e arly
retirement proposal that might be offered would affect those who have previously retired, Mayor
Kaysen advised previous retirees would not be affected.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes”
– a ll members o f t he g overning b ody.  M ain mo tion a s a mended c arried.  V oting “ yes” –  a ll
members of the governing body.
“AN OR DINANCE AMENDING SE CTION 6.08. 020(B), K EEPING OR
SLAUGHTERING OF CERTAIN ANIMALS – RESTRICTIONS WITHIN CITY, OF CHAPTER
6.08, ANIMAL CA RE A ND C ONTROL REGUL ATIONS GE NERALLY, OF  T ITLE 6,

ADJACENT TO E. 17TH STREET, WEST OF CONVERSE AVENUE)” -- referred to Public

“A RESOLUTION DESIGNATING THE SUNDAYS DURING 2010 THAT ANNUAL
LIQUOR LICENSEES MAY EXTEND DISPENSING ROOM HOURS OF OPERATION FOR
SALES U NTIL 2 :00 A .M. T HE F OLLOWING D AY.”  B ryan G rzegorczyk, Laramie C ounty
Liquor Association, spoke in favor of the resolution and advised the four Sundays being requested
are Super Bowl Sunday, Sunday of Memorial Day weekend, 4  of July and the first S unday ofth
Frontier D ays.  H e r eviewed fundraising e fforts b y liquor licensees th at a ssist w ith c ommunity
support programs, and stated the Association is developing a proposed program to provide driver
transportation services in support of responsible consumption.  Mr. Brown reported there was no
recommendation on the item from Finance Committee.  Mr. Brown moved to adopt, seconded by
Ms. Case.  Upo n inquiry, Mr. Grzegorczyk provided further information on the proposed driver
transportation program.  Pursuant to inquiry made at the Finance Committee meeting, Captain Jeff
Schulz, I nterim Po lice C hief, rep orted  t here was  n o n otable i ncrease i nvolving DUI st atistics
relative to extended hours approved for the four Sundays in 2009.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes”
– all members of the governing body with the exception of Ms. Broyles, Mr. Pierson and Mr. Spiker
voting “no”. (#5177)
“RESOLUTION –  A UTHORIZATION F OR TH E M AYOR A ND CITY C LERK TO
EXECUTE A S TATE H ISTORIC P RESERVATION O FFICE ( SHPO) C ERTIFIED L OCAL
GOVERNMENT G RANT A WARD F OR H ISTORIC PR ESERVATION B OARD M EMBER
ATTENDANCE AT THE 2010 SAVING PLACES CONFERENCE.”  Mr. Brown reported there
was n o r ecommendation on  th e i tem f rom F inance C ommittee.  Mr. B rown m oved to a dopt,
seconded by  M r. C ollins.  U pon inquiry, D on T hreewitt, U rban P lanning S ervices, no ted t he
Historical Preservation Board is part of the City’s Certified Local Government (CLG) program with
grants and funding assistance available as part of the City’s CLG status.  H e advised due to the
status the City is awarded funding annually, and explained training for Board members and staff
helps maintain CLG status for funding sponsorship.  He indicated the proposed grant award would
fund registration for 2 Board members and one city staff member to attend a training conference,
fulfilling requirements necessary to continue qualification for CLG grants, and stated expense to the
City for the training would involve use of a City vehicle and fuel (approximately $25.00), and that
all meal c osts w ould b e th e p ersonal r esponsibility of  a ttendees.  U pon inquiry, M r. T hreewitt
provided further information on training requirements relative to current and potential future grant
funds.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  (#5178)
[CA] “A RESOLUTION APPROVING AN AMENDED PROMISSORY NOTE FOR CLEAN
WATER SR F L OAN - 081 BET WEEN THE  ST ATE OF  W YOMING A ND TH E CITY OF
CHEYENNE, WYOMING FOR CHEYENNE’S RECYCLE WATER SYSTEM E XTENSION
PROJECT AND AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR, CITY CLERK AND THE DIRECTOR OF THE
BOARD OF PUBLIC UTILITIES TO SIGN THE AMENDED PROMISSORY NOTE” (Water
Enterprise Fund) -- referred to Finance Committee (sponsor - Mr. Valdez). 
[CA] “A RESOLUTION SUPPORTING THE CITY OF CHEYENNE’S APPLICATION FOR

PICNIC SHELTER PROJECT” (Community Facility Fees & In-kind labor) -- referred to Finance
Committee (sponsors - Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles and Mr. Pierson).

SOUTH OF AND ADJACENT TO CAMPSTOOL ROAD, EAST OF MORRIE AVENUE)” --
referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor - Ms. Ash).
[CA] “A RESOLU TION DE TERMINING THA T CO NDITIONS F OR A NNEXATION
REQUIRED BY WYO. STAT.§15-1-402 EXIST F OR THE PR OPERTY DESCRIBED AS A
PORTION O F SEC TIONS 1 2 A ND 1 3, T. 1 3N., R. 67W., O F TH E 6  P. M ., L ARAMIETH
COUNTY, W Y (GE NERALLY L OCATED E AST OF  SOUT HWEST DR IVE, SOUT H OF
INTERSTATE 80, WEST OF BNSF RAILROAD, AND NORTH OF WOODENSHOE ROAD,
INCLUDING CHEYENNE ANIMAL SHELTER AND ASSOCIATED RIGHTS-OF-WAY)” --
referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor - Ms. Ash).
PRELIMINARY PLATS/PRELIMINARY ZONE CHANGE:
Preliminary Plat for Woodhaven Subdivision, a replat of Lots 1 and 2, Block One, Farson
Addition and all of Block One, Dry Creek Twin Homes, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located east of and
adjacent t o W ills Ro ad, so uth o f t he Dry Creek C hannel an d Parkv iew Drive.  May or K aysen
advised the item was being withdrawn from the agenda pursuant to written request of the developer.
LEASES/CONTRACTS/LEGAL:
[CA] Contract b etween th e City of  C heyenne, T ransit D ivision a nd W yoming D epartment of
Health, Aging Division, for supportive services to older and disabled adults (Title III-B Program
Grant) -- referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Memorandum of  U nderstanding b etween the C ity of  C heyenne, P arks &  R ecreation
Department and Department of State Parks and Cultural Resources, Division of State Parks, Historic

at S loans Lake (Parks & Recreation Budget & In-kind labor and equipment use) -- referred to

Finance Committee. 
CHANGE ORDERS/CONTRACT MODIFICATIONS:
[CA] Contract Modification No. 1 to Contract No. 5364 between the City of Cheyenne and S&S
Builders, LLC for additional quantities needed to complete the signal installation at Dell Range and
Marble Avenue (2003-2006 1% Sales Tax).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (amount not to
exceed $2,917.00).  (#5364)
[CA] Contract Modification No. 1 to Contract No. 5477 between the City of Cheyenne and Recco,
Inc. d/b/a Five-R-Co. to lower the power lines to the Transfer Station gas.  Motion (per Consent
Agenda) carried (amount not to exceed $1,496.00).  (#5477)
Contract Modification No. 1 to Contract No. 5045 (Clerk's note:  Correct Contract No. is
5405) between the City of Cheyenne and J-R Engineering, LLC for design services on the 2009 Bus
Stop Upgrades Project (Federal Transit Authority & American Reinvestment and Recovery Act).
Mr. Brown moved to a pprove, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  I t was advised the Mayor's Council for
People with Disabilities had expressed concerns regarding the bus stop locations in proximity to
certain stores.  Upon inquiry, Joe Dougherty, Transit Director, provided information on transit stops
located along certain store areas off Dell Range Blvd.  an d alternatives reviewed to make stops
easier and safer for both buses and passengers to access.  He advised concerns had been raised
regarding moving t he stops o ut t o Dell Range so lo cations were chosen with easier access and
accessibility with minimal walking distance for passengers. Upon inquiry, Laura Page, Engineering
Office, advised minimum ADA standards are being met and that  c omprises were made in some
areas i n lieu o f ha ving t o a cquire r ight-of-way p roperty.  C oncerns w ere e xpressed r egarding
accessibility f rom d esignated l ocations f or th ose individuals w ith d isabilities.  M r. D ougherty
provided i nformation o n b us stop s tandards rel ative t o us er des tination di stances, i ndicating,
although not a perfect situation, locations of the stops are a reasonable accommodation; reviewed
other st op locations involving Frontier Mall and the post o ffice near Co nverse Ave.; discussed
evaluation of bus shelter advertising, if funding for the shelters is available, and stated curb-to-curb
transit services are available as an option for individuals having special needs. Upon inquiry, Ms.
Page reviewed logistics involving the location of the bus shelter near the post office, and clarified
the contract was for an amount not to exceed $29,790.00 (ARRA funding).  Motion carried. Voting
"yes" -- all members of the governing body. (#5045)
Contract M odification N o. 4  t o C ontract No. 4 968 be tween t he C ity o f C heyenne a nd
Wyoming D epartment of  T ransportation f or th e r econstruction of  Pe rshing B lvd f rom I -25 to
Pioneer Avenue (2003-2006 1% Sales Tax).  Mr. Brown moved to approve in an amount not to
exceed $557,013.00, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Upon inquiry, Doug Vetter, City Engineer, explained
the tota l project cost estimate is $6.63 million.  D iscussion included concern with the number of
traffic lanes proposed (2 lanes plus 1 turning lane), objection in the past from residents along the
route relative to loss of trees, and right-of-way issues.  Mr. Vetter advised, following an evaluation,
it had been determined that a 3 lane section of road should handle traffic volumes, and noted the
current absence of a center turn lane has resulted in accidents.  Motion carried.  Voting "yes" -- all
members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Pierson voting "no". (#4968)
[CA] Contract Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 5316 between the City of Cheyenne and J-2
Contracting Co., Inc. for partial release of retention funds, for the David R. Romero South Cheyenne
Community Park Project (1% Specific Purpose Sales & Use Tax) -- referred to Finance Committee.
CONSIDERATION OF BIDS:
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-7-10 for furnishing and installing one new single ram baler and one
new roller chain conveyor from JDM Equipment, LLC of Arvada, CO for the Transfer Station.
Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (amount not to exceed $343,653.00).
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-6-10 for furnishing one new street sweeper with conveyor belt from
Titan Machinery of Cheyenne for the Street & Alley Department (2003-2006 & 2007-2010 1% Sales
Tax) -- referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Consideration of Bid for surplus property from Total Energy Corp., North Salem, NY, for
two large propane storage tanks previously utilized by the Board of Public Utilities -- referred to
Finance Committee. 
[CA] Consideration o f Bi d f or surpl us pro perty f rom Green  Ri ver/Rock Spri ngs/Sweetwater
County - Joint Powers Water Board, (GRRS/JPWB), for an Opto-22 computer control system used
for filter backwash co ntrol at  t he o ld RL Sherard Water Treatment Plant -- referred t o Finance
Committee.
APPLICATIONS:
[CA] Transfer of ownership for a restaurant liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s
Office f or W ei Sh eng Qi u d/b /a Go lden Ho use C hinese R estaurant, 1651 Ca rey A ve., St e. 8,
Cheyenne, WY (License currently held by Yu Zheng d/b/a Golden House Restaurant, 1651 Carey
Ave., Ste. 8, Cheyenne, WY).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
ANNOUNCEMENTS/REPORTS/MOTIONS:
Announcement w as made t hat d ue t o t he Martin Luther King, Jr., holiday on Monday,
January 18, 2010, Finance Committee will meet at 11:00 a.m. and Public Services Committee will
meet at 12:15 p.m. on Tuesday, January 19, 2010, in Council Meeting Room 122; Vouchers meeting
will be held in Council Chambers at Noon.
OTHER CITY BUSINESS:
John Palmer suggested public discussion procedures be reviewed to provide for additional
input after governing body discussions; expressed concern with limited information provided on
meeting a gendas, a nd c ommented th at c ommunity r esidents n eed to h elp w ith f inancial
responsibility r elative t o f ee i ncreases.  Fr ank C ole c oncurred w ith M r. P almer's s tatement
concerning the pub lic di scussion pro cess, an d co mmented a ri ght t urn l ane i s n eeded o n Rue
Terre/Dell Range and that land had previously been donated by the Cole family to the City for that
purpose.  P acomio S andoval expressed h is a greement w ith p rior c omments in volving p ublic
comment at meetings, and suggested outdated laws be reviewed for potential elimination from the
codebook.  Dr. Rinne commented on a consitutent concern he had received regarding City snow
plows clearing snow resulting in blocking driveways and walkways after residents have previously
cleared them pursuant to ordinance requirements.
City Attorney Dan White requested the governing body meet in executive session to discuss
matters involving current and potential future litigation matters.  Mr. Collins moved t o meet in
executive session, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the
governing body.  Mayor Kaysen announced members would meet in executive session in Council
Chambers, n ot o pen t o t he pub lic; reques ted t he C ity Attorney, City Clerk, an d o ther st aff as
requested by the City Attorney, be present at the executive session, and stated there would be no
action taken by the governing body as a result of the executive session, and that the regular City
Council meeting would officially conclude at the close of the executive session.  (Clerk’s Note:
Executive session convened at 9:15 p.m. following a brief recess.)
There be ing no  further bu siness t o c ome be fore the governing bo dy p rior t o executive
session, t he meeting was o fficially a djourned a t 1 0:37 p .m. following c losure o f t he executive
session.
 Submitted by,
 
 
 
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle
 January 22, 2010

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
January 25, 2010
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil C hambers.  Pr esent w ere: M AYOR - Richard L . K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS:  Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Spiker
and Mr. Valdez.  Absent: Ms. Ash.  Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Lois Huff, Deputy
City Treasurer, and Dan White, City Attorney.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA]  are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda.) Upon request by Ms. Broyles, and pursuant to support received by
Mr Brown and Mr. Pierson, agenda item #18(c) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Collins
moved to approve remaining Consent Agenda items, seconded by Mr. Brown.  M otion carried.
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.
[CA] MINUTES FROM REGULAR MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON JANUARY
11, 2010.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
[CA] MINUTES FROM VOUCHERS MEETING OF THE GOVERNING BODY ON JANUARY
19, 2010.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Brown moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Valdez.
Upon i nquiry, Deput y City T reasurer L ois Huf f an d Ci ty Cl erk Caro l In tlekofer r eviewed
information available for a voucher payable to Cheyenne Frontier Days ($100.00), annual payment
for placement of  wireless communication equipment.   Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members
of the governing body present.
“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING ORDINANCE NO. 3860 DEFINING THE TERMS AND
CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT FOR NON-UNIFORMED EMPLOYEES OF THE CITY OF
CHEYENNE.”  E ric H ardgrave, C heyenne P ublic E mployees A ssociation ( CPEA) P resident,
expressed a ppreciation to Council f or l istening t o e mployees’ c oncerns r egarding be nefits a nd
employment issues, and for restoring the longevity pay plan.  Edward Melko expressed concerns
with Council members’ eligibility for City health care coverage, suggested Council members accept
reduced compensation due to budgetary concerns, and commented on assessing recreational fees for
youth programs relative to the recent lease agreement approved for VFW’s Pride Park softball fields.
It was noted that not all Council members participate in the health insurance plan. Claus Johnson,
Parks & Recreation employee, pr ovided co mments o n budget co ncerns, red uction o f employee
benefits, effect o n services pro vided if staffing levels are reduced, an d po tential furloughs.  He
suggested deferral of a scheduled $1,000,000 BOPU payment due to the current budget situation,
and discussed the Salary Task Force Committee’s recent proposal involving a compensation and
staffing level study, employee cost savings suggestions, and equitable compensation to governing
body members relative to employee compensation cuts.  John Palmer, Sanitation Dept. employee,
expressed appreciation for restoring the longevity pay plan; commented on state projections and
budget concerns for the next fiscal year; requested consideration of employee cost savings/efficiency
ideas; expressed that employees are dedicated to serving the City and community, and encouraged
careful review of expenditures.  Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Brown moved to approve
on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Mr. Brown moved to amend Section 7, by
inserting the language “after consulting with City Council leadership,” following the words, “The
Mayor”.  The section would then read “The Mayor, after consulting with City Council leadership,
shall have discretionary authority to declare furlough days, if necessary, due to budget constraints,”
seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Comments followed in opposition to the proposed amendment relative
to Council oversight of the Mayor’s executive administrative authority, as well as comments in
support of the amendment which would provide for communication from the Mayor to Council on
any possible employee furlough days authorized by the Mayor.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting
“yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of Ms. Case, Dr Rinne and
Mr. Valdez voting “no”.  Main motion as amended carried.  V oting “yes” – all members of the
governing body present. (#3880)
“AN ORDINANCE AMENDING ORDINANCE NO. 3861 DEFINING THE TERMS AND
CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT FOR SWORN OFFICERS OF THE CHEYENNE POLICE
DEPARTMENT.”  Mr. Brown moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by M r.
Valdez.  Mr. Brown  moved to amend Section 8, by inserting the language “after consulting with
City Council leadership,” following the words, “The Mayor”.  The section would then read “The
Mayor, after consulting with City Council leadership, shall have discretionary authority to declare
furlough days, if necessary, due to budget constraints,” seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Com ments
followed in opposition to Council overseeing the authority of the Mayor who serves as the City’s
executive b ranch o f go vernment, an d co ncern wi th t he ph rase “City Council l eadership” v s.
members o f t he e ntire C ity C ouncil.  B rief d iscussion followed o n t he p roposed a mendment
providing that notification be received from the Mayor prior to any furlough days being authorized.
Motion to amend carried.  V oting “yes” – all members o f t he governing body present with the
exception of Ms. Case, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Valdez voting “no”.  Main motion as amended carried.
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. (#3881)
“AN OR DINANCE A MENDING SECTION 6.08. 020(B), K EEPING OR
SLAUGHTERING OF CERTAIN ANIMALS – RESTRICTIONS WITHIN CITY, OF CHAPTER
6.08, ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL REGULATIONS GENERALLY, OF TITLE 6,
ANIMALS, AND AMENDING SECTION 6.20.010, DESIGNATION OF ANIMAL SHELTER,
OF CHAPTER 6.20, IMPOUNDMENT, OF TITLE 6, ANIMALS, OF THE CODE OF THE CITY
OF CHEYENNE, WYOMING.” Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Collins moved to
approve on second reading, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members
of the governing body present.
“AN OR DINANCE A MENDING TI TLE 17,  Z ONING, CH APTER 17.08, Z ONING
DISTRICTS E STABLISHED AND SECTION 17.08. 040 CH EYENNE CIT Y M AP OF  T HE
CHEYENNE CITY CODE, BY CHANGING THE ZONING CLASSIFICATION FROM MR-1
MEDIUM DENSITY RESIDENTIAL-ESTABLISHED DISTRICT TO MUB MIXED USE WITH
BUSINESS EMPHASIS DISTRICT FOR LOT 3 AND THE EAST 23-FEET OF LOT 4, BLOCK
3, A LTA-VISTA A DDITION, CH EYENNE, W YOMING ( LOCATED SOUTH OF  A ND
ADJACENT TO E. 17TH STREET, WEST OF CONVERSE AVENUE).”  Mr. Collins moved to
approve on second reading, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members
of the governing body present.
[CA] “A RESOLUTION APPROVING AN AMENDED PROMISSORY NOTE FOR CLEAN
WATER SRF LOAN - 081 BET WEEN THE  ST ATE OF  W YOMING A ND THE  CIT Y OF
CHEYENNE, WYOMING FOR CHEYENNE’S RECYCLE WATER SYSTEM EXTENSION
PROJECT AND AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR, CITY CLERK AND THE DIRECTOR OF THE
BOARD OF PUBLIC UTILITIES TO SIGN THE AMENDED PROMISSORY NOTE” (Water
Enterprise Fund).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.  (#5179)
“A RESOLUTION SUPPORTING THE CITY OF CHEYENNE’S APPLICATION FOR
A LAND AND WATER CONSERVATION FUND GRANT FOR THE SADDLE RIDGE PARK
PICNIC SHELTER PROJECT” (Community Facility Fees & In-kind labor).  Mr. Brown moved to
adopt, seco nded by Mr.  Valdez.  Mr.  Br own moved to amend by substitute, seco nded by Ms.
Broyles. It was c larified t he s ubstitute a uthorizes t he M ayor a nd o ther d esignees t o s ign t he
application and the Mayor to execute the grant agreement if the agreement is approved.  Motion to
amend ca rried.  Vo ting “ yes” – al l m embers o f t he go verning b ody prese nt.  M ain m otion as
amended by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.  (#5180)
“A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND THE CITY CLERK TO SIGN
A COUNTY FINAL PLAT FOR FRONTIER EAST, 1  FILING, A PORTION OF THE NW¼ OFST
SECTION 4, T. 13N., R. 66W., OF THE 6  P.M., LARAMIE COUNTY, WYOMING (LOCATEDTH
SOUTH OF AND ADJACENT TO CAMPSTOOL ROAD, EAST OF MORRIE AVENUE).”  John
Steil, Steil Surveying Services, agent for applicant Frontier Refining, requested a revised map that
had be en s ubmitted be  a cknowledged a s a  s ubstitute m ap.  Ke vin B urke, V ice-President a nd
Refinery Manager, advised Frontier is not planning to apply for annexation at this time but Frontier,
as indicated in a letter to the City, is willing to further discuss the topic and surrounding issues.  He
commented on the company’s support and involvement (mutual aid) with the county Fire District
and industrial wat er r ates r eceived from th e B oard of  P ublic U tilities, a nd a dvised th at b y n ot
annexing at this time, Frontier does not believe it is hindering the City’s growth in the area.  Jeff
Ketcham, L aramie C ounty C ommissioner, a dvised t hat C ounty C ommissioners u nanimously
supported the proposed County Final Plat, as did the County Planning Commission and the City
Planning Commission.  He noted the staff report indicated there were no comments from City Police
or Fire Depts. pursuant to the proposed plat and potential impact to City services, and encouraged
members of the governing body to review the minutes from the City Planning Commission meeting.
Paula Qualls, Board member, South Cheyenne Community Development Assoc., and member of
the County Planning Commission, spoke in support of the plat, and in opposition to annexation.
Larry Wolfe, Holland & Hart law firm, attorneys for Frontier Refining, spoke in support of the plat
and clarified the item before the governing body pertains to approval of the plat involving an 11 acre
parcel to be utilized for storage and parking.  He stated further conversations could be engaged in
between the City and Frontier regarding annexation issues and effects.  Mr. Collins moved to adopt,
seconded by Mr. Brown.  Mr. Collins moved to amend by including the substitute map, seconded
by Dr. Rinne.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.
Discussion followed on support for Frontier Refining and the proposed plat; Urban Planning staff’s
recommendation to not approve the plat and reasons for the recommendation; concerns with lack
of g rowth a reas for t he C ity, a nd p otential discussions w ith F rontier R efining involving future
annexation.  Main motion as amended by substitute map carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the
governing body present.  (#5181)
“A RESOLU TION DE TERMINING THA T CO NDITIONS F OR A NNEXATION
REQUIRED BY WYO. STAT.§15-1-402 EXIST F OR THE PR OPERTY DESCRIBED AS A
PORTION O F SEC TIONS 1 2 A ND 1 3, T. 13N., R . 6 7W., O F TH E 6  P. M ., L ARAMIETH
COUNTY, W Y (GE NERALLY L OCATED EAST OF  SOUT HWEST DR IVE, SOUT H OF
INTERSTATE 80, WEST OF BNSF RAILROAD, AND NORTH OF WOODENSHOE ROAD,
INCLUDING CHEYENNE ANIMAL SHELTER AND ASSOCIATED RIG HTS-OF-WAY).”
Brad Emmons, AVI, agent for the applicants, advised pursuant to a request for i nformation
concerning contiguity made at Public Services Committee, he had submitted an exhibit regarding
this for Council’s r eview.  J ohn P almer, q uestioned w hether th ere w ere a ny legal ob jections to
annexation of the property.  Upon inquiry, Dan White, City Attorney, stated he does not know of
any area landowners’ intentions if opposed to the annexation.  Donn Edmunds questioned access
points to the area.  M r. Collins reported there was no recommendation on the item from Public
Services Committee.  Mr. Collins moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Brown. It was noted that the
property owners requested annexation.  Discussion included potential future access to the area by
the developer and, upon inquiry, Gay Woodhouse, attorney representing individuals who live on
Southwest Dri ve, adv ised t hey are co ncerned about acc ess areas  an d are rel ying o n prev ious
information provided, during comments at prior meetings, involving issues that would be reviewed
during the development and platting process. She stated litigation is still ongoing over a previous
matter relative to annexation of Southwest Drive.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of
the governing body present with the exception of Ms. Case and Mr. Valdez voting “no”.  (#5182)
“A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO OFFER FINANCIAL INCENTIVES
TO INDUCE CERTAIN ELIGIBLE EMPLOYEES TO RETIRE FROM CITY SERVICE DURING
FISCAL YEAR 2009-2010” (sponsors - Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson and Mr. Spiker) -- referred to
Finance Committee.  Mr. Brown advised the item was discussed under other items for the agenda at
Finance Committee and provisions of Title 2, City Code, had been met.  Mr. Brown moved to adopt,
seconded by  M r. C ollins.  E ric H ardgrave, Cheyenne P ublic E mployees As sociation ( CPEA)
President, e xpressed a ppreciation f or the i ncentive p ackage b eing p roposed to h elp r educe or
potentially e liminate t he need for furloughs, a nd r equested t hat furloughs be u tilized before a ny
employee lay-offs are considered.  Edward Melko spoke in opposition to use of the sanitation fund
(i.e. Solid waste management fund) as the funding source for the retirement incentives, expressing
his reasons for disagreement with the funding source, and questioned the amount of City reserves.
Questions f ollowed regardi ng appro priate us es o f t he s olid was te f und.  Up on i nquiry, Vi cki
Nemecek, Asst. Public Works Director, provided information on the resolution establishing the solid
waste fund, use of the funds, and current fund balance ($8.8 million).  She advised $2.9 million was
expended for t he B elvoir Ran ch, an d t hat t he B elvoir co uld po tentially b e t he n ew landfill s ite.
Public Works Director Jim Elias advised staff is working on an overall solid waste management plan
and is moving through the process to propose options for a new landfill site, which may or may not
be located on the Belvoir.  Upon inquiry on whether the money to be taken from the fund must be
paid back if a landfill is not placed on the Belvoir, Dan White, City Attorney, opined his belief that
the governing body can determine where to move funds within the budget, and that a b udget re-
appropriation as prepared b y the City Treasurer would reflect proposed changes to budget areas
pursuant to the Mayor’s reduction measures, the employee ordinances approved earlier in the meeting
that will involve changes to the budget, and whatever action is taken on the funding for the retirement
incentives.  He stated that without having specifically researched the subject, he is unaware of any
external statutory controls concerning the transfer of funds within the budget.  Upon further inquiry,
Ms. Nemecek briefly reviewed the environmental monitoring contract for the Happy Jack landfill
site.  D uring comments, Mr. Brown raised a point of order with Mayor Kaysen ruling comments
should rem ain germ ane t o t he s ubject o f t he res olution.  Di scussion f ollowed a nd i ncluded
information from Ms. Nemecek on expenses associated with the hauling of solid waste to Ault, CO
and proposed plans to increase the fund amount.  Topics discussed included:  Opposition to using
money set aside in the solid waste fund for retirement incentives; moving of funds to another account;
whether the funds utilized would be repaid to the fund; using solid waste fund monies for paying
retirement e xpenses; o ne-time funding; current budget c oncerns involving reduced r evenues a nd
probable less funding to be received through action of the state legislature; the need to reduce City
costs, and overall support for the employee voluntary early retirement incentives.  Dr. Rinne moved
to amend by changing t he source of funding from t he solid waste fund t o general fund reserves,
seconded by Mr. Collins.  Mr. Melko commented that the proposed amendment is a more acceptable
fund t o use, and John Palmer questioned borrowing t he money with t he intent of paying it back
instead o f j ust re- appropriating i t.  Upo n i nquiry, Deput y City T reasurer L ois Huf f adv ised an
estimated 30 day reserve amount is $4.2  m illion, and that t he City’s un-designated reserves are
currently at $4.4 million; designated and un-designated amount is $7.4 million.  Comments followed
on concerns with using unencumbered reserves when it is for emergency purposes, and borrowing
(loaning) the monies from the solid waste fund and replenishing it in the future.  Motion to amend
failed. Voting “yes” – Ms. Case, Mr. Collins and Dr. Rinne.  Voting “no” – Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles,
Mr. Pierson, Mr. Spiker, Mr. Valdez and Mayor Kaysen.  Upon inquiry, Human Resources Director
Rich Wiederspahn clarified an individual that retires under the state retirement system can be rehired
by the same employer in the future, however, there is a penalty to the employer as it must repay the
retiree’s share in full back into the system, which would affect the budget.  Motion carried.  Voting
“yes” - all members of the governing body present. (#5183)
[CA] “A RESOLUTION DE TERMINING THA T CO NDITIONS F OR A NNEXATION
REQUIRED BY WYO. STAT. §15-1-402 EXIST F OR THE PR OPERTY DESCRIBED AS A
PARCEL OF LAND BEING SITUATED IN THE SW¼ NW ¼ OF SECTION 21, T. 14N.,  R. 66W.,
OF THE 6  P.M., LARAMIE COUNTY, WY (LOCATED SOUTH OF  PLAIN VIEW ROAD,TH
WEST OF POINT BLUFF, AND NORTH OF APACHE STREET)” -- referred to Public Services
Committee (sponsor - Ms. Ash).
LEASES/CONTRACTS/LEGAL:
[CA] Contract b etween th e C ity of  C heyenne, T ransit D ivision a nd W yoming D epartment of
Health, Aging Division, for supportive services to older and disabled adults (Title III-B Program
Grant).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.  (#5499)
[CA] Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Cheyenne, Parks &  Re creation

Sites and Trails, for a Motorboat Gas Tax Grant for fence/handrail along boat launch and promenade
at Sloans L ake (Par ks & Recreation Budge t &  In -kind labor an d equipment us e). M otion (per

Beverage Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Parks & Recreation Department and

and, after relinquishing duties of the chair to Council President Broyles, vacated Council Chambers.
Mr. Brown moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members
of the governing body present in Council Chambers.  Following announcement of the vote, Council

(#5501)
[CA] Professional Services Contract between the City of Cheyenne and Wyoming Travel a nd

Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5502)
[CA] Contract between the City of Cheyenne, Office of Youth Alternatives and State of Wyoming,

services.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5503) 
[CA] Program Funding Agreement between t he City o f Cheyenne, T ransit Division and United
Way of Laramie County for Bus Token Assistance for low to moderate income. Motion (per Consent
Agenda) carried. (#5504)
  
[CA] Contract between the City of Cheyenne, Office of Youth Alternatives and Laramie County
Community Partnership, Inc. to provide a range of academic and other enrichment activities to at risk
school age youth at  Johnson Jr. High -- referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Professional S ervices Agreement b etween th e City of Cheyenne a nd TriHydro C orp. for
environmental m onitoring at  Happy  J ack L andfill (S olid W aste F und) - - r eferred to F inance
Committee.
[CA] Cooperative A greement b etween th e C ity of  C heyenne a nd W yoming Department of
Transportation for Cheyenne Marginal-Vandehei Interchange (2007-2010 1% Sales Tax) -- referred
to Finance Committee. 
CHANGE ORDERS/CONTRACT MODIFICATIONS:
[CA] Contract Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 5316 between the City of Cheyenne and J-2
Contracting Co., Inc. for partial release of retention funds, for the David R. Romero South Cheyenne
