RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
February 22, 2010
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil Chambers.  P resent w ere: M AYOR -  R ichard L.  K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS: Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr.
Spiker and Mr. Valdez.  Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Barb Dorr, City Treasurer, and
Dan White, City Attorney.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA]  are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda.)  Upon request by Dr. Rinne, and pursuant to support received by
Ms. Ash and Mr. Collins, agenda item #13 was removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon request
by Ms. Ash, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Rinne and Ms. Broyles, agenda item #16(c)
was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Brown moved to approve remaining Consent Agenda
items, seconded by Mr. Spiker. Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on February 8, 2010.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
[CA] Minutes from Vouchers Meeting of the Governing Body on February 16, 2010.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Spiker moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Brown.
Upon inquiry regarding a voucher payable to AVI, City Engineer Doug Vetter briefly reviewed the
status of the Henderson Basin project, stating there is some remaining work for remapping of the
flood plain prior to the project being completed.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of
the governing body.
Mayor Kaysen opened a public hearing for the purpose of receiving comments and input for
renewal of  e xisting City Liquor Licenses ( retail, re staurant, lim ited r etail, resort, b ar a nd g rill
licenses, and microbrewery and winery permits) filed with the City Clerk’s Office.  City Clerk Carol
Intlekofer noted for the record that one restaurant liquor licensee (Lucky 7) did not file for renewal,
and reviewed the parked license status for applicants C.B. & Potts, Hitching Post and On the Border.
She advised On the Border had submitted a written request for an additional one year extension, as
authorized by Wyo. Statute, to become operational, and stated that the Mayflower was temporarily
closed for  remode ling pur poses.  Chris Cantwell , Director of Ope rations for O n The B order
restaurant pro ject, reviewed the current status the projec t and explained, if the re quest for the
additional year is approved, it is anticipated building construction will be completed in Oct. 2010.
Upon inquiry, Captain J eff Schulz, I nterim Police Chief, re viewed underage compliance checks
recently conducted, responded to inquiry concerning non-compliance of TIPS training records, and
indicated he would provide underage compliance results pursuant to checks conducted last fall.
There being no further comments or input and purpose of the public hearing having been met,
Mayor Kaysen closed the hearing and referred the applications to Finance Committee.
“Ordinance annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, a parcel of land being situated in
Sections 12 and 13, Township 13 North, Range 67 West of the 6  Principal Meridian, Laramieth
County, Wyoming (located east of Southwest Drive, south of Interstate 80, west of BNSF Railroad,
and north of Woodenshoe  Drive) .” Donn Edmunds questioned w hether any  studies had bee n
conducted regarding accessibility to the site, expressing concerns with traffic delays and the railroad
crossing in the area.  Gay Woodhouse, Woodhouse Roden LLC law firm, attorney representing area
home owners, requested a postponement to fur ther review impact issues involving the proposed
annexation and a Southwest Drive  Transpor tation Draina ge and U tility repor t that had bee n
prepared. She cited previous postponements requested by and approved for the developer for the
project, submitted a handout (on file with office of City Clerk) noting the prior postponement dates,
and requested equal consideration pursua nt to her client’s r equest for postponement.  Kathlee n
Sheehan, property owner near the proposed annexation area, requested a six month postponement
to allow time to re-e valuate he r prope rty situation and review  the re port.  Ken Clar k,
applicant/developer, pro vided in formation o n th e dr ainage report, n oting it w as ma iled to  Ms.
Sheehan in Aug. 2009, with Ms. Sheehan responding she did not receive the report.  Reporting for
Public Services Committee, Ms. Ash moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Collins.
Ms. Ash moved to postpone for one month (to March 22, 2010), seconded by Mr. Collins.  Upon
inquiry, City Clerk Carol Intlekofer advised a one month postponement would be to March 22 , atnd
which time the item would be referred back to Public Services Committee for review.  Discussion
followed and included the following topics: Annexation request by the property owner, state statute
annexation criteria and g overning body’s role in dete rmining whether criteria is met, and wha t
would be accomplished within a 30 day postponement relative to the annexation action vs. other
issues involving site plan/platting discussions.  Upon inquiry, Ms. Woodhouse reiterated the request
for postponement is to provide conce rned area property owners the same c ourtesy afforded Mr.
Clark (i.e. pr evious postponement re quests approved) to allow additio nal time to further r eview
documents.  Ms. Case moved to amend the motion to postpone from one month to three  months,
seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Mike Basom, Dray, Thomson, Dyekman law firm, attorney representing
Mr. Clark, spoke in opposition to the motion to postpone and stated the issues of concern that have
been raised regarding access, transportation, utility, and drainage should be discussed during the
platting process.  Speaking in favor of postponement and against the annexation generally were Ms.
Sheehan and Doris Garcia, citing personal impact to property owners in the area if the annexation
and proposed development of the area as proceeds and expressing concerns with health, safety and
welfare of residents, and future residents, in the area.  Comments followed on the time frame (one
month increments) a nd purpose of past postponement reque sts made by  and appr oved for  the
developer, and included statements in support of the motion to postponement by Ms. Sheehan and
Ms. Woodhouse.  Motion to postpone for thre e months failed. Voting “yes” – Ms. Case and Mr.
Valdez.  Voting “no” – Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr.
Spiker and May or Kaysen. Discussion con tinued on the f ormer Swan Ranch a nnexation action
recently approved that involved similar concerns with access and traffic, and information obtained
from Mr. Clark on his hesitancy to move forward with the expense of having an engineering report
prepared to address issues of concern involving access, traffic, and drainage topics without knowing
whether the annexation request will be approved.  Motion to postpone for one month (to March 22,
2010) carried.  V oting “yes” – Ms. B royles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Dr . Rinne, Mr. Va ldez and
Mayor Kaysen. Voting “no” – Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Mr. Pierson and Mr. Spiker.
“Ordinance creating Chapter 8.68, Vacant and Abandoned Residential Structures, of Title
8, Health and Safety , of the Code of  the City  of Cheyenne, Wyoming.” Ian Cattalier, State of
Wyoming, Construction Mana gement, question ed the effect the ordinanc e may have on va cant
properties the State rec ently purcha sed (ne ar Saf eway store off  Pioneer Ave .); the aba ndoned
property definition, and the time fr ame for payment according to the fee structure for abandoned
properties.  Upon inquiry, Dan White, City Attorney, reviewed the basic aspects and provisions of
the ordinance in response to Mr. Cattalier’s inquiry.  Frank Cole, developer, spoke in opposition to
ordinance provisions involving specific requirements on boarding up the structure s, and stated a
better definition of “utilities” vs. provided “services” should be provided.  Steven Miller spoke in
favor of the ordinance and in support of holding property owners accountable, cleaning up blighted
and a bandoned r esidential pr operties, a nd e ffect on  the  ne ighborhood pr operty va lues.  Jea nie
Tucker questioned whether there was any protection for abandoned homes located in a designated
historic district and the fees to be assessed and also read a statement from Jan Nelson Schroll in
support of preserving and promoting neighborhoods and registering abandoned houses. Reporting
for Finance Committee, Mr. B rown stated the re was no re commendation on the item fr om the
committee.  Ms. Ash moved to appr ove on second reading, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Dr. Rinne
moved to amend Section 8.68.070 B.1. and B.2. to delete the language following the word “secured”
as follows: B.1. “ by the use of Phillip s head two-inch screws” and B.2. “by the use of 16 pe nny
common nails”, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all members
of the governing body.  U pon inquiry regarding #6 in S ection 8.68.040, Mr. White advised this
wording was included to obtain information regarding plans or reasons why a particular structure
has bee n abandone d, and Of ficer Emmett L usher, Code Enf orcement, Ch eyenne Poli ce D ept.,
advised any information that can be utilized to quickly assist in identifying property ownership is
useful in abating properties.  Officer Lusher also advised it is important to board up properties to
protect them from crime and illegal activities, indicating every City Ward has issues with abandoned
properties.  Comments followed reg arding the diffe rence between utilities and service s.  Upon
inquiry, Mr. White advised the  International Property Maintenance Code (IPMC) only applies to
dangerous or  unsafe  structure s that are  capa ble of collapse, and structur es unfit for huma n
occupancy and explained it is unlawful to sell property that is in violation of the IPMC unless the
new owner acknowledges and agrees to be res ponsible for violations.  Upon furthe r inquiry, Mr.
White advised the ordinance supplements the IPMC, provides a financial incentive to p roperty
owners to maintain their proper ties, provides funds to assist with monit oring the prope rties by
building officials and police , and plac es restrictions on the building to allow f or an inspec tion
process.  Discussion followed on the purpose of the ordinance and possible future similar ordinance
to ad dress abandoned commercial buildings.  U pon inquiry regarding the $250 fee, Mr. White
clarified once the abandoned building is registered and the fee paid, the building official would have
a list of abandoned/vacated properties for the police and building official to monitor.  Upon inquiry,
Mayor Kaysen advised the authority to monitor ordinance pr ovisions would fall un der the Chief
Building Official’s area with enforcement through Nuisance Control and/or Police Dept.  Discussion
continued on other potential changes to ordinance wording, compliance time frame and penalty
provisions.  Mr. Cole provided further comments on the difference between  utilities and services.
Upon inquiry regarding issuance of misdemeanor citations, Mr. White reviewed the role of the Chief
Building Official and police department relative to issuance of citations.  Comments followed on
uninhabitable structures, similar legislation for abandoned commercial structures, and the terms
“utility” vs. “services”.  Motion to approve as amended on second reading carried.  Voting “yes”
– all members of the governing body.
“An Ordinance annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, a parcel of land being situated
in the SW ¼ NW¼ of Section 21, T. 14N., R .66W., of the 6  P.M., Laramie County, Wyomingth
(located south of Plain View Road, west of Point Bluff, and north of Apache Street) -- referred to
Public Services Committee (sponsor - Ms. Ash).
[CA] “Resolution certifying that the Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne is in agreement with
the Laramie County Board of Commissioners as to the current countywide Consensus Block Grant
application to t he State L oan and I nvestment Boa rd.” Motion (pe r Consent Ag enda) car ried.
(#5185)
“Resolution authorizing the transfer of funds in the approximate amount of $145,000 from
the City’s self-funded employee health benefit plan to the general fund.”  Mr . Brown moved to
adopt, seconded by Mr. Spiker.   Dr. Rinne moved to amend the  6th Whereas pa ragraph and the
Now, The refore, B e It Resol ved paragraph to delete the f ollowing language at the e nd of the
sentences: “to re duce the  number of pote ntial u npaid employee f urlough day s which may  be
imposed due to current budgetary concerns and conditions,” seconded by Mr. Collins.  Comments
followed on the purpose of the proposed amendment, which is to utilize the dollars toward funding
of job s in  lie u o f a ny po tential r eduction in  e mployee fo rce measures in stead o f s pecifically
referencing unpaid employee furlough days.  Mayor Kaysen stated the monies are a one-time lump
sum amount and not an ongoing revenue source, and that the intent of the resolution is to hopefully
defer/reduce the need for furlough days.  Upon inquiry, City Treasurer Barb Dorr confirmed the
money is a one-time infusion of money.  Brief discussion followed on the purpose of the proposed
amendment, and time frame of funding transfer (current or next fiscal year).  Motion to amend
failed.  Voting “yes” – Ms. Ash and Dr. Rinne.  Voting “no” – Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case,
Mr. Collins, M r. Pierson, Mr. Spiker, Mr. V aldez and May or Kaysen.  Discussion followed on
possible unpaid employee furlough days, concern with protection of employee jobs, retaining the
funding relative to re-implementation of a possible future self-funded program as a health insurance
option, and fiscal responsibility.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” –  Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr.
Collins, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Spiker, Mr. Valdez and Mayor Kaysen. Voting “no” - Ms. Ash, Ms. Case
and Dr. Rinne.  (#5186)
[CA] “Resolution re-appropriating the Fiscal Year 2010 budget of the City of Cheyenne according
to the provisions of W.S. §16-4-112 and §16-4-113” -- referred to Finance Committee (sponsors -
Mr. Brown and Mr. Spiker).
[CA] “Resolution designating the Chey enne Animal Shelter, 800 Southwest Drive, Chey enne,

donate to BOPU a private water and sanitary sewer system that runs through the Swan Ranch Rail

Board of Public Utilities (BOPU), and Cheyenne Frontier Days, to outline responsibilities for the
operation and maintenance of the sanitary waste station at Lake Absarraca -- referred to Finance
Committee. 
[CA] Consideration of FAA Grant No. 3-56-0005-45 between the City of Cheyenne, County of
Laramie, and the Cheyenne Regional Airport Board for the Rehabilitation of Taxiways A3 and B2 --
referred to Finance Committee. 
[CA] Amendment No. 4 to State Lease Agreement No. 8-09466 between the City of Cheyenne and
State of Wyoming for parking spaces in the Cox Parking Facility -- referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-8-10 for the Surplus Sale of “Two 1993 Toro Greens Aerators”
from the City of Cheyenne Golf Department.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (Mountain Vista
Greens, Ft. Collins, CO (one aerator), revenue to City  $1,200.00).
[CA] Consideration of Bid #M-13-10 for a contract between S&S Builders, of Cheyenne, WY, and
the City of Cheyenne for the Randa ll Bridge Enhancements Project (2007-2010 1% Sales Tax).
Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (rejected all bids).
Under other City  business:  J ohn Palmer expressed c oncerns with the g overning body’s
public participation process, commented on a recent editorial in the local newspaper written by a
member of City Council, and the city’s budget condition and costs associated with city services and
maintenance areas.  Joe E lkins, BC Cab, local business owner, expressed concerns with public
transport taxicab companies operating in violation of state law, referencing City Code provisions,
and lack of enforcement for the violations, which would provide revenue to the City to assist with
its financial situation.  Pacomio Sandoval also expressed co ncerns with the public participa tion
process at City Council meetings and with budget concerns and expenses, specifically referencing
the City ’s pas t Taco John’s Events Center  and B elvoir Ranch pur chases.  Donn Edmunds
commented on the budget situation and referenced a community in Colorado that is experiencing
the financial inability to provide support services involving urban growth (annexation) areas, and
urged the governing body to carefully consider housing development growth/annexation approval
actions in conjunction with the City’s financial ability to support affiliated services.
Mr. Collins made statements expressing his opinion regarding a recent executive session of
the governing body and allowable discussion topics.
City Attorney Dan White requested the governing body meet in executive session concerning
a pleading/filing involving litigation.  Ms. Broyles moved to meet in executive session, seconded
by Mr. Pierson.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  Mayor Kaysen
announced members would meet in executive session in Council Chambers, not open to the public;
requested the City Attorney, City Clerk, and other staff as requested by the City Attorney, be present
at the executive session, and stated there would be no action taken by the governing body as a result
of the executive session, and that the regular City Council meeting would officially conclude at the
close of the executive session.  (Clerk’s Note: Executive session convened at 8:16 p.m.)
There being  no further  busine ss to come be fore the g overning body prior to executive
session, the meeting was officially adjourned at 8:34 p.m. following closure of the executive session.
 
 Submitted by,
 
 
 
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle
 March 4, 2010

upcoming p oker e vents.  C omments f ollowed r egarding g ames being c onducted th at a re n ot
following the City’s recently enacted ordinance.  Upon inquiry, City Clerk Carol Intlekofer clarified
one permit had been issued since the ordinance went into effect and when individuals apply for a
tournament-style poker event permit in addition to the application form, they are also given a copy
of the ordinance and affiliated administrative guidelines. Comments continued on the administrative
guidelines.  Upon inquiry, City Attorney Dan White advised he would proceed with adopting the
administrative g uidelines u nder p rovisions o f t he Wy oming Ad ministrative P rocedure Ac t a nd
would communicate with Police Kozak to discuss the means of distribution of information to those
who may be affected.
Mr. Valdez commented on complaints he had received regarding pot holes throughout town.
Upon inquiry, Jim Elias, Public Works Director, advised the formation of pot holes are an on-going
problem, exacerbated this winter by freezing/thawing conditions. He requested citizens report pot
holes requiring repair through the on-line (City’s website) Request Partner reporting system or by

There b eing n o f urther b usiness t o come b efore t he go verning b ody, t he m eeting was

“An Ordinance amending Title 17, Zoning, Chapter 17.08, Zoning Districts Established and

(#3886)

financial burden annexation may cause her.  Ms. Woodhouse advised she has been meeting with her
clients as well as conducting other research during the most recent postponement time frame.  Ken
Clark, Gar rett Proper ties, develope r, advised h e started mee ting with landowne rs last summer
regarding the  pr oposed a nnexation a nd de velopment p roject to address i ssues, a nd sp oke in
opposition to postponement.  Comments followed regarding previously raised concerns with area
traffic, drainage, water and sewer, etc., which issues may not be able to be  completely addressed
until the platting process is started (i.e. after annexation), and cost to the developer to proceed with
the platting design process without knowing whether the annexation will be approved. Upon inquiry
regarding the inclusion of Woodenshoe Drive in the annexation area, Matt Ashby, Planning Services
Director, advised the key to including Woodenshoe Drive involves a long standing policy that has
been developed to assist with mitigating development impact on adjacent rights-of-way.  He noted
if changes were to be made to the annexation map by removing Woodenshoe Drive, “402 criteria”
would need to be re-evaluated.  Upon inquiry regarding measures taken to resolve Ms. Sheehan’s
concerns, Mr. Clark advised he has met with Ms. Sheehan and told her they would work with her
and others as the deve lopment moves forward during the plattin g process to seek solutions. M r.
Valdez moved to postpone for one month, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Motion to postpone failed.
Voting “yes” – Mr. Valdez.  Voting “no” –  Ms. Ash, Mr . Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Mr.
Pierson, Dr. Rin ne, Mr. Spiker and  Mayor Kaysen.  Ma in motion carried.  Vo ting “yes” – a ll
members of the governing body present with the exception of Mr. Valdez voting “no”.
“An Ordinance amending Title 17, Zoning, Chapter 17.08, Zoning Districts Established and
Section 17.08.040 C heyenne City  map of the Chey enne City  Code, by  chang ing the  zoning
classification from PUD Planned Unit Development District to MR-2 Medium Density Residential-

Drive, be tween the  Dry Creek  Channel and McCann A venue)” --  ref erred to Public Services

“A Resolution amending Resolution #4859 due to a shortfall in projected collection of the
Optional One Percent Sales Tax for calendar years 2007 through 2010.”  Mr. Brown moved to adopt,
seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Upon inquiry, Vicki Nemecek, Public Works Dept., provided information
on reduced level of funding percentages for certain areas and agencies affected, and clarified the
dollar amount proposed to be reduced for economic development.  Discussion followed on reduced
funding for economic development purposes; funding for the City’s LEADS membership, and other
available funding to assist with possible infrastructure requirements related to businesses that may
be intere sted in building in Chey enne.  Ms. Ne mecek provided in formation on infrastruc ture
development funding and explained the difference between budget line items for infr astructure
development vs. economic development and allowable use of each fund.  Concern was voiced with
reducing the funding level for economic development.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members
of the governing body present. (#5199)
“A Resolution authorizing the transfer of funds in the approximate amount of $400,000.00
from the City’s Solid Waste Management Fund to the General Fund.” Eric Hardgrave, Cheyenne
Public Employees Association (CPEA) President, spoke in favor of the resolution and intent of the
resolution.  Mr. Brown moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Concerns were expressed that
transferring the funds into the general fund at this time may be premature based on the current fiscal
year (FY) 2010 budget and upcoming discussion on the FY2011 budget to be held at a Council work
session scheduled for April 22.  Mr. Brown moved to postpone for two weeks (to April 26, 2010)
to allow for discussion to be he ld involving the resolution at the Counci l’s budget work session,
seconded by Mr. Collins.  U pon inquiry, City Treasurer Barb Dorr stated, based upon the last
analysis of the current budget, it appears revenues and expenditures may balance out for the FY2010
budget but it is not absolutely certain yet whether the funds may be needed for the current fiscal
year, noting the f unds, or a  portion thereof, may be needed to balance next year’s budget which
currently reflects a $1.4 million shortfall.  Discussion followed and included the following topics:
Governing body’s fiscal responsibility, postponement of the resolution to allow for information on
next year’s budget to be received at the work session, intent of the resolution, which is to eliminate
possible employee furlough days for the remainder of the current budget year, need to utilize the
funding for either the current and/or next fiscal year, and suggested use of City reserves vs. funds
from the Solid Waste Management fund. Ms. Dorr clarified the $400,000.00 will be included in
discussion at the Council’s budg et work se ssion with May or Kaysen providing  additional
information of funding topics that will be discussed at the work session.  Discussion continued.  Ms.
Dorr provided additional information regarding level of revenues being received and, upon inquiry,
advised the estimated level of City reserves at the end of FY2010, if revenues and expenditures are
even, is $6.75 million of which $4.4 million is available for use (less than a 30 day reserve) with the
remaining funds being encumbered.  Motion to postpone carried.  Voting “yes” – Mr. Brown, Ms.
Broyles, Mr. Collins, Mr. S piker and Mayor Kaysen.  Voting  “no” – Ms. Ash, Mr . Pierson, Dr.
Rinne and Mr. Valdez.
“A Resolution amending Resolution No. 2852 establishing a payment schedule for Stage II
of the  Che yenne Wat er P roject.”  Ed  Str ader s poke in favor o f t he re solution wh ich w ould
temporarily suspend the City’s annual payment to the Board of Public Utilities (BOPU).  Er ic
Hardgrave, CPEA President, spoke in favor of the resolution explaining suspension of the payment
will help save employee jobs.  Mr. Brown moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Comments
followed on the upcoming Council work session to discuss the FY2011 budget.  Mr. Brown moved
to postpone for two weeks (to April 26, 2010), seconded by Mr Collins.  Mr. Hardgrave stated the
resolution, relative to the $1.4 milli on shortfall as previously identified by the City Treasurer for
next y ear’s budg et, is a key  component in balanc ing the  budg et. Comments followed on the
governing body’s fiscal responsibility, public perception on deferring the City’s annual payment to
the BOPU and indebtedness to future Council members, postponement to allow for information to
be received during the upcoming budget work session, and informal comments being made that are
causing fear to employ ees relative to fina ncial circumstances if the  City does make  the annua l
payment.  Motion to postpone carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present
with the exception of Ms. Ash voting “no”.

body present.  Main motion as amended by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the

“A Resolution prioritizing the City of Cheyenne's three grant applications to the State Loan

O’Neil Avenue,  on April 26, 2010 at 6:00 p.m. for the City  of Chey enne Compre hensive

of Cheyenne Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) entitlement.
Announcement was made  of the a ppointment of Edwar d F. Murr ay, III to the Chey enne
Downtown Development Authority Board, to be confirmed April 26, 2010.                                   
     
Announcement was made of the reappointment of John Parks to the International Fire Code
Board of Appeals and Mona Pearl to the Cheyenne-Laramie County Economic Development Joint
Powers Board, to be confirmed April 26, 2010.
Under other business, Mr. Collins congratulated Ms. Ash for recently acquiring her masters
degree in Public Administration from the University of Wyoming.
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting  was
officially adjourned at 7:43 p.m. 
 
 Submitted by,
 
 
 
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC

MEETING: City Council | DATE: 2010-04-26 | CLIP_ID: 150 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 150

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
April 26, 2010
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil Chambers.  P resent w ere: M AYOR -  R ichard L.  K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS: Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Spiker
and Mr. Valdez.  Absent:  Ms. Case.  Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Barb Dorr, City
Treasurer, and Dan White, City Attorney.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA]  are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda.)  Upon request by Mr. Brown, and pursuant to support received by
Mr. Collins and Ms. Ash, ag enda item #16 wa s removed f rom the Consent Ag enda. Mr. Spiker
moved to approve  remaining Consent Ag enda items, sec onded by Mr. Valde z. Motion carried.
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.
[CA] Minutes from Reg ular Meeting of the Gove rning Body on April 12, 2010.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
[CA] Minutes from Vouchers Meeting of the Governing Body on April 19, 2010.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Brown moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Valdez.
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.
Mayor Kaysen opened a public hearing for the purpose of receiving comments and input for
the City of Cheyenne Comprehensive Consolidated Plan for 2010-2014 and the Annual Action Plan
for Fiscal Year 2010-2011 for the City of Cheyenne Community Development Block Grant (CDBG)
entitlement.  Deanne Widauf, Housing and Community Development Office, provided an overview
of the CDBG entitlement program and the Comprehensive Consolidated Plan, and cited some of the
identified Plan goals and objectives.  She noted the Consolidated Plan also incorporates the Annual
Action Pl an f or fi scal year 2 010-2011 fo r w hich th e City’s e stimated e ntitlement a llocation is
$580,253.00 with an anticipated additional $5,000 in program income.  Ms. Widauf described the
grant application process; public notifications and opportunities for input; oversig ht of the g rant
process by  the Adv isory Council, and the Advisory  Council’s review  and re commendations
involving elig ible applications.  She identi fied proposed re commended pr ojects and pr ogram
administration, and estimated funding allocation amount for each.  Upon inquiry regarding proposed
funding for a Parks and Recreation structural safety and restoration project, Rick Parish, Parks and
Recreation Direc tor, clar ified the proje ct involves re- siding a nd ener gy eff icient window
replacements for the Pioneer Park Activity Center.  Th ere being no further comments or input,
Mayor Kaysen advised the purpose of the hearing had been met and closed the hearing.
Mayor Kaysen welcomed students and their parents in the audience who were attending the
meeting in conjunction with a school project.
“An Ordinance annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, a parcel of land being situated
in Sections 12 and 13, Township 13 North, Range 67 West of the 6  Principal Meridian, Laramieth
County, Wyoming (located East of Southwest Drive, South of Interstate 80, West of BNSF Railroad,
and North of Woodenshoe Drive).”  Francis Shive; Doris Garcia; Ellie Sturman; Leo Garcia; Dave
Wilkinson; Kathleen Sheehan; Gay Woodhouse,  attorney representing residents along Southwest
Drive; D an F rank, F rank L aw O ffice, a ttorney re presenting Ms. Sheehan, a nd Jef f K etcham,
Laramie County Commissioner, spoke in opposition of the proposed annexation.  Among the topics
presented and discussed were:  City/County zoning regulations; health, safety and welfare concerns
involving the volume of train and vehicular traffic and affiliated traffic congestion and delays;
unknown property development plans by the developer; annexation criteria pursuant to Wyo. Stat.
§15-1-402; contiguity concerns relative to annexation of Swan Ranch area; county island creation;
mental a nd fi nancial st ress t o area residents a nd c oncerns in volving fu ture mon etary lia bility
involving infrastructure costs; request to eliminate Woodenshoe Drive  from the annexation area;
timeliness of emergency services response, and suggestion that a “sketch plan” be required to review
developer’s proposed  i nfrastructure, transportation and drainage solutions. Mike Basom, Dray,
Thomson and Dy ekman law  firm, attorne y repr esenting the devel oper, spoke in fa vor of the
annexation to enable the platting process to move forward to address issues raised involving safety
and traffic concerns.  He stated no changes to the area after annexation will be made until a plat is
prepared and approved by the g overning body.  Reporting  for Public Services Committee, Mr.
Collins moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Ms. Ash.  Discussion followed
and included: Area access; traffic and transportation issues; property owner’s (developer) request
for annexation; contiguity; area residents’ concerns that have been raised, and train traffic at the
crossing on Southwest Drive.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body
present with the exception of Mr. Valdez voting “no”. (#3889)
“An Ordinance amending Title 17, Zoning, Chapter 17.08, Zoning Districts Established and
Section 17.08.040 Cheyenne City map of the Cheyenne City Code, by changing the z oning
classification from PUD Planned Unit Development District to MR-2 Medium Density Residential-
Developing District f or L ots 1 through 14 inc lusive of Dry  Creek Twin Homes Subdivi sion,
Cheyenne, Wyoming, to be known as a portion of Woodhaven Subdivision (located west of College
Drive, between the Dry Creek Channel and McCann Avenue).”  Mr. Collins moved to approve on
second r eading, s econded b y M s. A sh.  M r. Sp iker d eclared a  c onflict o f in terest ( distant
relationship with the developer) and vacated Council Chambers.  Concern was expressed with uses
allowed under the MR-2 zone as approved by the Board of Adjustment.  Motion carried.  Voting
“yes” – all members of the governing body present in Council Chambers.  Following announcement
of the vote, Mr. Spiker returned to Council Chambers.
“An Ordinance amending Title 17, Zoning, Chapter 17.08, Zoning Districts Established and
Section 17.08. 040 Chey enne City  map of the Chey enne City  Code, by  chang ing the  zoning
classification from MR-1 Medium Density Residential-Established District to MUB Mixed Use with
Business Emphasis District for Lots 1 and 2; and the north 66-feet of Lots 3 and 4, Block 195,
Original City, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located at the southwest corner of the intersection of E. 23rd
Street and Russell Avenue).” Dr. Stephanie Erlich, homeowner in the area, spoke in favor of the
zone chang e and pr oposed use of the building w ithin the hist oric ne ighborhood.  Rev. Dan
McKinley, SonRise Church of the Nazarene (property owner), requested approval of the ordinance,
advising the object of the re-zoning request involves potential sale of the property to assist with
building a new church; that the church has a contract with a funeral home interested in the property,
and that this type of use would be suitable for the location.  Mr. Collins moved to approve on second
reading with Planning Commission restriction that “the use be limited to allow only a funeral home
and related services,” seconded by Mr. Spiker.  Comments were made regarding restricted property
use if sale of the property to the funeral home did not occur, and possible further discussion on the
topic at the next Publ ic Services Committee meeting.  Upon inquiry on whether other re-zoning
actions had involved r estrictions on the ty pe of businesse s allowed, L isa Paffor d,
Building/Development Office, provided information on two recent conditional zoning restrictions
approved by the governing body.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the g overning
body present.
“A Resolution authorizing the transfer of funds in the approximate amount of $400,000.00
from the City’s Solid Waste Management Fund to the General Fund.” (Postponed on 04-12-10).
Reporting for F inance Committee, Mr. B rown moved to a dopt, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Mr.
Brown moved to postpone for two weeks (to May 10, 2010), seconded by Dr. Rinne.  It was noted
that the Committee’s recommendation to postpone was to allow time for information to be received
at the Council’s budget work session (held April 22 ).  Motion to postpone failed.  Voting “no” –nd
all members of the governing body present.  Comments followed regarding the probability that the
funds would n ot be needed relative to FY 2010 employee furlough days or to balance the current
fiscal year budget, but that the funds will be needed to help balance the FY2011 budget; time frame
on transferring the amount into the g eneral fund, and replenishing the Solid W aste Management
Fund.  Main motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present with the
exception of Ms. Ash, Mr. Collins and Dr. Rinne voting “no”. (#5204)
“A Resolution amending Resolution No. 2852 establishing a payment schedule for Stage II
of the Cheyenne Water Project.” (Postponed on 04-12-10).  Mr. Brown moved to adopt, seconded
by Ms. Broyles.  Mr. Brown moved to postpone for two weeks (to May 10, 2010).  Motion failed
due to lack of a second to the motion.  Di scussion followed and included: “on/off budgeting”
practices; current economic conditions; governing body’s fiscal responsibility; reduced municipal
funding from the state ; public perc eption on defe rring the City ’s annua l pay ment to BOPU;
indebtedness to future governing bodies; suggestion of inserting a specific date in the resolution as
to when payment(s) to repay BOPU would be made; ba lancing the budget being a separate issue
from 5  Penny Sales Tax; reducing budget costs through attrition instead of further reductions inth
employee work force; re visiting the re solution topic next fiscal y ear relative to status of budg et
revenues/expenditures; partial payments scenario; employee job security; legal reviews reflecting
the annual payment is not a requirement, and concern with the effect on public services if additional
reductions in work force occur.  Upon inquiry regarding how many employee jobs may be affected
if the $1,000,000 payment is not deferred, City Treasurer Barb Dorr responded that approximately
15 jobs equates to $1,000,000.  Discussion continued and included:  Options for consideration (i.e.
use general fund reserves for the payment; impose additional reductions in work force, or delay the
payment); willingness by BOPU to m ake the payment; public perception; reluctance to i mpose
further work force reductions; across-the-board employee salary cuts and job sharing as cost savings
measures, and status  of budget savings suggestions submitted from e mployees.  Ma yor Kaysen
provided the f ollowing information in response to discussion topics: Post poning action will not
achieve a balanced budget required to be approved by July 1 ; stronger revenues than anticipatedst
for next fiscal year could allow for  a payment(s) to BOPU to be ac ted upon; resolution wording
providing for  suspension of the bond pay ment, not forg iveness of ma king the  pay ment; non-
opposition by the BOPU regarding delay of the City’s payment; clarification that bondholders will
be paid, and that water rates, per information provided by BOPU, will not increase based upon the
City’s suspension of pay ment.  He further informed that employ ee suggestions that have be en
submitted are being pursued and some have merit; general fund reserves amount is “borderline”
pursuant to the Resolution on the level of cash reserves, and that across-the-board employee salary
reductions had been a nalyzed.  M r. Spiker moved to amend r esolution wording  in the Now,
Therefore, Be It Resolved paragraph as follows: “ ... that Resolution No. 2852, adopted F ebruary
11, 1985, is hereby amended to temporarily suspend the $1,000,000.00 pay ment to the Boa rd of
Public Utilities which is due on December 1, 2010, FOR A PERIOD OF 1 YEAR.”, and strike the
remainder of  th e s entence, s econded b y M r. B rown.  [C lerk’s n ote: R emainder o f th e c urrent
sentence to be removed reads: “and the suspension of said payment will remain in force and effect
until such tim e as the  governing body elects to repea l the suspension.”] Ms. Dorr advised the
proposed amendment would mean there would then be a $2,000,000 burden on the general fund
budget for that year, and commented generally on budget considerations.  Comment followed on the
intent of the motion to amend, which was not to incur a $2 million dollar payment within a fiscal
year, but to insert a date specific for the City to make payment.  Mr. Brown withdrew his second to
the motion. Upon request for amendment wording assistance, City Attorney Dan White suggested
proposed language could be as follows: “ ... that Resolution No. 2852, adopted February 11, 1985,
is h ereby a mended to  te mporarily su spend the  $1 ,000,000.00 p ayment t o th e Board of  Pub lic
Utilities which is due on December 1, 2010 until December 1, 2011, and to temporarily suspend the
$1,000,000.00 payment to the Board of Public Utilities which is due on December 1, 2011 until
December 1, 2012.”  Mr. Spiker moved to amend per Mr. White’s suggested wording, seconded by
Mr. Brown.  Comments followed on specifying payment dates vs. current wording addressing one
payment and BOPU approval with the current wording.  Mr. Spiker withdrew his motion to amend
with concurrence by Mr. Brown as second to the motion.  Mr. Spiker moved to amend the paragraph
as follows: “ ... temporarily suspend the $1,000,000.00 payment to the Board of Public Utilities
which is due on December 1, 2010 UNTIL DECEMBER 1, 2012.", and revise affiliated language
as necessary in the resolution, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” –
all members of the governing body present.  Upon inquiry, Ms. Dorr advised yearly payroll costs
in total is approximately $34,000,000.  Comments followed on reducing employees’ salaries to make
up the $1,000,000 def icit.  Ms. Dorr a dvised a g ood portion of the $34,000,000 pay roll budget
involves health insurance coverage costs and a  percentage cut in pay would not affe ct insurance
costs unless employees were asked to pay a larger portion of the insurance payment.  Main motion
as ame nded ca rried. V oting “ yes” – Mr . Br own, Ms. Br oyles, Mr. Pierson , Dr. Rinne, Mayor
Kaysen.  Voting “no” - Ms. Ash, Mr. Collins, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Spiker. (#5205)
“A Resolution authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to s ign a Final Plat for BOPU
Subdivision, a replat of Block 149, Original City, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located at the northwest
corner of the intersection of Snyder Avenue and W. 24  Street).”  Brad Emmons, AVI, agent forth
BOPU, advised the plat is for a new BOPU administration building, noting the preliminary plat had
been previously approved as well as a resolution relative to State Land and Investment Board (SLIB)
funding.  Mr. Col lins reported there was no re commendation on the item fr om Public Services
Committee.  Mr. Pierson moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Comments followed on whether
utilization of vacant building sites in the community had been investigated; support for the project
and area enhancement for the Snyder/24th site, and past Council work session discussion relative
to the project and building site, which will add on to a present building.  Motion carried.  Voting
“yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of Mr. Collins and Dr. Rinne
voting “no”.  (#5206)
[CA] “A Resolution acknowledging receipt of and approving the “West Allison Road Corridor
Study” pre pared by Western Resea rch a nd Deve lopment, Ltd., for the Chey enne Me tropolitan
Planning Organization.” Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.  (#5207)

“A Resolution certifying that the Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne is in agreement
with the Laramie County Board of Commissioners as to the current Countywide Consensus Block
Grant application to the State L oan and Investment Board.” Cate Cundall, Town of Pine Bluf fs
Clerk/Treasurer, and Cindy  Schn eider, G rants Mana ger, pr ovided information on a pr oposed
substitute resolution reassigning previously allocated project funds to the Town of Pine Bluffs to
a different Town pr oject due to an emergency situation invol ving the Town’s non-w orking 911
response system.  Ms. Schneider clarified that under the consensus process, funding from the past
biennium has already been allocated to the Town and to enable a project change it must be agreed

Commissioners have the item on their upcoming meeting agenda.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting
“yes” – a ll members of the g overning body  prese nt.  Comm ent was ma de supp orting other
communities’ needs involvin g the consensus block grant process.  Main motion as amende d by
substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.  (#5208)
[CA] “A Resolution adopting the City of Chey enne Comprehensive Consolidated Plan 2010-

[CA] “A Resolution supporting providing funds from the City’s Optional One Percent Sales Tax

((2007 - 2010 1% Sales Tax) -- referred to Finance Committee (sponsors - Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms.

Preliminary Plat for Woodhaven Subdivision, a replat of L ots 1 & 2, B lock 1, Fa rson
Addition and L ots 1 through 14 inc lusive of Dry  Creek T win Homes Subdivision, C heyenne,
Wyoming (located east of and adjacent to Wills Road, south of the Dry Creek Channel and Parkview

have come before the governing body and will clean up several issues involving the project area,
and noted development intent is for town homes (multi-family housing).  Mr . Collins moved to
acknowledge receipt of the pre liminary plat with staff re commendations #1 and staf f

expressed that alleyways should be provided behind housing developments to provide for rear vs.
street front garages.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present in
Council Chambers with the exception of Dr. Rinne voting “no”.  Following announcement of the
vote, Mr. Spiker returned to Council Chambers.
[CA] Memorandum of  Under standing betwee n L aramie Cou nty, Wy oming, a nd the City  of
Cheyenne, to provide public transportation services to Laramie County Community College, the
City/County Health Department, and an area of Laramie County adjacent to the City.  Motion (per

[CA] Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and United States of America for limited hunting

celebration.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.  (#5536)
[CA] Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Cheyenne and Laramie County School

methamphetamine p revention a nd e ducation p rogram services. ( American R ecovery &

Department a nd Ma gic City  En terprises f or so rting, p rocessing, a nd ma rketing of  re cyclable
materials.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.  (#5056)

[CA] Contract Modification #1 to  Contract #5531 between the City of Cheyenne and The Sanborn
Map Company, Inc., Colorado Spring s, CO, for Hig h Resolution Aerial.  Moti on (per Consent
Agenda) carried (amount not to exceed $98,702.26).  (#5531)

d/b/a Five-R Company for Tyvek house wrap & reconfiguration of the retaining wall at the Transfer

$7,750.00).  (#5477)

portion of the City's Happy Jack Landfill property -- referred to Finance Committee.

(2007-2010 1%  Sales Tax).  Motion (per Consent Ag enda) car ried (a mount not to exceed
$355,060.35).  (#5542)

Inc., d/b/a Knife  River, for a nnual contract for fur nishing a ggregates for  the Street a nd Alley
Department (2007-2010 1% Sales Tax).  M otion (per Consent Agenda) carried (amount not to
exceed $22,500.00).  (#5545)
[CA] Consideration of Bid #M-20-10 for a contract between the City of Cheyenne and JTL Group,
Inc., d/b/a Knife River, for annual contract for hot plant mix, asphalt tack oil and cold mix for Street
and Alley Department (2007-2010 1% Sales Tax).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (amount
not to exceed $377,080.00).  (#5546)
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-10-10 between the City of Cheyenne and Rehrig Pacific Co., Los
Angeles, CA, for  furnishing and delivering  10,000 automated r efuse car ts for the Sanitation
Department.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (amount not to exceed $515,120.00).  (#5547)
Appointment of Edward F. Murray, III to the Cheyenne Downtown Development Authority
Board.  Mr. Valdez moved to approve, seconded by Collins.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all
members of the governing body present with the exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not vote
(Mayoral appointment).
                                         
Reappointment of John P arks to the International Fire Code Board of Appeals and Mona
Pearl to the Cheyenne-Laramie County Economic Development Joint Powers Board.  Mr. Collins
moved to approve, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the
governing b ody present with the exception of May or Ka ysen who did not vote (Ma yoral
appointments).
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held May 10, 2010 at 6:00 p.m. in City
Council Chambers to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyo. Stat
§ 15-1-402 exists for a parcel of land being situated in a portion of Tracts 7 and 10, Dell Range
Addition 2  Filing; Lot 3, Smithson View, together with a portion of Carla Drive, Thomas Road andnd
College Drive, Laramie County, Wyoming (generally located north of and adjacent to Carla Drive,
between Ridge Road and College Drive).
Under other business, Ms. Ash provided brief information on an educational project through
the State Dept. of Education involving a NASA funded grant involving construction of wind turbines
and middle school student participation, and that the project may provide an opportunity for city
involvement.
There being  no further  business to come before the g overning body , the meeting  was
officially adjourned at 8:09 p.m. 
 
 Submitted by,
 
 
 
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.

MEETING: City Council | DATE: 2010-05-10 | CLIP_ID: 152 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 152

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
May 10, 2010
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil Chambers.  P resent w ere: M AYOR -  R ichard L.  K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS: Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Ms. Case, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr.
Spiker and Mr. Valdez.  Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Barb Dorr, City Treasurer, and
Dan White, City Attorney.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.
RECOGNITION O F F IRE A ND R ESCUE C HIEF G UY E . C AMERON O N H IS
RETIREMENT.  City  Clerk Carol I ntlekofer rea d a May oral proc lamation into the rec ord
recognizing Chief Cameron for his years of service to the residents of Cheyenne and proclaiming
May 19, 2010 Guy  E. Cameron D ay.  May or Ka ysen pre sented Chief Came ron with the
proclamation, a plaque of appreciation for his 32 years of dedicated service to the City and a 100
year anniversary Fire Department commemorative medallion.  Appreciation was expressed by
Mayor Kaysen and members of the governing body on the Chief’s a chievements benefitting the
department and community.  Chief Cameron commented on his positive employment experience
with the City, and expressed appreciation to past and present mayors and members of the governing
body for their trust and confidence in him and also to co-staff with whom he has worked over the
years.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA]  are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda.)  Mr. Pierson moved to approve Consent Agenda items, seconded
by Mr. Spiker.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.
[CA] Minutes from Reg ular Meeting of the Gove rning Body on April 26, 2010.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
[CA] Minutes from Vouchers Meeting of the Gover ning Body on May  3, 2010.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Valdez moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Ms. Broyles.
Mr. Brown declared a conflict of interest (business interest) due to a voucher payable to Ameri-Tech
HVAC Services, and vacated Council Chambers. Upon inquiry regarding a voucher payable to
Union Pacific Railroad ($5,561.57 for flagging costs), Doug Vetter, City Engineer, explained the
majority of flagging expenses should be completed relative to the Norris Viaduct project.  Motion
carried.  Vo ting “ yes” – a ll m embers of the governing bo dy pr esent i n Co uncil Ch ambers.
Following announcement of the vote, Mr. Brown returned to Council Chambers.
Mayor Kaysen opened a public hearing for the purpose of receiving comments and input to
determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyo. Stat § 15-1-402 exists
for a parcel of land being situated in a portion of Tracts 7 and 10, Dell Range Addition 2  Filing;nd
Lot 3, Smithson View, together with a portion of Carla  Drive, Thomas Road and College Drive,
Laramie County, Wyoming (generally located north of and adjacent to Carla Drive, between Ridge
Road and College Drive).  Don Threewitt, Urban Planning, reviewed requirements and compliance
of c onditions c ontained in  Wy o. St at. § 15-1-402, in cluding s pecific in formation in dicating
compliance with Wy o. Stat. §15-1-402(a )(i) throug h (vi). Robin Huber que stioned whether  a
development proposal had been submitted, and requested the name of the developer.  Mr. Threewitt
clarified a development plan had not yet been submitted, and provided the names of the developers,
who are the property owners.  Mayor Kaysen advised any questions involving the prope rty to be
annexed could be communicated to Mr. Threewitt.  There being no further comments or input and
purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Kaysen closed the hearing.
“An Ordinance amending Title 17, Zoning, Chapter 17.08, Zoning Districts Established and
Section 17.08.040 Chey enne City  map of the Chey enne City  Code, by  chang ing the  zoning
classification from PUD Planned Unit Development District to MR-2 Medium Density Residential-
Developing District f or L ots 1 through 14 inc lusive of Dry  Creek T win Homes Subdivision,
Cheyenne, Wyoming, to be known as a portion of Woodhaven Subdivision (located west of College
Drive, between the Dry Creek Channel and McCann Avenue).”   Due to any perception of conflict
involving distant family  ties with the develo per, Mr. Spiker dec lared a conf lict of interest a nd
vacated Council Chambers.  Reporting for Public Services Committee, Ms. Ash moved to approve
on third and final r eading, seconded by Mr. Collins.  M s. Ash moved to amend by  subst itute,
seconded by Mr. Collins.  It was noted, pursuant to discussion and amendments recommended by
the Public Services Committee, the substitute includes the addition of the word “conditional” in the
ordinance entitlement and in Section 1.; inserts a new section which reads as follows: “That the zone
change was conditioned by  the Gove rning Body to allow only those uses by  right and uses by
administrative approval.  No other uses shall be allowed by Board Approval.  All other requirements
for the MR-2 Medium Density Residential-Developing District will remain as outlined in Section
17.48 of the Cheyenne City Code.”, and includes the following staff recommendation: “A condition
be placed on the approval of the zone change that the applicant record a “Notice of Conditional
Zone” to provide public notification of specific restriction to prospective buyers”.  It was further
noted the intent of the changes is to protect the neighborhood by providing that any development
of apartment buildings/complexes would require the consent of the governing body.  M otion to
amend carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present in Council Chambers.
Main motion as amended by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body
present in Council Chambers.  Following announcement of the vote, Mr. Spiker returned to Council
Chambers. (#3890)
“An Ordinance amending Title 17, Zoning, Chapter 17.08, Zoning Districts Established and
Section 1 7.08.040 Chey enne City  map of the Chey enne City  Code, by  chang ing the  zoning
classification from MR-1 Medium Density Residential-Established District to MUB Mixed Use with
Business Emphasis District for Lots 1 and 2; and the north 66- feet of Lots 3 and 4, Bloc k 195,
Original City, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located at the southwest corner of the intersection of E. 23rd
Street and Russell Avenue).”  Ms. Ash moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by
Mr. Collins.  Ms. Ash moved to amend by  substitute, seconded by Mr. Collins.  I t was noted,
pursuant to discussion and ame ndments rec ommended by the Public Services Committee, the
substitute includes the addition of the word “conditional” in the ordinance entitlement and in Section
1.; inserts a new section which reads as follows: “That the zone change was conditioned by  the
Governing Body as follows : The uses by  right shall be limited to # 1. Funeral home and re lated
services within the existing building or #2. Church and related services within the existing building,
no other uses shall be allowed by Administrative or Board Approval.  All other requirements for the
MUB Mixed Use with Business Emphasis District will remain as outlined in Chapter 17.88 of the
Cheyenne City Code.”, and includes following staff recommendation: “A condition be placed on the
approval of the zone change that the applicant record a “Notice of Conditional Zone” to provide
public no tification of s pecific re striction to  pr ospective bu yers.”  Upon inquiry, L isa Paffor d,
Assistant Development Director, clarified related (funeral) services would include offices related
to the funeral business, and services provided for an actual funeral and viewing areas.  Sh e also
advised a crematorium use would not be allowed in this type of zoning district, and to change the
use to include other services would require re-zoning.  Comments followed on the historical nature
of the neighborhood; support received from neighbors concerning the proposed use of the property,
limiting use of the site, and request for postponement received from the applicant’s agent.  Motion
to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  Ms. Ash moved to postpone
for two weeks (to May 24, 2010), seconded by Mr. Collins.  John Steil, Steil Surveying Services,
agent for applicant, advised the proposed purchaser of the property has inquired about adding a
garage onto the existing building to house funeral service vehicles and with the current language this
would not be allowed.  He noted support for postponement, suggesting the governing body could
consider amending the wording a t the curr ent meeting and move f orward with approva l of the
ordinance.  Motion to postpone carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.
“An Ordinance appropriating moneys for the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming for the various
purposes in conducting the municipal government of said city and fixing the amount of general and
special taxes as part of the revenue required to meet the said a ppropriation, all for the fiscal year
beginning July 1, 2010, and ending June 30, 2011” -- referred to Finance Committee (sponsor - Ms.
Broyles).
“An Ordinance approving and esta blishing revised water rates, as recommended by the
Board of Public Utilities to be effective January 1, 2011” –  referred to Finance Committee (sponsor
- Mr. Brown).
“An Ordinance approving and establishing revised sewer rates, as recommended by the
Board of Public Utilities to be effective January 1, 2011” –  referred to Finance Committee (sponsor
- Mr. Brown).
“An Ordinance approving and establishing revised tap fees, system development fees, pump
station fees a nd other re lated fees recommended by the B oard of Public Utilities to be e ffective
January 1, 2011” -- referred to Finance Committee (sponsor - Mr. Brown).
“An Ordinance approving and establishing revised administrative fees, service charges and
penalties as recommended by the Board of Public Utili ties to be eff ective January 1, 2011” --
referred to Finance Committee (sponsor - Mr. Brown).
“An Ordinance approving and establishing revised septic waste dump rates and  commercial
waste rates recommended by the B oard of Public Utili ties to be eff ective January 1, 2011” --
referred to Finance Committee (sponsor - Mr. Brown).
[CA] “A Resolution adopting the Cit y of Cheyenne Comprehensive Consolidated Plan 2010-
2014, which has been prepared by the Cheyenne Housing and Community Development Office”.
Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5209)
[CA] “A Resolution supporting providing funds from the City’s Optional One Percent Sales Tax
Infrastructure Development Fund for the purpose of  extending infrastructure required to provide
non-stop jet service between Cheyenne, Wyoming, and Dallas, Texas, on American Airlines”  (2007
- 2010 1% Sales Tax).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (not to exceed $200,000.00).  (#5210)
[CA] “A Resolution authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Crow Creek
Water Reclamation Subdivision, situated in a portion of the SE¼ of Section 3, T.13N., R.66W., 6th
P.M., Cheyenne, Wyoming (l ocated south of S. I ndustrial Road, ea st of S. Col lege Drive)” --
referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor - Ms. Ash).

 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
