MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2012-02-27 | CLIP_ID: 279 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 279

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
February 27, 2012
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil C hambers.  P resent w ere: M AYOR -  R ichard L.  K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS - Mr. Allen, Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne,
Mr. Spiker and Mr. Valdez.  Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Lois Huff, City Treasurer,
and Dan White, City Attorney.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda.)  Upon request by Mr. Collins, and pursuant to support received by
Mr. Pierson and Ms. Ash, agenda items #9 and 11 were removed from the Consent Agenda.  Mr.
Collins moved to approve  remaining Consent Ag enda items, sec onded by Mr. B rown.  Motion
carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body.
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on February 13, 2012. Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Brown and Mr. Valdez each declared a conflict of interest (business interest in vouchers
payable to Ameri-Tech HVAC Services and Radio Station KYOY F M respectively) and vacated
Council Chambers.  Mr. Allen moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by
Mr. Pierson.  Upon inquiry regarding a voucher payable to the Clerk of District Court, City Attorney
Dan White advised that in conjunction with the conde mnation filing for  the Holly wood Video
property, the court filing process requires the amount of the Ci ty’s last offer for the property be
submitted with filing  of the c omplaint.  Moti on carri ed.  Voting “yes” - - all member s of the
governing body present in Council Chambers.  Following announcement of the vote, Mr. Brown and
Mr. Valdez returned to Council Chambers.
Public Hearing for renewal of existing City liquor licenses (retail, restaurant, limited retail,
resort, bar and grill licenses, microbrewery and winery permits) filed with the City Clerk’s Office.
Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk, advi sed of 3 re staurant liquor lice nsees who did not file r enewal
applications; noted those licenses proposed for renewal that are currently in a “parked” status, and
explained there are renewal applications for 2 retail licensees who were initially approved, with
conditions, for licenses at the July 25, 2011 Council meeting, stating the licenses have not yet been
issued.  She reviewed the conditions for each of the 2 retail licensees (re: One East Sixteenth, LLC
and Let ‘Er Buck Investment Group, LLC d/b/a Steamboat’s); time frame for the conditions to be
met (i.e. no later than July 25, 2012), and offered a suggestion that consideration be given to extend
the time frame for conditions to be met to coincide with the end of the upcoming annual licensing
term as approval of renewal applications will be for the term of April 1, 2012 through March 31,
2013.  In response to inquiry, James Yates, speaking on behalf of Let ‘er Buck Investment Group,
LLC, advised they are pursuing renewal of the liquor license for The Commons area, but due to
property acquisition issues, they  may be applying at a future  date to cha nge the location for the
restaurant operation.  Upon inquiry and during discussion, Officer Steve Neisen, Cheyenne Police
Dept., reviewed information he had compiled for the department’s 2011 annual c ompliance and
licensing inspection report involving undercover observer operations, TIPS compliance by licensees,
number of ca lls for servic e, and c ompliance c hecks involving  sales to under age per sons.  He
explained the depar tment is supporting a community alcohol educ ation program involving such
issues as “over service” and underage drinking.  Discussion included concerns with sales to and
consumption by underage persons and increase in police calls for service for certain establishments.
There being no further comments or input and purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor
Kaysen closed the hearing and referred the applications to Finance Committee.
Ordinance amending Title 17, Zoning, Chapter 17.08, Z oning Districts Established, and
Section 17.08.040, Cheyenne City Map, of the Cheyenne City Code, by changing t he z oning
classification from P Public District to HR-2 High Density Residential-Developing District for Lot
1, Block 1, The Pointe, Sixth Filing, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located north of and adjacent to Dorothy
Lane, west of Powderhouse Road).  Reporting for Public Services Committee, Ms. Ash moved to
approve on second reading, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members
of the governing body.
 Resolution declaring as surplus the City-owned property located at 2100 Pioneer Avenue,
Cheyenne, Wyoming, commonly referred to as the City  of Chey enne Board of Public Utili ties
Administration building, together with all improvements thereon, and authorizing the Director of the
Board of Public Utilities and the City’s Purchasing Director to proceed with proposed sale of said
property pursuant to Wyo. Stat. §15-1-112.  John Ridge, Assistant City Attorney, advised pursuant
to Wyo. Stat. § 15-1-112(b) the City can sell the building directly to a political subdivision, of which
Cheyenne Housing Authority is considered, and explained a proposed substitute resolution includes
provisions involving sale of the property to the Housing Authority.  He advised if the Housing
Authority does not  meet the time frame in which to submit a qualified proposa l to purchase the
property, the substitute resolution then allows the City  to offer the property for s ale through the
public bidding process, noting proceeds from the sale will be utilized to offset the Board of Public
Utilities’ debt as required by statute.  Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Brown moved to adopt,
seconded by Mr. Collins.  Mr. Brown moved to amend by substitute, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Upon
inquiry, Dan White, City Attorney, advised it is the belief of the City’s legal staff that the City has
a statutory obligation to sell the property at the appraised value and that Cheyenne Housing Authority
will be given the “first shot” to purchase the property at the appraised value.  He further advised if
the Housing Authority chooses to not exercise the option, then the property will be offered for sale
pursuant to a publicly sealed bid process and Cheyenne Housing Authority could choose to submit
a sealed bid in a lesser amount, the same as any other interested bidder.  He reiterated proceeds from
the sale will be used to pay down BOPU’s debt as provided by statute.  Upon query, Mr. White
clarified the 30 day time frame for the Housing Authority to submit their proposal begins from the
date the property appraisal information is rec eived by the Housing Authority.  Motion to amend
carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body.  Main motion as amended by substitute
carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body. (#5356)
Resolution increasing the level of funding placed into the Solid Waste Management fund for
the specific purpose of providing funding to pay for increased professional services costs and solid
waste tipping fees, increased recycling costs, and increased costs for the lease/purchase of solid
waste equipment.  M r. Brown moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Mr. Brown moved to
amend by substitute, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  It was advised the substitute allows for a clerical
correction to amounts listed for the Vehicle and Equipment Replacement fund.  Jim Elias, Public
Works Director, e xplained fur ther staf f re view of th e amount reque sted for the  Vehicle  and
Equipment Replacement fund was conducted following the Finance Committee meeting, resulting
in another proposed substitute resolution being prepared, and requested approval of that substitute,
which reduces the requested amount for that fund from $133,500.00 ($1,602,000.00 annually) to
$116,833.00 ($1,401,996.00 annually).  He indicated the lesser amount proposed is due to delaying
the schedule for acquisition of vehicle and equipment leases/purchases for 6 months.  Motion to
amend failed.  Voting “no” -- all members of the governing body.  Mr. Brown moved to amend by
substitute (attorney stamp date of February 24, 2012) to incorporate the changes as presented by Mr.
Elias, seconded by Mr. Pierson. Upon inquiry, Mr. Elias provided further information on the reduced
amount being proposed and estimated savings, and noted that delaying the leasing of some of the
vehicles and equipment until calendar year 2013 will defer payments until fiscal year 2014.  Upon
inquiry, Lois Huff, City Treasurer, advised that in fiscal year 2014 two other lease payments will
expire.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body.  Upon inquiry
during discussion, Mr. Elias reviewed recycling costs associated with operating the various recycling
programs (curbside, e-waste, composting, household hazardous waste); cost of tipping fees relative
to not having a recycling program; challenges involved with collecting recyclables on a weekly basis
and effect on solid waste pickup schedules; expansion of recycling programs to multi-family units
as well as commercial establishments, and volume of household solid waste and effect of overall
community g rowth.  Discussion topics included sug gestion of a solid waste e nterprise fund;
recycling effects; recycling collection time frames, and recycling opportunities for multi-family
dwellings and commercial establishments.  Main motion as amended by substitute carried.  Voting
“yes” -- all members of the governing body. (#5357)
Resolution re-appropriating the Fiscal Year 2012 budget of the City of Cheyenne according
to the provisions of W.S . 16-4-112 &  16-4-113.  Mr. B rown moved to adopt, seconde d by Mr.
Pierson. Following brief co mments, Mr. Collins m oved to amend by  removing the amount of
$350,000.00 proposed f or a ne w phone system, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Discussion followed
regarding the need for a new phone system due to the system’s age and limited maintenance service
and e quipment r eplacement a vailability; ti me fr ame to a cquire a nd imp lement a  ne w s ystem;
unknown status of fiscal year 2013 budget revenues affiliated with anticipated state funding to be
received; concern with use of reserves for this type of purchase; suggestion of funding review for
inclusion in next year’s budget, and number of City-issued cell phones.  During discussion and upon
inquiry, Bob Bradshaw, Special Projects Director, provided information on the status of the current
phone system, explaining the limited serviceability of the system, which is approximately 20 years
old; outdated version of the system’s software, and the inability to replace failed individual user
phones as only refurbished phones (limited amount) are available.  He advised the requested funding
amount was for the first phase  of the re placement system involving the Municipa l Building and
perhaps another outside area, and would not cover  replacement of all phones in the sy stem.  He
clarified there is no backup to the phone system if it were to fail, noting funding for a new system
has been requested for quite a few years. During comment on City-issued cell phones, Mayor Kaysen
advised some employees utilize their own personal cell phones and not City ones.  Motion to amend
by removing the amount of $350,000.00 for a replacement phone system carried.  Voting “yes” --
all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Brown and Mayor Kaysen voting “no”.
Upon inquiry, Jim Elias, Public Works Director, reviewed fuel cost increases affecting the Fleet
Maintenance budget; inventoried and non-inventoried parts; Fleet Maintenance staffing level, and
outsourcing work for repairs that can not be done in-house.  Discussion followed on funding in the
amount of $65,000.00 for an employee salary and staffing analysis study, and timing of the study
affiliated with curre nt economic c oncerns and unknown fisc al year 2013 budget situation, and
potential effect on level of staffing.  Mr. Pierson moved to amend by removing the amount of
$65,000.00 proposed for the employee salary and staffing analysis study, seconded by Mr. Valdez.
Rich Wiederspahn, Human Resources Director, provided information on the benefits of the proposed
study, which has been contemplated since 2009, and expressed concerns with retaining and recruiting
qualified employees due to competitive salarie s offered by other e mployers.  Upon inquiry  he
clarified components of the study would be conducted as a package over an estimated five month
period, and indicated the study needs to be  a comprehensive regional study to be ef fective.  Mr.
Wiederspahn advised a salary survey that was recently conducted which focused on law enforcement
personnel resulted in salaries being increased to attract qualified police officers. Comments followed
regarding a similar study, referred to as the Anderson Study, that was conducted 20 years ago and
the inability to implement increases per that study due to l ack of funding.  Cl aus Johnson, City
employee and former Cheyenne Public Employees Association (CPEA) President, spoke in support
of the study and the difficulty the City has in retaining quality employees.  He stated the study would
include review of e mployee benefits and a  determination of appropriate job classifica tions and
whether the City is properly staffed.  He noted increasing costs to employees due to “frozen salaries”
and additional employee financial participation toward health and retirement expenses over the years.
Discussion included the following topics: Different levels of service between similar cities; job
classifications; employ ee c ompensation adjust ments and funding  conce rns; benef its of an
independent s tudy, a nd he alth ins urance sa vings (due  to less c laims su bmitted b y e mployees)
covering the cost of the study.  Motion to amend failed.  Voting “yes” -- Mr. Pierson and Mr. Spiker.
Voting “no” -- Mr. Allen, Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Valdez
and Mayor Kaysen. Upon inquiry, Mayor Kaysen provided a brief overview of his understanding of
the biennial budget status involving capital construction and direct distribution revenue amounts
affecting municipalities that is currently  before the state  legislature.  Comment of conc ern was
expressed relative to balancing the budget.  Mr. Spiker moved to postpone for two weeks (to March
12, 2012), seconded by Mr. Collins.  Discussion included state legislative budget decisions affecting
the upcoming  budg et y ear and not the cur rent budg et y ear; suggestion that re- appropriation
resolutions be submitted on the ag enda on a monthly instead of qua rterly basis; current status of
reserves; administrative Blue Form Committee process utilized for hiring employees or adjusting
salaries; two positions included for funding in the proposed re-appropriation, and support for as well
as ag ainst postponement.  During  discussion L ois Huff , City Treasurer, advised if the r e-
appropriation is approved the reserve level will be approximately $5.8 million, and Mayor Kaysen
provided information on the two employee salaries contained in the re-appropriation and explained
the review and approval process for hiring of employees through the Blue Form Committee.  Rick
Parish, Parks and Recreation Director, and Matt Ashby, Planning Services Director, reviewed their
justification for the two e mployee positions (one in each department) included in the r e-
appropriation.  Mayor Kaysen reviewed the status of the amount in reserves, explaining that due to
efforts of employees this amount was grown to $7.1 million at the close of June 30, 2011.  Motion
to postpone failed.  Voting “yes” -- Mr. Pierson, Mr. Spiker and Mr. Valdez. Voting “no” -- Mr.
Allen, Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Dr. Rinne and Mayor Kaysen.  Upon inquiry,
Ms. Huff reviewed the amount contained in the re-appropriation relating to Depot Plaza events and
explained this is a cumulative negative balance that has been carried forward for a number of years
that she is try ing to ba lance out so they  can sta rt fr esh for 2012, and Mr. B radshaw stated a n
accounting change is being made regarding the tracking of expenditures and reviewed Depot events
funding partnerships and provisions involving vendors at events.  Comments followed regarding the
Blue Form Committee, its formation a number of years ago, individuals comprising the committee,
including the Chair of Finance Committee, and possibility of monthly re-appropriation requests
being placed on the agenda.  Main motion as amended carried.  Voting “yes”-- Mr. Allen, Ms. Ash,
Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Valdez and Mayor Kaysen. Voting “no” -- Mr.
Pierson and Mr. Spiker. (#5358)
Resolution authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a County Final Plat for Country
Homes Subdivision, 3rd Filing, a replat of Lot 4, Block 5, Country Homes Subdivision, Laramie
County, Wyoming (located east of Cedar Avenue, between Grape and Peach Streets).  Brett Walker,
Development office, referenced a memo (on file with City Clerk’s office) dated February 24, 2012
issued to City Council members indicating continuing staff support for recommendation #1, which
would provide for a 26 ft. dedicated right-of-way to provide a pedestrian and vehicular connection
and not a road reservation, as suggested by the developer.  Bruce Perryman, AVI Engineering, spoke
in opposition to the staff recommendation and in support of a road reservation due to public access
concerns involving a right-of-way.  Upon inquiry, Dan White, City Attorney, advised if a right-of-
way is p latted and recorded, it b ecomes right-of-way dedicated to p ublic use, and expressed his
hesitancy in offering an opinion at the meeting on the locking/un-locking of a gate, affiliated with
the topic of public access, without having the opportunity to research.  Mr. Perryman submitted maps
(on file with City Clerk’s office) of the property area and discussed concerns with proximity of the
proposed right-of-way area to a n existing structure on the lot , public access to area relative to
residences and a gated area, and setback requirements.  He stated the developer’s preference is for
a road reservation, instead of the 26 f t. dedicated right-of-way, which would reserve the strip for
future road access and keep the property ownership private, and offered the option of a private access
easement.  He noted past development examples involving road reservations.  Comments followed
regarding  connectivity and right-of-way for future use, and staff continuing to discuss the issue with
the developer to hopefully reach an agreement.  Mr. Collins raised a procedural point of order with
Mayor Kaysen advising there was no motion on the floor.   John Volk discussed a past subdivision
development (re: Mustang Ridge) relative to road reservation vs. right-of-way access issues.  Mr.
Walker advised the  2nd plat filing f or Country  Homes Subdivision was approved w ith two
hammerheads in the layout in such a way that if certain lots did sell at a future date it would allow
connectivity and fulfill the patterns of the blocks.  James Perrott Macneil commented on provisions
he was aware of for property located on the east coast that allowed access to remain private.  Ms.
Ash moved to adopt, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Comments followed regarding future connectivity,
public vs. private access and effect on landowners, road reservation vs. dedicated right-of-way, and
possibility of a r oad re servation affiliated with a me morandum o f understanding with the
landowner(s).  Upon inquiry, Mr. White advised, pursuant to h is research, he could not find a ny
understanding or explanation of a road reservation as a term utilized in Wyoming Statutes.  Mr .
Collins moved to postpone for two weeks (to March 12, 2012), seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Comments
followed in support of postponement to allow staff and landowner(s) an opportunity to discuss the
matter further to protect the interests of both parties.  Motion to postpone carried.  Voting “yes” --
all members of the governing body. 
Following a brief recess, Mayor Kaysen reconvened the meeting at 9:07 p.m.
Resolution authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a  Final Plat for WYODI GS
Properties Subdivision, 2nd Filing, a r eplat of Lots 2 and 4, Block 4, Campstool Addition, Third
Filing, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located between Trucker Trail and Industry Court, west of the KOA
Campground).  Ms. Ash moved to adopt with staff recommendation #1, seconded by Ms. Broyles.
Comments followed reg arding conce rns of the de veloper wit h John Volk, Campstool L and
Company, advising that drainage issues will be approved by the City Engineer prior to the plat being
signed.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body. (#5359)
[CA] Resolution authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a County Final Plat for Prairie
Dog Alley Subdivision, a replat of the north half of Tract 38, Dell Range Addition, Third Filing,
Laramie County, Wyoming (located south of and adjacent to Summit Drive, east of Braehill Road).
Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5360)
Resolution a uthorizing the  Ma yor a nd the  City  Cle rk to s ign a  F inal Pla t f or Riv ett
Subdivision, a portion of the NE1/4 of Section 1, T.13N., R.67W., 6th P.M., Cheyenne, Wyoming
(located north of and adjacent to West Lincolnway, east of Westland Road).  Ms. Ash moved to
adopt, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Ms. Ash moved to ame nd to inclu de staff recommendation #1,
seconded by  M r. Collins.  Upon inqui ry, Br ett Walker, De velopment offic e, advise d staff
recommendation #1 is to record required easements on the lot adjacent to the east before signatures
are affixed to the map.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body
with the exception of Dr. Rinne voting “no”.  Discussion topics included: Accessibility concerns to
certain portions of the land; lack of right-of-way being included for roads for future access; unknown
factors involving future area development; MPO corridor study; area property owners’ involvement
in future g rowth relative to roads an d City criteria, and the pr oposed hotel deve lopment on the
property.  Upon inquiry , Br andon Cammara ta, Planning a nd Deve lopment Direc tor, provided
information on the preliminary plat review process, conceptual land use plan for the area affiliated
with the Missile Drive corridor plan, and the need for a road plan.  He clarified the MPO did delve
into what was the best approach for a road network for the area, and advised marketability factors
involving development or non-development of the area may affect road development.  John Steil,
Steil Surveying Services, agent for applicant, stated if they put streets in this would set the pattern
for any further development and they are not sure what will be developed at this time.  Upon inquiry,
Matt Ashby, Planning Services Director, advised of the general purpose of subdivision regulations
and that placing a condition for right-of-way may be premature.  Main motion as amended carried.
Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body with the exception of Ms. Ash and Dr . Rinne
voting “no”. (#5361)
Resolution granting with conditions an exception for deve lopment of a small waste water
system pursuant t o th e “ 201 A greement” fo r p roperty de scribed a s a  tr act of  la nd in
N1/2N1/2NE1/4NE1/4 of Section 11, Township 13 North, Range 67 West, of the 6th P.M. (a/k/a
4121 West 5th Street), Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming.  Ray Martin, attorney representing
Profile Properties, LLC, applicant, questioned the conditions affiliated with the exception request.
Jim Flesher, Planning and Development office, reviewed the conditions which includes annexation
of the property.  Mr. Martin spoke in opposition to the annexation condition, advising the applicant
does not desire to annex all of the property at this time due to potential acquisition of the property
by WYDOT for future re-design and reconstruction of the I-25/I-80 interchange, and referenced a
lease that had bee n entered into with Dy na Nobel.  He sugges ted a condition be placed on the
property that if the owner sells the property or develops any of the property in the future, at that time
it should be annexed.  Discussion followed on the 201 exception and conditions recommended by
staff and City-County Health Department, Environmental Health Division.  During comments, Mr.
Flesher p rovided r easons fo r s taff’s re commendations a nd the  wa stewater ho lding ta nk tha t is
proposed as a compromise, and Gary Hickman, Environmental Health, clarified the holding tank
could not be held in perpetuity as septic systems are not allowed within City limits.  James Perrott
Macneil spoke in opposition to the annexation condition.  Ms. Ash moved to adopt.  Motion died
due to lack of a second to the motion.
[CA] Resolution granting an exception for development of a small wastewater system pursuant to
the “201 Agreement” for property described as a portion of Tract 1, Lincoln Valley Tracts, Section
36, Township 14 North, Range 66 West, of the 6th P.M. (a/k/a 6509 Tate Road), Cheyenne, Laramie
County, Wyoming.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5362)
[CA] Resolution a uthorizing the  su bmission of  a  B usiness R eady Com munity, Comm unity
Enhancement Grant application to the Wyoming Business Council on behalf of the Governing Body
of the City  of Chey enne for completion of the Polk A venue Greenway segment.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried. (#5363)

(recyclable) materials.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5377)
Amendment No. 1 to Contract No. 5775, Professional Services Agreement between the City
of Cheyenne, Police Department, and DLR Group, Inc., for the Cheyenne Public Safety Center site
analysis -- referred to Finance Committee.  Mr. Brown reported the item was reviewed under other
items for the agenda at Finance Committee and provisions of Title 2, City Code, had been met.  Mr.
Brown moved to approve in an amount not to exceed $34,770.00, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Chief
Brian Kozak, Police Dep artment, provided infor mation on service s previously provided by  the
company regarding a space needs analysis, which assisted with the determination that a new public
safety center was needed, and recommended site locations for the new facility.  He stated the scope
of services to be provided through the amendment will allow DLR Group to provide an architectural
design concept and analysis, which will include square  footage and f loor plans; detailed budg et
information, and an exterior view of the building.  He noted the information will be provided to the
public for their  knowledge relative to the upcoming  6  penny ballot proposition.  J ohn Palmerth
expressed concern that the building project was being placed on the ballot without previously having
acquired the infor mation that is requested throug h the amendme nt, and s uggested, if the ba llot
question passes, waiting and using 6  penny funds to pay for the services to receive the information.th
Upon inquiry on whether money that may be expended now f or the additional services could be
reimbursed at a later date from 6th penny funds if the ballot question is approved, Dan White, City
Attorney, expressed his hesitancy  in offer ing an opi nion at the meeting  without having the
opportunity to research state statutes.  Discussion topics included: How the estimated cost for the
new Public Safety Center was determined; services under the initial contract; need for specific
information to share with voters; suggestion the contractor be approached to inquire whether some
services might be donated; concern with future potential benefit to the contractor relative to other
professional services for the project, and comments in support as well as non-support of expending
money for the a dditional services prior to the ballot question being approved by voters.  Motion
failed.  Voting “yes” -- Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Valdez and Mayor Kaysen.  Voting “no” -- Mr.
Allen, Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Spiker.

Boulevard reconstruction project (Phase IV) (2003-2006, 2007-2010 1% Sales Tax, Board of Public
Utilities, Federal Highway Administration funds) -- referred to Finance Committee.

Department, and Merrill, Inc. of Chey enne, Wyoming.  Motion (per  Consent Ag enda) carried.
(#5805)
[CA] Consideration of B id #R-25-12 for f urnishing one new r oll-off truck for the Sanitation
Division from Peterbilt of Wyoming, Cheyenne, Wyoming -- referred to Finance Committee.
Announcement was made  of the a ppointment of J ames W. Hea rne, Tuc ker Fagan and
William C. Beaman, to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming-Laramie County, State of Wyoming Joint
Powers Board for Frontier Park improvements to be confirmed March 12, 2012.
Under other business, Rick Parish, Director of Parks and Recreation, reminded those present
of a  City Cou ncil w ork s ession on  AD A c ompliance ma tters inv olving t he de partment t hat is
scheduled for February 29, 2012 at noon.
There being no further business to come before the governing body, Mayor Kaysen adjourned
the meeting at 10:07 p.m.
      
 Submitted by,
Carol Intlekofer, MMC
City Clerk

body present.  Mr. Brown moved to approve the renewal application filed by One East Sixteenth,
LLC  with the condition that a lease agreement with a restaurant establishment to operate within the
building must be signed no later than July 25, 2012 or the license will revert to the City, seconded
by Mr. Allen.  It was noted the license was initially approved July 25, 2011 with the same condition
and the motion on the floor confirms the condition remains in p lace.  M s. Intlekofer clarified if
renewal of the license is approved, the license term will be the same as other annual licenses, which
term is from April 1  through March 31  each year, and if the licensee does not comply with thest st
condition by the July 25  date, the City may need to pursue legal procedures available to revoke theth
license.  Motion ca rried.  V oting “yes” -- all members of the g overning body present with the
exception of Dr. Rinne voting “no”.  Mr. Brown moved to divide the question to allow for separate
action o n th e liq uor r enewal a pplication f iled b y L et ‘ Er Bu ck Investment G roup, L LC d/ b/a
Steamboat’s, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Motion to divide the question carried.  Voting “yes” -- all
members of the governing body present.  Mr. Brown moved to approve the renewal application filed
by Let ‘Er Buck Investment Group, LLC d/b/a Steamboat’s with the condition that construction of
the establishment must begin no later than July 25, 2012 or the license will revert to the City,
seconded by Mr. Spiker. James Yates, Let’Er Buck Investment Group, advised he was present to
answer any questions and stated they are planning on fulfilling the July deadline condition.  Pursuant
to inquiry conce rning use of the te rm “c onstruction” vs. “r emodeling”, Matt Ashby , Planning
Services Director, expressed his belief that if a condition is for a building to be “under construction”
or “remodeled” that there is no difference in terminology as far as both would require a building
permit.  Discussion included the following topics:  Concerns with regard to the initial issuance of
the license, which wa s for a  specific restaurant theme pla n within a newly developed area (The
Commons) in n orth Cheyenne; parking and property acquisition issues involving the i nitial site
within The Commons development; possible future change in location (to Dell Range Blvd.) for the
proposed restaurant affiliated with us e of the  license, a nd utilizing retail liquor licenses f or the
purposes of economic development.  Mr. Yates provided information on Steamboat’s project status,
advising they are close to entering into a lease agreement for a different site; reviewed his history
as a business/restaurant owner in Wyoming, specifically Cheyenne, and being fiscally responsible
to shareholders involved in the projec t, and monetar y investment by  shareholders to date, and
explained the business plan has re mained the sa me.  S helly Clements, Let ‘Er Buck Investment
Group shareholder, provided information relative to parking issues at the initially proposed business
lots located at The Commons, which has resulted in the group looking for an alternative location.
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present with the exception of
Ms. Ash and Dr. Rinne voting “no.”  Ms. Broyles moved to divide the question to allow for separate
action on the liquor renewal application filed by Two Bar Bowl, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Motion
to divide the question carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present with the
exception of Ms. Ash and Mr. Va ldez voting “no”.  Ms. Broy les moved to approve the renewal
application for Two Bar Bowl, seconded by Mr. Spiker.  Co mment of concern was expressed
regarding underage drinking at t he establishment.  Robert L anghoff, Two Bar Bowl, provided
information re lating to thei r efforts to reduce  and eliminate potential unde rage drinking
opportunities, advising they have diligently worked with the Police Department and have passed all
compliance checks and TIPS certifications, and have taken responsible steps to enforce policies.  Ms.
Ash stated that due to child issues she would be excusing herself from attendance at the remainder
of the City Council meeting (City Clerk note: Ms Ash vacated Council Chambers at 6:55 p.m.).
Upon inquiry, Officer Steve Neisen, Cheyenne Police Department, explained he has worked closely
with staff at Two Bar Bowl on ways to reduce and eliminate drinking under age (DUA) availability
within the establishment’s open concourse area, and provided information on enforcement strategies
and the number and types of police calls for service.  Mr. Langhoff explained his concerns with
enforcement and communication, and sug gested more timely communication to all licensee s be
provided by the Police Department regarding the number of  calls for  service affiliated with the
department’s annual report submitted during the renewal process, and particularly prior to the annual
public hear ing.  D iscussion followed a nd included informa tion from Offic er N eisen re garding
security, enforcement, the department’s new community alcohol educational program, and the unique
environment involving the bowling  alley as b oth an adult and y outh recreational area.  Motion
carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present.  Ms. Broyles moved to divide
the question to allow for separate action on the liquor renewal application filed by Stillwater, Inc.
d/b/a Mingles, seconded Mr. Pierson.  Motion to divide the question carried.  Voting “yes” -- Mr.
Allen, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Spiker.  Voting “no” -- Mr. Brown, Mr. Valdez
and Mayor Kaysen.  Ms. Broyles moved to approve the renewal application for Stillwater, Inc. d/b/a
Mingles, seconded by Mr. Spiker.  Owen Groshart, Mingles representative, stated he was available
to answer any questions.  Upon inquiry, Officer Neisen reviewed the number and types of incidents
that had occurred based on c alls for ser vice, per the de partment’s annual report, and e xplained
operational changes that have or will be occurring and training that will be provided to servers by
the Police Department regarding “over service” situations.  M otion carried.  Vo ting “yes” -- all
members of the governing body present.  Ms. Broyles moved to divide the question to allow for
separate action on the liquor renewal application filed by W.W. Enterprises, Inc. d/b/a Les’ Lamp
Lounge, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Motion to divide the question failed (due to a tie vote).  Voting
“yes” -- Mr. Allen, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Pierson and Mr. Spiker. Voting “no” -- Mr. Brown, Dr. Rinne,
Mr. Valdez and Mayor Kaysen.  Discussion followed on the main motion, excluding those renewal
licenses already acted upon.  Officer Neisen responded to inquiries regarding underage drinking
concerns at various locations within the community, specifically a recent incident at Romero Park;
confirmed the Lamp Lounge has a very positive system for tracking of incidents; addressed training
and changed practices and policie s for many liquor licensee s (i.e. Red L obster, Pizza Hut/Wing
Street (east location) and Crown Bar) based upon the department’s report information and inquiry
by City Council members during this year’s renewal process.  Dave McGee, provider of security
services for Lamp Lounge, reported on incident tracking and security operations at the Lamp, and
stated they are working closely with the Police Department.  Comments followed regarding DUAs,
possible legislation to require a “must appear” status when someone is cited into municipal court for
an underage drinking offense, and self-responsibility of youth and young adults to know right from
wrong.  Main motion to approve re newal of remaining liquor lice nses (re: those not acted upon
pursuant to separate motions) carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present.
  
Appointment of James W. Hearne, Tucker Fagan and William C. Beama n to the City  of
Cheyenne, Wyoming-Laramie County, State of Wy oming Joint Powers B oard for Frontier Park
improvements.  Ms. Broyles moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Allen.  Motion carried.  Voting
“yes” -- all members of the governing body present with the exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not
vote (Mayoral appointments).
Announcement was made of the Appointment of Catherine Nicholas and Maida Wedell to
the Arts In Public Places Committee to be confirmed March 26, 2012.
Under other business, Deputy City Attorney Erik Rasmussen requested the governing body
meet in executive sessi on to discuss matters involving pe nding potential litigation.  Mr. Pierson
moved to meet in executive session, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all
members of  the  g overning bo dy pr esent.  Ma yor Ka ysen a nnounced me mbers would me et in
executive session in Council Chambers, not open to the public; requested the Deputy City Attorney,
City Clerk, and other staff as requested by the Deputy City Attorney, be present at the executive
session, and stated there would be no action taken by the governing body as a result of the executive
session, and that the regular City Council meeting would officially conclude at the close of the
executive session.  (Clerk’s Note: Executive session convened at 7:55 p.m. following a brief recess.)
There being no further business to come before the governing body prior to the executive
session, the meeting was officially adjourned at 8:21p.m. following closure of the executive session.
      
 Submitted by,
Carol Intlekofer, MMC
City Clerk
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle
March 22, 2012

MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2012-03-26 | CLIP_ID: 289 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 289

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
March 26, 2012
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil C hambers.  P resent w ere: M AYOR -  R ichard L.  K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS - Mr. Allen, Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins,  Dr. Rinne, Mr. Spiker and
Mr. Valdez.  A bsent: Mr. Pierson.  A lso present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Lois Huff, City
Treasurer, and Dan White, City Attorney.  Mayor Kaysen recognized members of the Mighty Eagles
4-H Club present at the meeting.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda.)  Upon request by Mr. Collins, and pursuant to support received by
Mr. Brown and Mr. Allen, agenda item # 18(b) was re moved from the Consent Ag enda.  U pon
request by Ms. Ash, and pursuant to support received by Mr. Collins and Ms. Broyles , agenda items
#17(b) and (c) were removed from the Consent Agenda.  Mr. Collins  moved to approve remaining
Consent Agenda items, seconded by Mr. Allen .  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the
governing body present.
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on March 12, 2012. Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Brown and Mr. Valdez each declared a conflict of interest (business interest in vouchers
payable to Ameri-Tech HVAC Services and Radio Station KYOY F M respectively) and vacated
Council Chambers.  Mr. Spiker moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by
Mr. Allen.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present in Council
Chambers.  Following announcement of the vote, Mr. Brown and Mr. Valdez returned to Council
Chambers.

College Business Park, 3rd Filing, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located east of and adjacent to N. College

moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” --
all members of the governing body present.

second reading, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Motion carr ied.  Voting  “yes” -- all members of  the
governing body present.
[CA] Resolution re-appropriating the Fiscal Year 2012 budget of the City of Cheyenne according
to the provisions of W.S. §16-4-112 & 16-4-113. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5367)
[CA] Resolution authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for The Crossroads
Center, Second Filing, a replat of a portion of Lots 2 and 4, and all of Lot 3, Block 2, The Crossroads
Center, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located north of and adjacent to Greenway Street, east of College
Drive).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5368)
Resolution granting, with conditions, an exception for development of a small wastewater
system pursuant to the ‘201 Agreement’ and authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to execute a
development agreement for property described as a tract of land in N1/2N1/2NE1/4NE1/4 of Section
11, Township 13 North, Range 67 West, of the 6th P.M. (a/k/a 4121 West 5th Street), Cheyenne,
Laramie County, Wyoming.  Ms. Ash moved to adopt, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Ms. Ash moved to
amend by substitute dated as to form March 26, 2012, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Brief history of the
agenda item topic and purpose of the proposed substitute were noted.  It was advised the applicant
has agreed to annex two parcels now and a third parcel in the future in exchange for the exception
to ‘201 agreement’ provisions, and that the exception will be in effect for 10 years.  Upon inquiry
and with no objection ra ised by City Council members, Mayor Kaysen stated he would open the
floor again for comments from the public due to the substitute being proposed.  Ray Martin, legal
counsel for the applicant, expressed appreciation to staff and governing body members for their
willingness to work together to reach a compromise for the best interests of all parties.  Motion to
amend carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present.  Comments followed
regarding Wyo. Dept. of Transportation’s shortage of funding for road projects and concern that an
anticipated reconstruction project expected to involve some of the land may  not move forwa rd,
affecting the exception and tempora ry permit for the  small wastewater system.  Main motion as
amended by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present with the
exception of Ms. Ash voting “no”. (#5369)
[CA] Resolution authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for College Business

Addition, Fourth Filing, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located east of and a djacent to N. Coll ege Drive,

[CA] Resolution authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Gateway South,

Wyoming (located at the southeast corner of the intersection of W. Fox Farm Road and Walterscheid
Boulevard) -- referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor -- Ms. Ash).
[CA] Resolution approving Sanitary Sewer Service, by Outside User Agreement, with Michael

Mr. Valdez).
[CA] Resolution recognizing and Supporting the use of Fiscal Year 2011-2012 Ward 1

[CA] Resolution approving a proposition to impose the 1% Specific Purpose Sales and Use Tax

August 21, 2012 -- referred to Finance Committee (sponsors -- Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins,

[CA] Professional Servic es L etter of Intent betwee n the City  of Chey enne a nd Kaiser  and

(#5810)
Contract between the City of Cheyenne, Youth Alternatives, and Laramie County Community

a conflict of interest (employment conflict) and vacated Council Chambers.  Mr. Brown moved to
approve, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing
body present in Council Chambers.  F ollowing announcement of the vote, Ms. Ash returned to
Council Chambers. (#5811) 
Contract between the City of Cheyenne, Youth Alternatives, and Laramie County Community

moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the
governing body present in Council Chambers.  Following announcement of the vote, Ms. As h
returned to Council Chambers. (#5812)
[CA] Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Police Department, and Laramie County Sheriff’s
Department and Laramie County, Wyoming, for housing City prisoners at the Laramie County
Detention Center.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5813)
[CA] Professional Se rvices Agreement b etween th e City  of  Che yenne a nd Al l T raffic Da ta
Services, Inc. for data collection for the Updated Turning Movement Count Project (Metropolitan
Planning Organization (MPO) Federal funding) -- referred to Finance Committee.  
[CA] User Ag reement between the City of Cheyenne, Parks and Recreation Department, and
Cheyenne Warriors Football Club, LLC, for the purpose of holding arena football games and related
practices at the City of Cheyenne-owned Ice and Events Center -- referred to Finance Committee.
 
[CA] Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Transit Division, and Stride Learning Center,  to
provide a  Chey enne T ransit bus to use in service  of Stride’s Clie nts -- refe rred to Financ e
Committee.
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Tatooine Electronic
Systems, Inc., for recycling of electronic waste received at the Felix Pino Transfer Station Waste
Facility and Happy Jack Landfill -- referred to Finance Committee. 
Contract Modifica tion No. 2 to Cont ract No. 5496 betwee n th e City of Chey enne,
Engineering Department, and Ayres Associates for additional design services for the East Pershing
Boulevard reconstruction project (Phase IV) (2003-2006, 2007-2010 1% Sales Tax, Board of Public
Utilities, Federal Highway Administration funds) (postponed from March 12, 2012).  Mr. Brown
moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Mr. Brown moved to amend by substitute, seconded
by Mr. Valdez.  It was clarified the substitute provides for an increase in the modification amount
to $41,645.00 for additional design work.  Doug Vetter, City Engineer, advised the modification was
originally intended to have the consultant reconfigure the East Pershing project in two separate
corridors, and with the amendment an additional segment is being included to extend the projec t
west by seven blocks due to additional federal funds that are available.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Vetter
estimated construction cost for the additional segment will be about $400,000.00.  Motion to amend
carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present.  Comments followed regarding
funding and splitting the project into phases, additional segment and related design cost ($21,175.00)
per the amendment, and  previous demolition of two houses in the projec t area.  Main motion as
amended by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present with the
exception of Dr. Rinne voting “no”. (#5496)
Amendment No. 1 to Professional Services Agreement/Contract No. 5613 between the City
of Cheyenne on behalf of the Cheyenne Metropolitan Planning Organization and Felsburg, Holt and
Ullevig for South Greeley Highway Corridor Plan - Supplemental B udget Request.  Pat Crank,
attorney repr esenting local busi ness owner Maury  Br own, spoke in opposition to the plan as
currently drafted.  He e xplained his client is co ncerned about highway traffic control struc tures
envisioned in  the  pla n th rough im plementation o f r aised me dians; effect of  lim ited a ccess t o
businesses in the area, and proposed future side road accesses along the “backside” of businesses.
Mr. Crank provided information on stakeholders’ meetings that had been held to receive public
comments in c onjunction w ith fo rmulation o f t he pla n, no ting tha t Mr . Brown  a nd/or his
representative had voiced opposition to the raised median concept at the meetings, and encouraged
consideration of other alter natives.  H e spoke in opposit ion to the proposed ame ndment to the
agreement, stating the additional services to be provided, which includes more time to receive  public
comments, was not a serious commitment to listen to residents and business owners in the ar ea
pursuant to their previous input.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Crank reviewed stakeholders’ meetings held so
far and made  statements in support of the c onsultant and MPO staff listening to those who ha d
voiced opposition to the concept of raised medians.  Mark Shubert, business owner in South Greeley
Highway area, spoke in opposition to the plan and the proposed amendment.  He commented on lack
of communication with business owners; raised median concerns; out of state consultants; MPO
authority; state highway department involvement and timing r egarding reconstruction plans, and
suggested o ther t raffic fl ow options in  lie u o f r aised me dians.  Joh n Pa lmer e xpressed h is
concurrence with most of Mr. Shubert’s comments and spoke in opposition to the plan and cost of
the study.  Tom Mason, MPO Director, reviewed the project generally, stating the need for a corridor
plan had been identified by MPO committ ee members, consisting of representatives of City and
County governments and State WYDOT, as a  planning project.  He explained this is a long ter m
project, which will not be implemented in the nea r future, to pro-ac tively address the corr idor’s
traffic problems.  He  stated a w ide variety of solution options  are being reviewed and that the
amendment will ena ble the consultant to continue w ork on the plan, w hich includes ad ditional
meetings with the pu blic and property owners in the area, and the goal is to address, t hrough
planning, the best way to deal with traffic issues and anticipated future volume increases on South
Greeley highway.  He a dvised the consultant, a Colora do firm, is a wel l known transpor tation
planning firm and was selected to provide initial service s through the usual review and approval
process.  Up on inquiry, Mr. Mas on described the purpose of raised center medians as a safety
solution and current problems associated with numerous points of acc ess to properties along the
corridor; stated the draft plan and initial maps are not y et finalized as a policy statement and are
subject t o re vision(s), an d p rovided i nformation o n planning fo r f uture ar ea gro wth t hrough
additional north-south roads, tra ffic safety solutions and curre nt volume of traffi c.  Mr. Mason
advised efforts of the study will also help with beautification along the corridor by including a plan
for sidewalks and bike ways, etc.  Mr. Mason provided clarification on additional expenses related
with the amendment; information on the consultant’s work achieved under the original proposal and
additional work pursuant to the amendment, and noted the final plan will be presented to the public
and property owners and also to the MPO committee and City  and County governing bodies for
approval.  Upon inquiry as to status of the plan if the  amendment was not approved, Mr. Mason
indicated MPO staff will take what information they have and try to finalize, but the plan may not
be complete.  Discussion included the following topics: Raised center medians; service roads and
traffic circulation; access issues that may affect property owners; traffic volume along the corridor;
initial scope of the pr oject; rights-of-way acquisition conce rns af filiated with future  are a
developments or redevelopments; stakeholders’ meetings; purpose of the amendment, which will
include additional stakeholders’ meetings, and provisions of the orig inal agreement and cost of
consultant’s services to date.  During discussion, Mr. Mason provided additional information upon
request and noted the City’s governing body serves as the fiscal agent for the MPO.  Mr. Shubert
expressed his concerns with the effect of raised medians/barriers on businesses; communication with
stakeholders, and traf fic flow issues a nd alterna tives.  Dino Moncec chi, resident in the a rea,
suggested waiting to do a final plan based upon an updated traffic analysis when WYDOT is closer
to acquiring funding to do reconstruction of the highway.  Bob McCue, stating he does work for Mr.
Brown, spoke in opposition to the amendment, commenting  on the cost involved to complete the
plan and questioning whether provisions of the initial contract required the consultant to produce a
deliverable product.  Mr. Brown moved to approve in an amount not to exceed $20,050.00.  Motion
died due to lack of a second to the motion.
[CA] Contract Modification No. 2 to Contract No. 5697 between the City of Cheyenne and STC
Construction Co., C heyenne, Wyoming, for bridge repairs on the W estland Road Ove rlay and
Improvements Project (2007-2010 1% Sales Tax).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (amount
not to exceed $19,089.35). (#5697)
[CA] Amendment Number Six to Cooperative Agreement, Contract No. 4968, between the City
of Cheyenne and Wyoming Department of Transportation for reconstruction of Pershing Boulevard
from  I-25 to Pioneer Avenue (2007-2010 1% Sales Tax) -- referred to Finance Committee. 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-23-12 for furnishing stage drapery for the City of Cheyenne Civic
Center.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (Rose Brand Wipers, Inc., Secaucus, NJ; amount not
to exceed $46,125.00)
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-30-12 for surplus sale of one Express Dual 1000 reel grinder, one
Anglemaster 2000 bed knife grinder, and one Toro greens aerator for the City of Cheyenne, Parks
and Recreation Department, Golf Division.  M otion (per Consent Agenda) carried (Custer Golf

[CA] Consideration of B id #M-11-12 for  annual Contrac t between the City  of Cheyenne and
Simon Contractor, Cheyenne, Wyoming, for annual Contract for furnishing aggregate for the Street
and Alley Division (2007-2010 1% Sales Tax).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (amount not

[CA] Consideration of Bid #M-12-12 for annual Contract between the City of Cheyenne and Knife
River, Cheyenne, Wyoming, for annual Contract for hot plant mix, asphalt tack oil and cold mix for
the Street and Alley Division (2007-2010 1% Sales Tax).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (hot

[CA] Consideration of B id #M-13-12 for Contract betwe en the City  of Chey enne, Parks and
Recreation Department, and Chalk Buttes Landscaping, Inc., Douglas, Wyoming, for Lions Park
Remediation project.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (amount not to exceed $136,698.00).
(#5816)
[CA] Consideration of B id #R-31-12 for furnishing 68 new de sktop computers for  the City of
Cheyenne, Information Technology Division, pursuant to the City ’s replacement program (2011-
2014 1% Sales Tax) -- referred to Finance Committee. 
   
[CA] Consideration of Bid #M-14-12 for a Contract between the City of Cheyenne, Street and
Alley and 1% Construction Divisions, and Miller & Sons Construction, Inc.,  Cheyenne, Wyoming,
for the annual concrete overlay project (2007-2010, 2011-2014 1% Sales Tax) -- referred to Finance
Committee. 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-26-12 for furnishing one new 2012 stake bed truck from Spradley
Barr Motors, Inc., Cheyenne, Wyoming, for the Sanitation Division (Solid Waste fund) -- referred
to Finance Committee. 
[CA] Consideration of B id #R-27-12 for f urnishing one  new se mi-truck fr om Peterbilt of
Wyoming, Ch eyenne, Wyoming, f or the  Sa nitation D ivision ( Solid Wa ste fu nd) - - refer red to
Finance Committee.
  
Appointment of Catherine  Nicho las and Maida  Wedell to the Arts I n Public Pl aces
Committee.  Mr. Collins moved to approve, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes”
-- all members of the governing body present with the exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not vote
(Mayoral appointments).
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held Monday, April 9, 2012 at 6:00 p.m.
in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, for Fiscal Year 2012-2013
Annual Action Plan, City of Cheyenne Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) entitlement.

2013 Annual Ac tion Pl an, City of Chey enne Community  Deve lopment Block G rant (CDB G)
entitlement.  Deanne Widauf, Housing and Community Development Program Manager, provided
an overview of the CDBG entitlement program; reviewed the annual action plan, which is consistent
with the 5 year Comprehensive Consolidated Plan, and the City=s estimated entitlement allocation
amount of $375,173.00, which is 21% le ss than last year, and anticipated program income in the
amount of $5,000.00.  She noted funds have been utilized for programs that address decent housing,
homeless prevention, senior and youth needs, special population needs, neighborhood revitalization,
and expanding economic opportunities.  Ms. Widauf explained the grant application process; public
notifications and opportunities for input, and review and recommendations of eligible applications
by the Advisory Council.  She reviewed the Advisory Council=s proposed recommended public
service projects ($55,000.00) and general service projects ($109,400.00) f or funding, including
program administration ($76,034.00), and estimated funding allocation amount for each project.

MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2012-05-14 | CLIP_ID: 295 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 295

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
May 14, 2012
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil C hambers.  P resent w ere: MAYOR -  R ichard L.  K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS - Mr. Allen, Ms. Ash, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Spiker and
Mr. Valdez.  A bsent: Mr. Brown.  A lso present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Lois Huff, Ci ty
Treasurer, and Dan White, City Attorney.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda.)  Mr. Collins  moved to approve Consent Agenda items, seconded
by Ms Broyles.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present.
[CA] Minutes from Reg ular Meeting of the Gove rning Body on April 23, 2012. Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Valdez declared a conflict of interest (business interest in Radio Station KYOY FM) and
vacated Council Chambers.  Mr. Collins moved to appro ve payment of vouche rs as pre sented,
seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Motion carr ied.  Voting “ yes” -- all member s of the g overning body
present in Council Chambers.  Following announcement of the vote, Mr. Valdez returned to Council
Chambers.
Mayor Kaysen opened a Publ ic Hearing to determine w hether compliance of anne xation
conditions required by Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402 exist for a parcel of land being situated in a portion of
the N½ of the N½ of the NE¼ of the NE¼ of Section 11, T.13N., R.67W. of the 6th P.M., Laramie
County, Wyoming (generally located at the end of West 5th Street, west of Southwest Drive, a/k/a
4121 W. 5th Street).  Jim Flesher, Urban Planning Office, reviewed requirements and compliance
of conditions c ontained in Wy o. Stat. §15- 1-402, including specific information i ndicating
compliance with Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402 (a)(i) through (vi).  Upon inquiry, Mr. Flesher advised there
is a building currently located on the property and stated annexation of the parcel was pursuant to
an exception to the 201 agreement recently approved by the governing body.  There being no further
comments or input and purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Kaysen closed the public
hearing.
An Ordinance amending the City of Cheyenne’s Sanitation Fee Schedule.  Jim Elias, Public
Works Director, advised City ordinance requires an annual review of the fee schedule with rate
increases based upon the Southeast Wyoming Consumer Price Index (CPI), which is currently 4.1%,
and that the proposed fee increases are in the amount of 4.1% for commercial and residential solid
waste collection and dis posal services.  Mr. Elias repor ted that a 1%  increase was approved for
Fiscal Year 2011 (C PI was 3.4%) and no incr ease was approved for Fiscal Year 2012 (CPI was
3.2%).  He  noted increased costs in City operations involving expanded areas of service due to
population and commercial growth, and expansion of services in such areas as curbside recycling,
lawn waste, electronic waste and household hazardous waste.  He advised the proposed rates will
increase the monthly fee to a ty pical residential customer by $0.85 and the a verage commercial
account (one pick-up a week) by $3.00 a month.  J oe McCord expressed concerns regarding the
proposed increase, costs for roll-off containers, and Sanitation truck routes, and requested Sanitation
policies be reviewed to determine efficiency of pick-up routes.  Reporting for Finance Committee,
Mr. Spiker moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Elias
stated his belief that the City is competitive cost-wise in pricing for roll-off containers compared to
private haulers, and explained route patterns that are utilized involving alleys and on-street pick-ups
involving the automated container pick-up process.  He further advised that the increase in funding
from the proposed rate increases would assist to off-set costs, such as transportation costs affiliated
with fuel, maintenance, repairs, parts and tires.  Concern was expressed regarding the method of
billing for multiple business tenants located in one building, and recycling fees assessed involving
multiple tenants within residential apartment-type buildings.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all
members of the governing body present.
An Ordinance approving and establishing revised water rates, sewer rates, tap fees, system
development fees, administrative fees, service charges and pe nalties and septic a nd commercial
dump rates, a s recommended by the B oard of Public Utili ties -- re ferred to F inance Committee
(sponsors - Mr. Brown, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Valdez).
An Ordinance pursuant to Section 2.2.1 Z oning Map Amendments, Section 5.1.2 Zoning
Districts established and Section 5.1.3 Official Zoning Map (Cheyenne City Map), of the Unified
Development Code by changing the zoning classification from MUB Mixed-Use Business-Emphasis

(located at the southwest corner of the intersection of Fillmore Avenue and Rock Springs Street) --

[CA] Resolution amending the City of Cheyenne Annual Action Plans for Fiscal Years 2009-2010

[CA] Resolution amending the City of Cheyenne Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year 2011-2012 --

[CA] Resolution authorizing the Mayor and the  City Clerk to sign a County Final Plat for M

[CA Resolution authoriz ing the  May or and the  City  Clerk to sign a  Coun ty Final Plat for
Welchester S ubdivision, a  r eplat o f t he W est H alf o f T ract 2 1, C restmoor, L aramie C ounty,

Public Services Committee (sponsor - Ms. Ash).  (sponsor - Ms. Ash)
[CA] Resolution a uthorizing the  Ma yor a nd the  City  Cle rk to s ign a  F inal Pla t f or L ewis

[C A] Resolution authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Kum & Go 952

Agreement betwee n the City  of Chey enne a nd Merc er G roup, I nc., for a  Personnel
Organizational, Classification and Compensation Study and Analysis.  Rich Wiederspahn, Human
Resources Director, reviewed the Request for Proposal (RFP) process that was utilized resulting in
a recommendation from the City’s Employment Strategy Group (ESG) committee to enter into the
agreement with the Mercer Group.  He provided information on criteria used to evaluate and rank
proposals received; scope of services that will be provided under the agreement, and benefits to the
City involving an independent study and analysis.  Phillip Robertson, representative of the Mercer
Group, reviewed components that will be included in the study and analysis with regard to the areas
of compensation and classification, stating the classification portion will include review of positions
through use of employee questionnaires and interviews, overall point score based on 10 factors,  and
qualifications and skills needed to fulfill job descriptions, with the goal of providing information on
equal pay for equal work scenarios.  He noted that the compensation element will include a regional
salary survey and comparison with other similar market pay plans.  He advised that if the study and
analysis results reflect that certain salary areas should be adjusted, implementation of any
adjustments could be structured to occur over whatever time frame the City decides.  Upon inquiry,
Mr. Robertson stated the c lassification study would be conduc ted prior to the or ganizational
(staffing) study .  Commenting in support of the a greement wer e:  Vicki Ne mecek, Assistant
Director, Public W orks Department; Officer John Gay , representative for the Chey enne Police
Protective Association; Sara Vasquez, President, Cheyenne Public Employees Association (CPEA);
Todd Feezer, Assistant Director, Parks and Recreation Department, and member of the ESG; Claus
Johnson, City employee, former CPEA president and member of the ESG, and Robin L ockman,
Deputy City Treasurer and member of the ESG.  Comments included the following topics: Benefits
of the  stu dy a ssisting wi th e stablishing the worth of pa rticular j obs r elative to p ay sc ales;
information from the study helping the City with future planning as well as having a long term plan
in place for employees; having an employee master plan as a mechanism to provide administrative
guidance on staffing  and compe nsation levels;  study and analysis as a g ood investment when
compared to the percentage of budget attributed to employee costs (i.e. 74% of general fund budget
for Fiscal Year 2013 involves personnel costs); benefits of having a thorough analysis of salaries
to ascertain any minimum/maximum salary caps per classification; concerns with the City’s lack of
current competitiveness r elating to retention of curre nt employ ees a nd rec ruitment of new
employees affiliated with salary levels, and importance of an independent staffing level study by a
professional firm vs. City administrative staff.  Mr. Spiker reported there was no recommendation
on the item from Finance Committee.  Mr. Collins moved to approve, seconded by Ms. Ash.  Upon
inquiry, Lois Huff, City Treasurer, clarified funding for the study is off-set from previous savings
on employee health insurance coverage costs.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Wiederspahn reviewed various
reasons that employees have left employment with the City, explaining his belief that it is critical
to focus on maintaining employees, and noted the importance of having a market pay plan that is
comparable with neighboring states and the need to review current pay plan inequities.  Discussion
included the following topics: Reasons to approve the study; employees expressing support for the
study; concern with lack of f unding to timely  implement any  salary adjustments that may  be
recommended; an analysis being helpful in determining staffing levels, and employee morale.  Upon
inquiry, Mr. Robertson clarified the scope of services for compensation areas to be studied does not
include consideration of the employee benefits package, noting that the factoring in of benefits into
a salary study is hard to measure as different types of benefits have different importance levels to
individual employees.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present
with the exception of Mr. Pierson and Mr. Spiker voting “no”. (#5838)
[CA] Memorandum of  Under standing betwee n the City  of Chey enne, T ransit Division, and
Laramie Cou nty, Wy oming, to  pr ovide pu blic tr ansportation s ervices to  L aramie Cou nty

[CA] Consideration o f B id # R-29-12 f or fu rnishing one ne w 2 012 s tationary so lid wa ste
knuckleboom crane from Ameri-Tech Equipment Company, Casper, Wyoming, for Solid Waste
Transfer Station (Solid Waste Management fund).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (amount
not to exceed $167,500.00).
[CA] Consideration o f B id # R-32-12 f or fu rnishing thr ee ne w 2012 cab a nd c hassis w ith

(amount not to exceed $683,702.00).
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-33-12 for furnishing five new 2012 cab and chassis with automated

[CA] Consideration of Bid #M-16-12 for a contract between the City of Cheyenne, Public Works

Wyoming, for the Fiscal Year 2012 Milling and Utility Adjustments Project for Street and Alley
Division (2007-2010, 2011-2014 1% Sales Tax) -- referred to Finance Committee.

[CA] Consideration of B id #M-15-12 for  a contr act between City  of Chey enne, Public Works

Wyoming, for the Fiscal Year 2012 City Overlay Project (2007-2010, 2011-2014 1% Sales Tax) --
referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-34-12 for furnishing three new 2012 cab and chassis with rear load
sanitation ref use collec tion bodies with ti ppers f or the Sanitation Division fro m Peterbilt of
Wyoming, Cheyenne, Wyoming (Solid Waste Management fund) -- referred to Finance Committee.
Appointment of Howard A. Hill, Sr., to the Mayor’s Council for People with Disabilities.
Mr. Co llins mov ed to  a pprove, s econded b y Mr . A llen.  Mo tion carried.  Vo ting “ yes” --  a ll
members of the governing body present with the exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not vote
(Mayoral appointment).
[CA]  Designation of Official Voting Delegate and Alternate Delegate for the City of Cheyenne
at the 2012 Wy oming Association of Municipalities Ann ual Convention.  Moti on (per Consent
Agenda) carried (Mayor Kaysen, Official Voting Delegate; City Clerk Carol Intlekofer, Alternate
Delegate).
Announcement was made of the Appointment of Micha el R. O’Donne ll to the Boar d of
Adjustment, to be confirmed May 29, 2012.
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held May 29, 2012 at 6:00 p.m. in City
Council Chambers, Municipal Building, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, for a restaurant
liquor license a pplication filed with the City  Clerk's Office for Judi Bufkin d/b/a Judi’s Cajun
Kitchen, 1719 Central Ave., Cheyenne, Wyoming. 
Announcement was made that due to the Memorial Day Holiday on Monday, May 28, 2012,
the regularly scheduled meeting of the Governing Body will instead be held on Tuesday, May 29,
2012 beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, Municipal Building, 2101 O’Neil Avenue,
Cheyenne, Wyoming.
Under other business:
Announcement was made that a calcutta, benefitting the Cheyenne Boys and Girls Club, will
be held Thursday, June 7, 2012 beginning at 7:00 p.m. at Uncle Charlie’s Lounge, 6001 Yellowstone
Road, Che yenne, Wy oming, in  c onjunction w ith the  a nnual Uncle Cha rlie’s “ DONE” g olf
tournament (15% of proceeds to the Cheyenne Boys and Girls Club).
Upon inquiry, Rick Parish, Director, Parks and Recreation Department, provided information
concerning a  pa st Wy o. De pt. of  Tr ansportation ( WYDOT) beautification p roject on  Wes t
Lincolnway involving trees and landscaping areas that has resulted in future maintenance by the City
after completion of the project.  He noted department staff has worked on irrigation system repairs
and replacement of trees, which may be covered by warranty, and discussed the current status of the
trees and watering system.  Doug Vetter, City Engineer, advised when the project was accepted from
WYDOT last fall, it was his understa nding that the war ranty WYDOT had with the landsc ape
contractor for  the tree s would be extended to the City .  May or Ka ysen provided a dditional
information on staff contact with the landscape contractor involved.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Parish also
provided information on Forestry staff watering efforts for City tree areas along Pershing Blvd. and
staffing levels and olde r equipment a ffecting service s.  I t was noted that the D owntown
Development Authority also assists with watering trees downtown.
Upon inquiry regarding the status of replacing non-working lights on the Depot Plaza, Mayor
Kaysen advised the  initial lighting fixtures and ba llasts that were  installed have f ailed to work
properly; that a solution has been found and lighting replacements are in progress.
There being  no further  business to come bef ore the  governing body , May or Ka ysen
adjourned the meeting at 7:17 p.m.
      
 Submitted by,
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
May 29, 2012
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil C hambers.  P resent w ere: M AYOR -  R ichard L.  K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS - Mr. Allen, Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Spiker and Mr. Valdez.
Absent: Mr. Collins and Mr. Pierson.  Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Lois Huff, City
Treasurer, and Dan White, City Attorney.  The pledge of allegiance, led by members of the Mayor’s
Youth Council, was recited.
Expression of Appreciation to Mayor’s Youth Council and State of the Youth report.  Mayor
Kaysen and Jan Spires, May or’s Youth Council Coordinator, commended member s of the 2011-
2012 Mayor’s Youth Council and prese nted those members present with a cer tificate and gift of
appreciation. Those recognized were: Dean Jackson - Chair, Ian Dome - Vice-Chair, John Matsen -
Co-Secretary, Tyler Bedwell, Juliette Givhan, Joey Marchand, Robert McGarry, McKinzea Olsen,
Jacob Peterson and Gary Sayler.  Those members unable to attend were: Kadi Davis - Co-Secretary,
Addie Fleming and Margarita Medrano.  Mr. J ackson provided a State of  the Youth re port and
described various activities and issues the g roup was involved in during the  past year.  He noted
members lea rned va luable lessons with regar d to leade rship and educ ational experienc es that
included involvement with local government staff, tours of several City facilities and operations, and
participation in community efforts.  Mr. Jackson was presented with a plaque recognizing his service
during the past school year as chair of the Youth Council.  Mayor Kaysen expressed appreciation
to members for their time, commitment and dedication, and also to members’ families for their
support.
