MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2012-11-13 | CLIP_ID: 340 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 340

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
 November 13, 2012
Due to the V eterans Day holiday, the Gover ning Body of the City  of Chey enne instead
convened in regular session on this date beginning at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers.  Present were:
MAYOR  -  Richard L. Kaysen; COUNCIL MEMBERS - M r. Allen, Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms.
Broyles, Mr. Collins, Mr. P ierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Spiker a nd Mr. Valde z.  Also present: Carol
Intlekofer, City Clerk; Lois Huff, City Treasurer, and Dan White, City Attorney. 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda.)   Upon request by Ms. Broyles, and pursuant to support received
by Mr. Collins and Ms. Ash, agenda item #10 was removed from the Consent Agenda.  Mr. Collins
moved to approve remaining Consent Agenda items, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Motion carried.
Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body.
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on October 22, 2012.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
[CA] Minutes from Special Meeting of the Governing Body on October 31, 2012.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Valdez moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Brown.
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body.
  
Mayor Kaysen opened a public hea ring to rec eive comments and input for a tra nsfer of
ownership for a retail liquor license application filed with the City Clerk's Office for Los Abuelos
Mexican Restaurant, LLC d/b/a Los Abuelos Mexican Restaurant, 1601 Central Avenue, Cheyenne,
Wyoming (License currently held by One East Sixteenth, LLC, 1601 Central Avenue , Cheyenne,
Wyoming).  Upon inquiry , Imelda Onate with L os Abuelos advised they  are hoping to ope n the
restaurant on Dec . 31.  Upon furthe r inquiry , Carol I ntlekofer, Cit y Clerk, ve rified a  previous
extension approved by  the g overning body  of t he time frame condition place d on the license ,
pertaining to a lease agreement with a restaurant establishment to operate within the building, had
been met.  There being no further comments and purpose  of the he aring having been met, Mayor
Kaysen closed the hearing and referred the item to Finance Committee.
[CA] RESOLUTION - Certifying that the Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne has agreed on
the Town of Burns substitution project to be submitted to the State Loan and Investment Board for
the 2011-2012 Countywide Consensus Block Grant funding.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
(#5441)
RESOLUTION -  Su pporting th e Ci ty o f Ch eyenne’s a pplication f or a  L and a nd Wa ter
Conservation Fund Grant for the Martin Luther King, Jr. Park Quickstart Tennis Court Project.  Mr.
Brown moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Upon inquiry, Todd Feezer, Assistant Director,
Parks and Rec reation Depar tment, provided an upda te o n the project stating  the ar ea ha s been
rehabilitated with demolition of the old courts; that new irrigation and sod have been installed, with
trees to be planted in the spring, and reviewed grant funding that has been received as well as other
anticipated funding.  He advised they hope to complete construction in the spring and noted the tennis
courts would be located on the west side of the park.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” - all members
of the governing body. (#5442)
[CA] RESOLUTION - Authorizing the City of Cheyenne to approve and accept the FY2012 Grants
to encourage arrest policies and enforcement of Protection Orders Program from the U.S. Department
of Justice Office on Violence Against Women in the amount of $300,000.00 (Award No. 2012-WE-
AX-0058).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5443)
RESOLUTION - Determining conditions for annexation required by Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402
exist for a parc el of land being situated in a portion of the Ea st Half of the  East Half (E½E½) of
Section 20, Township 14 North, Range 66 West of the 6th P.M., Laramie County, Wyoming (located
approximately 150 feet west of the intersection of Converse Avenue and Ogden Road).  Ed Murray,
speaking on behalf of Murray Properties, property owner in the vicinity, referenced comments of
concern he had voiced at the Oct. 22 City Council meeting, and submitted and discussed 3 hand-outs
(on file with City Clerk’s office) depicting property involving the proposed annexed area and near
vicinity (1. Enlargement of PlanCheyenne Land Use Map; 2.  Map of area including parcel owned
by Murray Properties; 3. Exhibit D (map) as submitted with the Petition for Annexation).  Mr. Murray
expressed concerns with inconsistencies in the road network proposed in the maps submitted with the
Petition for Annexation relative to the land use map adopted with PlanCheyenne, and explained that
the proposed road network submitted with the annexation request would de prive his company of
being able to utilize their property for future use as identified in PlanCheyenne and pursuant to zoning
classification.  He indicated an orderly and coordinated transportation plan must be fac ilitated as
contemplated in PlanCheyenne, and in conjunction with easements acquired during the Storey Blvd.
extension project and including collector/connecting streets to allow access.  He further commented
that the issue involving the road network plan, as proposed as part of the annexation packet, should
be a ddressed th rough th e pla tting process and no t be  c onsidered a s a n a pproved r oad p lan in
conjunction with determining that annexation conditions had been met.  Frank Cole, property owner
of the pa rcel proposed for  annexation as well as land in the vicinity , referenced and discussed a
written agreement of record the Cole family has with the City that laid out accesses off Storey and
Converse and water “stub-outs”, and stated that, officially, the PlanCheyenne map has no bearing.
Reporting fo r P ublic Services Co mmittee, M s. As h mo ved to  a dopt, se conded b y Ms.  Broyles.
Comment was made concerning discussion on the resolution at the last Public Services Committee
meeting relative to communication between the property owner, developer, staff and those currently
working on an update  to the PlanChey enne do cument.  Upon inquiry  regarding the proc ess for
updating the Master  Transpor tation Plan, Matt Ashby , Planning Ser vices Dire ctor, a dvised an
amendment to the tra nsportation plan would involve a public he aring befor e the Planning
Commission and require a resolution adopted by the governing body, noting public input is allowed
throughout the process.  Upon further inquiry, Mr. Ashby stated that, at this point, Exhibit D is just
a “figure” submitted with the Petition for Annexation and that during the platting process discussions
would be held regarding the road network plan.  Brad Emmons, AVI, agent for Scenic Development,
Inc. who is planning a development project on the proposed annexed parcel, advised they are trying
to ensure they conduct the right traffic study to accompany the platting process relative to a collector
vs. local road, and expressed they feel they can separate the long range master plan from the proposed
development action.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Emmons stated that depictions in Exhibit D matches existing
curb cuts and stub-outs, and commented that Exhibit D labels the road in question as E. Carlson Street
but that st reet name is f or reference only and not necessarily the final street name.  Comme nts
followed regarding request for postponement of the item, as previously received by AVI, which would
have allowed time for further information to be acquired vs. adoption of the resolution; frustration
and concerns with incr emental annexations/additions relative to the road network system; recent
detention pond construction near East Carlson Street and land in the area being located in the county
and not within city  limits, and ar ea street network addressing future growth for the community’s
health, safety and welfare.  Mr. Emmons explained the purpose of the request to postpone was to
provide for the annexation ordinance to coincide with timing of re-zoning and preliminary and final
plat processes, and advised of the options available regarding postponement of the resolution vs.
delaying  the introduction of the annexation ordinance.  He verified preference for adoption of the
resolution at the pre sent meeting ; stated timing is critica l f or Scenic De velopment, re garding
resolution approval, to enable them to move forward with project financing, and noted delaying
ordinance introduction would provide time to work on the road network issue.  Mr. Cole provided
a brief history on certain road alignments and configurations in the area, including accesses on Storey
and Con verse a nd distance be tween a ccess p oints, a nd c ommented o n to pography pr oblems,
infrastructure, Cole family working with the City for numerous years on many developments, and the
recent detention area.  Discussion topics included: Location of the detention area (within Section 21);
road network system and effect on future area development as well as Murray Properties parcel;
whether adoption of the resolution legally mandates approval of the future annexation ordinance that
will be sub mitted, and effect of any changes in conditions that may occur following resolution
adoption.  Upon inquiry regarding whether adoption of the resolution compels a favorable vote on
the ensuing annexation ordinance, Dan White, City Attorney, stated that pursuant to comments that
have been made a situation is developing whereby he needs to advise the governing body that he may
have a conflict of interest (family related) involving a concerned party to the discussions and that the
question should be refer red to another staff a ttorney or outside counse l, and indicated he  was
declining to render any legal advice on the question posed at this time.  Upon a hypothetically phrased
general question with regard to whether the governing body adopts a resolution determining that an
area meets all six conditions for annexation, is the governing body then compelled to vote for the
related annexation ordinance, Mayor Kaysen requested Mr. White reply to the inquiry on a process
basis only.  Mr. White advised it would be helpful to conduct legal research on the topic, and stated
his initial impression is if the governing body adopts a resolution that finds that the Wyo. Stat. § 15-1-
402(a) annexation criteria have been met, the governing body could not later make a different finding
in the absence of a significant change of circumstances that would provide a substantive basis for the
change.  Comments followed and included: State statute wording regarding action on anne xation
ordinances; past actions on annexation ordinances following resolution adoptions determining that
conditions had been met; further legal review, and reason for postponing action at some point in the
annexation process to coincide with re-zoning and platting.  Mr. Allen moved to amend, seconded
by Mr. Collins, by adding the following language within the proposed resolution:  “The approval of
this resolution is not intended to and shall not be construed as modifying any of the components of
the Cheyenne Area Master Transportation Plan contained within PlanCheyenne, adopted in November
2006”.   M r. Cole spoke in o pposition to t he amendment, commenting that if the amendment is
approved the same wording should be included in other future annexation related resolutions.  Mr.
Murray spoke in support of the amendment, commenting that any transportation network plan should
comply with long range transportation plans adopted by the City and that the area is a very important
part of the  community and its g rowth.  Discussion followed on the per centage of the  area being
discussed vs. percentage of the proposed annexation property; use of land by property owners relative
to City and County boundaries; support for planning efforts, and whether resolution adoption would
be a commitment to the road plan depicted in Exhibit D.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Ashby expressed his
belief that definitive action on a road plan takes place during the platting process and that the master
(transportation) pla n is  int ended to  pr ovide fo r h aving a  ro ad n etwork in  pla ce a nd se rves a s a
guideline for open discussion to meet transportation needs.  Mr. Murray commented that the
amendment would pr ovide a history  to those new membe rs of the g overning body who will be
addressing the annexation or dinance next y ear.  Further comments included the topics of ro ad
network configuration; property owners’ competing interests, and potential changes to PlanCheyenne
due to the current review being conducted.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” -- Mr. Allen, Mr.
Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Valdez and Mayor Kaysen.  Voting “ no” -- Ms.
Ash, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Spiker.  Discussion on the main motion, as amended, followed and included
the following topics:  Condit ions/criteria being met for annexation vs. Exhibit D as a stree t issue,
overall area development for best interests of the community, and school district student capacity and
communication with the school district with regard to the development (apartment complex) planned
for t he parcel proposed to be  annexed.  Mr. Collins noted, for the re cord, that he hoped if the
governing body changes its mind in the future (City Clerk note: Regarding resolution adoption and
future annexation ordinance action) that it will not be considered to be arbitrary or capricious as the
discussion record reflects governing body’s concerns about the roads in the area and that an update
to the Master Transportation Plan may be made to r eflect area arterial and collector roads.  A lso
during discussion, Mr. Emmons again reviewed  postponement options to align with the platting time
frame, advising the goal is to start development proje ct construction next spring.  Main motion as
amended carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Rinne
voting “no”. (#5444)  Following announcement of the vote, Mayor Kaysen requested all interested
parties continue to look at the road networking, safety and topography issues to resolve.
[CA] RESOLUTION - A uthorizing the Gover ning Body of the City  of Chey enne to a dopt the
revised statement of investment policy.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5445)
RESOLUTION - Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to execute: a State Small Business
Credit Initiative (“SSBCI”) Allocation Agreement with the United States Department of Treasury;
a Cooperative Agreement among seventeen Wyoming Municipalities to provide for the administration
of SSBCI funding in accordance with Federal requirements; and a Service Agreement under which
Wyoming Smart Ca pital N etwork, LLC, w ill a ssist i n im plementation a nd ov ersight o f S SBCI
Program Funding -- referred to Finance Committee.  Mr. Brown advised the item was reviewed under
other items for the agenda at the Nov. 5  Finance Committee meeting and provisions of Title 2, Cityth
Code, had be en met.  Mr. B rown moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Valde z.  Upon inquiry , Dan
White, City Attorney, advised City Council had previously reviewed 3 agreements affiliated with the
resolution and since the form of some of the a greements had changed he felt the governing body
should review again for approval.  He further clarified the changes strengthen provisions in favor of
the participating municipalities.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body.
(#5446)
[CA] RESOLUTION - Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Chaplin
Park Annex, a replat of Lots 1-6 and the 16-foot vacated alley, Block 16, Park Addition, Cheyenne,
Wyoming (located between Richardson and Cosgriff Courts, and between Dey Avenue and Ames
Court) -- referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor - Ms. Ash).
[CA] RESOLUTION - Re-appropriating the Fiscal Year 2013 budget of the City of Cheyenne
according to the provisions of W.S . §16-4-112 and 16-4-113 - - referred to  Finance Commit tee
(sponsor - Mr. Brown).
[CA] RESOLUTION - Directing the Solid Waste Division to provide curbside collection services
for automated containers for all residential addresses in the city, except for certain addresses where
curbside collection is not feasible -- referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor - Mr. Brown).
[CA]  RESOLUTION - Approving Outside User Water/Sewer Services, by User’s Agreement, with
the Microsoft Corporation, Lot 3, Block 6, North Range Business P ark, Third Fi ling,  L aramie
County, Wyoming -- referred to Finance Committee (sponsor - Mr. Valdez).
[CA] Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and RBC Global Asset Management (U.S.) Inc. to
provide investment advisory services (Solid W aste, 2007-2010, 2011- 2014 1% Sales Ta x & 1%
Specific Purpose Tax).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5925)
[CA] Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Transit Division, and Stride Learning Center for
use of a 2006 Chevrolet El Dora do bus for ser vices for  Stride clients -- r eferred to Financ e
Committee. 
[CA] Professional Servic es Ag reement betwee n the City  of Ch eyenne, Parks &  Recre ation
Department, and AVI, PC for design and engineering services on Polk Avenue greenway segment
(1% Specific Purpose Sales & Use Tax & Wyoming Business Council Community Enhancement
grant) -- referred to Finance Committee. 
[CA] Second Amendment to Contract #4966 between the City of Cheyenne and Saddle Ridge, LLC,
pertaining to Saddle Ridge  Subdivis ion gr eenway sy stem improvements. Motion (per Consent
Agenda) carried. (#4966)
[CA] Consideration of B id #M-3-13 for  a contr act be tween the  City  of Chey enne, Par ks and
Recreation  Department, and S & S Builders, LLC, Cheyenne, Wyoming, for the Pioneer Park Parking
Lot Improvement Project (Parks Facilities funds) -- referred to Finance Committee. 
Appointments of Robert Mathia and Melissa Leger to the Downtown Development Authority
Board. Mr. B rown moved to a pprove, seconded b y Mr. Collins.  Upon inqui ry, Mayor Kaysen
clarified the appointments are to fulfill terms for individuals who were not able to complete their
appointed term, and explained the appointment process that involves review and recommendation of
proposed appointees by the Downtown Development Authority Board.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes”
--   all members of the governing body with the exception of Ms. Ash and Dr. Rinne voting “no” and
Mayor Kaysen who did not vote (Mayoral appointments).
[CA] Authorization to purchase Utility Rocket 5GHZ quadband communication equipment in the
amount of $167,999.72 from CDW- G for the Cheyenne Police Department (SLIB Funding).  Motion
(per Consent Agenda) carried (amount not to exceed $167,999.72).  
[CA] Designation of Official Voting Delegate and Alternate Delgate for the City of Cheyenne at
the 2013 Wyoming Association of Municipalities Winter Workshop Business Meeting -- referred to
Finance Committee.
Announcement w as ma de of  the  a ppointment o f C arla Th urin to the Laramie Cou nty
Community  Juvenile Services Joint Powers Board to be confirmed November 26, 2012.
Under other City business:
Brad Harrington commented on discussion held previously during the meeting regarding the
Resolution for conditions for annexation and stated he feels the entire planning process should be
reviewed.  He also expressed his belief that the City-owned area of the “downtown hole” should
either be sold or given away to those owning the other 2/3rds portion.
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was officially
adjourned at 7:29 p.m.
 Submitted by,
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle
 November 24, 2012

MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2012-11-26 | CLIP_ID: 343 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 343

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
 November 26, 2012
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil C hambers.  P resent w ere: M AYOR -  R ichard L.  K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS - Mr. Allen, Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne,
Mr. Spiker and Mr. Valdez.  Also present: Kristy Anderson, Deputy City Clerk; Lois Huff, City
Treasurer, and Dan White, City Attorney. 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda.  Mr. Collins moved to approve Consent Agenda items, seconded
by Mr. Brown.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body.
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on November 13, 2012.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Brown declared a conflict of interest (business interest in vouchers payable to Ameri-Tech
HVAC Services) and vacated Council Chambers.  Mr. Spiker moved to approve payment of vouchers
as presented, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing
body present in Council Chambers.  Following announcement of the vote, Mr. Brown returned to
Council Chambers.
  
ORDINANCE - Granting a Franchise by the City of Cheyenne to Cheyenne Light, Fuel and
Power Company, its successors and assigns, the right to furnish, sell and distribute electricity to the
City and to all persons, businesses, and industry within a portion of the City in Cheyenne Light, Fuel
and Power  Company’s Certificated Ter ritory and the r ight to ac quire, c onstruct, install, locate,
maintain, operate and extend into, within and through said City all facilities reasonably necessary to
furnish, sell and distribute electricity within the City and the right to make reasonable use of all streets
and other public places and public easements as herein defined as may be necessary; and fixing the
terms and conditions thereof -- referred to Finance Committee (sponsor - Mr. Brown).
ORDINANCE - Granting a Franchise by the City of Cheyenne to High West Energy, Inc., its
successors and assigns, the right to furnish, sell and distribute electricity to the City and to all persons,
businesses, and industry within a portion of the City in High West’s Certificated Territory and the
right to acquire, construct, install, locate, maintain, operate and extend into, within and through said
City all facilities reasonably necessary to furnish, sell and distribute electricity within the City and the
right to make reasonable use of all streets and other public places and public easements as herein
defined as may be necessary; and fixing the terms and conditions thereof -- referred to Public Services
Committee (sponsors - Mr. Brown). 
ORDINANCE - Pursuant to Section 2.2.1 Zoning Map Amendments, Section 5.1.2 Zoning
Districts Established and Section 5.1.3 Of ficial Zoning Map (Cheyenne City Map), of the Unified
Development Code, changing the zoning classification from MR-1 Medium Density Residential -
Established District to MUB Mixed Use with Business Emphasis District for Lots 30 and 31, Block
1, Eastridge, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located at the northwest corner of the intersection of East Pershing
Boulevard and Converse Avenue) -- referred to Public Services Committee (sponsors -- Mr. Allen,
Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Spiker, Mr. Valdez and
Mayor Kaysen).
[CA] RESOLUTION - Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Chaplin
Park Annex, a replat of Lots 1-6 and the 16-foot vacated alley, Block 16, Park Addition, Cheyenne,
Wyoming (located between Richardson and Cosgriff Courts, and between Dey Avenue and Ames
Court).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5447)
[CA] RESOLUTION - R e-appropriating the Fiscal Year 2013 budget of the City of Cheyenne
according to the provisions of W.S. §16-4-112 and 16-4-113.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
(#5448)
 RESOLUTION - Directing the Solid Waste Division to provide curbside collection services
for automated containers for all residential addresses in the city, except for certain addresses where
curbside collection is not feasible.  Speaking in opposition to the proposed resolution were:  Matthew
Potter, Frank Cole, Mike Luna, Trish Becklinger, Randy Byers, Paula Gordinier, John Rogers, Mike
Hand (submitted petition - on file with City Clerk’s office), Dennis Auker, Kenneth Barrow, Brad
Emmons (submitted photos - on file with City Clerk’s office), Don Erickson and Jan Nelson-Schroll.
The following conce rns wer e ra ised:  hardship on re sidents involving lack of  acc ess to move
containers from bac k to front of re sidence; lack of stora ge areas in fr ont of reside nces; need for
implementation of rules re garding placement of garbage cans; refuse debris due to wind;  nar row
street widths in some areas and sanitation truck operators maneuvering around parked cars and motor
homes, and traffic congestion; addressing pick-up concerns relative to overgrown trees in alley ways
obstructing pathways of trucks; home owners responsibility for trimming trees in alleys; definition
of “feasibility” in relationship to exemptions; containers left in the street if resident is out of town;
containers in streets detra cting from community  bea utification; z oning a nd UDC (Unifie d
Development Code) re quirements which ma y conflict with the re solution, and issues with heavy
traffic and highly dense areas involving parked cars on streets.  Upon inquiry, Jim Elias, Public Works
Director, advised the Solid Waste Director is still reviewing properties eligible for exemptions so the
list is not all inclusive at this time.  Reporting for Public Services Committee, Ms. Ash stated there
was no recommendation on the item from the committee.  Ms. Ash moved to adopt, seconded by Mr.
Pierson.  Discussion foll owed on the list of exempted properties, stre ets that should be on the
exempted list, and concerns with the impact on traffic patterns on busy streets such as Dell Range and
Pershing.  Upon inquiry, Dennis Pino, Director of Solid Waste, reviewed houses located on Dell
Range and Pershing Blvd. and advised they are still reviewing areas for exemptions, noting there will
still be some areas that will continue to have alley pick-ups.  In response to query on what benefits
the resolution will provide, Mr. Elias noted there would be an estimated 25% savings in fuel, future
equipment would be significantly less expensive as they could purchase single-arm vehicles instead
of dual-arm vehicles, alley maintenance would decrease, route efficiency would be realized, and a
decrease in insurance costs would be anticipated as trucks won’t have to maneuver in alleys, which
is where the majority of sanitation-related accidents occur.  Mr. Elias further added the department
is looking at getting GPS software packages for the trucks, which will assist with providing better
pick-up routes.  Mr. Pino explained incidents resulting in damages occur fairly regularly involving
alley trees and tree  branches.  He  explained depar tment efforts involving container pick-ups for
elderly or handicapped residents, who will remain exempted under the resolution.  Further discussion
continued on issues with Sanitation t rucks driving down alleys, including the cost inefficiency of
trucks running  both alley  and stree t routes, and the ne cessity to identify  additional  areas for
exemption.  Upon inquiry regarding a procedural question, Dan White, City Attorney, advised the
motion on the floor to adopt the resolution is now the “property” of the governing body and can only
be withdrawn with unanimous approval of the council.  Mr. Brown moved to call for the question (to
limit debate), seconded by Mr. Collins.  Mr. White clarified the motion was not debatable.  Motion
to call for the question to cease debate carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body

MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2012-12-10 | CLIP_ID: 345 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 345

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
 December 10, 2012
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil C hambers.  P resent w ere: M AYOR -  R ichard L.  K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS - Mr. Allen, Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne,
Mr. Spiker and Mr. Valdez.  Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Lois Huff, City Treasurer,
and Dan White, City Attorney. 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda. Upon request by Mr. Collins, and pursuant to support received by
Mr. Pierson and Dr . Rinne, ag enda item #24( c) was removed from the Consent Ag enda.  U pon
request by Ms. Broyles, and pursuant to support received by Mr. Collins and Mr. Pierson, agenda
item #12 was removed from the Consent Agenda.  Mr. Collins moved to approve remaining Consent
Agenda items, seconded by  Mr. B rown.  Motion car ried.  Voting  “yes” -- all member s of the
governing body.
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on November 26, 2012.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Brown declared a conflict of interest (business interest in voucher payable to Ameri-Tech
HVAC Service s) and va cated Co uncil Chambers.  Mr. V aldez moved to approve  payment of
vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of
the governing body present in Council Chambers.  Following announcement of the vote, Mr. Brown
returned to Council Chambers.
Mayor Kaysen opened a public hearing to receive comments and input for a Bar and Grill
liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s office for The Suite, LLC d/b/a The Suite, 1901
Central Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming.  Upon inquiry , Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk, clar ified the
current licensee at the pr emises is a diffe rent bu siness entity than this applicant and ha s been
operating under a Bar and Grill liquor license.  She stated that if this application is approved, The
Suite, LLC will be issued a new Bar and Grill liquor license and the current license for the site will
be returned to the City, keeping the same number of available Bar and Grill liquor licenses (i.e. 3).
Ms. Intlekofer advised The Suite, L LC is a new re staurant operation.  Ther e being no further
comments and the purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Kaysen closed the hearing and
referred the application to Finance Committee.
 
Mr. Collins m oved to cha nge the or der of  the ag enda to b ring forward the or dinance
pertaining to granting of a franchise to High West Energy, Inc. before the ordinance pertaining to
granting of a franchise to Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power Company, noting that action that may be
taken on the High West Energy franchise may affect discussion and action on the item involving the
Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power  franchise, seconded by Ms. Ash.  I n response to a proc edural
inquiry, Dan White, City Attorney, reviewed provisions of Robert’s Rules of Order relative to the
motion and customary  and usual pra ctices of the g overning body, and advise d if there  was no
objection from City Council members, the motion was procedurally in order.  Following inquiry by
Mayor Kaysen and with no objection raised by City Council members, motion carried.  Voting “yes”
-- all members of the governing body.
ORDINANCE - Granting a Franchise by the City of Cheyenne to High West Energy, Inc.,
its successors and assigns, the right to furnish, sell and distribute electricity to the City and to all
persons, businesses, and industry within a portion of the City in High West’s Certificated Territory
and the r ight to ac quire, construct, install, locate, ma intain, operate and e xtend into, within and
through said City all facilities reasonably necessary to furnish, sell and distribute electricity within
the City and the right to make reasonable use of all streets and other public places and public
easements as herein defined as may be necessary; and fixing the terms and conditions thereof.  Upon
request by Mayor Kaysen, a brief informational review of the process that resulted in the proposed
ordinance, as well as the proposed ordinance for granting a franchise to Cheyenne Light, Fuel and
Power Company (CLFP), was provided by Dan White, City Attorney.  Mr. White also discussed the
following five topics affiliated with both of the proposed franchise ordinances: Franchi se fees;
relationship between the proposed franchise ordinance for CLFP and its request for reimbursement
from the City, under current franchise provisions, for recently discovered overpayments of certain
customers’ franchise fees; main issue of whether the City wants to franchise another provider (i.e.
High West Energy) for electric services within the Ci ty; proposed agreement between CLFP and
High West Energy (HWE) regarding the division of service territories, creating essentially a non-
competition concept, and benefits of having the division of territories approved by the Public Service
Commission (PSC), and rate regulation regarding “fairness” issues relative to HWE’s rates not being
subject to regulation by the PSC, and CLFP rates being subject to regulation by the PSC.  During his
comments, Mr. White advised that legal staff would probably be proposing an amendment for each
ordinance to clar ify what “approval” means with re gard to the PSC and service  territorie s as
contained in the concluding paragraphs of the ordinances.  Brian Heithoff, general manager, High
West Energy, Inc., stated that HWE currently serves 14 accounts within the City limits; provided a
brief overview of the company ’s organizational structure, of fice locations and s ites served, and
advised rates are set and regulated by a Board of Directors.  He noted tha t HWE wishes to serve
future annexed areas to the City within its certificated territory, and that the company is able to serve
additional customers.  Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Brown moved to approve on second
reading, seconded by Mr. Pierson.  Mr. B rown moved to amend by substitute ordinance, which
includes the amendment made at the Dec. 3, 2012 Finance Committee meeting that removes the
proposed franchise fee increase, seconded by Mr. Spiker.  Da le Steenbergen, Greater Cheyenne
Chamber of Commerce, spoke in opposition to any franchise fee increases at this time, referencing
the need to keep local taxes low, the effect of increases on community businesses and economic
development competitiveness, noting a letter dated Dec. 10, 2012 from Cheyenne LEADS that had
been submitted on the topic of economic expansion considerations (on file with office of City Clerk).
Discussion followed and included the following topics: Comments in support as well as non-support
of the proposed amendment; franchise fees assessed by other Wyoming and regional municipalities;
purpose of franchise fees; fees as a “pass through” charge to ratepayers; City street and right-of-way
maintenance expense concerns; limited City revenue generation options available pursuant to state
statutes; proposed incremental fee increases over the 25 year term of the franchise ordinance; past
revenue amounts received by the City pursuant to the current franchise ordinance with C LFP;
capability of “re-opening” the franchise ordinance fee provision to potentially amend (increase) fees
in the future if desired; unknown stability of the utility market involving costs for services; other
increased costs to consumers (ex: fuel); incremental franchise fee increases, and number of current
HWE customers within the City with future customers affiliated only with new annexed areas.
During discussion and upon inquiry, clarification was made of the motion on the floor, which would
amend HWE’s fr anchise fees to be 3 perc ent for the  entire franchise term with no incrementa l
increases.  Upon inquiry, Lois Huff, City Treasurer, advised franchise fees received are credited to
the general fund.  Motion to amend by substitute failed.  Voting “yes” -- Ms. Ash, Dr. Rinne and Mr.
Spiker.  Voting “no” -- Mr. Allen, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Valdez
and Mayor Kaysen.  Pursuant to inquiry, Mark Stege, Vice President of Operations, Cheyenne Light,
Fuel and Power Company , briefly reviewed the history of discussions and neg otiations between
CLFP and HWE pursuant to pre vious request by the governing body, and a pr oposed settlement
agreement involving service territories for each entity to be approved by the governing body and the
PSC, and noted that CLFP has no objection to the City granting a franchise to HWE.  Discussion
followed on pa st requests by  HWE for a  City franchise; concerns with community  growth and
customers being served by two providers with differing rates and policies; unknown dependability
of HWE’s services; rate setting approval and regulations by a private Board of Directors vs. the PSC;
issues of fairness; rural vs. urban lifestyles and conditions; entity partnerships and community
contributions, and providing HWE the opportunity to provide services within its certificated area.
Questions arose concerning certain sections of the proposed ordinance, applicable to both HWE and
CLFP franchise ordinances, regarding whether the ordinance, if approved on final reading, could be
amended or terminate d in the future a s noted in Section 14. 1, For feiture, of the ordina nce;
clarification regarding waiving of City building permit fees as outlined in Section 3.5, Franchise Fee
Payment in Lieu of Other Fees and Charges, and Section 4.5 (b) relative to abandoned facilities and
further legal review of what would be required for an abandoned facility to be removed at the cost
of the franchise service provider.  In response to the questions raised, Mr. White expressed his legal
belief that Section 14.1 of the ordinance, considered to be a contract, provides for termination only
for cause, such as failure of the franchisee to fulfill provisions contained in the ordinance.  He stated
as Section 3.5 begins with the phrase “... In connection with the operation of facilities to furnish, sell
and distribute electricity within the City ..”, if the franchisee is constructing a building structure all
of the regular permit fee requirements would apply, noting additional clarification to this section
could be done if needed.  Upon query and there being no objection voiced by City Council members,
Mayor Kaysen requested a representative for HWE and CLFP each provide their interpretation of
what the word “abandoned” meant to their respective company operations with respect to Section
4.5 (b).  Mr. Heithoff stated abandonment to them means that when they have a service location that
is no longe r used f or a pe riod of time and ther e’s no r eal future use f or the ser vice, it would be
removed, and clarified, upon inquiry, that measures would be taken so the property would not pose
any safety concerns.  Randy Leinen, Director of Operations, CLFP, stated delving deeper into what
abandonment means may be needed, and cited an example of a former physical building facility
within the Cit y that the company  had vac ated a nd h ad subsequently made dr ainage and othe r
property improvements to alleviate abandonment conditions.  He noted that abandonment could also
mean a service line that is no longer used or has failed, advising in many instances CLFP won’t dig
up a City street to remove an underground line as damage would be more expensive than leaving the
line in place.  It was noted that an abandoned service line scenario is different than an abandoned
physical (building) facility.  Pursuant to inquiry, Mr. Heithoff provided information on the following:
Composition of HWE’s Board of Directors (seven members with each Director representing a
geographically located dis trict which c urrently includes the a reas of Chey enne, H illsdale and
PineBluffs, WY; Hereford, CO, and Kimball and Potter, NE); Board delegation of authority of some
areas of ope rations to Mr. Heith off with other ar eas, including customer rate issues, being  the
Board’s responsibility; fairness issue; current customers within the City wishing to continue with
services provided by HWE; class of service type and amount of energy used as factors in determining
fees, and the company’s reliability record.  During discussion, question was raised on whether the
governing body has the legal authority to make a final decision on which entity (i.e. HWE or CLFP)
could provide service to a specific area that was annexed in the future.  Mr. White expressed his
understanding that if the agreement between HWE and CLFP is approved, both by the City Council
for the issuance of dual franchises and then by the PSC, and a future annexation(s) occurs, those
customers in the annexed area would have to be served by the entity approved by the PSC for that
certificated area and that the governing body, on its own, does not have decision-making authority
to change each entity’s approved service area without consent of the PS C.  He a dded his further
understanding that the PSC, as a matter of law, retains jurisdiction to alter certificated territories.
Randy Reed, legal counsel for HWE, stated the statutes regarding the topic are less than a “model
of clarity” and expressed HWE’s position that the City does have and retains authority to determine
what electric utilities operate within its corporate boundaries under home rule (state constitution) and
state statutes.  He further noted that Section 14.3 of the franchise ordinance indicates the City retains
all legal remedies that it would otherwise have under law, and that he believes one of those remedies
would be the right to repeal the franchise ordinance.  John Sundahl, attorney for CLFP, stated a
franchise ordinance is a contract between the parties and if, for example, a franchisee has a vested
financial interest and provides services within its certificated area, it was his belief that the City
could not revoke/terminate the franchise, commenting that potential legal liability to the City could
occur.  He also indicated if the governing body wanted to address the right to revoke or terminate,
it should be more specifically worded in the franchise ordinance for review by PSC.  He expressed
his opinion that the PSC has continuing jurisdiction, and advised that he wouldn’t rely on the ability
of the City  to take bac k a franchise once granted.  Motion to approve the or dinance on second
reading failed (due to a tie vote).  Voting “yes” -- Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Pierson
and Mr. Valdez.  Voting “no” -- Mr. Allen, Mr. Collins, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Spiker and Mayor Kaysen.
Following announcement of the vote, Mr. Brown raised a point of orde r requesting procedural
clarification pertaining to the f uture status of the agenda item due to the motion failing.  May or
Kaysen advised the item, pursuant to the current meeting’s process, will not be moving forward for
further review or action at either the next Finance Committee meeting or the next City Council
meeting.
ORDINANCE - Granting a Franchise by the City of Cheyenne to Cheyenne Light, Fuel and
Power Company, its successors and assigns, the right to furnish, sell and distribute electricity to the
City and to all persons, businesses, and industry within a portion of the City in Cheyenne Light, Fuel
and Power Company’s Certificated T erritory and the r ight to ac quire, construct, install, locate,
maintain, operate and extend into, within and through said City all facilities reasonably necessary
to furnish, sell and distribute electricity within the City and the right to make reasonable use of all
streets and other public places and public easements as herein defined as may be necessary; and
fixing the terms and conditions thereof.  Upon confirmation by Dan White, City Attorney, Mayor
Kaysen advised that information provided and issues discussed by Mr. White prior to discussion on
the previous agenda item pertaining to the franchise ordinance for High West Energy (HWE) also
applied to this item.  Mark Stege, Vice President of Operations, Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power
Company, explained the Nov. 20, 2012 filing for a new franchise agreement involves an electrical
services franchise only and, if approved by the governing body, then filing for a natural gas franchise
would follow.  He requested approval of the ordinance and reviewed examples of the company’s
assistance over the years with local economic development efforts; commented on CLFP’s service
reliability; noted improvements and projects the company has completed, as well as current and
future projects and investments in the community, to provide for the future supply of electricity and
natural gas, and stated the company has been a community partner for 130 years.  Mr. Brown moved
to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Mr. Brown moved to amend by substitute
ordinance, which includes the amendment made at the Dec. 3, 2012 Finance Committee meeting that
removes the proposed franchise fee increase, seconded by Mr. Spiker.  Dale Steenbergen, Greater
Cheyenne Chamber of Commerce, commented in opposition to a significant increase in tax burden
on businesses, total tax areas affecting businesses, the need to have the ability to c ompete with
recruitment of businesses with re gard to economic de velopment, and c oncern with a 25 y ear
commitment to increased taxes under the proposed franchise term.  Sam McKeown, Norco, Inc.,
expressed his belief the City has become, over time, more regressive toward business, and spoke in
opposition to any increased costs to busi nesses and current economy concerns.  May or Kaysen
thanked Mr. McKeown for his email comments received earlier in the day (on file with office of City
Clerk).  Discussion followed on the amount of revenue the City has received over the past 20 years
in franchise revenues from CLFP, support as well as non-support for the proposed amendment and
new f ranchise ordinanc e g enerally, and status of the c urrent CL FP fra nchise ordina nce if  the
proposed ordinance should fail.  Upon inquiry, Mr. White advised if the proposed ordinance fails,
the current franchise ordinance (Ordinance No. 3146) would remain in effect.  Motion to amend by
substitute carried.  Voting “yes” -- Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Mr. Collins, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Sp iker, Mr.
Valdez and Mayor Kaysen.  Voting “no” -- Mr. Allen, Ms. Broyles and Mr. Pierson.  In response to
inquiry, Mr. Stege verified expiration date of the current franchise ordinance is Dec. 31, 2016, and
clarified CLFP was seeking a new agreement at this time due to HWE’s  request for a franchise
ordinance and the desire to have concurrent agreements between the two utility entities, and was also
due to CLFP’s significant investment in its new Cheyenne generation substation relative to a new
long term franchise agreement.  It was noted that CLFP started its process for the new generation
substation approximately 1 ½ years ago.  Main motion to approve the ordinance, as amended, on
second reading failed.  Voting “yes” -- Mr. Collins, Mr. Spiker and Mr. Valdez.  Voting “no” -- Mr.
Allen, Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne and Mayor Kaysen.
ORDINANCE - Pursuant to Section 2.2.1 Zoning Map Amendments, Section 5.1.2 Zoning
Districts Established and Section 5.1.3 Official Zoning Map (Cheyenne City Map), of the Unified
Development Code, changing the zoning classification from MR-1 Medium Density Residential -

    RESOLUTION - Authorizing t he C ity Treasurer to discharge uncollectible debts in the
amount of $247,178.18, pursuant to Wyo. Stat. §16-4-502.  Mr. Brown moved to adopt, seconded
by Mr. Valdez.  Upon inquiry regarding procedures utilized in collecting debts and whether the debts
to be discharged could continue to be collected if the resolution was adopted, Lois Huff, Ci ty
Treasurer, clarified even though the debts would be written-off, the City can continue to pursue
collection for  payment.  She revie wed c ollection eff orts by staff a nd stated re vised collec tion
procedures are being reviewed, noting implementation of a new accounts receivable system will
assist with better tracking and querying capabilities.  U pon inquiry, Dan White, City Attorney,
advised asserting liens against property is governed by state statute and c areful review would be
needed to determine whether that could be utilized, and stated once an uncollectible is sent to the
City’s collection agency, the City  can’t take it back unle ss the ag ency agrees.  Upon additional
inquiry during discussion, Mr. White advised he has been researching the law to determine whether
the list of debto r names can be published in the future .  Discussion topics included: Bulk of
uncollectibles due to charges at the landfill and sanitation; age of accounts on the list proposed to
be discharged; debt accumulation under different personal or business names, and revised collection
procedures per Ms. Huff’s comments.  Ms. Huff provided information on the measures that may be
instituted to assist with reduced future uncollectibles, and the aggregate amount of uncollectible debt
for the past few years.  Upon inquiry, Mayor Kaysen clarified internal review for the collection of

the intersection of Cribbon Avenue and West 28  Street, consisting of approximately 8,451 squareth
feet (estimated value  o f $30,000.00), and pa yment of ca sh considera tion in ex change for  rea l
property owned by Christensen’s, Inc., consisting of approximately 52,990 square feet (estimated
value of $188,100.00), generally located west of Cribbon Avenue near the intersections of Cribbon
Avenue and Talbot Court and Dodge Court, Cheyenne, Wyoming -- referred to Finance Committee
(sponsors - Mr. Allen, Ms. Ash, Mr. Valdez).
[CA] Preliminary Plat for Okie Addition, First Filing, a portion of Section 28, T.14N., R.67W., 6th
P.M., C heyenne, Wy oming ( located a t t he n ortheast c orner o f th e in tersection o f E . Pe rshing
Boulevard and Windmill Road) -- referred to Public Services Committee.
[CA] Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Public Works Department, and KONE, Inc. for
maintenance service on various elevators in City buildings.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
(#5930)  
[CA] Community Based Family Support and Preser vation Grant Contract betwe en the City  of
Cheyenne, Youth Alter natives, and the  Wy oming De partment of F amily Service s, Protection
Services Division, to provide in-home support and mentoring services to under-served families and
strengthen the ability of parents to provide care for their children.  Motion (per Consent Agenda)
carried. (#5931)
Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Public Works Department,
and Solid W aste Professionals of Wy oming, for Happy Jack Landfill Expansion and closure of
existing cells (Solid Waste Management fund).  Mr. Brown moved to approve in an amount not to
exceed $1,683,483.40, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Comments followed in support of the agreement
to address landfill issues for the future.  Upon inquiry, Jim Elias, Public Works Director, advised he
is hopeful a portion of the new cells will be operational by Sept. 2015, noting that estimated date
would coincide with the end date of the solid waste contract involving the Ault, CO site.  He also
provided fur ther information on the landfill project, including  the anticipate d maxi mum life
expectancy of the new cells and potential funding through the  State Revolving Loan Fund program,
stating the project will be completed in phases.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Elias stated there may be other
possibilities for the future and other options are continually being reviewed with regard to the issue
of solid waste.  M ayor Kaysen added that future technology may also present an opportunity to
pursue reduced landfill costs.  Motion carried.  Voting "yes" -- all members of the governing body.
(#5932)
[CA] Agreement betwee n the City  of C heyenne and The L amar Companies, Ba ton Rouge ,
Louisiana, for placement of billboard advertising signs -- referred to Finance Committee. 
[CA] Grant Award Ag reement betwee n the City  of Chey enne a nd the Wy oming Of fice of
Homeland Security for a grant in the amount of $100,000 for the City of Cheyenne Fire and Rescue
Department (Region 7 State Regional Emergency Response Team) -- referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Agreement be tween th e City  of  Che yenne, O ffice of  Yo uth Al ternatives, a nd L aramie
County, Wyoming, for juvenile probation services -- referred to Finance Committee. 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-5-13 for furnishing one new brush chipper for the Forestry Division
from Vermeer Colorado, Commerc e City, Colorado (2011- 2014 1%  Sales Tax ).  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried (amount not to exceed $37,004.00 with trade-in). 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-12-13 for f urnishing one new aerial platform fire apparatus and
small equipment for the City of Cheyenne Fire & Rescue Department (State Loan and Investment
Board grant, 2011- 2014 1% Sales Tax).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (accept bid submitted
by Front Range Fire, Frederick, CO; amount not to exceed $1,061.882.00 with trade-in).
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-6-13 for furnishing one new 2012-2013 airless truck mounted paint
striping mac hine for the  Traf fic Division (2011-2014 1%  Sales Tax) -- re ferred to Financ e
Committee.
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-15-13 for furnishing 120 portable radios, installing one vehicular
charger a nd trading  in 120 surplus Motorola p ortable radios for  the City  of Chey enne, Police
Department (1% Specific Purpose Sales & Use Tax) -- referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-9-13 for furnishing one new 2013 rubber tire front end loader and
trading in one salvaged 2004 Caterpillar 924G for the City of Cheyenne, Sanitation and Landfill
Divisions (Solid Waste Management fund & insurance) -- referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Diagonal Parking Permit application filed with  the City Clerk’s off ice by Chaplin Park
Development Group, LLC, requesting approval of implementation of diagonal parking spaces along
Dey Avenue in association with the renovation of the historic Chaplin School project -- referred to
Public Services Committee. 
 Appointments of Tyler Bedwell, Savannah Brown, Jon Chenchar, Alex Cole, Kadi Davis,
Ian Dome, Juliette Givhan, Alex Farkas, Addie Fleming, John Matsen, Margarita Medrano, Rachel
Moseley and Jacob Peterson to the Mayor’s Youth Council.  Mr. Allen moved to approve, seconded
by Mr. Collins.  Voting “yes” --  all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor
Kaysen who did not vote (Mayoral appointments).
Announcement was made that due to the Christmas holiday, the December 24, 2012 regularly
scheduled meeting of the Governing Body will instead be held on Thursday, December 20, 2012
beginning at Noon in City Council Chambers.  Finance and Public Services Committees will be held
at their usual times, 11:00 a.m. and 12:00 p.m. re spectively, on Monday, December 17, 2012 and
Tuesday, December 18, 2012 in Room 122, Municipal Building.
Announcement was mad e of the Appointments of Victor ia J. Fry, Megin Rux and  F red
Lacey III to the Cheyenne Historic Preservation Board, and Dr. Brad Kincheloe to the Cheyenne
Laramie County Board of Health, to be confirmed December 20, 2012. 
Announcement was made of the Re-appointments of Randy Byers, Bob Clary and Michael
Peel to the B uilding Code B oard of Appeals; Tony Adams and A nn Redman to the Personnel
Commission; Kurt Zunker to the Fire Civil Service Commission; Cindy Pomeroy to the Police Civil
Service Commission; Don Threewitt and Kelly Buchhammer to the Cheyenne Historic Preservation
Board; Maynard J. Richmeier to the Cheyenne Housing Authority; Ted Gertsch, Leland G. Clabots
and Carol Wurdemann to the Housing & Community Development Advisory Council, and Michael
O’Donnell to the Board of Adjustment, to be confirmed December 20, 2012. 
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held December 20, 2012 at 12:00 p.m.
in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, for the purpose of receiving
public comment on the proposed trade of real property owned by the City of Cheyenne, being a
parcel of land on the west side of Cribbon Avenue near the intersection of Cribbon Avenue and West
28th Street. The proposed parcel to be traded for real property owned by Christensen’s Inc., situated
along Cribbon Avenue near the intersections of Cribbon Avenue and Talbot Court and Dodge Court.
Under other business:
Mayor Kaysen advised of an additional item for the agenda due to timeliness involved with
the item and requested Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk, read the title of the item as follows:  Wellness
Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and WINhealth Partners for WINhealth Partners
Wellness Program services.  Mayor Kaysen referred the item to Finance Committee.
Brad Ha rrington re ferenced p ast co mments m ade a t p revious C ity C ouncil m eetings
regarding concerns with [United Nations] Agenda 21 by himself and governing body members,
noting a recent public meeting that had been held organized by future County Commissioner M. Lee
Hasenauer.  He reviewed communications with governing body members since those meetings, and
expressed he would like to move forward with discussion on his concerns regarding freedoms and
individual rights.  Mr. Harrington challenged the mayor to a public debate on the topic, and extended
an invitation to governing body members to attend.  Mayor Kaysen advised that the request has been
noted.   
There being  no further  business to come bef ore the  g overning body, the meeting  was
officially adjourned at 8:56 p.m.
 Submitted by,
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle
 December 20, 2012

---
