MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2012-12-20 | CLIP_ID: 347 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 347

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
 December 20, 2012
Due to t he holiday season, the Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne instead met in
regular session on this date beginning at 12:00 p.m. in Council Chambers.  Present were: MAYOR -
Richard L. Kaysen; COUNCIL MEMBERS - Mr. Allen, Ms. Ash, Mr. B rown, Ms. Broyles, Mr.
Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne (arriving at 12:45 p.m.), Mr. Spiker and Mr. Valdez.  Also present:
Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Lois Huff, City Treasurer, and Dan White, City Attorney. 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda. Upon request by Mr. Brown, and pursuant to support received by
Mr. Collins and Ms. Ash, ag enda item #20 was removed from the Consent Agenda.  Mr. Collins
moved to approve remaining Consent Agenda items, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Motion carried.
Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present.
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on December 10, 2012.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Valdez moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by Mr. Pierson.
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present.
Mayor Kaysen opened a public hearing for the purpose of receiving public comment on the
proposed trade of real property owned by the City of Cheyenne, being a parcel of land on the west
side of Cribbon Avenue near the intersection of Cribbon Avenue and West 28  Street. The proposedth
parcel to be traded for real property owned by Christensen’s Inc., situated along Cribbon Avenue
near the intersection of Cribbon Avenue and Talbot Court and Dodge Court.  Rick Parish, Director
of Parks and Recreation, reviewed the parcels of land involved in the proposed trade, which is
adjacent to Pioneer Park baseball facility, and briefly reviewed improvements that are being made
to the park area.  He explained that during the platting process it was determined that Christensen’s
Inc. was encroaching on a portion of City-owned property and, pursuant to discussions, it is proposed
to tr ade the City’s property (approximately 8,451 sq. ft.) for approximately 52,990 sq. ft. of
Christensen’s Inc. property (plus monetary cash consideration to make up the valuation difference).
He advised property appraisals have been completed on the parcels and noted benefits of the City
acquiring the land and developing it as green space for a playground with a picnic shelter.  He stated
the funding source for the cash consideration would be from money acquired from selling the City’s
property located near Windmill and Dell Range to Menard’s.  There being no further comments and
purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Kaysen closed the hearing.
 
ORDINANCE - Pursuant to Section 2.2.1 Zoning Map Amendments, Section 5.1.2 Zoning
Districts Established and Section 5.1.3 Official Zoning Map (Cheyenne City Map), of the Unified
Development Code, changing the zoning classification from MR-1 Medium Density Residential -
Established District to MUB Mixed Use with Business Emphasis District for Lots 30 and 31, Block
1, E astridge, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located at the northwest corner of the intersection of  Ea st
Pershing Boulevard and Converse Avenue).  Reporting for Public Services Committee, Ms. Ash
moved to approve on third and final r eading, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Motion carried.  Voting
“yes” -- all members of the governing body present. (#3963)
ORDINANCE - Pursuant to Section 2.2.1 Zoning Map Amendments, Section 5.1.2 Zoning
Districts Established, and Sectio n 5.1.3 Official Zoning Map of the Unifie d Development Code,
changing the zoning classification from P Public District to CBD Central Business District for Lot
1, Block 1, 2100 Pioneer Subdivision, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located at 2100 Pioneer Avenue).  Ms.
Ash moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  In response to inquiry, Ben
Trautwein, Caldwell Banker, explained the purpose of the zone c hange request is to enhance the
ability to sell  the property.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body
present. 
ORDINANCE - Amending Section 12.16.020, Planting of certain species of trees and shrubs
in public rights-of-way - Limited, of Chapter 12.16, Trees and Shrubs, of Title 12, Streets, Sidewalks
and Public Places, of the Cheyenne City Code pertaining to the planting of certain trees within the
tree lawn area -- referred to Public Services Committee (sponsor - Ms. Ash).
 
[CA] RESOLUTION - Re- appropriating the Fiscal Year 2013 budg et of the City  of Cheyenne
according to the provisions of W.S. §16-4-112 and 16-4-113.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
(#5451)
RESOLUTION - Designating local banks as depositories for municipal funds.  Mr. Collins
and Mr. Spiker each declared a conflict of interest (board member affiliation with certain financial
institutions) and vacated Council Chambers.  Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Brown moved
to adopt, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing
body present in Council C hambers.  Following  announcement of the vot e, Mr. Collins and Mr.
Spiker returned to Council Chambers. (#5452)
RESOLUTION - Designating the Sundays during 2013 that annual liquor lice nsees may
extend dispensing room hours of oper ation for sa les until 2:00 a.m. the following da y.  Br yan
Grzegorczyk, President, Laramie County Liquor Association,  reviewed the dates of the four Sundays
being requested (Feb. 3, Super Bowl; March 17, St. Patrick’s Day; July 21, first Sunday of Frontier
Days, a nd Nov. 10, Sunday before Veterans Day).  He spoke in support of the resolution and
provided information on the Association’s safe ride (taxi) for patrons program and the Association’s
various fund raisers and charity work benefitting the community.  Mr. Brown reported there was no
recommendation on the item from Finance Committee.  Mr. Brown moved to adopt, seconded by
Mr. Collins.  Comments followed in opposition to the extension of Sunday hours as well as
appreciation for the positive programs and projects promoted by the Association.  Motion carried.
Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present with the exception of Ms. Broyles, Mr.
Pierson and Mr. Spiker voting “no”. (#5453)
RESOLUTION - To name the parking structure located between Carey and Pioneer Avenues
and 16  (i.e. Lincolnway) and 17  Streets in the City of Cheyenne as the “Jack R. Spiker Downtownth th
Parking Structure”.  Mr. Spiker declared a conflict of interest and vacated Council Chambers.  Ms.
Ash reported there was no recommendation on the item from Public Services Committee.  Ms. Ash
moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Comments followed on the lack of standards for naming
City parks and structures, the number of years Mr. Spiker has served the community as its Mayor
and as a member of City Council, and the numerous projects and improvements Mr. Spiker has been
involved in of benefit to the community .  Motion carr ied.  Voting  “yes” -- all member s of the
governing body present in Council Chambers.  Following announcement of the vote, Mr. Spiker
returned to Council Chambers.  Mayor Kaysen advised a date will be scheduled in the future for the
dedication of naming the structure. (#5454)
                                                   
[CA] RESOLUTION - Certifying that the Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne has agreed
upon the Laramie County Projects to be submitted to the State Loan and Investment Board for the
February 2013 meeting  for County wide Consensus B lock Gra nt Funding  in the amount  of
$721,407.86.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5455)
[CA] RESOLUTION - Certifying that the Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne has agreed
upon the Town of Pine Bluffs Projects to be submitted to the State Loan and Investment Board for
the February 2013 meeting  for County wide Consensus B lock Grant Funding in the amount of
$161,000.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5456)
[CA] RESOLUTION - Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a County Final Plat for
Swan Ranch Rail Park, 6  Filing, a portion of Sections 22, 23 and 27, T.13N., R.67W., 6  P.M.,th th
Laramie County, Wyoming (located west of Clear Creek Parkway, south of Overland Trails Business
Park Subdivision).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5457)
[CA] RESOLUTION - Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a County Final Plat for
Trinity Estates, a portion of the W½SE¼, Section 1, T.14N., R.67W., 6th P.M., Laramie County,
Wyoming (located east of and adjacent to I-25, north of Riding Club Road).  Motion (per Consent
Agenda) carried. (#5458) 
[CA] RESOLUTION - Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a County Final Plat for
Arp Elementary School, 1st Filing, a replat of Lots 1 and 12, Block 3, Niobrara Energy Park, and a
portion o f t he S W¼ o f t he N W¼ o f S ection 9 , T .13N., R .66W., 6 th P .M., Laramie C ounty,
Wyoming (located east of and adjacent to Reiner Court, between Hinkley Drive and E. Allison
Road).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5459)
RESOLUTION - Authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk of the City of Cheyenne to enter into
an agreement for the trade of real property owned by the City of Cheyenne to Christensen’s, Inc., a
Wyoming corporation, described as a parcel of land generally located west of Cribbon Avenue near
the intersection of Cribbon Avenue and West 28  Street, consisting of approximately 8,451 squareth
feet (estimated value of $30,000.00), and pa yment of ca sh considera tion in ex change for  rea l
property owned by Christensen’s, Inc., consisting of approximately 52,990 square feet (estimated
value of $188,100.00), generally located west of Cribbon Avenue near the intersections of Cribbon
Avenue and Talbot Court and Dodge Court, Cheyenne, Wyoming.  Mayor Kaysen advised this item
was related to the public hearing held earlier in the meeting.  Mr. Brown moved to adopt, seconded
by Mr. Valdez.  Motion carried.  Voting "yes" -- all members of the governing body present. (#5460)
[CA] RESOLUTION - Approving Outside User Water/Sewer Services, by User’s Agreement, with
Swan Ranch Properties, LLC, Lot One, Block 1, Energy Park One, Laramie County, Wyoming --
referred to Finance Committee (sponsor - Mr. Valdez).
[CA] RESOLUTION - Directing the City Clerk to schedule a Public Hearing pursuant to Section
5.12.040(2) of the Cheyenne City Code to receive public comment on violations of City ordinances
and state la ws pertaining to the sale of a lcoholic beverages, which violations have  occurred at
‘Mingles Bar’ and to provide a notice of said Public Hearing to Stillwater, Inc., dba ‘Mingles Bar’ --
referred to Finance Committee (sponsor - Ms. Broyles). 
Preliminary Plat for Okie Addition, First Filing, a portion of Section 28, T.14N., R.67W., 6th
P.M., Ch eyenne, Wy oming ( located a t t he n ortheast c orner o f th e in tersection o f E . Pe rshing
Boulevard a nd Windm ill R oad).  Ms. Ash moved to acknow ledge re ceipt with staff
recommendations #1 through 5, seconded by Ms. Broyles.  Mo tion carried.  Vo ting "yes" -- all
members of the governing body present.
[CA] Agreement betwee n the City  of Chey enne a nd The L amar Companies, Ba ton Rouge ,
Louisiana, for placement of billboard advertising signs.  M otion (per Consent Agenda) carried..
(#5939) 
[CA] Grant Awar d Ag reement betwee n the City  of Chey enne a nd the Wy oming Office of
Homeland Security for a grant in the amount of $100,000 for the City of Cheyenne Fire and Rescue
Department (Region 7 State Regional Emergency Response Team).  Motion (per Consent Agenda)
carried. (#5940)
[CA] Agreement b etween th e City  of  Che yenne, O ffice of  Yo uth Alternatives, a nd L aramie
County, Wyoming, for juvenile probation services.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5941)
Wellness Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and WINhealth Partners for
WINhealth Partners Wellness Program services.  Mr. Brown moved to approve, seconded by Mr.
Valdez.  Comments followed on the benefits that have resulted from the program and cost savings
that have been realized.  Motion carried.  Voting "yes" -- all members of the governing body present.
(#5942)
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne on behalf of the Cheyenne
Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO) and Transit Plus for the 2013 Transit Development Plan
for Cheyenne Transit Program (MPO Planning funds) -- referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Contract Modifica tion No. 3 to Cont ract No. 5496 bet ween the City  of Chey enne,
Engineering Department, and Ayres Associates for additional design services for the East Pershing
Boulevard reconstruction project (Phase IV) (2003-2006, 2007-2010 1% Sales Tax, Board of Public
Utilities, Federal Highway Administration funds) -- referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-6-13 for furnishing one new 2012-2013 airless truck mounted paint
striping machine for the Traffic Division (2011-2014 1% Sales Tax).  Motion (per Consent Agenda)
carried (a ccept bid from Peterbilt of Chey enne, WY for a total bid amount, with trade -in, of
$269,573.00).
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-15-13 for furnishing 120 portable radios, installing one vehicular
charger a nd trading  in 120 surplus Motorola portable r adios for the City of Chey enne, Police
Department (1% Specific Purpose Sales & Use Tax).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (accept
bid from Mot orola Solutions, W estminister, CO, for a total bid amount, with trade -ins, of
$589,708.00).
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-9-13 for furnishing one new 2013 rubber tire front end loader and
trading in one salvaged 2004 Caterpillar 924G for the City of Cheyenne, Sanitation and Landfill
Divisions (Solid Waste Manag ement fund &  insurance).  Motion (per Con sent Agenda) carried
(accept bid from Wyoming Machinery, Cheyenne, WY, for a total bid amount, with trade- in, of
$185,723.00).
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-8-13 for furnishing one new 2012-2013 backhoe loader from Titan
Machinery, Cheyenne, WY, for the Concrete Division (2011-2014 1% Sales Tax) -- referred to
Finance Committee.
[CA] Diagonal Parking Permit application filed with the City Clerk’s office by Chaplin Park
Development Group, LLC, requesting approval of implementation of diagonal parking spaces along
Dey Avenue in association with the renovation of the historic Chaplin School project.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
[CA] Bar and Grill liquor license application for The Suite, LLC d/b/a The Suite, 1901 Central
Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.
Appointments of Victoria J. Fry, Megin Rux and Fred Lacey III to the Cheyenne Historic
Preservation Board, and Dr. Brad Kincheloe to the Cheyenne Laramie County Board of Health.  Mr.
Collins moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing
body present with the exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not vote (Mayoral appointments).
Re-appointments of Randy Byers, Bob Clary and Michael Peel to the Building Code Board
of Appeals; Tony Adams and Ann Redman to the Personnel Commission; Kurt Zunker to the Fire
Civil Service Commission; Cindy Pomeroy to the Police Civil Service Commission; Don Threewitt
and Kelly Buchhammer to the Cheyenne Historic Preservation Board; Maynard J. Richmeier to the
Cheyenne Housing Authority; Ted Gertsch, Leland G. Clabots and Carol Wurdemann to the Housing
& Community Development Advisory Council, and Michael O’Donnell to the Board of Adjustment.
Mr. Collins m oved to appr ove, seconded by Ms. Broy les.  Voting  “yes” -- all members of the
governing bod y present with the exception of May or Ka ysen who did not vote (Ma yoral
appointments).
 
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held January 14, 2013, at 6:00 p.m. in
City Council Chambers to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyo.
Stat. §15-1-402 exist for a parcel of land being situated in a portion of the east half of the east half
of Section 20, and a portion of the southwest quarter of the southwest quarter of the northwest
quarter o f S ection 2 1, T ownship 1 4 N orth, R ange 6 6 W est o f t he 6 th P.M., Laramie C ounty,
Wyoming (located approximately 1500 feet north of the intersection of Converse Avenue and Ogden
Road).
             Announcement was made that the Sine Die meeting of the Governing Body will be held at
2:30 p.m., and th e First Regular Meeting of the Gover ning Body will be held at 3:00 p.m., on
Monday, January 7, 2013 in the Civic Center, 510 W. 20  Street; a reception to follow in the Civicth
Center Lobby.
Announcement was made that due to the Sine Die meeting of the Governing Body and the
First Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on Monday, January 7, 2013, regularly scheduled City
Council Committee meetings will instead be held in the Municipal Building, 2101 O’Neil Avenue,
Room 122, Cheyenne, Wyoming, as follows:  Finance Committee will meet Tuesday, January 8,
2013 at 11:00 a.m. and Public Services Committee will meet Wednesday, January 9, 2013 at Noon.
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held January 14, 2013 at 6:00 p.m. in
City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, for a transfer of ownership for
a retail liquor license application filed with the City Clerk's Office for RMH Franchise Corporation
d/b/a Applebee’s Neighborhood Grill & Bar, 1401 Dell Range Blvd., Cheyenne, Wyoming (License
currently held by Concord Neighborhood Corporation d/b/a Applebee’s Neighborhood Grill & Bar,
1401 Dell Range Blvd., Cheyenne, Wyoming).
Under other business:
Mr. Spiker stated th at at the Dec. 10th Cit y Council meeting , the motion to approve the
ordinance on 2nd reading to grant a franchise to High West Energy, Inc. had failed and, as he had
voted on the prevailing side, he moved to reconsider the vote on the ordinance, seconded by Ms.
Broyles.  Mayor Kaysen clarified the procedure involving a motion to reconsider.  Brian Heithoff,
General Manager for High West Energy, Inc. (HWE), spoke in favor of the motion to reconsider and
noted the following reasons in support of reconsidering the item as well as support for the ordinance:
Economic development purposes; growth and services expansion; certainty of service area providing
stability; infrastruc ture investments and ability  and commitment to serve ne w ac counts; non-
exclusive fr anchise, an d continuance of  se rvice to e xisting a ccounts a nd the  a bility fo r t hose
customers to retain ownership rights in HWE (City Clerk note:  During comments, Dr. Rinne joined
the meeting  at 12:45 p.m.).  During  his comments, Mr. Heithoff c larified i nformation he had
provided at previous meetings.  Comments followed in opposition as well as support for the motion
to reconsider.  Discussion topics included:  "Straddling" City Council membership involving voting
actions by current/outgoing members and incoming/newly elected members relative to the timing
of action that may be taken on 2nd reading vs. final reading of the ordinance (if the motion to
reconsider and subsequent vote on the ordinance is approved); carry-over of other agenda items
between current and incoming Council members; 25 year franchise commitment if the ordinance is
approved on final reading, and support for granting HWE the opportunity to provide services within
its approved territory.  Motion to reconsider carried.  Voting "yes" -- Ms. Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms.
Broyles, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Spiker and Mr. Valdez.  Voting "no" --  Mr. Allen, Mr. Collins, Dr. Rinne
and Mayor Kaysen.  Upon request by Mayor Kaysen, Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk, read the ordinance
entitlement as follows:  ORDINANCE - Granting a Franchise by the City of Cheyenne to High West
Energy, Inc., its successors and assigns, the right to furnish, sell and distribute electricity to the City
and to all persons, businesses, and industry within a portion of the City in High West’s Certificated
Territory and the right to acquire, construct, install, locate, maintain, operate and extend into, within
and through said City all facilities reasonably necessary to furnish, sell and distribute electricity
within the City and the right to make reasonable use of all streets and other public places and public
easements as her ein defined as may  be nec essary; and fixi ng the terms and c onditions thereof.
Mayor Kaysen advised the motion now on the floor was to approve the ordinance on 2nd reading,
noting the ordinance version was the one initially submitted for the agenda dated Nov. 21, 2012.
Shawn Taylor, Executive Director, Wyoming Rural Electric Association, advised of dual utility
franchises that have been approved for other areas in Wyoming and amicable working relationships
between the utility companies; discussed rate regulating through the Public Services Commission
(PSC) and past state leg islative action that provides non- profit cooperatives, such as HWE, the
ability to "opt out" of rate regulation through the PSC and to determine its rates through action by
the cooperatives' board of directors, and reviewed options available to c ustomers to c ontest rate
changes that may  be implemented throug h a boar d of direct ors.  Dale Stee nbergen, Executive
Director, Greater Cheyenne Chamber of Commerce, commented that both companies (i.e. HWE and
Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power Compnay (CLFP)) are involved in proposed franchise ordinances
and have negotiated a proposed agreement as previously requested by the governing body, and spoke
in support of keeping fees down and leaving the opportunity open for future review of increases.
Mayor Ka ysen cla rified the c urrent motion on t he floor did not include a n ordinanc e ver sion
containing a specific time frame for review of the franchise fee for possible incremental increases.
Mr. Spiker moved to amend by substitute ordinance dated 12/20/2012, seconded by Mr. Pierson.
It was noted that the pr oposed substitute contains a provision that the fr anchise fee  would be
reviewed with the opportunity to increase the fee by one-half of a percent 7 years following approval
of the ordinance, and also at two additional 7 year interval periods during the 25 year term of the
franchise.  Mr. Allen raised a point of order questioning whether the motion to reconsider had been
disposed of with Mayor Kaysen clarifying the vote had been taken on the motion and the motion
carried by a 6 to 4 af firmative vote.  U pon inquiry, City Attorney Dan Whi te reviewed changes
contained in the proposed substitut e as f ollows:  Editorial error w as corrected which r emoved
reference to the inclusion of natura l gas services; wording changes in the conc luding paragraph
relating to the e ffectiveness of the franchise, which will not occur until the allocation of se rvice
territory is approved by the PSC, and language changes to Article 3.1 a. which provides that at the
7, 14 and 21 year time frames during the franchise term there is an option for the City Council to
increase the franchise fee by one half percent increments.  He explained the option for reviewing and
increasing the franchise fee at each seven year interval provides the right, but not the obligation, of
City Council to decide whether to increa se the fe e at that time, and tha t the signific ance of the
wording is that it reserves the unilateral right by Council to change the fee and would not require the
consent of either HWE or CLFP.  He noted the proposed wording would pertain to both franchise
ordinances which, if approved, would result in both entities being treated equally.  Upon inquiry on
wording of the current franchise agreement with CLFP and the ability to re-negotiate the franchise
fee during  the term of the  ag reement, Mr. White provided information pursua nt to provisions
contained in current franchise Ordinance #3146, noting proposed amendments to  th e fran chise
ordinance would involve a notification process and that good faith negotiations involving the fee
could be conducted but the ordinance does not provide any unilateral clauses giving the City rights
to raise the fee.  Discussion followed and included the following topics:  Concern with lack of
flexibility to review the franchise fee at times other than the three 7 year time frame periods outlined
in the proposed substitute ordinanc e; postponing the  item to allow for public notific ation and
participation; City Council public meeting schedule if the proposed ordinance was approved on 2nd
reading at the current meeting (i.e. 3rd and final reading review at the Jan. 8th Finance Committee
meeting and potential action at the Jan. 14th City Council meeting); wording involving future review
schedule of the fr anchise fee  as we ll as ordinance provisions invol ving pote ntial future
amendment(s); cooperative negotiations between the utility companies; involvement by staff and
utility company representatives regarding the proposed f ranchise fee amount and re commended
franchise term during drafting of the ordinances for both companies, and rate approval process.
During discussion and upon inquiry, Mr. Heithoff confirmed that technically any approval to a
change in fra nchise fee, pursuant to discussions to amend the ordinanc e, would be thr ough the
cooperative's board of directors and not by HWE members.  Motion to amend by substitute carried.
Voting "yes" --  all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Rinne voting "no".
Gary Kelley advised he is a customer of both HWE and CLFP and spoke in support of the services
provided by each company and approval of dual franchises.  He encouraged the governing body to
keep expenses down and to provide the public with the opportunity to comment on any fee increases
that are "passed through" to customers.  Discussion followed on competitive vs. non-competitive
services that ma y re sult b y a pproving du al f ranchise a greements; f airness i ssues; c ommunity
partnering and contr ibutions provided by CLFP; concern with limit ing growth opportunities for
CLFP as well as HWE; providing HWE the opportunity to provide electric utility service within the
City; concern with difference in rate regulation between the two companies; length of franchise term
(i.e. 25 y ears); ot her services provided to re sidents by outside providers, a nd continuity of the
membership of the governing body due to staggered terms and changes in elected officials.  Main
motion to approve on 2nd reading as amended by substitute ordinance carried.  Voting "yes" --  Ms.
Ash, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Pierson, Mr. Spiker and Mr. Valdez.  Voting "no" -- Mr. Allen,
Mr. Collins, Dr. Rinne and Mayor Kaysen.  Mayor Kaysen advised the ordinance would be reviewed
again at the F inance Committee meeting on Jan. 8, 2013 at 11:00 a.m . in Room 122, Municipal
Building, and be back before the governing body on 3rd reading at its Jan. 14, 2013 City Council
meeting.
Dr. Rinne stated that at the December 10th City Council meeting, the motion to approve the
ordinance on 2nd reading to grant a franchise to Cheyenne Light Fuel and Power Company (CLFP)
had failed and, as he  had voted on the pr evailing side, he moved to re consider the vote on the
ordinance, seconded by Mr. Collins.  Mayor Kaysen verified the votes taken on the ordinance at the
Dec. 10th Cit y Council meeting and confirmed that Dr. Rinne ha d voted on the prevailing side.
Upon request by Mayor Kaysen, Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk, read the ordinance entitlement as
follows:  ORDINANCE - Granting a Franchise by the City of Cheyenne to Cheyenne Light, Fuel and
Power Company, its successors and assigns, the right to furnish, sell and distribute electricity to the
City and to all persons, businesses, and industry within a portion of the City in Cheyenne Light, Fuel
and Power Company’s Certificated Territory and t he right to acquire , construct, install, locate ,
maintain, operate and extend into, within and through said City all facilities reasonably necessary
to furnish, sell and distribute electricity within the City and the right to make reasonable use of all
streets and other public plac es and public easements as herein defined as may be necessary; and
fixing the terms and conditions thereof.  M ark Stege, Vice President of Operations for CLFP,
requested support of the motion to rec onsider and spoke  in favor of  allowing CLFP to continue
providing se rvices, no ting the  c ompany's h istory of  e conomic de velopment a nd c ommunity
partnership efforts.  Comments followed and included the following topics:  Support of the motion
to reconsider and ordinance generally; "straddling" the vote between 2nd and final readings of the
ordinance between outgoing and incoming City Council members; current franchise ordinance with
CLFP and remaining franchise time frame; fairness issues and tre ating each utility company the
same, and future placement order on the agenda for the ordinances involving HWE and CLFP.  Upon
inquiry, Ms. Intlekofer and Dan White, City Attorney, advised the governing body has the authority
to change the agenda order at its meetings if desired.  Motion to reconsider carried.  Voting "yes" --
all members of the governing body.  Mayor Kaysen advised the motion now on the floor was the
main motion to approve the ordinance on 2nd reading as amended at the Dec. 10th meeting.  John
Sundahl, a ttorney r epresenting C LFP, u rged a doption o f a  s imilar a mendment ( i.e. s ubstitute
ordinance) for the CLFP ordinance as the amendment made on the previous agenda item for HWE.
Mr. White reviewed changes contained in a proposed substitute ordinance that adds a clause at the
end of the ordinance to indicate if the ordinance is approved it would partially repeal the existing
franchise ordinance with CLFP (Ordinance #3146) insofar as electric service is concerned but would
preserve the existing franchise ordinance with regard to gas services; noted editorial changes were
made in the approval clause to clarify the ordinance would not be effective until approved by the
governing bo dy, p ublished in  a ccordance wi th l aw, and  a ffirmatively a pproved b y the  Pub lic
Services Commission as to the allocation of service territory, and that the franchise fee section was
changed to have the same wording as that approved for HWE relative to the three 7 year franchise
fee review time frames with unilateral rights by City Council to increase fees by no more than one-
half of one percent during each of the 7 year periods outlined in the substitute ordinance.  He stated
City Council could unilaterally impose a franchise fee increase and would not need the consent of
CLFP, however, the wording does not obligate City Council to increase the fee.  Mr. Sundahl noted
there was a slight change to Section 18.2 in the proposed ordinance for CLFP, which differs from
the substitute approved f or HWE, with reg ard to e xisting fr anchise electrical services vs. g as
services.  Dale Steenbergen, Executive Director, Greater Cheyenne Chamber of Commerce, spoke
in favor of the franchise ordinance for CLFP.  Mr. Brown moved to amend by substitute ordinance
dated 12/20/2012 which contains the changes explained by Mr. White, seconded by Mr. Pierson.
Mayor Kaysen clarified the substitute, if approved, gives the governing body unilateral rights to
address potential franchise fee increases on a defined incremental basis.  Motion carried.  Voting
"yes" -- all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Rinne voting "no".  M ain
motion to approve on 2nd reading as amended by substitute ordinance carried.  Voting "yes" -- all
members of the governing body.
 
Appreciation was expressed to Public Works Department and Street and Alley Division
employees for snow clearing and removal services after the most recent snow storm.  Mayor Kaysen
expressed appreciation on behalf of the City and community to outgoing City Council members (Ms.
Ash, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson and Mr. Spiker) for their years of elected service.
There being  no further  business to come bef ore the  g overning body , the meeting w as
officially adjourned at 2:10 p.m.
 Submitted by,
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk

 RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
January 7, 2013
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in “Sine Die” Session on this date at 2:30
p.m. in the Cheyenne Civic Center.  Those present were: MAYOR - Richard L. Kaysen; COUNCIL
MEMBERS - Mr. Allen, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Collins, Mr. Pierson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Spiker and
Mr. Valdez.  Also present were Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk, and Dan White, City Attorney. 
Following the pledge of allegiance, Mayor Kaysen welcomed those in attendance and stated the
purpose of the session was to ce remonially recognize outgoing Council members for  their years of
service on C ity Council.  He commente d generally on community  leadership and g overning body
achievements; expressed appreciation to outgoing Council members for their time, effort and dedication
to the community, and recognized the supporting roles of families, friends and co-workers.
At Mayor Kaysen’s request, Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk, read a ceremonial resolution in its
entirety honoring outgoing Council member Amber Ash, entitled as follows:  “A Ceremonial Resolution
in Recognition of the Honorable Amber Ash for her Dedication and Outstanding Contributions to the
City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, and its Residents.”  Mayor Kaysen noted Ms. Ash was sworn in as a
County Commissioner earlier in the afternoon and explained, pursuant to state statute, Ms. Ash wa s
ineligible to hold both the position of City Council member and County Commissioner at the same time,
which was why she was not seated at the dais.  He advised Ms. Ash had submitted her resignation as
a member of City Council prior to being sworn in at the County.  Mayor Kaysen presented Ms. Ash with
an engraved plaque noting her 4 years of membership on City Council and thanked her for her service
to the community.  Ms. Ash briefly commented on her years of service, expressed appreciation for being
able to s erve the c ommunity a s a  City  Cou ncil m ember, a nd sta ted s he wa s lo oking fo rward to
continuing her service to the community as a County Commissioner. (#5461)
At Mayor Kaysen’s request, Ms. Intlekofer read a ceremonial resolution in its entirety honoring
outgoing Council member Patrick Collins, entitled as follows:  “A Ceremonial Resolution in
Recognition of the Honorable Patrick Collins for his Dedication and Outstanding Contributions to the
City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, and its Residents.”  Mayor Kaysen presented Mr. Collins with an engraved
plaque noting his 12 y ears of member ship on Cit y Council and thanked him for  his service  to the
community. M r. Collins briefly  commented on his y ears of servic e as a  City  Council member,
expressing appreciation to the voters of Ward II, co- City Council members who had served with him,
City staff, and members of his family for their support. (#5464)
At Mayor Kaysen’s request, Ms. Intlekofer read a ceremonial resolution in its entirety honoring
outgoing Council member Don Pierson, entitled as follows:  “A Ceremonial Resolution in Recognition
of the Honor able Don Pier son for his Dedic ation and Outstanding  Contributions  to the City  of
Cheyenne, Wyoming, and its Residents.”  Mayor Kaysen presented Mr. Pierson with an engraved plaque
noting his 20 years of membership on City Council and thanked him for his service to the community.
Mr. Pierson briefly commented on his years of service as a City Council member and thanked the voters
of the community for allowing him to serve them. (#5462)
At Mayor Kaysen’s request, Ms.  Intlekofer read a ceremonial resolution in its entirety honoring
outgoing Cou ncil m ember Ja ck R.  Spi ker, e ntitled a s f ollows:  “ A C eremonial Re solution in
Recognition of the Honorable Jack R. Spiker for his Dedication and Outstanding Contributions to the
City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, and its Residents.”  Mayor Kaysen  presented Mr. Spiker with an engraved
plaque noting his most recent 4 years of membership on City Council and thanked him for his 16 years
of se rvice, b oth a s a  Cou ncil m ember a nd fo rmer Ma yor, to  the  c ommunity.  M r. Spi ker b riefly
commented on his years of service as a City Council member and former Mayor and expressed his
appreciation to City staff, to voters for entrusting their vote in him, and to members of his family for
their support. (#5463)
On behalf of the governing body, Mayor Kaysen expressed appreciation to Mr. Collins for his
leadership as City Council President for 2012 and presented him with an engraved gavel plaque.
Mayor Kaysen announced the First Regular Meeting of the governing body involving newly
elected and continuing members would convene at 3:00 p.m. in the Civic Center.
There being no further business previously noted for t he “Sine Die” Session, Mayor Kaysen
adjourned the meeting at 2:50 p.m.
 Submitted by,
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk

PUBLISH: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle
 January 11, 2013
   RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
 
Office of City Clerk
 
January 7, 2013
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne assembled for its First Regular Meeting for 2013
on this date at 3:00 p.m. in the Cheyenne Civic Center.  Purpose of the First Regular Meeting was to
recognize and administer oaths of office to those individuals who were elected, or re-elected, at the most
recent general election to serve as members of the governing body, as well as provide for certain
administrative func tions.  Rod Hott le provided introduc tory comments and ser ved as ma ster of
ceremonies prior to the meeting being officially convened.
Father August Koeune, Pastor, St. Mary’s Cathedral, delivered the invocation.
The Honorable Michael K. Davis, Justice of the Wyoming Supreme Court, administered the oath
of elected office to Richard L. Kaysen as Mayor,  followed by administration of oath of elected office
for the following newly elected and re-elected City Council members:  Jimmy  Valdez and Annette
Williams, Ward I; Bryan M. Cook and Dicky Shanor, Ward II, and Jim Brown and Mike Luna, Ward
III.
Mayor Kaysen officially called the First Regular Meeting to order at 3:10 p.m.  Those present
were: MAYOR - Richard L. Kaysen; COUNCIL MEMBERS - Mr. Allen, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr.
Cook, Mr. L una, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Shanor, Mr. Va ldez and Ms. Wi lliams.  A lso present were Carol
Intlekofer, City Clerk, and Da n White, City Attorney.  Following  the pledg e of allegiance, led by
members of the Mayor’s Youth Council, Mayor Kaysen provided welcoming comments and remarked
on the community role of the governing body and future financial challenges due to the economy.  He
expressed appreciation to those individuals in the community who serve as elected public officials; to
City staff who assisted with the “Sine Die” and current meeting arrangements; to Justice Davis, Father
Koeune, Mr. Hottle, and membe rs of the Ma yor’s Youth Council and Cheyenne Public Employees
Association who participated and assisted with the meeting and reception, to the families of governing
body members for their support, and to Wyoming citizens serving in the military.
Election of City Council President for 2013.  Mayor Kaysen announced, pursuant to City Code,
he would be conducting the election but would not be participating in the vote.  Ms. Broyles moved to
nominate and elect Dr. Rinne as City Council President for 2013, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Mr. Brown
moved that nominations cease, seconded by Mr. Valdez.  Motion to cease nominations carried.  Voting
“yes” – all members of the g overning body with the exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not vote.
Motion to nominate and elect Dr. Rinne carried.  Voting “yes”-- all members of the governing body with
the exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not vote.
Election of City Council Vice President for 2013.  Mayor Kaysen announced, pursuant to City
Code, he would be conducting the election but would not be participating in the vote.  Dr. Rinne moved
to nominate and elect Ms. Broyles as City Council Vice President for 2013, seconded by Mr. Allen.  Mr.
Brown moved that nominations cease, seconded by Mr. Cook.  Motion to cease nominations carried.
Voting “yes”-- all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not
vote.  Motion to nominate and elect Ms. Broyles carried.  Voting “yes”-- all members of the governing
body with the exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not vote.
Approval of Appointment of City  officials (pursuant to Titl e 2 of the  Code of the City  of
Cheyenne) as follows:  Matthew J. A shby, Planning Services Director; James Edward Elias, Public
Works Director; Paul S. Galeotos, Municipal Court Judge; Randy  K. Hays, Assistant City Treasurer
(Board of Public Utilities); Lois A. Huff, City Treasurer; Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk/Assistant City
Treasurer; Ronnald J. Jeffrey, Juvenile Court Judge; Brian N. Kozak, Chief of the Chey enne Police
Department; James A. Martin, Chief of the Cheyenne Fire and Rescue Department; Mark T. Moran,
Municipal Court Judge; Richard L. Parish, Parks and Recreation Director, and Daniel E. White, City
Attorney.  Mr. Valdez moved to approve the appointments “en masse”, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Motion
carried.  Voting “yes”-- all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Kaysen who
did not vote (Mayoral appointments).  Following announcement of the vote, Justice Davis administered
the oath of appointment to the above listed City officials.
Following the benediction by Father Koeune, Mayor Kaysen announced that refreshments would
be served in the Civic Center lobby immediately following the meeting.
There being no further business previously noted for the First Regular Meeting, the meeting was
officially adjourned at 3:33 p.m.
 Submitted by,
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle
 January 11, 2013

MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2013-01-14 | CLIP_ID: 354 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 354

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
Office of City Clerk
 January 14, 2013
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning
at 6 :00 p .m. i n C ouncil C hambers.  P resent w ere: M AYOR -  R ichard L.  K aysen; C OUNCIL
MEMBERS - Mr. Allen, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Cook, Mr. Luna, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Shanor, Mr.
Valdez and Ms. Williams.  Also present: Carol Intlekofer, City Clerk; Lois Huff, City Treasurer, and
Dan White, City Attorney. 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no separate
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its
normal sequence on the agenda.)  Mr. Brown moved to approve Consent Agenda items, seconded
by Mr. Valdez.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body.
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on December 20, 2012.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
[CA] Minutes from Sine Die Session of the Governing Body on January 7, 2013.  Motion (per
Consent Agenda) carried.
[CA] Minutes from the First Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on January 7, 2013.  Motion
(per Consent Agenda) carried.
Mr. Brown and Mr. Valdez each declared a conflict of interest (business interest in vouchers
payable to Ameri-Tech HVAC Services and Radio Station KYOY F M respectively) and vacated
Council Chambers.  Mr. Allen moved to approve payment of vouchers as presented, seconded by
Ms. Williams.  Mo tion carried.  Vo ting “yes” -- all members of the governing body present in
Council Chambers.  Following announcement of the vote, Mr. Brown and Mr. Valdez returned to
Council Chambers.
Mayor Kaysen opened a public hea ring to determine w hether compliance of anne xation
conditions required by Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402 exist for a parcel of land being situated in a portion of
the east half of the east half of Section 20, and a portion of the southwest quarter of the southwest
quarter of the northwest quarter of Section 21, Township 14 North, Range 66 West of the 6th P.M.,
Laramie County, Wyoming (located approximately 1500 feet north of the intersection of Converse
Avenue and Ogden Road).  Jim Flesher, Planning and Development Office, reviewed annexation
requirements and criteria pursuant to Wyo. Stat. § 15-1-402, stating  that the proposed a rea to be
annexed deviates subs tantially from the City ’s PlanCheyenne, Unified Development Code and
Master Transportation Plan documents.  He reviewed staff findings with regard to compliance, or
non-compliance, with Wyo. Stat. § 15-1-402 (a) (i) through (vi).  Mr. Flesher advised of areas of
non-compliance involving c riteria outlined in W.S. § 15-1-40 2 (a) (i) through (iii), noting the
following topics: Storm water drainage facility involving the proposed annexed area, which would
be located outside of the area to be annexed; inability to utilize the limited “strips” of open public
space area; street(s) connectivity problems relative to existing roadways and the transportation plan,
and “piecemeal” development affecting long range planning, zoning and future property uses.  He
stated findings involving conditions outlined in W.S. § 15-1-402 (iv through vi) had been met with
regard to prope rty contig uity, franchises being  in place to se rve the  proper ty, and anne xation
summary notification requirements.  Frank Cole, United W estern Corporation, petitioner f or
annexation, stated that the first three items (i.e. findings previously noted by Mr. Flesher as not being
in compliance) pertained to platting problems and not annexation.  He requested postponement of
a companion agenda item (#21 - Resolution), which had been referred to Public Services Committee
under the approved Consent Agenda motion earlier in the meeting, as he would not be available to
attend the Committee meeting.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Cole verified the property to be annexed is on the
east side of Converse Ave. a nd was not the Sce nic property development a rea located w est of
Converse Ave.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Flesher confirmed the first three criteria items contained in Wyo.
Stat. § 15-1-402 were those that have not been met; the last three criteria items have been met.  Upon
inquiry, Brandon Cammarata, Planning and Development Director, advised a preliminary plat related
to the proposed development was postponed at the recent Planning Commission meeting for further
review to addre ss concerns, which include  the open spa ce planned for the ar ea.  Ma yor Kaysen
advised of city code language relative to items for Committee referral not being eligible for removal
from th e Consent Ag enda, a nd indicated that a t the next P ublic Service s Commi ttee mee ting
members could consider recommending postponement of the affiliated Resolution agenda item at
that time, per Mr. Cole’s request.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Cole acknowledged that would be acceptable
to him.  There being no further comments or input and purpose of the hearing having been met,
Mayor Kaysen closed the public hearing.
Mayor Kaysen opened a public hearing to receive comments and input for a transfer of
ownership for a retail liquor license application filed with the City Clerk's Office for RMH Franchise
Corporation d/b/a Applebe e’s Ne ighborhood Grill & B ar, 1401 D ell Rang e B lvd., Chey enne,
Wyoming ( License cur rently held by  Concord Ne ighborhood Corporation d/b/a Applebe e’s
Neighborhood Grill &  Ba r, 1401 De ll Range  Blvd.,  Cheyenne, Wy oming).  There  being  no
comments or input and purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Kaysen closed the
hearing and referred the application to Finance Committee.
 
ORDINANCE - Pursuant to Section 2.2.1 Zoning Map Amendments, Section 5.1.2 Zoning
Districts Established, and Secti on 5.1.3 Official Zoning Map of the Unifie d Development Code,
changing the zoning classification from P Public District to CBD Central Business District for Lot
1, Block 1, 2100 Pioneer Subdivision, C heyenne, Wyoming (located at 2100 Pioneer A venue).
Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Allen moved to approve on third and final reading,
seconded by Mr. Luna.  M otion carried.  V oting “yes” -- all members of the governing body.
(#3964)
ORDINANCE - Granting a Franchise by the City of Cheyenne to High West Energy, Inc.,
its successors and assigns, the right to furnish, sell and distribute electricity to the City and to all
persons, businesses, and industry within a portion of the City in High West’s Certificated Territory
and the r ight to acquire , construct, install, locate , maintain, opera te and e xtend into, within and
through said City all facilities reasonably necessary to furnish, sell and distribute electricity within
the City and the right to make reasonable use of all streets and other public places and public
easements as herein defined as may be necessary; and fixing the terms and conditions thereof.  Brian
Heithoff, General Manager for High West Energy, advised he was available to answer any questions.
Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Brown moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded
by Mr. Valdez.  Mr. Brown moved to amend by substitute ordinance dated 01-11-2013, seconded
by Mr. Luna.  Upon inquiry, Dan White, City Attorney, advised the substitute changes language in
Section 2.3 rela ting to the ter m of the fr anchise due t o delays since the initial ordinanc e wa s
submitted.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body.  Main
motion, as amended by substitute, carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body with
the exception of Dr. Rinne and Mayor Kaysen voting “no”. (#3965)
ORDINANCE - Granting a Franchise by the City of Cheyenne to Cheyenne Light, Fuel and
Power Company, its successors and assigns, the right to furnish, sell and distribute electricity to the
City and to all persons, businesses, and industry within a portion of the City in Cheyenne Light, Fuel
and Power Company’s Certificated Territory and the r ight to ac quire, construct, install, locate,
maintain, operate and extend into, within and through said City all facilities reasonably necessary
to furnish, sell and distribute electricity within the City and the right to make reasonable use of all
streets and other public places and public ea sements as herein defined as may be necessary; and
fixing the terms and conditions thereof.  Mark Stege, Vice President of Operations for Cheyenne
Light, Fuel and Power, advised he was available to answer any questions.  Mr. Brown moved to
approve on third and  final reading, seconded by Mr. Valde z.  Mr. Brown move d to amend by
substitute ordinance dated 01-11-2013, seconded by Mr. Cook.  City Attorney Dan White advised

Cammarata read the letter (dated Feb. 11, 2013) which explained Scenic Development’s position that
it may not be able to move forward with its apartment project as they are not the land owners of the
parcel and conditions that are being recommended by the Public Services Committee, associated with
the pr eliminary plat, are no t a greeable to t he la nd ow ner ( i.e. Co le fa mily).  Ca sey Pa lma, St eil
Surveying Services, agent for the applicant, Scenic Development, encouraged Council members to
review the conditions being recommended for appropriateness, and suggested that perhaps there might
be some wa y to find a flexible compromi se between the par ties.  Ed Murra y commented on the
preliminary plat with Mr. Allen raising a point of order that discussion should remain pertinent to the
zoning classific ation item. May or Ka ysen re quested Mr. Murra y provide his comments on the
preliminary plat when that item would be on the floor later in the meeting.  Mr. Allen reported there was
no recommendation on the item from the Public Services Committee.  Mr. Allen moved to approve on
second reading, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Comment followed regarding discussion at the Public Services
Committee meeting regarding wording in S ection 7. of the ordinance which reads: “ ... That this
ordinance shall be in full force and effect upon its approval and publication and upon the official filing
of the affiliated Scenic Subdivision final plat map with the County Clerk and Ex-Officio Register of
Deeds for Laramie County, Wyoming.”  Mr. Allen moved to amend Section 7. to read as follows,
seconded by Mr. Luna:  “ ... That this ordinance shall be in full force and effect upon its approval and
publication and  upon the approval and publication of an ordinance annexing said property.”  Discussion
followed and included the following topics: Customary agenda procedure involving annexation, zoning
and platting items that are affiliated, and concerns that the usual procedure was not being followed for
the Scenic Development items; support for the apartment project; timing of actions to be taken on the
zoning classification relative to a nnexation and preliminary /final plat; support for a nd against the
proposed amendment, and possible postponement of the item.  During discussion and upon inquiry, Mr.
Cammarata provided information pertaining to a previously adopted resolution determining conditions
for annexation had been met (re: Scenic Development project property) relative to delayed introduction
of the annexation ordinance.  Motion to amend failed (due to a tie vote).  Voting “yes” -- Mr. Allen, Mr.
Cook, Mr. Luna, Mr. Shanor and Ms. Williams.  Voting “no” --  Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Dr. Rinne,
Mr. Valdez and Mayor Kaysen.  Comments followed in non-support of the zone cha nge due to the
failed motion to amend and changing the zone classification prior to the property being annexed, and
timing of actions to enable annexation and the zone change to be completed together.  Upon inquiry,
Mr. Palma advised general discussions have been held on whether a property to be annexed should have
the zoning determined prior to annexation, and expressed his opinion that it would be appropriate to
either postpone the item or deny it and resubmit it with the final plat.  Main motion failed.  Voting “no”
-- all members of the governing body.
ORDINANCE - Pursuant to Sec tion 2.2.1, Zoning Map Amendment, Section 5.1.2, Z oning
Districts established, and Section 5.1.3, Official Zoning Map, of the Cheyenne Unified Development
Code, changing the zoning classification from A-1 Agricultural and Rural Residential District to MR-2
Medium Density Residential – Developing District for a tract of land situated in a portion the East Half
of the East Half (E½E½) of Section 20 and a portion of the Southwest Quarter of the Southwest Quarter
of the Northwest Quarter (SW¼ SW¼ NW¼) of Section 21, T.14N., R.66W., 6th P.M ., Cheyenne,
Laramie County, Wyoming, to be known as the Bluffs, 9  Filing (located approximately 1,500 feetth
north of the intersection of Converse Avenue and Ogden Road) -- referred to Public Services Committee
(sponsor -- Mr. Allen).
ORDINANCE - Pursuant to Section 2.2.1, Zoning  Map Amendment, Section 5.1.2, Zoning
Districts Established, and Section 5.1.3, Official Zoning Map, of the Cheyenne Unified Development
Code, changing the zoning classification from P Public to NB Neighborhood Business for Lot 1, Block
4, Storey Boulevard Extension, Cheyenne, Wyoming (located east of and adjacent to Converse Avenue,
approximately one-quarter mile south of Storey Boulevard) -- referred to Public Services Committee
(sponsor -- Mr. Allen).
RESOLUTION - Determining that conditions for annexation required by Wyo. Stat. §15-1-402
exist for a parcel of land being situated in a portion of the East Half of the East Half of  Section 20 and
a portion of the Southwest Quarter of the Southwest Quarter of the Northwest Quarter of Section 21,
Township 14 North, Range 66 West of the 6th P.M., Laramie County, Wyoming (located approximately
1,500 feet north of the intersection of Converse Avenue and Ogden Road) (postponed from 1-28-13).
James Perrot Macneil commented in opposition to all annexations, i ncluding any property he or the
Union Pacific owns.  Mr. Allen moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Brown.  Mr. Allen moved to postpone
to March 11, 2013, seconded by Mr. Brown.  It was noted postponement is at the request of the
applicant.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body.
[CA] RESOLUTION - Approving Water and Sanitary Sewer Service, by User’s Agreement, with
Merrill, Inc., a Wyoming Corporation, 4703 Wright Court, Cheyenne, Wyoming.  Motion (per Consent
Agenda) carried. (#5475)
[CA] RESOLUTION - Approving Outsider User Water/Sewer Services, by User’s Agreement, with
Microsoft Corporation, Lot 2, Block 1, North Range Business Park, Fifth Filing, Laramie County,
Wyoming.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5476)
[CA] RESOLUTION - Re- appropriating the  Fisca l Year  2013 budg et of the Cit y of Chey enne
according to the provisions of W.S. §16-4-112 and 16-4-113 -- referred to Finance Committee (sponsor
-- Mr. Brown).
[CA] RESOLUTION - Directing the City Attorney to petition the First Judicial District Co urt,
Laramie County, Wyoming, for an order suspending, for a period not to exceed thirty (30) days, Retail
Liquor License No. 39 issued by the City of Cheyenne to Stillwater, Inc., dba ‘Mingles Bar’ -- referred
to Finance Committee (sponsors -- Mr. Allen, Mr. Brown, Ms. Broyles, Mr. Cook, Mr. Luna, Dr. Rinne,
Mr. Shanor, Mr. Valdez and Ms. Williams).
[CA] RESOLUTION - Approving the Cheyenne Area Street Enhancement Toolbox -- referred to
Public Services Committee (sponsor -- Mr. Allen).
[CA] RESOLUTION - Approving the West Lincolnway Streetscape plans (landscape and fence) --
referred to  Pub lic Ser vices Co mmittee (s ponsors - - M r. Al len, Ms.  Broyles, Mr . V aldez an d M s.
Williams).
Preliminary Plat for Scenic Subdivision, a tract of land situated in a portion of the East Half of
the East Half (E½E½) of Section 20, T.14N., R.66W., 6th P.M., Laramie County, Wyoming (located
north of and adjacent to the existing WalMart store) (Annexation in process).  Ed Murray, vicinity
landowner, spoke in opposition to approval of the preliminary plat.  He expressed his concerns with the
proposed Scenic development pa rcel as submitted by  the prope rty owner in conjunction with the
annexation application; convoluted procedure involving the parcel’s affiliated annexation, zoning and
platting processes, and lack of communication by the property owner (Cole family) and failure to look
at comprehensive and “big picture” planning for the area.  He reviewed his further concerns relative to
Exhibit D, network transportation plan involving the area, that was submitted with the initial annexation
application, stating the transpor tation plan ref lected in th e exhibit is  inconsistent with the Master
Transportation Plan incorporated into the Cit y’s PlanCheyenne.  During his comments, Mr. Murra y
displayed and referred to an enlar ged copy of Exhibi t D (map) a nd a diagram depicting the Master
Transportation Plan map portion from PlanCheyenne for the area, and discussed north-south and east-
west collector roads in Section 20.  He noted that the north-south collector road reflects the extension
of Rue Terre north to Storey Blvd., and that specific land uses (zoning classifications) affecting the
Murray property, as currently depicted in PlanCheyenne, show an emphasis on mixed use commercial
and mixed use residential.  Describing the Murray property as “the donut hole” situated at the cross-
roads of the collector roads, Mr. Murray stated that changing the City’s transportation network plan, as
proposed by the property  owner pursuant to Exhi bit D, will have a de trimental effect on Murr ay
property development plans.  He explained his failed attempts to discuss the issues with the property
owner; spoke in support of proper community growth and good community stewardship, and noted the
City’s vested financial interests in Storey Ave. and Converse Ave. roadway extensions and associated
infrastructure.  He indicated that a recent Exhibit C, submitted by the applicant for the preliminary plat,
has resulted in three staff conditions being proposed in conjunction with the preliminary plat.  In
concluding his comments, Mr. Murray provided copies of Section 4.3.2, Transportation Network Plan,
contained in the City’s Unified Development Code (UDC), reciting the wording outlined in Section a.,
General Requirements, and provisions # 1. 3. and 4.; stated his opinion that compliance with the rules
of the UDC have not been met, and reiterated his opposition to approval of the preliminary plat.  Ed
Cole, Cole family, landowner, advised that what Scenic Development is proposing makes no difference
on how the final transportation plan is adopted for Section 20.  He briefly reviewed history of the City’s
acquisition of property from the Cole family along Storey and Converse, noting the City allowed four
entrances into the land, one of which involves the Scenic Development area, and that planning staff now
want to allow two other entrances, which was not part of the original plan.  He advised the Cole family
and City staff do not agree on the way the streets should be aligned; commented on the slow ra te of
commercial development in the area, and spoke in f avor of the quality project proposed by Scenic
Development and that it is a g ood project for the City , noting the time a nd money that Scenic ha s
invested.  He stated his belief that the street alignment issue does not make any difference in whether
this is approved.  Casey Palma, Steil Surveying Services, clarified there are four proposed conditions
attached with the recommendation on the preliminary plat and that one of the conditions should address
some concerns as it is a revision to the traffic impact study and analysis.  He advised that Scenic is
favorable to re vising the tra nsportation impact study and networ k plan prior to the f inal plat being
submitted.  Mr. Murray clarified his previous comments were made to specifically address concerns
involving the project area as well as for betterment of the community through comprehensive area
planning that includes the transportation network, instead of piecemeal incremental developments.
James Perrot Macneil spoke in opposition to t he preliminary plat as the prope rty has not y et been
annexed, and against all community development generally.  Mr. Allen moved to acknowledge receipt
of the preliminary plat with staff conditions #1 through 3 as listed in the 02-01-2013 memo from the
City Planning and Development Department, and requiring a revised Traffic Impact Study to provide
consistency with the Transportation Network as required under Section 4.3.2 (re: UDC), seconded by
Mr. Brown.  Comments followed regarding the convoluted nature of issues and procedures involving
development of the property; landowners’ and developers’ reliance on PlanCheyenne and the UDC
(ordinance) tra nsportation require ments; sugg estion that customary  vs. non-customary  proce dures
involving the process affiliated with preliminary plats, annexations and zone chang es be reviewed;
concerns with preliminary plat issues; support for Scenic Development’s housing (apartment) project
and its benefi t to the City; PlanCheyenne as a compre hensive plan a nd possible plan chang es for
flexibility; rec ognition of validity  of staff  conce rns; co llector stre et plans g enerally; increme ntal
development, and approval of the preliminary plat providing an opportunity for the developer to move
forward with its project.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body with the
exception of Mr. Valdez voting “no”.
[CA] Preliminary Plat for The Bluffs, 9  Filing, a tract of land situated in a portion the East Half ofth
the East Half (E½E½) of Section 20 and a portion of the Southwest Quarter of the Southwest Quarter
of the Northwest Quarter (SW¼ SW¼ NW¼) of Section 21, T.14N., R.66W., 6th P.M., Cheyenne,
Laramie County, Wyoming (Annexation in process) (located approximately 1,500 feet north of the
intersection of Converse Avenue and Ogden Road) -- referred to Public Services Committee.
[CA] Use Agreement to permit Level 3 Communications, LLC, limited use of the public right-of-way
for the installation of f iber optic c ommunications systems and setting  a fe e -- referred to Financ e
Committee.
[CA] Professional Servic es Ag reement betwee n the City  of Chey enne a nd No el Griffith, J r. &
Associates A rchitects for the provision of sc hematic de sign, de sign development, c onstruction
documents, bidding documents, bidding assistance and construction management for the Municipal
Pool Renovation and Expansion Project (1% Specific Purpose Sales & Use Tax) -- referred to Finance
Committee.
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and DHM Design Corporation
for the provision of schematic design, design development, construction documents, bidding documents
and bidding assistance for the Converse Softball Complex Renovation project (Menard property sale
proceeds) -- referred to Finance Committee.
[CA] Contract Modification No. 1 to Contract No. 5911 be tween the City of Cheyenne, Parks and
Recreation Department, and Ayres Associates for additional retaining wall design to stabilize steep
shoreline areas around Lake Minnehaha in Holliday Park (SLIB Grant funding).  Motion (per Consent
Agenda) carried (amount not to exceed $21,680.00). (#5911)
[CA] Authorization to purchase traffic striping paint under Wyoming Department of Transportation
Bid No. 12-325TZ (2011-2014 1% Sales Tax).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (amount not to
exceed $37,127.10).
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-17-13 for furnishing two new medium/heavy duty transit buses with
wheelchair lifts for the City of Cheyenne, Public Works Department, Transit Division (partial State
Loan and Investment Board and Wyoming Department of Transportation funds) -- referred to Finance
Committee.
[CA] Consideration of Bid #R-19-13 for furnishing ballistic vests for the Police De partment from
Skaggs Uniforms, Salt L ake City , Utah (Misce llaneous F ederal Gra nts) -- ref erred to Fina nce
Committee.
Appointment of John G. Knepper to the Board of Adjustment. Dr. Rinne move d to approve,
seconded by Mr. Allen.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body with the
exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not vote (Mayoral appointment).
Re-Appointments of Mal R. Burnside, Marty Crowe, Michael A. Metzler, and  Jason Stephen
to the Contractor Licensing Board; and William C. Beaman to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming-Laramie
County, State of Wyoming Joint Powers Board for Frontier Park improvements.  Dr. Rinne  moved to
approve, seconded by Mr. Allen.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -- all members of the governing body
with the exception of Mayor Kaysen who did not vote (Mayoral appointments).
 
[CA] Request to approve , pursuant to Wy o. Stat. §12-5-402 (b ), a sponsor relationship betwee n
Cheyenne Frontier Days, Inc. and Miller/Coors, a malt beverage industry representative, in conjunction
with the 2013, 2014 and 2015 annual Cheyenne Frontier Days community event -- referred to Finance
Committee.                                            
Announcement was made of the appointments of Earl B. Kincheloe to the Cheyenne Housing
Authority Board; Beth Pratt to the Mayor’s Council for People with Disabilities, and Nicholas Pickering
to the Building Code Board of Appeals, to be confirmed February 25, 2013.
Announcement was made that due to the Presidents’ Holiday on Monday, February 18, 2013,
regularly scheduled City Council Committee meetings will instead be held in the Municipal Building,
2101 O’Neil Avenue, Room 122, Cheyenne, Wyoming, as follows: Financ e Committee will meet
Tuesday, February 19, 2013 at 11:00 a.m. and Public Services Committee will meet W ednesday,
February 20, 2013 at Noon.
 Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held Monday, February 25, 2013 at 6:00
p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Ave., Cheyenne, Wyoming, for renewal of existing City
liquor licenses (retail, restaurant, limited retail, resort, bar and grill licenses, and microbrewery permits)
filed with the City Clerk’s Office.
Under other business:
Tom Lindsey commented on lack of development of the “downtown hole” off of Lincolnway
and suggested a multi-purpose building be built on the sit e, including an underground parking area,
which could house a health food restaurant, office space, short and long term housing, and outdoor area
on the top of the building for activities and possibly a garden area.
Dennis Pa checo spo ke in s upport of  de veloping the  “ downtown h ole”, a nd dis cussed h is
concerns with poor road conditions within the City.  He specifically referenced the vicinity of Pershing
Blvd. and Logan Ave. as an example.  Mayor Kaysen provided information on street improvements at
19th/20th and Converse t hat will begin this sum mer and extend west to the ceme tery complex on
Pershing, and noted ther e are also plans for improveme nts on Logan as funding becomes available.
Comment was made thanking Mr. Pacheco for expressing his concerns.
County Commission Chairman Troy Thompson was recognized as being in attendance at the
meeting.
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was officially
adjourned at 7:28  p.m.
 Submitted by,
 
 Carol Intlekofer, MMC
 City Clerk
