– all members of the governing bod y.  Dr. Rinne moved to amend Section 10.44.70 by deleting 
the last sentence and replacing it with “Wyoming State Statute 31 -18-802 with Tables 2 and 2, 
seconded by Mr. Luna.  Discussion included potential postponement and concerns involving 
including statutes as they can be amended.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all members 
of the governing body.  Dr. Rinne moved to amend Section 10.44.060 line two by adding the term 
“overweight”, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion to amend failed due to a tie vote.  Voting “yes” –

Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Luna and Mr. Shanor.  Dr. Rinne moved to postpone to November 
23, 2020, seconded by Mr. Ro ybal.  Discussion continued relating to the following concerns and 
topics:  Additional time requested to consider and evaluate proposed amendments, compliance 
with State and Federal regulations, enforcement, option s to table or postpone ordinance  and 
protecting longevity and integrity of city streets .  Kris Jones, City Clerk, provided clarification

North, Range 67 West, of the 6th P.M., Laramie County – referred to Finance Committee.

16, Township 13 North, Range 66 West of the 6th P.M., Laramie County, Wyoming (located south

[CA] Minimum Revenue Guaranteed Payment Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, 
Wyoming, and Cheyenne Regional Air Service Focus Team (CRAFT), for Skywest Airlines to 
provide scheduled flight services between Cheyenne, Wyoming and Denver, Colorado  (General 
Fund).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $148,350.50) (#7253) 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Cheyenne Metropolitan 
Planning Organization (MPO) and Ayres Associates for the Converse Avenue Reconstruction Plan 
(MPO Federal Funds) .  Motion (per Consent Agen da) carried (in an amount not to exceed 
$120,175.00) (#7254) 
 
Memorandum of Understanding between EQ Capital , LLC, and the City of Cheyenne to 
build a technology ecosystem in Wyoming focused on investing in tech startups.  Brandon Ames, 
Chief Economic Development Officer, provided details of the Memorandum of Understanding  
(MOU).  Mr. Ames advised the city bares no fi nancial responsibility relating to the MOU , that 
Cheyenne was chosen due to the proximity to Denver, CO. and the purpose is to help startup 
companies in Cheyenne.  He reported the intent is to partner with the city to create business 
opportunities noting EQ Capital, LLC was instrumental in the development of companies such as 
Door Dash and Air BNB.  Governing body members requested consideration to postpone and to 
have a City Council work session to learn more about the opportunity and long-range expectations 
of the MOU.   Mr. Ames advised the owners of EQ Capital, LLC are currently in route to Cheyenne 
and he would speak with  them regarding meeting with members of the g overning body.    
Discussion included the desire to learn more regarding the agreement and the exciting possibilities 
   
for Cheyenne.     Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Luna moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. 
White.  Mr. Laybourn moved to postpone to November 23, 2020, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Motion 
to postpone carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.                 
 
[CA] Development and Maintenance Agreement between Cheyenne -Laramie County

Consideration of Bid #E -7-21 for Ice Control Product for the City of Cheyenne Street & 
Alley Division (2015-2018 & 2019-2022 1% Sales Tax). Vicki Nemecek, Public Works Director, 
reported that although there are alternative products such as sand, the Ice Slicer product eliminates 
broken windshields and the need to sweep streets follow ing snow events.  Upon inquiry, Ms. 
Nemecek advised the city has used this product for approximately 15 years.  Concerns were voiced

Linings & Geotextile Products, Inc., for the Happy Jack Landfill Phase 2, Cells 1 and 2 and Cell 
3 Excavation Earthworks (Geosynthetics Procurement Base Bid) project (Solid Waste Fund) .

(#7258)

for the City of Cheyenne, Cheyenne Police Department (Coronavirus Emergency Sup plemental 
Funding, Bureau of Justice Assistance (CESF)).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (accepted

Appointments of Kaylee Ashley, David Barker, Ty Bronder, Garrison Cook, Ashen Doty,

 Presentation of the Annual DDA Budget Report.  Amber Ash, DDA Director, presented a

MEETING: City Council Meeting - Agenda Only | DATE: 2020-11-23 | CLIP_ID: 774 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 774

   
RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
November 23, 2020 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:06 p.m. via electronic conference meeting .  Attending electronic conference meeting  were: 
MAYOR - Marian Orr, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Rocky Case, Bryan Cook, Ken Esquibel, Pete 
Laybourn, Mike Luna, Dr. Mark Rinne, Dicky Shanor and Jeff White. Absent: Scott Roybal.  Also 
attending: Kris Jones, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
 Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda. )  Upon request by Mr . White, and pursuant to support 
received by Mr. Cook and Mr. Luna, agenda item #17(a) was removed from the Consent Agenda. 
Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Rinne and Mr. White, 
agenda item  #19(b) was removed from the Consent Agenda.  Mr. Luna moved to approve  
remaining items, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body present.  
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on November 9, 2020.  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Amending Chapter 10.44, Weight Limits, of Title 10, 
Vehicles and Traffic, of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming. (Postponed from 
November 9, 2020). Chief Brian Kozak, Police Department, expressed appreciation to all parties 
involved with their assistance on the ordinance and reported the amendment has been mutually 
agreed upon by city  staff and the trucking industr y.  Tom Cobb,  City Engineer, advised the 
ordinance was a collaborative effort and voiced appreciation to Chief Kozak for working with the 
trucking industry.  Mayor Orr expressed appreciation to members of city staff and other entities 
for their work.  Sheila Foertsch, Wyoming Trucking Association, thanked all parties involved for 
the additional work and time spent on the ordinance.  Ms. Foertsch advised she is comfortable with 
the amendment and believes it’s a good product  of compromise by all parties.  Mayor Orr 
referenced comments made via the chat function in Zoom in support of the ordinance.  Rick Fierro, 
Ram Trucking, thanked Mr. Cobb and Chief Kozak,  noting a lot of time was  spent working to 
refine the ordinance and advised the finished product will be conducive for everyone.   Reporting 
for Public Services Committee, Mr. Cook moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. 
Luna.  Dr. Rinne moved to amend by substitute dated November 23, 2020, seconded by Mr. Cook.  
Dr. Rinne explained the amendment is the final product of all of the meetings and discussion that 
has taken place between Chief Kozak and  the trucking industry.  Upon inquiry, Joe Chenchar, 
Assistant City Attorney, advised Sc hedules H & I were submitted  and approved by him earlier 
today.  Upon inquiry, Kris Jones, City Clerk, explained the schedules are part of the ordinance and 
   
included in the substitute and do not require a separate motion to approve.  Mr. Chenchar explained 
the schedules are incorporated by reference in the ordinance text.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing bod y present.  Concerns were voic ed regarding timing of 
implementing the ordinance amendment and that due to the Covid-19 Pandemic, small businesses 
are struggling who participate in the chain of services , noting it could be devastating to them.  
Comments were made commending the work product and collaboration between city staff and 
industry partners and additional information was provided on previous comments made in support 
of the ordinance by members of city staff and the trucking industry.  Additional comments were 
made related to the ordinance amendment not being affected by the Covid-19 Pandemic and that 
the ordinance requires truckers to abide by state and federal laws when within city limits and that 
any time is a good time to implement.  Discussion included opposition to adding new restricted 
routes within the city that didn’t exist before.  It was further noted that the trucking industry spoke 
in favor of the ordinance amendments.  Main motion as amended carried.  Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body present with exception of Mr. Case and Mr. Shanor voting “no”.        
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending Section 2.84.070, Board of Adjustment, of 
Chapter 2.84, Miscellaneous Boards and Commissions, of Title 2, Administration and Personnel, 
of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, to correct cross references to the Board 
of Adjustment.  Mr. Cook moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Luna.  Motion 
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending Section 15.52.060(B), Notification of 
Issuance or Denial -Appeal, and Section 15.52.100 , Variances, of Chapter 15.52, Solar Access 
Permit System, of Title 15, Buildings and Construction, of the Municipal Code of the City of 
Cheyenne, Wyoming, to correct cross references to the Board of Adjustment.  Mr. Cook moved to 
approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members 
of the governing body present. 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Establishing a Planned Unit Development (PUD) District 
for property generally located northwest of the intersection of North Gate Avenue and Yellowstone 
Road.  Mr. Cook moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr . Luna.  Upon inquiry, 
Charles Bloom, Planning and Development Director, advised there was discussion by the Planning 
Commission related to concern with a sunken garden within the development that may not be ADA 
compatible.  C asey Palma, Stile Surveying Services, agent for owner, reported a sunken garden 
was designed that will also serve as a detention pond and the owner opted for a walkway to look 
down on the area.  Mr. Palma advised they have and are still looking for possibilities to provide 
an ADA pathway over the top.  He further noted the street  has over a 5% grade and that a letter 
has been submitted by the project architect related to ADA accessibility, noting ADA compliance 
is not required because it is private and not accessible by the general public.  Motion carried.  
Voting “yes” - all members of the governing body present. 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION - Authorizing the City Treasurer to discharge uncollectible debts in the 
amount of $39,348.39 for City of Cheyenne accounts and $23,290.93 for Board of Public Utilities 
sanitation accounts pursuant to Wyoming Statute §16 -4-502.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#6102) 
   
[CA] RESOLUTION – Approving water and sanitary sewer services, by Outside User Water 
and Sanitary Sewer Services Agreements, for Tri-State Generation and Transmission, Lot 4, Block 
10, North Range Business Park, 3 rd Filing, situated in the NE¼ SE¼ of Section 4,  Township 13, 
North, Range 67 West, of the 6 th P.M., Laramie County.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. 
(#6103) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – To rededicate unknown funds and unused donations from various 
accounts within the City of Cheyenne’s Agency Fund – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsor 
– Mr. Luna)   
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Repealing a portion of Resolution No. 5951 which pertains to the 
dedication of General Fund Reserves to design and build a second level on the Cheyenne 
Municipal Court Building – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Luna) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Certifying CONNECT 2045:  Update to the Master Transportation and 
Future Land Use Plan of PlanCheyenne for the City of Cheyenne and the Cheyenne Urban Area – 
referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Case) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a final plat for The 
Enclave at Northgate, a replat of a portion of Lots 6 and 7, all of Lot 8, and the east half of Lots 9 
thru 12, Block 19, North Cheyen ne 2 nd Filing, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming 
(located northwest of the intersection of North Gate Avenue and Yellowstone Road) – referred to 
Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Case) 
 
[CA] Preliminary Plat for Sweetgrass, 5th Filing, a subdivision of a portion of the N ½ of Section 
16, Township 13 North, Range 66 West of the 6th P.M., Laramie County, Wyoming (located south 
of E. College Drive, east of Sweetgrass Drive) .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried 
(acknowledged Planning Commission’s recommendation to approve). 
 
Memorandum of Understanding between EQ Capital , LLC, and the City of Cheyenne to 
build a technology ecosystem in Wyoming focused on investing in tech startups. (Postponed from 
November 9, 2020).   Mr. Luna moved to approve, seconded by Mr. White.  Mr. White explained 
city staff worked to come up with an amendment to address concerns.  Upon inquiry, Ms. Jones 
confirmed that Mr. Laybourn cast an affirmative vote at the November 16 th Finance Committee 
meeting, therefore, the agenda item met Consent Agenda criteria.  Mr. White moved to amend by 
substitute dated November 20, 2020, seconded by Mr . Luna.  Appreciation was voiced for the 
amendment and work by Brendan Ames, Chief Economic Development Officer, Attorney’s office 
and EQ Capital, noting the amendment removes previous concerns and provides for mutual official 
recognition that the parties we will work together on the project.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body  present with the exception of Mr. Laybourn voting 
“no”.  Main motion as amended carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present 
with exception of Mr. Laybourn voting “no”. (#7259)   
 
 
   
[CA] Development and Maintenance Agreement between Cheyenne-Laramie County 
Corporation for Economic Development, the City of Cheyenne, and the Cheyenne Business Park 
Owners Association for the Cheyenne Business Parkway Corridor Plan .  Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried. (#7260) 
 
[CA] Grant agreement between Memorial Hospital of Laramie County d/b/a Cheyenne Regional 
Medical Center and the City of Cheyenne Police Department for Law Enforcement Assisted 
Diversion (LEAD) Program officer overtime and client support (CRMC LEAD Grant) – referred 
to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7221  between the City of Cheyenne and 
Containment Systems for additional services to complete the Expansion of Landfill Permanent 
Litter Fence Project (Solid Waste Fund).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not 
to exceed $17,435.00). (#7221) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #3 to Contract #5932 between the City of Cheyenne and Solid Waste 
Professionals of Wyoming, for Happy Jack Landfill Expansion to extend the contract to March 31, 
2022 (Solid Waste Fund).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#5932) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract # 7216 between Memorial Hospital of Laramie 
County d/b/a Cheyenne Regional Medical Center and the City of Cheyenne Police Department for 
Law Enforcement Assisted Diversion (LEAD) Program (CRMC LEAD Grant) – referred to 
Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7117 between the City of Cheyenne and Western 
Research and Development, Ltd. for additional  design services for the 2020 Signal Upgrade 
Design Services Contract (2015-2018 1% Sales Tax) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid # S-2-21 for a contract between the City of Cheyenne and Casper 
Electric, Inc., for the 24 th / 25th / Carey / Pioneer Traffic Signal Upgrade Project (2015-2018 1% 
Sales Tax) .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (accepted bid in an amount not to exceed 
$677,384.84). (#7261) 
 
 Consideration of Bid #S-8-21 for a contract between the City of Cheyenne and JTL Group 
Inc. d/b/a Knife River, for the 2020 Miscellaneous Concrete Project (2015-2018 & 2019-2022 1% 
Sales Tax).  Mr. Luna moved to accept the bid in an amount not to exceed $443,436.48, seconded 
by Mr. White . Upon inquiry, Tom Cobb, City Engineer, provided information on locations of 
concrete work to be completed through th e bid.  Mr. Cobb reported this phase of the project will 
exhaust approximately half of available project funding and that the other half wi ll be expended 
through a future bid for remaining locations planned to be improved.  Motion carried.  Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body present. (#7262) 
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
   
 Upon inquiry by Mayor Orr, Robin Lockman, City Treasurer, provided information on the 
September 2020 sales tax collection explaining  she received an email from  the Department of 
Revenue that additional revenue was from the Roundhouse Windmill Project in an approximate 
amount of $2 million dollars.  She further reported that current 6th Penny Sales Tax collection is 
predicted to be complete by July of 2021, however it could be sooner if sales tax income remains 
strong.  Mayor Orr urged everyone to get together in January to start discussions on  future 6th 
Penny Sales Tax projects  and acknowledged that while it seems like a long way away , a lot of 
planning remains to be done.  No further comments were made related to the Revenue Report as 
presented. 
 
 Announcement of a Public Hearing was made to be held December 14, 2020 at 6:00 p.m. 
via electr onic conference meeting, to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions 
required by Wyoming Statute §15 -1-402 exist for land located southeast of the intersection of 
Powderhouse Road and Carlson Street.   
  
  There bein g no fur ther business to co me before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 6:40 p.m.  
 
 
 
        Submitted by, 
       
 
        Kristina F. Jones, City Clerk 
 
  
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  December 2, 2020

December 14, 2020

MAYOR - Marian Orr, C OUNCIL MEMBERS – Rocky Case,  Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, 
Mike Luna, Dr. Mark Rinne , Scott Roybal, Dicky Shanor and Jeff White.  Absent: Bryan Cook.  
Also attending: Kris Jones, City Clerk. [Clerk’s note: the pledge of allegiance was not recited due

 Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to

by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda. )  Mr. Luna moved to approve, seconded by Mr. White.  
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.  
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on November 23, 2020.  Motion 
(per Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
Mayor Orr opened a public hearing  to determine whether compliance of annexation 
conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15 -1-402 exist for land located southeast of the 
intersection of Powderhouse Road and Carlson Street.  Seth Lloyd, Planning and Development 
Department, advised the annex ation request was submitted by the landowner,  provided 
information on the property  and reviewed requirements of and compliance with annexation 
conditions contained in state statutes.   There being no further comments or input and purpose of 
the hearing having been met, Mayor Orr closed the hearing. 
 
ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending Chapter 10.44, Weight Limits, of Title 10, 
Vehicles and Traffic, of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming .  Reporting for 
Public Services Committee, Mr. Case moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by 
Mr. Roybal. Upon inquiry related to if scales have been purchased,  Chief Brian Kozak, Police 
Department, explained the Police Department has some scales that Highway Patrol loaned them a 
few years ago that they may be able to keep.  Chief Kozak advised that if they are unable to keep 
the scales, the city would purchase scales with drug forfeiture funding.  Support was expressed to 
Chief Kozak, the trucking industry and City employees for their work involved with the ordinance.  
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present with exception of Mr. 
Case, Mr. Luna and Mr. Shanor voting “no”. (#4333) 
 
ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Amending Section 2.84.070, Board of Adjustment, of 
Chapter 2.84, Miscellaneous Boards and Commissions, of Title 2, Administration and Personnel, 
of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, to correct cross references to the Board 
   
of Adjustment.  Charles Bloom, Director of Planning and Development, advised the  ordinance 
corrects cross references to the Board of Adjustment in Title 17.  Mr. Case moved to approve on 
third and final reading, seconded by Mr . Luna.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of 
the governing body present. (#4334) 
 
ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Amending Section 15.52.060(B), Notification of 
Issuance or Denial -Appeal, and Section 15.52.100, Variances, of Chapter 15.52, Solar Access 
Permit System, of Title 15, Buildings and Construction, of the Municipal Code of the City of 
Cheyenne, Wyoming, to correct cross references to the Board of Adjustment . Charles Bloom , 
Director of Planning and Development, advised the ordinance corrects cross references to Title 17 
in Title 15.  Mr. Case moved to approve on third and final  reading, seconded by Mr . Roybal.  
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. (#4335) 
 
ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Establishing a Planned Unit Development (PUD) District 
for property generally located northwest of the intersection of North Gate Avenue and Yellowstone 
Road.  Seth Lloyd, Planning and Development Department, advised  the zone change request to 
PUD would allow for a  duplex development.  Mr. Case moved to approve on third and final  
reading, seconded by Mr . Luna.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” - all members of the governing 
body present. (#4336) 
 
ORDINANCE –1st READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land

MEETING: City Council Meeting - Agenda Only | DATE: 2020-12-28 | CLIP_ID: 779 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 779

   
RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
December 28, 2020 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:06 p.m. via electronic conference meeting .  Attending electronic conference meeting  were: 
MAYOR - Marian Orr, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Rocky Case, Bryan Cook, Ken Esquibel, Pete 
Laybourn, Mike Luna,  Dr. Mark Rinne , Scott Roybal, Dicky Shanor and Jeff White.   Also 
attending: Kris Jones, City Clerk. The Pledge of Allegiance was recited. 
 
 Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda. )  Upon request by Dr. R inne, and pursuant to support 
received by Mr. Cook and Mr. Roybal, agenda item #13 was removed from the Consent Agenda.  
Mr. Luna moved to approve remaining items, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body.  
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on December 14, 2020.  Motion 
(per Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land 
located southeast of the intersection of Powderhouse Road and East Carlson Street .  Charles 
Bloom, Planning and Development Director, advised the annexation request is from Laramie 
County School District #1 for the purpose of constructing a new elementary school for grades 5-6 
and explained there is an affiliated item for a zone change request  and final plat on the agenda.    
Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Case moved to approve on second reading,  
seconded by Mr. Luna.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from County A-1 Agricultural and Rural Residential 
to P Public District for a tract of land generally located southeast of the intersection of 
Powderhouse Road and East Carlson Street.  Charles Bloom, Planning and Development Director, 
advised the zone change request is related to the previous annexation request from Laramie County 
School District #1 for the purpose of constructing a new elementary school for grades 5-6.  Mr. 
Case moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Luna.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” 
– all members of the governing body. 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Unified Development Code (UDC) to 
define, establish permissibility, and create specific use standards for the use ‘Mini Storage’.  Mark 
Christensen, Planning and Development  Department, explained the amendment stems from a 
specific request and updates storage-personal and storage-park and combines them as a cohesive 
   
definition.  Mr. Christensen advised that if a storage unit park is located in certain zoned areas, 
they must meet  certain criteria and noted that staff recommends approval.   Mr. Case moved to 
approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members 
of the governing body. 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending Section 2.04.020, Mayor -Election-Term of 
Office, of Chapter 2.04, Mayor and City Council, of Title 2, Administration and Personnel, of the 
Municipal Code of the city of Ch eyenne, Wyoming .  Dr. Rinne explained the ordinance 
amendment changes the Mayor’s office employees from regular employees to “at will” so future 
mayors can choose their own staff members.   Dr. Rinne clarified this change does not include the 
current staff members in the mayor’s office  and that the change s is intended for the future.  Mr. 
Case moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Cook.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” 
– all members of the governing body. 
 
 RESOLUTION – Designating local banks as depositories for municipal funds . Brenda 
Moreaux, Deputy City Treasurer, provided information on the resolution stating statutes require 
municipalities designate local banks  as depositories for municipal funds.  She explained staff 
supports approval of a proposed substitute resolution which adds Wells Fargo Bank to the listing.  
Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Luna moved to adopt, seconded by Mr.  White.  Mr. Luna 
moved to amend by substitute dated December 16, 2020, seconded by Mr.  Cook.  Ms. Moreaux 
advised all banks were given a deadline  to respond and Wells Fargo had a late response so the 
amendment now includes that bank.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body.  Main motion as amended carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body. (#6108) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Reappropriating the Fiscal Year 2021 Budget of the City of Cheyenne 
according to the provisions of W.S. §16 -4-112 & §16 -4-113.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#6109) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Supporting the City of Cheyenne’s application for a Land and Water 
Conservation Fund Grant to replace playground safety surfacing (revenue to the city).  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried.  (#6110) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Capital 
Heights Addition, Third Filing, a replat of all of Lots 3 and 4, Block 1018, Capital Heights 
Addition, Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located west of and adjacent to Dillon Avenue 
north of Foyer Avenue, currently addressed as 3810 Dillon Avenue).  Connor White, Planning and 
Development Department, provided information on the property including location and noted the 
final plat creates 4 lots for development of 4 townhomes .  Mr. White reported both the Planning 
Commission and city staff recommend approval.  Mr. Case moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. 
White.  Comment was made in opposition of the resolution and how the proposal isn’t a good fit 
for an established neighborhood as this type of development could impact property value.  Further 
comments were made acknowledging that city staff is making recommendations in compliance 
with current city code regulations.  It was further noted that the proposed final plat meets existing 
city code regulations.   Upon inquiry, Mr. White confirmed the replat consists of dividing 2 lots 
   
into 4 individual lots and the town houses will be approximately 20 ft. wide.   Comments were 
made relating to other similar lots within existing neighborhoods that have not had any negative 
impact on value or esthetics.  Upon inquiry, members of Planning and Development staff and Ward 
I City Council members confirmed they have not received any negative communication or 
comments from area residents regarding the proposed development.  Additional comments in 
support of the proposed infill project were voiced.  Upon inquiry, Charles Bloom, Planning and 
Development Director, provided information on the notification process which is the responsibility 
of the contractor to provide to area residents.  Mr. Bloom advised the required notice shall be 
provided and sign age posted prior to the first P lanning Commission meeting.   Motion carried.   
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Rinne voting “no”. 
(#6111) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Approving a Special Use Permit for oil and gas support services for Lot 
1, Block 1, Plains Industrial Park, 2 nd Filing, Laramie County, Wyoming .  Charles Bloom, 
Planning and Development Director, advised the city received a request to authorize a drilling 
operation to go along with oil extraction that was approved by the Board of Adjustment in 
December of 2019.  Mr. Bloom explained that Section 5.8.7 of the Unifie d Development Code 
allows the Governing Body to temporarily defer all or a portion of the development requirements 
in City Code and noted that the development will be temporary.  Mr. Bloom reported the proposed 
substitute includes the following deferral co ntributions: Deposits in the City’s Agency Fund for 
$29,389.59 in the Greenway Account, $5,962.50 in the Forestry account and $27,610.00 in the 
Park Enhancement Account which is park in lieu fees that are required at time of subdivision.  He 
further advised that staff recommends approval and that the exhibit referenced in the resolution is 
the last item in the pdf packet.  Mr. Case moved to adopt, seconded by Mr.  Roybal.  Mr. Case 
moved to amend by substitute dated December 17, 2020, seconded by Mr . Roybal.  Motion to 
amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  Main motion as amended 
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#6112) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to sign a final plat for Coyote 
Ridge, a plat of a portion of the northwest quarter of Section 20, Cheyenne, Laramie County, 
Wyoming (located at the southeast corner of Powderhouse Road and East Carlson Street) – 
referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Rocky Case) 
 
[CA] Grant award agreement with the State of Wyoming Office of Homeland Security for a grant 
from the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), FEMA, Grant Programs Directorate, 
SHSP Grant Fiscal Year 2020 in the amount of $115,000.00, for the Cheyenne Regional Response 
Team #7 (DHS Grant Code: EMW -2020-SS-00062).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. 
(#7268) 
 
[CA] Contract between the City of Cheyenne and Peak Wellness, Alcohol Receiving Ce nter, to 
provide alcohol and drug detoxication services to individuals (General Fund ).  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $115,000.00). (#7269) 
 
   
[CA] Contract between the City of Cheyenne and Safe Harbor to provide a safe and secure 
environment to families who have been affected by abuse (General Fund) .  Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $17,500.00). (#7270) 
 
 [CA] Contract between the City of Cheyenne and Cheyenne Housing Authority to provide 
supportive senior services (General Fund) .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount 
not to exceed $25,000.00). (#7271) 
 
 [CA] Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Laramie County Sheriff’s Department and 
Laramie County, Wyoming, for housing City pr isoners at the Laramie County Detention Center 
(Replaces Contract No. 7165 approved 4/27/2020).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#7165) 
 
[CA] Juvenile Housing Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Laramie County for the 
housing of juvenile detainees in the Laramie County Juvenile Services Center located at the Archer 
Complex (Replaces Contract No. 7166 approved 4/27/2020) .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#7166)         
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7 181 between the City of Cheyenne and Waste 
Management of Colorado, Inc., Denver CO, for Waste Management Recycling Services to extend 
the term of the agreement to December 31, 2021 (Solid Waste Fund) .  Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried. (#7181) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract # 7241 between the City of Cheyenne and Mid-
America Pool Renovation, Inc., for the Cheyenne Aquatic Center Main Pool Shell Resurfacing 
Project (Specific Purpose Sales Tax Overage Funds).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an 
amount not to exceed $43,850.00). (#7241) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #2 to Contract # 7207 between the City of Cheyenne and  Front 
Range Roofing Systems, LLC, for Fleet Maintenance Facility and Parks Maintenance Facility 
Roof Replacements (General Fund).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to 
exceed $5,660.00). (#7207) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #2 to Contract #6927 between Wyoming Homeland Security and 
the City of Cheyenne extending the term of the grant through August 31, 2021 (DHS Grand Code:  
EMW-2018-SS-00065) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #E-16-21 for furnishing three (3) new greens mowers, for the City of 
Cheyenne, Golf Division (Golf Improvement Fund) .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried 
(accepted bid from L.L. Johnson Distributing Company, Denver, CO, in an amount not to exceed 
$113,030.10). 
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
 No comments were made on the Revenue Report as presented. 
 
   
 Appointments of Gus Lopez to the Cheyenne -Laramie County Board of Health; Wendy 
Soto and Erin LeBlanc to the Housing and Communit y Development Advisory Council; Dustin 
Brown, Richard Maxted, and Ben Moritz to the Board of Adjustment, and Michael Vigil to the 
Building Code Board of Appeals.  Mr. Luna moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Shanor.  Motion 
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Orr who 
did not vote (mayoral appointments). 
 
 Announcement was made of  the Sine Die and First Regular Meetings of the Governing 
Body will be held Monday, January 4, 2021 beginning at 6:00 p.m. in the Cheyenne Civic Center, 
510 West 20th Street, Cheyenne, Wyoming and via electronic conference meeting. 
 
 Announcement was made that due to the Sine Die and First Regular Meetings of the 
Governing Body on Monday, January 4, 20 21, regularly scheduled Cit y Council Committee 
meetings will instead be held as follows: Finance Committee will meet at Noon on  Tuesday, 
January 5, 2021 via electronic conference meeting  and Public Services Committee will meet at 
Noon on Wednesday, January 6, 2021 via electronic conference meeting.  Additionally, all Finance 
Committee meetings for 2021 will be held at Noon instead of 11:00 a.m. 
 
 Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held January 11, 2021 at 6:00 p.m. via 
electronic conference meeting, to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required 
by Wyoming Statute §15-1-402 exist for land located southeast of the intersection of High Plains 
Road and South Greeley Highway. 
 
  There bein g no fur ther business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 6:35 p.m.  
 
 
        Submitted by, 
       
 
        Kristina F. Jones, City Clerk 
 
  
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  January 6, 2021

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
January 25, 2021 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. at the Cheyenne Civic Center and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: 
MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich , Bryan Cook, Ken 
Esquibel, Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne, Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff 
White.  Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited.  [Clerk’s note:  
Mr. Esquibel attended the meeting via electronically] 
 
 Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda.)  Mayor Collins noted agenda item #17(a) was inadvertently 
placed on the consent agenda. Upon request by Mr. Johnson, and pursuant to support received by 
Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Cook, agenda item # 17(a) was removed from the Consent Agenda.  Mr. 
Segrave moved to approve  remaining items, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Votin g 
“yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on January 11, 2021.  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land 
located east of and adjacent to South Greeley Highway between High Plains Road and Terry Ranch 
Road.  Reporting for Public Services Committee, Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, 
seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from County A-1 Agricultural and Rural Residential 
to AG Agricultural and HI Heavy Industrial for land located east of and adjacent to South Greeley 
Highway between High Plains Road and Terry Ranch Road.  Eric Crosby inquired on the industrial 
use planned for the land.  Brad Emmons , AVI PC, agent f or the applicant, advised the proposed 
zone will allow the land to be used for a data center project, noting it is not overall industrial in 
nature.  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.   
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from LI (Light Industrial) to MR (Medium -Density 
Residential) for property generally located northeast of the intersection of Pebrican Avenue and 
East 2 nd Street.  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Cook.  Mr. 
Segrave declared a conflict of interest due to a business relationship  and did not participate in  
   
discussion or voting.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the 
exception of Mr. Segrave who didn’t vote.  
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification from MR (Medium -Density Residential) to CB 
(Community Business) for property generally located northeast of the intersection of Carbon 
Avenue and East 13 th Street.  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr.  
Cook.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to sign a final plat for Bison 
Business Park, a plat of portions of Sections 28, 29, and 32, Township 13 North, Range 66 West 
of the 6 th P.M., City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located east of and adjacent to 
South Greeley Highway between High Plains Road and Terry Ranch Road).  Dr. Rinne moved to 
adopt, seconded by Mr.  Cook.  Dr. Rinne moved to postpone to February 8, 2021, seconded by 
Mr. Cook.  Motion to postpone carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a final plat for 
Sweetgrass, 5th Filing, a subdivision of a portion of the N½ of Section 16, Township 13 North, 
Range 66 West of the 6 th P.M., City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located south of 
East College Drive and adjacent to Sweetgrass Drive.  Dr. Rinne moved to adopt with revised final 
plat map dated January 19, 2021, seconded by Mr.  Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body. (#6118) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Adopting an amendment to the Future Land Use Map in PlanCheyenne, 
amending the land use category for property generally located east of South Greeley Highway at 
Terry Ranch Road from Agricultural and Mixed-Use Employment to Industrial and amending the 
Urban Service Boundary and Natural and Cultural Resources Area.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#6119) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing submission of a Federal Emergency Management Agency 
Preparedness Grant Application under the Assistance to Firefighters Grant Program, on behalf of 
the Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne, for the purpose of purchasing a fire engine – referred 
to Finance Committee.  Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Roybal advised the resolution had 
been reviewed under other items for the agenda at the January 19, 202 1 Finance Committee 
meeting, therefore, provisions of Title 2 of City Code have been met.  Mr. Roybal moved to adopt, 
seconded by Mr. Cook .  Cheyenne Fire and Rescue Interim  Chief John Kopper  provided 
information on the resolution and explained they are requesting a  grant to replace  the current 
Engine #1 which is in dire need of replacement and noted the grant requires a 10% match.  Upon 
inquiry, Interim Chief Kopper explaine d it is recommended that front line engines should be no 
older than 10 years  old.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  
(#6120) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing submission of a Federal Emergency Management Agency 
Preparedness Grant Application under the Assistance to Firefighters Grant Program, on behalf of 
the Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne, for the purpose of purchasing new automotive 
   
extrication equipment for all front line apparatus for Cheyenne Fire Rescue  – referred to Finance 
Committee.  Mr. Roybal advised the resolution had been reviewed under other items for the agenda 
at the January 19, 2021 Finance Committee meeting, therefore, provisions of Title 2 of City Code 
have been met.  Mr. Roybal moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. White.  Cheyenne Fire and Rescue 
Interim Chief John Kopper explained the grant application is a joint regional application and is for 
extraction equipment.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#6121) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Cheyenne Police Department to apply for Office on 
Violence Against Women OVW-2021-37003 Improving Criminal Justice Responses to Domestic 
Violence, Dating Violence, Sexual Assault and Stalking Grant Program CFDA Number 16.590 -
Grants to Encourage Arrests Policies and Enforcement of Protection Orders Program – referred to 
Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Roybal) 
 
 Preliminary Plat for Campstool Addition, 5 th Filing, generally located north of Venture

explained item #15 is on the consent agenda for referral to the Finance Committee.  Dr. Rinne

 Letter of Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Police Department, and the United 
States Department of Justice, Drug Enforcement Administration, for locating and eradicating illicit 
cannabis, and investigating and prosecuting those cases.  Sergeant Tim Meyrick, Cheyenne Police 
Department, advised the Police Department is in support of the agreement and explained the funds 
can be used for  overtime, training and approved equipment purchases.   Upon inquiry, Sergeant 
Meyrick explained the annual dollar amount for cannabis enforcement doesn’t usually exceed the 
agreement amount.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve in the amount of $65,000.00, seconded by Mr. 
Segrave.  Upon further inquiry, Sergeant Meyrick explained the primary purpose of the agreement 
is for cannabis eradication, but it can apply to other types of illegal substances that may be 
encountered during cannabis eradication .  Comment was made noting cannabis is legal in some 
form in 39 states.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the 
exception of Mr. Johnson voting “no”. (#7274) 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenn e, Cheyenne Metropolitan 
Planning Organization, and West Edge Collective LLC, for FY 2021 MPO Public Engagement 
and Web Support Services (MPO Federal funds) .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an 
amount not to exceed $31,200.00). (#7275) 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and GLM Design Group 
for the submission of two Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) Capability - 
and Capacity- Building Funding grant applications to FEMA for the City of Cheyenne (2019-2022 
1% Sales Tax).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $32,000.00). 
(#7276) 
 
   
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Little Joe Company, 
LLC, for the Janitorial Services for City of Cheyenne Facilities Project (General Fund, Fleet 
Maintenance Fund & Solid Waste Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and L and L, Inc. for the 
provision of golf services at the Airport Golf Clubhouse – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Lease Agreement  between the City of Cheyenne and L and L, Inc. for the use of the 
Kingham Prairie View Clubhouse and the provision of golf services at the Kingham Prairie View 
Golf Course – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Cheyenne and Laramie County 
School District Number One (LCSD #1) to provide LCSD #1 use of city owned softball fields for 
practices and competitions – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and GLM Design Group 
for drainage engineering support (2019-2022 1% Sales Tax) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract # 7206 between the City of Cheyenne and Inman 
Roofing, Inc., to replace wood nailer on Cheyenne Aquatic Center roof (General Fund -CIP 
Account).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $3,475.10). (#7206) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7257 between the City of Cheyenne and Clean Air 
and Water Systems, LLC, for the Happy Jack Landfill Phase 2, Cells 1 and 2 and Cell 3 Excavation 
Earthworks project for additional labor to install liner in the leachate trench (Solid Waste Fund) – 
referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7258 between the City of Cheyenne and Northwest 
Linings & Geotextile Products Inc., for the Happy Jack Landfill Phase 2, Cells 1 and 2 and Cell 3 
Excavation Earthworks project for additional liner and shipping cost for the leachate trench  (Solid 
Waste Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #2 to Contract #6798 between the City of Cheyenne and Trihydro 
Corporation to extend the Environmental Monitoring at the Happy Jack Landfill for an additional 
three years (Solid Waste Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S-9-21 for a contract between the City of Cheyenne and 4 Quarters 
Excavation & Development for the East Cheyenne Community Park -Parking Lot and Trailhead 
Construction Project (Specific Purpose Sales Tax) .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried ( in an 
amount not to exceed $117,499.00). (#7277) 
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
 No comments were made on the Revenue Report as presented. 
 
   
 Reappointment of Gregg Jones to the Brownfields Revolving Loan Committee.   Upon 
inquiry, it was advised Mr. Jones has served on the Brownfields Revolving Loan Committee for 
approximately 3 years.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion carried.  
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Collins who did 
not vote (mayoral appointment).   
 
 Appointment of Don Pierson to the Police Civil Service Commission.  Mr. Segrave moved 
to approve, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body with the exception of Mayor Collins who did not vote (mayoral appointment).  
 
 Under other business:  
  
 Mr. White noted the annual audit report by McGee, Hearne and Paiz, LLP was heard 
recently by members of the governing body and resulted in a clean audit with no recommendations.  
Mr. White expressed appreciation to the City Treasurer’s offices under the leadership of City 
Treasurer Robin Lockman.  Mayor Collins congratulated Ms. Lockman for the successful audit. 
 
 Mr. Johnson expressed condolences for the recent passing of prior city employee Scott 
Smith.  Mayor Collins also expressed condolences. 
 
 Mr. Laybourn reported on the ribbon cutting ceremony held at the Cheyenne A quatic 
Center for their reopening.  He also  commented on the Civic Center and how the Cheyenne  
Symphony Orchestra has been able to continue performing at this venue, noting however, the need

preparing the venue for various uses. 
 
  There bein g no fur ther business to come before the governing body, the meeting was

        Submitted by,

MEETING: City Council Meeting - Agenda Only | DATE: 2021-02-22 | CLIP_ID: 790 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 790

   
RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
February 22, 2021 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:0 0 p.m. via electronic conference meeting .  Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins , 
COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Bryan Cook, Ken Esquibel, Richard Johnson, Pete 
Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne, Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White.  Also present: Kris Jones, 
City Clerk. 
 
 Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda. )  Upon request by Mr.  Laybourn, and pursuant to support 
received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Johnson, agenda items #16 & 17 were removed from the Consent 
Agenda.  Mr. White moved to approve remaining items, seconded by Mr. Roybal.  Motion carried.  
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on February 8, 2021.  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for r enewal applications for existing City liquor 
licenses (retail, restaurant, limited retail, resort, bar and grill licenses, microbrewery, satellite 
distillery, winery and special malt beverage permits) filed with the City Clerk’s Office.  There 
being no comments or input and purpose of the hearing having been met, the applications were 
referred to Committee of the Whole  to be held on March 3, 2021 at 6:00 p.m. at the Cheyenne 
Civic Center and via electronic conference meeting, and Mayor Collins closed the hearing. 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Unified Development Code (UDC) 
Section 5.8.4, Fences.  Brandon Swain voiced support for the ordinance.   Reporting for Public 
Services Committee, Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr.  Segrave.  
Comment was made related to the proposed allowed 7’ height of privacy fences d iscouraging 
people from seeing over them to adjacent areas that may contain debris that needs to be picked up.  
It was also noted the rationale of increasing privacy fences from 6’ to 7’ is to align with what the 
International Building Code ( IBC) allows and that fences over 6’ require a building permit. Dr. 
Rinne moved to amend  Section 4(a)(2) by changing the fence height from  7’ to 6’, seconded by 
Mr. Cook.  Dr. Rinne noted the reason for the amendment would be to keep fence height the same 
with what it has been historically and because 7’ fences would require a building permit.  Upon 
inquiry, Charles Bloom, Planning and Development Director, advised that both 6’ and 7’ fences 
could be a visual barrier and it is u p to the governing body to determine what is aesthetically 
appropriate for neighborhoods.  He further noted that different fence heights ranging from 6’ -8’ 
aren’t uncommon in neighborhoods generally and that 7’ fence pickets are n’t available for 
   
purchase but 8’ pickets can be purchased and cut down.  Mr. Bloom further explained upon inquiry 
that the proposed setback from side streets is the main scope  of the ordinance.  Motion to amend 
carried.  Voting “ yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Esquibel 
and Mr. Segrave voting “no”.  Main motion as amended carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of 
the governing body. 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Unified Development Code of the City of 
Cheyenne, Wyoming, to create the definition, ‘Family Unit’ and amend the definition of ‘Dwelling 
Unit’.  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr.  Segrave.  Concern was 
expressed related to ordinance timing due to a housing crisis in the community and there not being 
an efficient way to monitor or enforce the ordinance.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members 
of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel and Mr. Laybourn voting 
“no”.  
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending various sections of Chapter 12.04, Streets, 
Sidewalks, and Driveways Generally, of Title 12, Streets, Sidewalks and Public Places, of the 
Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming . Amber Ash , Downtown Development Authority 
Director, advised the DDA board met last week and voted to support the ordinance.   She further 
explained she  has been working on th e ordinance with city staff for several months to find a 
solution to address downtown sidewalks without putting a burden on property owners.   It was 
noted that one concern is that if a property is located between 2 buildings, there can be issues with 
meeting DDA requirements.   Patti R iesland, Mayor’s Council for People with Disabilities,  
commented on 2 studies conducted in the areas of 16th St. to 24th St. and from Warren to Pioneer 
that had results indicating an abundance of  disrepair between 16 th and 19th Streets.  She further 
noted that conditions are causing  difficulty for walking in certain areas  and there are  overall 
accessibility concerns resulting in negative economic impact as people with disabilities have issues 
with navigating aspects of  downtown streets, sidewalks and curbs .  Reporting for Finance 
Committee, Mr. Roybal moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. White.  Mr. Roybal 
moved to amend by substitute submitted February 16, 2021 by the attorney’s office, seconded by 
Mr. White.  Alessandra McCoy Fakelman, Deputy City Attorney, explained the substitute includes 
clarification regarding responsibilities of the city and adjacent property owners noting the city is 
only responsible for curb and gutter and that language related to liens was also refined.  Motion to 
amend by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  Support for the 
ordinance was expressed.  Main motion as amended carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body. 
 
ORDINANCE –1st READING – Pursuant to Section 2.2.2 Planned Development 
Regulating Plan and Section 5.6.2 PUD -Planned Unit Development District, of the Cheyenne 
Unified Development Code (UDC) amending Ordinance Number 3741, which established The 
Village Planned Unit Development (PUD), to allow mixed use business (MUB) District  Use on 
Lot 28 of Block 2 of The Village PUD located southwest of the intersection of Powderhouse Road 
and Old Town Lane – referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Rinne) 
 
 
 
   
ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending Chapter 5.68, Body Art Establishments and 
Operations, of the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming – referred to Finance Committee. 
(Sponsor – Dr. Aldrich) 
 
ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending Section 5.12.150, Suspension or Revocation 
of License; Denial of Permit, of Chapter 5.12 , Alcoholic Liquor and Malt Beverages, of Title 5, 
Business Licenses and Regulations, of the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming – referred to 
Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Roybal) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to sign a final plat for Cahill Park 
Addition, Filing No. 5, a replat of Lot 2, Block 1, Cahill Park Addition, Filing No. 4, Cheyenne, 
Laramie County, Wyoming (located south of and adjacent to Dell Range Boulevard between 
Windmill Road and Moran Avenue).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.  (#6123) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the sale of surplus city-owned property generally located at 
the northeast corner of Morrie Avenue and east Lincolnway, together with improvements thereon, 
and authorizing the Mayor to proceed with sale and transfer of the property.  Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried.  (#6124) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Calling for an Americans with Disabilities Act Compliance evaluation 
and transition plan for the City of Cheyenne Municipal Building .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#6125) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing creation of a Community Technology Advisory Council and 
Directing the Mayor to appoint the same .  Gunnar Malm, County Commissioner, requested 
clarification on the composition of members of the advisory council.  Mayor Collins provided 
advisory council information explaining he is looking to bring a group of experts together to help 
him understand what is needed to enhance technology and promote a technology driven 
environment moving forward for businesses.  It was noted that the advisory council will help  
determine what is needed to make the city’s tech community stronger.  Mayor Collins further 
explained it is not anticipated that the advisory council will result in any financial impact.  Eric 
Trowbridge, CEO of Array, spoke in support of the resolution and advisory council and provided 
information on the broadband task force outlining 7 key recommendations to make sure the city is 
prepared for the future in technology.  Mr. Trowbridge advised it would be ideal that the advisory 
council deliver information to the governing body on an ongoing basis.  Dr. Rinne moved to adopt, 
seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Discussion followed on possible language amendments to clarify the 
intent of the advisory council providing clarification on the member composition.  As sponsor of 
the resolution, Dr. Aldrich advised she was amenable to proposed amendments as the advisory 
council is non-binding and may include people that live outside of city limits and noted technology 
doesn’t stop at the city limits.  Upon inquiry, Mayor Collins provided additional information on 
the intent of the advisory council noting it will be a  group of individuals with knowledge in the 
field of technology providing advice for the future of technology.  Dr. Rinne moved to amend the 
5th “Whereas” paragraph by replacing “residents” with “members” and deleting the remainder of 
the paragraph, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Mr. Malm stated he is supportive of the amendment as it 
clarifies the membership and noted he  supports the advisory council.  Mr. White suggested a 
   
friendly amendment related to the motion on the floor r eplacing “residents” with “members” and 
deleting the remainder of the 8th paragraph.  Dr. Rinne accepted the proposed friendly amendment 
with Dr. Aldrich concurring as second to the motion.   (Amendment with friendly amendment: 
Paragraph 5, replace “residents” with “members” and remove the remainder of the sentence to 
read:  “Whereas, the Community Technology Advisory Council will be comprised of seven (7) 
members” and in the Be it further Resolv ed paragraph, replace “residents with “members” and 
remove “residents from the  City of Cheyenne, the County of Laramie and its incorporated towns 
and cities”). Motion to amend, including the friendly amendment, carried.   Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body.  Main motion as amended carried.  Voting “yes” – all members 
of the governing body. (#6126) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing creation of an Innovation and Entrepreneur Advisory 
Council and Directing the Mayor to appoint the same .  Dr. Rinne moved to adopt, seconded by 
Mr. Segrave.  Dr. Aldrich explained this is a non -binding advisory council , there is a lot of 
entrepreneurial activity in the community and many other communities have this type of council.  
Dr. Aldrich further noted the Univer sity of Wyoming has received funding and will partner with 
LCCC to provide the opportunity to hear from people in many different fields about areas of 
interest that attract people and keep people in our community.   Dr. Rinne moved to amend by 
replacing “residents” with “members” and deleting the remainder of the paragraph for paragraphs 
6 and 9, seconded by Dr. Aldrich.  Motion to amend carried.   Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body.  Main motion as amended carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body.  As a point of clarification, City Clerk Kris Jones noted agenda item #19 may have 
inadvertently not been requested to be removed from the agenda, and Mayor Collins explained the 
item can remain on the agenda. (#6127) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Reappropriating the Fiscal Year 2021 Budget of the City of Cheyenne 
according to the provisions of W.S. 16 -4-112 & 16 -4-113 – referred to Finance Committee. 
(Sponsor – Mr. Roybal) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing submission of a Federal Emergenc y Management Agency 
Preparedness Grant under the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) 
Program, on behalf of the Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne, for the purpose of providing 
additional staffing – referred to Finance Committee.  (Sponsor – Mr. Roybal) 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Cheyenne Metropolitan 
Planning Organization (MPO), and BenchMark Engineers, PC for the Walterscheid Boulevard 
Reconstruction Plan (MPO Federal Funds).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount

[CA] Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and LuckyDog Recreation, Ashton, ID, for the

[CA] Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Star Playgrounds, Littleton, CO, for the 
South Lions Park Play System Project (Community Facility Fees Fund and Land and Water 
   
Conservation Grant) .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed 
$249,499.00). (#7289) 
 
[CA] Grant Award Agreement with the State of WY Office of Homeland Security for a grant 
from the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), FEMA, Grant Programs Directorate, 
SHSP Grant Fiscal Year 2018 in  the amount of $3,418.28 for the Cheyenne Regional Response 
Team #7  (DHS Grand Code:  EMW -2018-SS-00065).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.  
(#7290) 
 
[CA] Section 5307 COVID-19 Emergency Relief for Operations Grant Agreement between the

[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract # 7134 between the City of Cheyenne and  AVI

[CA] Contract Modification #1 for Renewal and Amendment of Agreement #7033 (Contract

Organization, to remediate hazardous substances to renovate the building located at 1605 Central

[CA] Contract Modification #8 to Contract # 6162 between the City of Cheyenne and 
CenturyLink Communications, LLC, for modification to the City’s Metro Ether net network

[CA] Consideration of Bid #S -1-21 for a Contract between the City of Cheyenne and Simon 
Contractors, for the 24 th Street Mill and Overlay Project (2015-2018 and 2019 -2022 1% Sales

[CA] Consideration of Bid #S-11-21 for a Contract between the City of Cheyenne and CXT, Inc. 
an LB Foster Company, Spokane, WA, for the Cheyenne Junior League Pre -Cast Restroom and 
Concession Building Project (Community Facility Fees and Recreation Mill Grant) – referred to

[CA] Consideration of Bid #E-13-21 for furnishing eight (8) new four-door 2021 Model Utility 
(SUV) Police Interceptors, and one (1) 2021 Utility Cargo Vehicle (Van) for the City of Cheyenne, 
Cheyenne Police Department  (2019-2022 1% Sales Tax) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #E-14-21 for furnishing eight (8) Motorola APX8500 Mobile Radios 
for the City of Cheyenne, Cheyenne Police Department (2019-2022 1% Sales Tax) – referred to 
Finance Committee. 
 
   
[CA] Request to expand retail liquor license premise dimensions for HEJE, Inc. d/b/a Outlaw 
Liquors, 4503 Western Way, Suite C – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
 No comments were made on the Revenue Report as presented. 
 
 Appointment of Mark G. Francisco as Chief of Police for the City of Cheyenne.  Dr. Rinne 
moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Roybal.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body with the exception of Mayor Collins who did not vote (mayoral appointment). 
  
 Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held Monday, March 8, 2021, at 6:00 
p.m. in the Cheyenne Civic Center, 510 W. 20 th Street, Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via electronic 
conference meeting, for a restaurant liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s office 
for Machapuchare Inc. d/b/a Durbar Nepalese & Indian Bistro, 3515 E. Lincolnway, Cheyenne, 
Wyoming. 
 
 Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held Monday, March 8, 2021, at 6:00 
p.m. in the Cheyenne Civic Center, 510 W. 20 th Street, Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via electronic 
conference meeting , to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by 
Wyoming Statute §15-1-402 exist for land located north of Dell Range Boulevard west of Whitney

 Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held Monday, March 8, 2021, at 6:00

Wyoming Statute §15-1-402 exist for land located north of Dell Range Boulevard east of Griffith

 Under other business:  
  
 Amber Ash, Director of DDA, provided an update on the downtown  graffiti abatement 
program stating removal from buildings with the permission of property owners is in process.  She 
noted the DDA is also working with CoreCivic to apply paint that was provided by the Public 
Works Department to trash receptacles that have been ta gged.  It was further advised that Black 
Hills Energy has also been applying paint to graffiti on their boxes and David Hatch, owner of the 
Hynds Building, has whitewashed plywood on the Bell Building.  She noted that the DDA hopes 
to be able to install cameras in downtown areas to help curb graffiti activity in the future.  Ms. Ash 
expressed appreciation to Mark Christensen, Planning and Development, for presenting the West 
Edge Overlay District information to their board.  Mayor Collins thanked Ms. Ash for her efforts 
in supporting downtown.  Upon inquiry, Ms. Ash provided information on the mural program and 
explained generally the murals haven’t historically been tagged and that they provide vibrancy to 
downtown and help detour graffiti. 
 
 
   
 Mr. White moved to meet in executive session pursuant to Wyoming Statute §16-4-405(x),    
for the purpose of  a personnel matter related to Collective Labor Bargaining with Cheyenne 
Professional Fire Fighters, International Association of Fire Fighters, Local No. 279, seconded by

announced members would meet in executive session v ia private conference call, not open to the

present and stated there would be no action taken by the governing body as a result of the executive 
session, and that t he regular City Council meeting would officially conclude at the close of the 
executive session. (Clerk’s Note: executive session convened at 7:04 p.m.).     
 
 Following closure of the executive session, Mayor Collins reconvened the regular meeting 
at 8:03 p.m.   
 
  There bein g no fur ther business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 8:03 p.m.  
 
        Submitted by, 
       
 
        Kristina F. Jones, City Clerk
