RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
May 10, 2021 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Bryan Cook, Ken Esquibel (via 
Zoom), Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne , Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff 
White.  Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
 Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda. )  Upon re quest by  Dr. Rinne , and pursuant to support 
received by Mr. Johnson and Mr. White, agenda item #32 was removed from the Consent Agenda.  
Mr. Roybal moved to approve remaining items, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on April 26, 2021.  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation 
conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15 -1-402 exist for land located north of Pershing 
Boulevard and west of Christensen Road.   Seth Lloyd, Planning and Development Department, 
explained they received a petition to annex the land, provided information on the property  and 
reviewed requirements of compliance with annexation conditions contained in state statutes.  Mr. 
Lloyd explained agenda items #21 & # 22 are affiliated with the annexation  and s ingle-family 
homes and duplexes are proposed for the area.  Upon inquiry, Mr. Lloyd explained the intersection 
of Pershing & Christensen is currently outside of city limits.  There being no further comments or 
input and purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the hearing. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation 
conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15 -1-402 exist for land located east of and adjacent to 
South Greeley Highway [US 85], north of Chalk Bluff Road. Seth Lloyd, Planni ng and 
Development Department, explained they received a petition to annex the land, provided 
information on the property and reviewed requirements of compliance with annexation conditions 
contained in state statutes.  Mr. Lloyd explained agenda items #23 & #24 are affiliated with the 
annexation and advised the land is proposed to be used for industrial purposes.  Upon inquiry, Mr. 
Lloyd explained there are approximately 432 acres that will be annexed between the prior public 
hearing annexation and this one.  Concern was expressed with expanding emergency services to 
annexed areas.  Mr. Lloyd advised Police Department and Fire Department  are asked to review 
annexations and plats and he doesn’t believe there were any comments made, noting however, the 
   
absence of comments doesn’t mean there won’t be any concerns with expanding services.  
Comment was stressed that the city needs to make sure services can be covered  when new areas 
are annexed.  There being no further comments or input and purpose of the hearing having been 
met, Mayor Collins closed the hearing. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation 
conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15 -1-402 exist for land located southwest of the 
intersection of Br aehill Road, Parkhill Road, and Panorama Drive. Seth Lloyd , Planning and 
Development Department,  explained they received a petition to annex the land, provided 
information on the property and reviewed requirements of compliance with annexation conditions 
contained in state statutes.  Mr. Lloyd explained agenda items #25 & #26 are affiliated with the 
annexation and duplex development is proposed for the area. There being no further comments or 
input and purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the hearing. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for a bar and grill liquor license application filed

approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr . White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all

of the revenue required to meet the said appropriation, all for t he fiscal year beginning July 1,

(#4361) 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the City of Cheyenne’s Solid Waste Fee 
Schedule.  Vicki Nemecek, Director of Public Works, explained this is the annual amendment of 
the fee schedule and provided information on the areas of increase.  Ms. Nemecek reported that 
residential trash and recycling services are subsidizing other services.  She provided details on 
proposed changes which include: removal of 1.5 yard waste containers, removal of acceptance of 
single items at transfer station, increased fee for 1.5 cubic yard container cleaning, increased fee 
for disposition of tires based on weight, and removal of “There is no guarantee the optional yard 
waste collection program will be available upon return” sentence in Note 11.   Ms. Nemecek 
advised that upon request from members of the governing body,  she will work on a media 
campaign for informational purposes for the solid waste program.  Ms. Nemecek provided 
clarification on removal of 1.5 cubic yard waste containers and the increase in cleaning fee of the 
1.5 cubic yard container.  Upon further inquiry, Ms. Nemecek advised over the years they have 
been looking at whether containers are picked up on the street or in an alley and explained that 
pick up location is consistent per  block and/or neighborhood .  Ms. Nemecek exp lained, u pon 
inquiry, that there was a previous increase for the yard waste program of $1.20 so they could invest 
in more equipment , drivers and bins so the program could be expanded, and bins are available . 
She further explained since the program fee increase, money is not being lost on the program, but 
services aren’t being used efficiently as there aren’t enough subscribers.  Additional drivers and 
equipment are being utilized in other areas of the solid waste program for additional pick-ups, etc. 
During discussion related to Colorado taking plastic numbers 1-6, it was noted the expectation is 
plastics recycling overall will decrease, not increase.  Appreciation was expressed to Ms. Nemecek 
for working on the PSA regarding recycling.  Ms. Nemecek provided information on the “Recycle 
Coach” app which can assist customers.  Upon further inquiry related to why plastic recycling isn’t 
expanding, Ms. Nemecek advised  contractors typically are not willing to take a loss due to 
accepting materials they will lo se money on such as plastics .  Ms. Nemecek noted tin cans, 
cardboard and glass provide a positive return, however, to accept glass, they would have to increase 
program fees.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. White.   Motion 
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Unified Development Code (UDC) to 
increase the total lot coverage of the MD1, MD2, P -CV1, P-CV2, and P-CV3 lot types to 80% .    
Dr. Rinne advised there was no recommendation on the item at the Public Services Committee .  
Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr.  Segrave.  Dr. Rinne reported 
concerns were raised during the Public Services Committee that although the proposal is to allow 
greater building coverage in those lot types, it would leave a negative effect relating to decreased 
landscaping requirements.  Comment was made that caution was raised by the Board of Public 
Utilities relating to water usage concerns involving landscaping water requirements.  Additional 
   
concerns were raised in areas relating to landscaping, primarily trees, which have died due to lack 
of maintenance in areas such as around the airport terminal.  Comments were made that developers 
follow landscaping requirements when  properties are developed, but those green areas  are not 
maintained after completion.  Concerns were raised  related to management and enforcement of 
landscaping requirements and request was made to take this o pportunity to look at  the current 
landscaping code for possible revisions.   Mayor Collins advised staff is currently working with 
property owners on possible improvements.  It was further advised  each development will be  
required to resize runoff facilities to accommodate terrain changes involving landscaping.  Motion 
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body  with exception of Dr. Aldrich, Mr. 
Laybourn and Dr. Rinne voting “no”.   
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Creating Chapter 8.29, Hood System Cleaning 
Companies, of Title 8, Health and Safety, of the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming. Division 
Chief Byron Mathews, Cheyenne Fire and Rescue Department, reported the  creation of  the 
ordinance is for hood cleaning contractors to ensure that those contractors who clean hood systems 
are properly licensed, insured and trained.  Mr. Mathews advised this ordinance m irrors the fire 
extinguisher business licensing requirement.  Mr. Mathews, upon inquiry, provided information 
on a recent incident where an individual who did not have proper training provided services to a 
local restaurant  and the restaurant equipment was left at high risk for catching  fire and food 
contamination.  Mr. Matthews explained that  with approval of the ordinance, the fire department 
will know who is providing service s and can make sure they are qualified. He reported last year 
there were approximately 10 instances where hood  systems were  not properly maintained or 
cleaned.  It was noted that the ordinance was drafted at the request and in consultation with local 
HVAC and knowledgeable hood cleaning contractors.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve on second 
reading, seconded by Dr. Aldrich.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body.

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
May 24, 2021 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Bryan Cook, Richard Johnson, 
Pete Laybourn,  Dr. Mark Rinne , Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave  and Jeff White.  Absent: Ken 
Esquibel.  Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
 EXPRESSION OF APPRECIATION TO THE 2020-2021 MAYOR’S YOUTH 
COUNCIL AND STATE OF THE YOUTH ADDRESS. Jan Spires, Youth Alternatives and staff 
advisor to the Mayor’s Yout h Council, expressed appreciation to Youth Council members, 
recognized their year in service and introduced Emily Lucero , Chair, for the Mayor’s Youth 
Council, who presented the State of the Youth Address.  Ms. Lucero  reviewed projects and 
programs the group participated in throughout the year.  She expressed appreciation to Ms. Spires, 
Michael Skinner , City Public Information Offi cer, Ha ylee Chenchar and Amber Ash with the 
Downtown Development Authority , Mayor Collins and fellow Youth Council members.  Ms. 
Spires thanked the member’s parents for allowing them to participate  with the council and  
introduced and presented awards to th e following members: Kaylee Ashley, David Barker, Ty 
Bronder, Garrison Cook, Makiya Green, Nevaeh Green, Emily Lucero, Zoey Lundin and Elizabeth 
Stump.  
 
 Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda ).  Mr. Johnson declared a conflict of interest due to an 
employment affiliation and did not vote.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve, seconded by Mr. White.  
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of 
Mr. Johnson who did not vote. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on May 10, 2021.  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for a retail liquor license transfer of location 
application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Poor Richard’s, from 2233 E. Lincolnway to 
1808 O’Neil Ave., Cheyenne, Wyoming .  Inquiry was made related to the location and scope of 
the business and it was noted no representatives were present to report on the inquiry.  There being 
no further comments or input and purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed 
the hearing and referred the application to Finance Committee. 
 
   
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for a retail liquor license  transfer of ownership 
application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for ARCHCO Albany, LLC d/b/a Albany Restaurant, 
Bar, and Package Li quor, 1506 Capitol Ave., Cheyenne, Wyoming (license currently held by 
Albany, Inc. d/b/a Albany Restaurant, Bar and Liquormart).  Brian Bau, ARCHCO Albany, LLC 
representative, advised he was available to answer any questions.   There being no  further 
comments or input and purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the hearing 
and referred to application to Finance Committee. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for a bar and grill liquor license application filed 
with the City Cler k’s Office for Capitol Cuisine LLC  d/b/a Ike’s Bar & Grill , 122 West 6 th St., 
Cheyenne, Wyoming. Upon inquiry, Brian Eicholtz, Ike’s Bar & Grill, provided information on 
the extensive remodel of the building and advised the business will be a neighborhood bar and 
grill.  There being no  further comments or input and purpose of the hearing having been met, 
Mayor Collins closed the hearing and referred the application to Finance Committee. 
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Amending the City of Cheyenne’s Solid Waste Fee 
Schedule.  Vicki Nemecek, Public Works Director, advised she was available for any questions.  
Reporting for Finance Committee,  Mr. Roybal moved to approve on third and final  reading, 
seconded by Mr.  Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body  
present with the exception of Mr. Cook voting “no”. (#4361) 
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Amending the Unified Development Code (UDC) to 
increase the total lot coverage of the MD1, MD2, P-CV1, P-CV2, and P-CV3 lot types to 80% .    
Dr. Rinne advised there was no recommendation on the item at the Public Services Committee .  
Dr. Rinne moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr.  Johnson.  Comments 
were made regarding continue d lack of maintenance of landscaping following planting resulting 
in death of plants/trees which are not being replaced.  Discussion included the need to review 
landscaping requirements and maintenance responsibilities.  It was noted that the proposed 
amendment only effects certain lot types  and is a way to save water usage .  Concern was raised 
regarding reduced area of green in some areas to 50’ x 50’, noting landscaping is important for 
various reasons.  Dr. Rinne moved to amend all references to 80%  be changed to 70%, seconded 
by Dr. Aldrich.  Dr. Rinne noted the proposed amendment is an attempt to compromise, and his 
preference would be to revisit in a year.  It was reported that some lots currently have less than the 
70% required.  Motion to amend failed. Voting “yes” - Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne and 
Mr. White.  Voting “no” - Mayor Collins, Mr. Cook, Mr. Johnson, Mr. Roybal and Mr. Segrave. 
Main motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body  present with exception 
of Mr. Laybourn and Dr. Rinne voting “no”. (#4362)  
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Creating Chapter 8.29, Hood System Cleaning 
Companies, of Title 8, Health and Safety, of the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming .  Mr. 
Roybal moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Dr. Aldrich.  Upon inquiry, 
Division Chief Byron Mathews, Cheyenne Fire & Rescue Department, clarified that businesses 
will be required to be licensed moving forward with no provisions to grandfather businesses.  Chief 
Mathews explained that although there may be an initial impact on businesses due to uniformity 
and initial higher cost for cleaning , eventually there would be a cost savings  which will result in 
   
an overall safety for consumers moving forward.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of 
the governing body present. (#4363) 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending Section 5.12.030, Licenses and Permits -
Types, of Chapter 5.12, Alcoholic Liquor and Malt Beverages, of Title 5, Business Licenses and 
Regulations, of the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming .  Mr. Roybal moved to approve on 
second reading, seconded by Mr . Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body present.   
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending various sections of Chapter 5.12, Alcoholic 
Liquor and Malt Beverages, of Title 5, Business Licenses and Regulations, of the Code of the City 
of Cheyenne, Wyoming .  Mr. Roybal moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr . 
White. It was noted that initially it was believed  delivery services may reduce DUI’s, however, 
after the li mited 6-month period during the COVID pandemic, they actually increased.  Further  
comments included: support for the ordinance, limited time frame and increased alcohol intake 
due to the COVID pandemic may have contributed to the increase of DUI’s, more establishments 
will likely participate if delivery is available permanently and the importance of businesses being 
able to compete and provide additional services.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of 
the governing body present with the exception of Mr. Laybourn and Dr. Rinne voting no. 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending various sections of Chapter 5.12, Alcoholic 
Liquor and Malt Beverages, of Title 5, Business Licenses and Regulations, of the Code of the City 
of Cheyenne, Wyoming Mr. Roy bal moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr.  
Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.   
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Repealing Chapter 2.52, Personnel Commission, and 
creating a new Chapter 2.52, Personnel System, of Title 2, Administration and Personnel, of the 
Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming. Seth Lloyd, Planning and Development Department and 
CPEA representative, noted concerns relating to this and the following agenda items pertaining to 
proposed changes to the Personnel Commission.  Mr. Lloyd reported d issolving the commission 
is concerning to city employees  and requested clarification on the effect this will have on 
employees, urging caution proceeding with the proposed changes.  Linda B urt, Personnel 
Commission Vice Chair , voiced concerns and explained members of the commission are 
volunteers and the commission  provides fairness and due process .  Ms. Burt noted  the proposal 
calls for the hearing officer to be paid for by the city which may give the appearance of bias.  Dr. 
Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. White.   Dr. Rinne moved to amend 
by substitute dated May 24, 2021, seconded by Mr.  White.  City Attorney Mike O’Donnell 
explained the amendment clarifies that the existing grievance procedure  will not be eliminated .  
Mayor Collins overruled a point of order raised regarding comments not being germane to the 
agenda item on the floor.  Upon inquiry, Mayor Collins advised concerns were raised on removing 
the opportunity of having a jury of peers participate in hearing procedures for city employees.  Mr. 
Lloyd reported there is an impression by city employees that the commission is a trial by jury and 
if the city appoints a hearing officer, that person may be predisposed to rule in favor of the city.  It 
was additionally noted employees fear the new procedure won’t be as fair as the current process. 
Upon inquiry, Mr. O’Donnell provided information on the current Personnel Commission which 
   
consists of 7 members - 3 city employee representatives and 4 citizens appointed by the Mayor.  
Mr. O’Donnell explained that due to the volunteer status of members, it can be difficult to assemble 
the commission for hearings.  Motion to amend carried.  Comments followed relating to support 
for the ordinance, informal grievance process,  concerns involving one individual to serve as 
hearing officer, establishing a fair process, inclusion of a neutral party hearing officer, providing 
training to Personnel Commission members and potential of a conflict of interest when employee 
representative members of the commission are employees of the same department the petitioner is 
employed by.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body  
present.  Main motion as amended carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body  
present. 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Repealing Chapter 2.92, Personnel System, and creating 
a new Chapter 2.92, Administrative Hearing Procedure, of Title 2, Administration and Personnel, 
of the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming.  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, 
seconded by Mr . Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body  
present.   
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Granting a non -exclusive franchise to Visionary 
Communications, Inc., within the rights -of-way of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming .  Stacy 
McDonald, Visionary Broadband, expressed appreciation and explained the business in the 
community and state.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Dr. Aldrich.  
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.  
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Unified Development Code (UDC) to 
align the UDC fee schedule with the fee adoption practices of the City .  Dr. Rinne moved to 
approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members 
of the governing body present. 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land 
located north of Pershing Boulevard, west of Christensen Road .  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on 
second reading, seconded by Mr.  Roybal.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body present. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from County A-1 Agricultural and Rural Residential 
to MR Medium -Density Residential for land located north of Pershing Boulevard, west of 
Christensen Road.  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr.  Segrave.  
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.   
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land 
located east of and including South Greeley Highway (US 85), north of Chalk Bluff Road .  Dr. 
Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Upon inquiry, Tom Cobb, 
City Engineer, advised he has been in contact with the state regarding the proposal to annex South 
Greeley Highway and anticipates receiving a response this week.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – 
all members of the governing body present.   
   
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from County A -2 Agricultural to AG Agricultural, 
LI Light Industrial, and HI Heavy Industrial for land located east of South Greeley Highway (US 
85), north of Chalk Bluff Road.  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. 
Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land 
located southwest of the intersection of Braehill Road, Parkhill Road, and Panorama Drive .  Dr. 
Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr . Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body present. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from County AR Agricultural Residential to MR 
Medium-Density Residential for land located southwest of the intersection of Braehill Road, 
Parkhill Road, and Panorama Drive.  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by 
Mr. Roybal.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.   
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Approving and establishing revised water and sewer 
rates, tap a nd system development fees, administrative fees, service charges and penalties, and 
septic and commercial waste dump rates, as recommended by the Board of Public Utilities .  Mr. 
Roybal moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr . White.  Comments were made 
acknowledging that fee increases aren’t generally favored and that BOPU did an excellent job of 
looking at surrounding communities’ fee structures as references for the fee adjustments.  Motion 
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Appropriating moneys for the City of Cheyenne, 
Wyoming for various purposes in conducting the municipal government of said City and fixing 
the amount of general and special taxes as part of the revenue re quired to meet the said 
appropriation, all for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2021 and ending June 30, 2022.  Mr. White 
moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Mr. White moved to amend by 
substitute dated May 20, 2021 including the following amendments: increasing the City Attorney 
Division by $123,200.00 and decreasing Miscellaneous Division by the same amount; increasing 
the Clean and Safe Division by $73,000.00 and decreasing the Miscellaneous Division by the same 
amount and increasing the Compliance Division by $18,278.00 and increase revenue from reserves 
in the same amount, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Dr. Rinne moved to divide the question to discuss 
and vote on the amendments separately, seconded by Mr. Johnson.  Motion carried.   Voting “yes” 
– all members of the governing body present with the exception of  Mr. Roybal and Mr. White 
voting “no”.  Item #1-motion to approve increasing the City Attorney Division by $123,200.00 
and decreasing Miscellaneous Division by the same amount carried.  Voting “yes” – all members 
of the governing body present.  Item #2-increasing the Clean and Safe Division by $73,000.00 and 
decreasing the Miscellaneous Division by the same and amount .  Discussion included:  Use of 
one-time funds for on-going expenses such as permanent full -time employees, options for other 
funding sources that may be available for Depot Plaza repairs and maintenance, and efforts to fund 
positions from the general fund rather than one-time funding.  Upon inquiry, Robin Lockman, City 
Treasurer, advised depending on sales tax collections, it could be possible to use some 
   
discretionary funds to aid in moving employees under the general fund.  Comments were made 
regarding sales tax funding for the Botanic Gardens operations and maintenance which is currently 
be utilized for a few employees’ salaries and concerns relating to depleting that funding.  Support 
was voiced for moving full -time staff under the general fund instead of temporary tax funding.  
Upon inquiry, Mayor Collins clarified the proposed funding could be allocated to other areas of 
the budget if the motion fails.  Additional discussion includ ed the importance of repairing and 
maintaining the Depot Plaza for tourism and image, noting improvements will help generate sales 
tax and other revenue.  Comments were made on the value of operations and maintenance funding, 
functions of the Clean & Safe Division, and lack of available funding to move Botanic Gardens 
staff under the general fund.   Upon inquiry, Mayor Collins advised a vote in favor of the motion 
before the governing body would move the funding into the Clean & Safe Division.  Ms. Lockman, 
upon inquiry, reported the funding in question would only take care of the salary for one position, 
noting there is still significant amount of benefits to be covered.  Jason Sanchez , Community 
Recreation & Events Deputy Director, explained a recent site visit was done at the Depot Plaza 
and several areas for repair and maintenance were identified and that funds from this amendment 
would be used for that purpose.  Mr. Sanchez  reviewed Depot Plaza areas that need maintained 
and noted the goal is to restore  the plaza.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body present with Mr. Cook, Mr. Johnson, Dr. Rinne and Mr. White voting “no”.  Item 
3-increasing the Compliance Division by $18,278.00 and increase revenue from reserves in the 
same amount. Comments were made regarding a recent Ward I Town Hall public meeting which 
highlighted nuisance issues.  Supportive comments were voiced noting the importance of assisting 
in the efforts.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.   Main 
motion as amended by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of t he governing body  
present.  The following is a summary of the proposed budget , including the aforementioned 
amendments: General Fund, $53,795,619; Weed and Pest, $ 573,274; Youth Alternatives Grants, 
$882,886; Recreation Programs, $1 ,477,947; Community Development Block Grant, $ 617,074; 
Law Enforcement Grants, $ 252,616; Transportation Planning, $ 866,101; Transit, $2,603,121; 
Juvenile Justice, $ 67,640; Special Friends, $ 84,664; Development Impact Fees, $ 212,800; One 
Percent Sales Tax 2019 -22, $11,087,381; Speci fic Purpose Option Tax,  $601,905; Youth 
Activities/Ropes, $18,221; Golf Facilities, $276,590; Fleet Maintenance, $4,460,139; Solid Waste 
Management, $19,301,898; Civic Center, $ 2,057,777; Ice & Events Center, $828,665; Perpetual 
Care, $ 3,000; Total City, $ 100,069,318; Water Enterprise, $ 23,619,580; Sewer Enterprise, 
$14,123,800; Total Appropriation, $137,812,698. 
 
 ORDINANCE –1st READING – Creating a new Chapter 2.80, Urban Renewal Authority, 
of Title 2, Administration and Personnel, of the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming – referred 
to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Segrave) 
 
 ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending the Unified Development Code (UDC) to 
create the Urban Use Overlay District – referred to Public Se rvices Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. 
Rinne) 
 
 
 
   
 ORDINANCE –1st READING – Creating Section 13.04.141, Fee Assessment on Gross 
Revenues, of Chapter 13.04, Board of Public Utilities, of Title 13, Public Utilities Generally, of 
the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyo ming – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. 
Segrave) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Rescinding Resolution No. 6023 which establishes that all revenue from 
City Contract No. 5902 be split evenly between the City of Cheyenne Solid Waste Enterprise Fund, 
the Board of Public Utilities, and the newly established Belvoir Ranch Recreation Special Revenue 
Fund.  Cari Cuffney spoke in favor of the anticipated substitute to be introduced and noted the 
contract provides ongoing maintenance funds for the Belvoir Ranch masterplan development.  Mr. 
Roybal moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. White.  Mr. Roybal moved to amend by substitute dated 
May 17, 2021, seconded by Dr. Aldrich.  Mr. O’Donnell provided information on the substitute 
stating the original proposed resolution redirected all money to the general fund and the proposed 
substitute amendment directs 2/3 of the funding to the general fund and 1/3 to the Belvoir Ranch 
Recreation Special Revenue fund.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body present with the exception of Mr. Johnson voting “no”.  Main motion as amended 
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of Mr. 
Johnson voting “no”.  (#6146)   
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Downtown Development Authority (DDA) to generate 
revenue for general operating funds .  Amber Ash, Executive Director of DDA, explained that as 
part of the annual strategic planning process  and in effort to become financially stable, it was 
determined the DDA would seek approval of a resolution authorizing approval to generate revenue 
utilizing concepts such as advertising options, apparel sales, sponsorships as well as other revenue 
generating efforts.  She explained the DDA has faced challenges relating to unstable revenues over 
the last few years and they wish to look at different ways for sustainability.  Ms. Ash reported at 
the May 17th Finance Committee meeting, a recommendation to postpone the resolution to the next 
meeting of governing body was made.  In response to that, a substitute was drafted which removes 
flexibility for funding options leaving  specified options.  Wendy Volk  voiced support and 
applauded what the DDA has presented to council.  Mr. Roybal moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. 
White.  Mr. Roybal moved to postpone to June 14, 2021, seconded by Mr. Laybourn.  Dr. Rinne 
advised a substitute amendment was forthcoming and requested the postponement be voted down 
in order to consider the amendment.  Motion to postpone failed.  Voting “no” all members of the 
governing body present with the exception of Mr. Laybourn voting “yes”.   Dr. Aldrich moved to 
amend by substitute dated May 24, 2021, seconded by Mr. Roybal .  Mr. O’Donnell provided 
information on the substitute noting it removes the flexibility and only allows for funds to be raised 
for the listed items .  Comments and ad ditional details were provided on the proposed substitute 
amendment.  Concerns were raised relating to allowing full flexibility and the potential appearance 
of competition with merchants located downtown.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body present with the exception of Mayor Collins, Mr. Johnson and Dr. 
Rinne voting “no”.  Additional concerns were raised regarding advertising , amount of available 
DDA reserve funding and turnover rate of executive directors and board members during the past 
6 years which contributes to the success of the DDA.   Main motion as amended carried.  Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body  present with the exception of Mr. Laybourn voting 
“no”.  (#6147) 
   
[CA] RESOLUTION – Approving the budget of the Cheyenne Regional Airport Board for the 
fiscal year beginning July 1, 2021 and ending June 30, 2022 – referred to Finance Committee. 
(Sponsor – Mr. Roybal) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Approving the budget of the Cheyenne Downtown Development 
Authority for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2021 and ending June 30, 2022 – referred to 
Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Roybal) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the City Treasurer to discharge uncollectible debts in the 
amount of $16,953.97 pursuant to Wyo. Stat. §16-4-502 (BOPU uncollectible debts) – referred to 
Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Laybourn) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a final plat for Saddle 
Ridge, 16th Filing, a plat of a portion of  Section 25, Township 14 North, Range 66 West, of the 
6th P.M., Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located north of Pershing Bo ulevard, west of 
Christensen Road) – referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Rinne) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a final plat for Bison 
Business Park, 2nd Filing, a plat of a portion of  Sections 32 and 33, Township 13 North, Range 66 
West, of the 6 th P.M., Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located east of South Greeley 
Highway [US 85], north of Chalk Bluff Road) -- referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor 
– Dr. Rinne) 
 
[CA] Memorandum of Understa nding between the City of Cheyenne and Cheyenne Frontier 
Days, Inc., for the use of city-owned land and buildings for parking, camping, and other activities 
during the 2021 Cheyenne Frontier Days Celebration.   Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.  
(#7343) 
 
[CA] Lease Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the Cheyenne Artist Guild, Inc., for 
the Van Tassell Carriage House located at 1701 Morrie Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming .  Motion 
(per Consent Agenda) carried. (#7344) 
 
[CA] Payment Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Blue Cross Blue Shield to provide 
a rebate payment to the City of Cheyenne in the amount of $275,000.00 for group health insurance 
benefits for City employees.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#7345) 
 
[CA] Agreement betwe en the City of Cheyenne and WJE, LLC, Cheyenne, WY, for 
development fees for Saddle Ridge 16th Filing, final plat – referred to Public Services Committee. 
 
[CA] Renewal of Contract #6836 between the City of Cheyenne and Blue Cross Blue Shield for 
group health insurance benefits for City employees.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried.  
(#6836) 
 
   
[CA] City Contract No. 150, Notice of Renewal of Lease Number 57 -82HW-1-0171 from the 
United States Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service,  to lease the High Plains 
Grasslands Research Station – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Contract modification #1 to Contract #7256 between the City of Cheyenne and Dan Hart 
Patrol Service, LLC, for the Happy Jack Landfill Phase 2, Cells 1, 2 and 3 Excavation Earthworks 
project for additional liner & shipping cost for the leachate trench (Solid Waste Fund) – referred 
to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Contract modification #2 to Contract #7258 between the City of Cheyenne and Northwest 
Linings & Geotextile Pro ducts Inc., for the Happy Jack Landfill Phase 2, Cells 1, 2 and 3 
Excavation Earthworks project for a force majeure cost increase for unprecedented condition in 
the polypropylene and resin market (Solid Waste Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Consideration to purchase between the City of Cheyenne, and Wyoming Machinery 
Company, Cheyenne, Wyoming, to replace the undercarriage, track shoes, and related components 
on a Caterpillar D5K Dozer (City Block #5901) (Fleet Maintenance Fund).  Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $45,398.64). 
 
[CA] Bar and grill liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for HRARG DH 
Cheyenne, WY, LLC, d/b/a Dog Haus, 3838 Atkin St., Cheyenne Wyoming.  Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried. 
 
[CA] Restaurant liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Tres Amigos 
Incorporated d/b/a Tres Amigos Family Mexican Restaurant, 2414 W. Lincolnway, Cheyenne, 
Wyoming.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 Appointment of John B. Kopper as Chief of the Cheyenne Fire and Rescue Department.   
Mr. Roybal moved to approve, seconded by Dr. Aldrich.  Supportive comments were voiced 
relating to the appointment of Mr. Kopper as Fire Chief by members of the governing body.  
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of 
Mayor Collins who did not vote (mayoral appointment).  Following announcement of the vote, the 
oath of office was administered to Chief John B. Kopper by City Clerk Kris Jones. 
 
 Reappointment of Mary Guthrie and Matthew Pope to the Board of Public Utilities Board 
of Directors.  Mr. White moved to approve, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” 
– all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Collins who did not vote 
(mayoral appointments).   
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
 No comments were made on the Revenue Report as presented. 
 
 
   
 Announcement was made of Public Hearing to be held June 14, 2021 at 6:00 p.m. in City 
Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via electronic conference 
meeting, to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute 
§15-1-402 e xist for land located northeast of the intersection of Dell Range Boulevard and 
Whitney Road. 
 
 Announcement was made that a Calcutta, benefitting the Black Dog Animal Rescue, will 
be held Friday, June 4, 2021 beginning at 6:00 p.m. at Alf’s Pub and Bar, 1 622 E. 19 th Street, 
Cheyenne, Wyoming (35% of proceeds go to the Black Dog Animal Rescue). 
 
 Mayor Collins noted an additional Public Hearing announcement and requested the City 
Clerk read it into the record: 
 
 Announcement of Public Hearing to be held Jun e 14, 2021 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council 
Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via electronic conference meeting, for 
proposed budgets for the City of Cheyenne and Board of Public Utilities for Fiscal Year 2022. 
 
 Under other business: 
 
  Upon inquiry, Mayor Collins advised redefining the boundaries for voting districts and 
city council wards is considered following data collection of the census.  Mayor Collins reported 
this is considered when there have been sufficient growth changes warranting a change to balance 
the council wards.   
 
 Dr. Aldrich commented on the recent Ward I public forum that was held at David Romero 
Park and the lighting of the airport fountain. 
 
 Mr. Johnson provided information on an upcoming community cleanup to be held on June 
6, 2021 at the Ames Underpass beginning at 10 a.m. 
  
  There bein g no fur ther business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 8:04 p.m.  
 
        Submitted by, 
       
 
        Kristina F. Jones, City Clerk 
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  June 2, 2021

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
June 14, 2021 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Bryan Cook, Ken Esquibel (via 
Zoom), Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne, Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave  and Jeff 
White.  Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
 Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be  no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda ).  Mr. Roybal moved to approve, seconded by Mr. White.  
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing.   
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on May 24, 2021 .  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for proposed budgets for the City of Cheyenne and 
Board of Public Utilities for Fiscal Year 2022.  There being no comments or input and purpose of 
the hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the hearing.   
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation 
conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15 -1-402 exist fo r land located northeast of the 
intersection of Dell Range Boulevard and Whitney Road.   Seth Lloyd, Planning & Development 
Department, provided a staff report and advised the area sought to be annexed contains 18 acres 
of land to be known as Meadowlark  Estates for mixed use development of commercial and 
residential dwellings.  Mr. Lloyd provided details relating to compliance of annexation criteria.  
There being no further comments or input and purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor 
Collins closed the hearing. 
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Amending Section 5.12.030, Licenses and Permits -
Types, of Chapter 5.12, Alcoholic Liquor and Malt Beverages, of Title 5, Business Licenses and 
Regulations, of the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming.  Mr. Roybal move d to approve on 
third and final reading, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of 
the governing body. (#4365) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending various sections of Chapter 5.12, Alcoholic 
Liquor and Malt Beverages, of Title 5, Business Licenses and Regulations, of the Code of the City 
of Cheyenne, Wyoming  (delivery).  Mr. Roybal moved to approve on third and final reading, 
   
seconded by Mr. Segrave .  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governi ng body 
with the exception of Dr. Rinne voting “no”.  (#4366) 
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Amending various sections of Chapter 5.12, Alcoholic

(#4367)    
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Repealing Chapter 2.52, Personnel Commission, and

Chapter 2.92, members of the CPEA support the proposed substitutes.  Dr. Rinne moved to

members of the governing body.  Main motion as amended carried.  Voting “yes” – all members

 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Repealing Chapter 2.92, Personnel System, and creating

of the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming.   Dr Rinne moved to approve on third and final 
reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  D r. Rinne moved to amend by substitute dated June 2, 2021, 
seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  
Main motion as amended carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the

 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Granting a non -exclusive franchise to Visionary 
Communications, Inc., within the rights-of-way of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming.    Mr. Roybal 
moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Dr. Aldrich .  Motion carried.  Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body. (#4370) 
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Amending the Unified Development Code (UDC) to 
align the UDC fee schedule with the fee adoption practices of the City.  Dr. Rinne moved to

members of the governing body. (#4371) 
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land 
located north of Pershing Boulevard, west of Christensen Road.  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on 
third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Cook.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of 
the governing body. (#4372) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from County A-1 Agricultural and Rural Residential 
to MR Medium -Density Residential for land located north of Pershing Boulevard, west of 
   
Christensen Road.  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Cook.  
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#4373)   
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land 
located east of and including South Greeley Highway (US 85), north of Chalk Bluff Road.    Betsey 
Hale, Cheyenne Leads, expressed support  and appreciation to city staff for their efforts on the

MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2021-06-28 | CLIP_ID: 805 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 805

   
RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
June 28, 2021 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, C OUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Bryan Cook , Ken Esquibel, 
Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne, Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave  and Jeff White.  
Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
 Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motio n.  There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda ).  Mr. Roybal moved to approve, seconded by Mr. White.  
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.   
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on June 14, 2021.  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 ORDINANCE –EMERGENCY READING – Amending Section 10.80, Bicycles, of Title 
10, Vehicles and Traffic, of the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming (Sponsor – Mr. Segrave). 
Mayor Collins advised that the City Attorney reported a large vendor of electronic scooters (e-
scooters) has plans to locate here beginning in July and has requested emergency approval of 3 
ordinances in order to provide for appropriate licensing and enforcement regulations prior to their 
arrival.  Michael O’Donnell, City Attorney, explained there are 3 proposed ordinances related to 
e-scooter and e-bicycle legislation.  He noted there are currently e-scooters operating in the city 
and it is anticipated there will be more companies coming to Cheyenne.  Mr. O’Donnell advised 
the ordinances focus on public safety particularly  noting the upcoming Cheyenne Frontier Days 
(CFD) event.  Upon request, Mr. O’Donnell reported on this agenda item and the 2 affiliated 
ordinances and advised this ordinance amends City Code Section 10.80 and i s a modification of 
the existing bicycle ordinance and includes definitions for e -scooters and related devices.  He 
advised Chapter 10.82 creates a regulatory structure for the devices that are for hire only, noting it 
specifically excludes the DDA Re-Ride Program.  He further reported it sets up the structure for a 
business license and fees, a series of requirements for how the business shall be run, insurance and 
indemnification requirements, suspension and revocation provisions that are established within the 
City Code administrative hearing process and public education required.  He noted e nforcement 
occurs through the Police Department, City Clerk, Compliance Division and occasionally through 
the Planning & Development Department.  It was further advised there are anticipated amendments 
to Chapter 10.82.  Mr. O’Donnell provided highlights of the proposed Indemnification Agreement 
which was reviewed by Bird Rides, Inc., a large operator planning to operate in Cheyenne, noting 
there are significant insurance and indemnification requirements.   Mr. O’Donnell explained 
amendments to Chapter 5.04 include adding the license in the business license section of the City 
   
Code.  Mayor Collins provided information relating to approval on Emergency Reading and 
explained a motion to suspend the rules is required, noting a three-quarters affirmative vote (8 out 
of 10 members of the Governing Body) is required to proceed for  emergency approval.  Mayor 
Collins advised if the motion to suspend the rules fails, the ite m would be referred to the Finance 
Committee for a recommendation.  Mr. White moved to suspend the rules and hear this ordinance 
as an emergency ordinance pursuant to Wyoming State Statute 15 -1-115(c), seconded by Mr.  
Roybal.  During public comment, Jeremiah Mahoney spoke in support of approving regulations 
prior to an influx of scooters being utilized by citizens.  Michael Covato, Bird Rides, Inc., Territory 
Manager, expressed enthusiasm for the opportunity to  locate in Cheye nne.  Upon inquiry, Mr. 
Covato advised the company has been internally assessing operations in Cheyenne over the last 
year and did outreach earlier this year, however formal conversations began several weeks ago.  It 
was noted from members of the Governing  Body that although there is excitement for the 
operation, th e emergency ordinance regulatory process  seems rushed and additional time to 
research and make appropriate decisions  is preferred .  Upon inquiry, Mr. Covato provided 
operations expectations and i nformation relating to CFD events , seasonal operations, and local 
management.  Mr. Covato expressed the desire to p artner with local members of the community 
to hire a local Fleet Manager.  Comments were made related to  time frame for scooters to arrive 
and time necessary to prepare required licensing and insurance provisions.  Upon further inquiry, 
Mr. Covato provided information on the number of e -scooters the company plans to start with  
locally which will be monitored for potential increases.  It was advised that geofencing regulations 
and limitations would be enforced, noting changing the area of the geofence is a simple process.  
Mr. O’Donnell noted the anticipated amendment defines geofencing that allows for flexibility at 
the discretion of the director, noting the director will work with companies to determine what those 
requirements should be.  Hamilton Byrd, local concert promoter, reported he and his partner have 
recently launched Bandwagon e-scooters in the community and they have been working with the 
Downtown Development Authority ( DDA) and the Metropolitan Planning Organization ( MPO) 
for several months.  Mr. Byrd reported the top speed of a scooter is limited to 20 kilometers per 
hour, helmets are suggested  and currently they have 32 e-scooters in operation.  He advised the 
MPO provided them with suggested geofencing requirements and noted the age minimum is 16 
for operation.  He further advised upon inquiry, that he supports regulations and will work with 
the city to become compliant  and confirmed alteration of geofencing is easily obtained.  Jenny 
Clough expressed s afety concerns  for riders and pedestrians  related to street and sidewalk 
conditions.  Ms. Clough voiced s upport of e-scooters but cautioned operations during C FD.   
Motion (to suspend the rules) carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the 
exception of Mr. Johnson voting “no”.  City Clerk Kris Jones read the ordinance entitlement into 
record upon request of Mayor Collins.  Upon inquiry, City Clerk Kris Jones explained that under 
the emergency ordinance procedure, a three-quarters affirmative vote (8 out of 10 members of the 
Governing Body) in order for the ordinance to pass.  Mr. Segrave moved to approve, seconded by 
Mr. White.  It was noted by m embers of the governing body that the issues brought up by Ms. 
Clough demonstrates the need for requirements to be addressed immediately and that other cities 
have had to ban scooters as businesses came in without regulations in place.  Additional comments 
were made in support of efforts by the attorney’s office and support was voiced for the e-scooters 
but concern was expressed related to the  fast paced approval of the ordinances.  Mayor Collins 
noted occasionally the need arises for  approval of emergency procedures.    Upon inquiry, Mr. 
O’Donnell reported an ordinance exists that addresses skateboards in the Central Business District 
   
(CBD).  It was noted that in the future e lectric unicycle s will be considered for inclusion of 
regulations set forth within the affiliated ordinances.  Mayor Collins and Mr. O’Donnell confirmed 
that these vehicles would be allowed to operate on the greenway as  they are categorized by state 
statute as non-motorized due to engine size. Mot ion carried.  Voti ng “yes” – all members of the 
governing body with the exception of Mr. Johnson voting “no”.  (#4378)  
 
 ORDINANCE –EMERGENCY R EADING – Creating a new Chapter 10.82, Motor -
Assisted Scooters, Electric Bicycles, and Bicycles Equipped with GPS, of Title 10, Vehicles and 
Traffic, of the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming (Sponsor – Mr. Segrave).  Mr.  White 
moved to suspend the rules and he ar this ordinance as an emergency ordinance pursuant to 
Wyoming State Statute 15-1-115(c), seconded by Mr.  Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – 
all members of the governing body  with the exception of Mr. Johnson voting “no”.  Mr. Roybal 
moved to appro ve, seconded by Mr.  Segrave.  Mr. O’Donnell read into record the following 
proposed amendments:  Section 10.82.020-Definitions and Exclusions-addition of “Geofencing” 
means the use of a virtual perimeter in which the use of a dockless vehicle is either res tricted or 
the speed of the dockless vehicle is reduced when in use; 10.82.050-Dockless Vehicle Operations-
F-Notices of violations or broken or inoperable dockless vehicles: 1.  License holders shall have 
two hours after receiving notice of a violation , and 10.85.050(I):  License holders shall adhere to 
geofencing requirements, as determined and at the discretion of the director.  Mr. Segrave moved 
to amend by referenced language changes provided by Mr. O’Donnell, seconded by Dr. Aldrich.  
Upon inquiry, Mr. O’Donnell provided enforcement processes and confirmed the city would work 
within the spirit of the law for enforcement efforts.  M otion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” - all 
members of the governing body.  Dr. Rinne moved to postpone to July 12, 2021, seconded by Mr. 
Cook.  Support and  opposition was expressed for t he proposed postponement.  Jillian Harris, 
Transportation Planner for MPO, provided details on the history of efforts to implement legislation 
for regulations which began in February 2021.  Ms. Harris advised that introduction of e-scooters 
was inevitable and that the MPO has taken necessary steps to work with city staff and e-scooter 
operators to  protect the citizens.  Ms. Harris  explained the MPO had been working with the 
Bandwagon providers and Bird Rides, Inc. contacted the MPO in March and presented a 
memorandum of understanding ( MOU) which was catalyst to move th e legislation as quickly as 
possible in the best interest of the community from a public safety standpoint.  Michael Covato, 
Bird Rides, Inc., advised there are planning logistics that can’t be done until an ordinance outlining 
regulations is in effect, voicing opposition to  the postponement.  Kris Jones, City Clerk, upon 
inquiry, advised staff has been working on ordinance details including the business license 
component, noting final document details will require additional adjustments pushing 
implementation further out if postponed.  Mr. O’Donnell shared that coordination with insurance 
companies requires time to assure all requirements are in place, noting that a delay would most 
likely result in missing the timeline of being ready prior to CFD.  Mr. Johnson noted for the record 
he opposes rushed approval which denies the public opportunity to participate.  Mr. O’Donnell 
reported future ordinance amendments can take place after approval through the regular council 
approval process, noting the importance of having regulations in place prior to implementation of 
e-scooters in the community.  Motion to postpone failed.  Voting “yes” - Mr. Cook, Mr. Johnson 
and Dr. Rinne.  Voting “no”  - Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. 
Roybal, Mr. Segrave and Mr. White.  M r. O’Donnell reported that the Indemnification and 
Insurance provisions will be finalized by staff, can be adjusted when necessary, and are not a part 
   
of the ordinance but are referenced in the ordinance.  Dr. Rinne moved to amend by capping the 
number of e -scooters to a total of 80, seconded by seconded by Mr. Cook .  It was noted that 
Bandwagon already has 32 e-scooters active and that limiting the amount could raise legal concern 
with regard to restraint of trade.  Comments were made in support and  in opposition of the 
proposed amendment, and support was voiced for a free market approach.  Mr. O’Donnell voiced 
concern with a first come first serve environment  limiting those who can apply for a license to 
operate.  Tom Mason , MPO D irector, advised that w ithout rules and regulations in place , the 
program should be restricted to a pilot program  and that he anticipates use of e -scooters as mode 
of transportation, noting 80 scooters isn’t sufficient for that purpose.  Additional comments were 
made in support of letting the mar ketplace and company expertise determine the number  of e-
scooters the community needs.  Boyd Wiggam voiced opposition to capping the e-scooter amount 
and cautioned against restraint of trade noting he believes a cap would be detrimental in allowing 
this as a transportation type in the community .  He further voiced  support of e-scooters in the 
community.  Additional detailed comments were made in support and  in opposition of capping 
fleet numbers, free trade/market concept, restraint of trade, public safety concerns and uncharted 
territory relating to e -scooters.   Motion to amend failed.  Voting “no” – all members of the 
governing body with the exception of Mr. Johnson and Dr. Rinne voting “yes”.   Main motion as 
amended carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body  with the exception of Mr. 
Johnson voting “no”.  (#4379)

7, 2021 Noon.

hard work and efforts relating to the June 26th Superday activities and noted the excellent condition

appreciation for his drive and work ethic noting he was raising awareness and funds for his church. 
  
  There bein g no fur ther business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 8:10 p.m.  
        Submitted by, 
       
 
        Kristina F. Jones, City Clerk
