MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2023-05-22 | CLIP_ID: 908 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 908

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
May 22, 2023  
  
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins , COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich  (via Zoom) , Ken Esquibel, 
Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne, Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave  and Jeff White.  
Absent: Bryan Cook.  Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Esquibel.  
Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. 
 
Expression of Appreciation of the 2022- 2023 Mayor’s Youth Council and State of the 
Youth Address was made. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on May 8 , 202 3.  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Ordinance appropriating moneys for the City of 
Cheyenne, Wyoming for the various purposes in conducting the municipal government of said 
City and fixing the amount of general and special taxes as part of the revenue required to meet the 
said appropriation, all for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2023 and ending June 30, 2024.  
Reporting for Committee of the Whole, Mr. Johnson moved to approve on second reading, 
seconded by Mr. Segrave. Mr. Johnson moved to amend to decrease the Capital Improvement 
Expenses line item in the Mayor’s Department General Fund expenditure by $105,000.00 and 
increase the Capital Improvement Expenses line item in the Miscellaneous Department’s General 
Fund expenditure budget by the same amount  and to increase the Special Distribution from the 
State line item in the Intergovernmental General Fund revenue category by $23,000.00 and t he 
Capital Improvement Expenses line item in the Miscellaneous Department’s General Fund 
expenditure budget by the same amount, seconded by Mr . Roybal .  Motion to amend carried.  
V oting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. Mr. Johnson moved t o amend to 
increase the Special Distribution from the State line item in the Intergovernmental General Fund 
revenue category by $50,000.00 and increase the Nuisance Abatement line item in the Compliance 
Department’s General Fund expenditure budget in the s ame amount, seconded by Dr. Rinne. 
Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.  Mr. Johnson 
moved to amend to increase the Special Distribution from the State line item in the 
Intergovernmental General Fund revenue c ategory by $127,280.00 and increase Parks Projects 
line item in the Miscellaneous Department’s General Fund expenditure budget in the same amount, 
seconded by Mr . Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body 
present.  Mr. Johnson moved to amend to decrease the Miscellaneous Department “Transfer to 
Reserves” line item by $60,000.00 and increase the City Council Department as follows:  
$20,000.00 in the Ward 1 Contingency line item, $20,000.00 in the Ward 2 Contingency line item, 
and $20,000.00 in the Ward 3 Contingency line item , seconded by Mr . Laybourn. Mr. Johnson 
moved to amend the amendment to increase the “Transfer to Reserves” line item by $124,445.00 
for a total of $184,445.00 and increase the City Council Department as f ollows: $41,485.00 in 
Ward 1 Contingency line item, $41,485.00 in the Ward 2 Contingency line item, and $41,485.00 
in the Ward 3 Contingency line item for a total in each Ward Contingency Fund of $61,485.00, 
seconded by Mr. Laybourn. Motion to amend the amendment failed due to a tie vote.  V oting “yes” 
– Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. White.  V oting “no” – Mr. Johnson, Dr. Rinne, 
Mr. Roybal and Mr. Segrave.  Motion to amend carried.  V oting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body present with the exception of Dr. Aldrich who voted “no”. Main motion as 
amended (amended four times) carried.  V oting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. 
The following is a summary of the proposed budget including aforementioned ame ndments: 
General Fund , $66,215,278; Weed and Pest, $ 710,000; Youth Alternatives Grants, $930,480; 
Recreation Programs, $2,099,698, Surface Water Management, $6,028,882; Community 
Development Block Grant, $548,667; Law Enforcement Grants, $211,976; Miscellaneous Federal 
Grants, $929,612; Transportation Planning, $1,078,409; Transit, $3,560,683; Juvenile Justice, 
$170,745; Special Friends, $ 58,325; Development Impact Fees, $ 1,028,200; One Percent Sales 
Tax 2019-22, $13,089,895; Specific Purpose Option Tax, $574,456; Youth Activities, $ 19,207; 
Golf Facilities, $ 374,300; Fleet Maintenance, $ 6,389,579; Solid Waste Management, 
$19,985,856; Civic Center, $ 2,613,314; Ice & Events Center, $ 1,057,783; Perpetual Care , 
$27,000; Total City, $ 127,502,066; Water Enterprise, $ 28,772,400; Sewer Enterprise, 
$15,372,000; Total Appropriation, $171,846,746. 
      
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Ordinance approving and establishing revised water and 
sewer rates, tap and system development fees, administrative fees, service charges and penalties, 
and septic and commercial waste dump rates, as recommended by the Board of Public Utilities .  
Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. White moved to approve on second reading, seconded by 
Mr. Esquibel .  Moti on carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.   
Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Mr. Esquibel.  
              
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Ordinance amending the Official Zoning Map of the City 
of Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from MR Medium -Density Residential to MUB 
Mixed-Use Business Emphasis for land located at Lot 29, Block 1, Eastridge. Reporting for Public 
Services Committee, Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr.  Segrave.  
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. Public comment was 
made by: Shane Hansen, Steil  Surveying Services. Comments were made by the following 
members of the governing body: Dr. Rinne and Mr. Segrave.  
 
 
 
              
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Major Street Plan Official Map 2017, by 
updating the entire Major Street Plan Official Map with newly platted and built roads and with the 
most recent Master Transportation Plan (Connect 2045) and other recently adopted Master 
Transportation Amendments.  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr . 
Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. 
 
ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending Section 5.12.030, Licenses and Permits -
Types, of Chapter 5.12, Alcoholic Liquor and Malt Beverages, of Title 5, Business Licenses and 
Regulations, of the  Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming – referred to Finance 
Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. White) 
              
ORDINANCE –1st READING – Creating Chapter 2.96, Ethical Obligations of Public

Services Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Aldrich)     
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Stadium 
View Addition, 4th Filing, a replat of Lots 8 and 9, Block 4, Stadium View Addition, 3 rd Filing, 
City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located northeast of the intersection of Bevans 
Street and Grove Drive). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6325)       
      
[CA] RESOLUTION – Approving the budget of the Cheyenne Regional Airport Board for the 
Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2023 and ending June 30, 2024.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#6326) 
  
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the City of Cheyenne to join with other political 
subdivisions of the State of Wyoming as a participant in the Wyoming Cooperative Liquid Assets 
Securities System (Wyoming CLASS) to pool funds for investment.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#6327) 
  
[CA] RESOLUTION – Supporting the Cheyenne Regional Airport Board in the application for 
and acceptance of federal assistance from the Federal Aviation Administration under the 
Bipartisan Infrastructure Law to assist in constructing a passenger boarding bridge connected to 
the passenger terminal.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6328) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Approving the budget of the Cheyenne Downtown Development 
Authority for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2023 and ending June 30, 2024 – referred to 
Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. White)                
  
[CA] RESOLUTION – Approving water services, by outside us er agreement, for properties to 
be known as Ironhorse 3rd Filing, Laramie County, Wyoming generally located southeast of West 
Riding Club Road and Hynds Boulevard – referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. 
Cook)                  
  
 RESOLUTION – Approving sanitary sewer service, by outside user agreement, for Myers, 
Austin et al, for the property at 3730 Rawlins Street, Laramie County, Wyoming (located 
northwest of the intersection of Rawlins Street and McCann Avenue) – referred to Public Services 
Committee (Sponsor – Mr. Cook). Mayor Collins recessed the meeting at 6:46 p.m. in order to 
hold a Special Meeting of the Public Services Committee to consider the resolution.  Mayor Collins 
reconvened the City Council meeting at 6:54 p.m.  Dr. Rinne moved to adopt, seconded by Mr.  
Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. (#6329) 
 
 Pipeline Easement Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Samson Exploration, 
LLC for installation and maintenance of pipelines on City owned property (Revenue to the City) 
(Postponed from May 8, 2023) . Mr. White moved to approve, seconded by Mr . Esquibel.  Mr. 
White moved to postpone to June 12, 2023, seconded by Mr. Esquibel.  Motion to postpone carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. 
 
[CA] Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Cheyenne, Cheyenne Regional 
Medical Center, and American Medical Response to establish the terms and conditions under 
which the parties  will manage mutual care as it relates to community paramedicine and non -
emergency transport.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#7764) 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Terracon Consultants, 
Inc. for Landfill Leachate System Design, Modification and Maintenance Contract (Solid Waste 
Fund) -- referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7531 between the City of Cheyenne and Waste 
Management of Colorado, Inc. for the Recycling Services Project to extend the agreement to April 
15, 2024 (Solid Waste Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Renewal of Contract #7535 between the City of Cheyenne and Blue Cross Blue Shield of 
Wyoming for Third Party Administrator Services and Group Health Insurance benefits for City 
employees (Self Insurance Fund) – referred to Finance Committee.       
 
[CA] Renewal of Contract #7536 between the City of Cheyenne and Granular Insurance 
Company for Stop Loss Insurance for City employees (Self Insurance Fund) – referred to Finance

[CA] Consideration of Bid #E-22-23 for furnishing Bituminous Asphalt Hot Mix, Tack Oil, and

Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (accepted bid from JTL 
Group Inc. d/b/a Knife River, Cheyenne, in an amount not to exceed $439,625.00). 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #E-23-23 for furnishing Aggregates on an annual basis for the City

Consent Agenda) carried (accepted bid from JTL Group Inc. d/b/a Knife River, Cheyenne, in an 
amount not to exceed $40,0000.00).  
 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S -20-23 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and

2021 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund) .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carrie d (in an amount

[CA] Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Stryker for a Lifepak 15

Community Emergency Medical Services Grant) .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an

[CA] Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Power Equipment Company

[CA] Consideration of Bid #S-13-23 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Z &

[CA] Consideration of Bid #E-19-23 for one (1) palletized paint striper unit for the City of

Reappointment of John Edwards to the Board of Public Utilities.  Mr . Segrave moved to

June 12, 2023  
  
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Bryan Cook, Richard Johnson, 
Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne, Tom Segrave and Jeff White. Absent: Ken Esquibel and Scott 
Roybal. Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was recited.

be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda . Mr. Johnson declared a conflict of interest and vacated 
council chambers.  Mr. Segrave moved to approve , seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.

[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on May 22, 2023.  Motion (per

White. There being no further comments or input, and purpose of the hearing having been met, 
Mayor Collins closed the public hearing and referred the application to Finance Committee.

conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15- 1-402 exist for about 2.06 acres of land located 
northwest of the intersection of Thomas Road and Ridge Road, Laramie County, Wyoming.  There 
being no comments or input, and purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed 
the public hearing.

4512 Rawlins Street, Laramie County, Wyoming (located south of Rawlins Street east of 
Cleveland Ave.).  There being no comments or input, and purpose of the hearing having been met,

of the hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing.        
 
ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Ordinance appropriating moneys for the City of

said appr opriation, all for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2023 and ending June 30, 2024.  
Reporting for Committee of the Whole, Mr. Johnson moved to approve on third and final reading, 
seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Mr. Johnson moved to amend to decrease the Miscellaneous Department 
“Transfer to Reserves” line item by $5,000 and increase the Professional Development line item 
in the City Council Department by the same amount , seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Motion to amend 
carried.  V oting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. Mr. Johnson moved to amend 
to decrease the Miscellaneous Department “Transfer to Reserves” line item by $75,618.00 and 
increase various payroll expenditure line items in the Community Recreation and Events 
Department, Botanic Gardens Division, by the same amount, and to decrease the Specific Purpose 
Option Tax Fund Botanic Gardens Operations and Maintenance account payroll line items by 
$75,618.00 and decrease the Specific Purpose Option Tax revenue by the same amount, seconded 
by Dr. Rinne.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” –  all members of the governing body 
present.  Main motion as amended  carried.  V oting “yes” – all members of the governing body  
present. The following is a summary of the proposed budget including aforementioned

Clerk, City Engineer, Chief of Cheyenne Fire Rescue, City Treasurer and Kipp Sanders, Cheyenne 
Fire Rescue. (Clerk’s Note: executive session convened at 7:16 p.m.)

officially adjourned at 7:44 p.m.

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
June 26, 2023  
  
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich (via Zoom), Bryan Cook, Ken 
Esquibel, Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne, Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff 
White. Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
  
 Mayor Collins congratulated Dr. Rinne for being presented the Person of the Year award 
by the Greater Cheyenne Chamber of Commerce. 
 
Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda . Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support 
received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Segrave, items #22, 29(c), 30(a) and 31(d) were removed from 
the Consent Agenda.  Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Mr. 
Segrave and Mr. White, items #29(h) & 29(i) were removed from the Consent Agenda.  Upon 
request by Mr. Segrave, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Cook, item #29(j) 
was removed from the Consent agenda. Mr.  Laybourn moved to approve  remaining items , 
seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.

Consent Agenda) carried.

for Animal Shelter Services (General Fund) .  Mr. White moved to approve in an amount not t o

Firefighters Grant).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (accepted bid from Professional Sales

2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund, 2012 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund, Civic Center Fund,

Mr. White moved to accept the bid in an amount not to exceed $1,532,862.00, seconded by Mr. 
Segrave. Motion carried with all members of the governing body voting “yes” with the exception

body: Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Segrave. (#7785)

Airport Board d/b/a Cloud Nine Restaurant & Bar, 300 East 8 th Ave., Cheyenne, WY. Mr. White 
advised there was no recommendation from Finance Committee.  Mr. White moved to approve, 
seconded by Mr. Roybal.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with 
the exception of Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. White voting “no” .  Public comment was 
made by: Mike Moser, Executive Director of the Wyoming State Liquor Association.  Comments 
were made by the following members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. 
Esquibel, Mr. Johnson, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Roybal and Mr. Segrave.  
 
[CA] Request to amend a previously approved outdoor seating area for consumption relating to  
the City of Cheyenne Bar & Grill Liquor License held by Paris West  Restaurant and Bar, located 
at 1719 Central Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
Reappointments of Merle Smith and Richard Vallee to the Public Transit Advisory Board; 
Stefanie Reese and Danica Mrozinsky to the Cheyenne Downtown Development Authority; 
Kenneth Dugas to the Urban Renewal Authority; JJ Chen to the Cheyenne -Laramie County 
Economic Development Joint Powers Board; Kathy Emmons, Jeffrey Merton O’Holleran a nd 
Carla Thurin to the Laramie County Community Juvenile Services Joint Powers Board; and 
Mackenzie Howard to the Community Action of Laramie County Board of Directors.  Mayor 
Collins noted Stefanie Reese’s appointment is not due for reappointment and removed her from 
the reappointments.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Collins who did 
not vote (mayoral appointments). 
 
Appointments of Timothy Johnson and Joel Hickerson to the Laramie County Community 
Juvenile Services Joint Powers Board; Michael Rucker to the Public Transit Advisory Board; and 
Janelle Rose, Judy Moss, and Landyn Medina to the Cheyenne Downtown Development Authority 
Board.  Mr. Laybourn moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” 
– all members of the governing body with the exception Mr. Johnson voting “ no” and Mayor 
Collins who did not vote (mayoral appointments). 
 
There were no comments made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
There were no comments made on the Revenue Report as presented. 
 
Announcement was made that a calcutta benefitting Cheyenne area charities will be held 
on Saturday, July 29, 2023 at 5:30 p.m. in the Cowboy Bistro, located beside the Rodeo Committee 
Cabin at Frontier Park, Cheyenne, Wyoming, in conjunction with the 2023 Cheyenne Frontier 
Days Rodeo (10% of proceeds go to bona fide charities).    
 
Announcement was made that due to the Independence Day holiday on Tuesday, J uly 4, 
2023, regularly scheduled City Council Committee meetings will instead be held as follows: 
Finance Committee will meet at 10:00 a.m. Wednesday, July 5, 2023 and Public Services 
Committee will meet at Noon on Wednesday, July 5, 2023.  Both meetings w ill be held at 2101 
O’Neil Avenue, Room 104 and via electronic conference meeting. 
 
The following members of the governing body made comments under other business: Mr. 
Johnson and Mr. White. 
 
 There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 9:02 p.m. 
 
        
        Submitted by, 
 
              
        Kristina F. Jones, 
        City Clerk 
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  July 5, 2023

MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2023-07-10 | CLIP_ID: 914 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 914

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
July 10, 2023  
  
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich , Bryan Cook, Ken Esquibel, 
Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne, Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave  and Jeff White. 
Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda. Upon request by Mr. Cook, and pursuant to support received 
by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Roybal, items #21 and 22 were removed from the Consent Agenda.  Upon 
request by Mr. Laybourn and pursuant to support received by D r. Aldrich and Mr. Segrave, item 
#26(a) was removed from the Consent Agenda.  Upon request by Dr. Rinne and pursuant to support 
received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Esquibel , item #28(a) was removed from the Consent Agenda.   
Mr. Segrave moved to approve remaining items, seconded by Mr. Roybal.  Motion carried. Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on June  26, 2023.  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
              
ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Creating Chapter 2.96, Ethical Obligati ons of Public 
Officials, Public Members and City Employees, of Title 2, Administration and Personnel, of the 
Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, specifying the ethical duties and obligations 
of Public Officials, Public Members and Employees of the City of Cheyenne  (Postponed from 
June 26, 2023).  Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Cook moved to approve on second 
reading, seconded by M r. Segrave.  Mr. Cook moved to amend section 2.96.050(A)(2) to strike 
the words “Advocate or” and in section 2.96.060 to strike in the 1st sentence “or the removal of a 
public official or public member from his or her office or position”, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  
Motion to amend carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception 
of Mr. Johnson and Mr. Roybal  voting “no”. Mr. Cook moved to strike section 2.96.040(B ), 
seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion to amend carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body with the exception of Mr. Johnson and Mr. Roybal voting “no”.  Mr. Cook, moved to amend 
existing City Code section 2.52.010 to insert “in Chapter 2.96 of city code or” after the phrase 
“Unless otherwise provided”, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion to amend carried. Voting “yes” 
– all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Johnson and Mr. Roybal  voting 
“no”.  Main motion as amended failed due to a tie vote.  Voting “yes” - Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel, 
Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Segrave and Mr. White.  Voting “no” Mayor Collins, Mr. Cook, Mr. Johnson, 
Dr. Rinne and Mr. Roybal. 
ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending Chapter 15.20, National Electrical Code 
Adopted-Appendix K, International Building Code -Administrative Provisions Adopted, of Title 
15, Buildings and Construction, of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, 
updating the Incorporated National Electrical Code Provisions as specifie d.  Mr. Cook moved to 
approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body with the exception of Mr . Johnson voting “no”.  Comment was 
made by the following members of the governing body: Mr. Johnson. (#4509) 
              
ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land 
located northwest of and adjacent to the intersection of Thomas Road and Ridge Road.  Mr. Cook 
moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” 
– all members of the governing body. (#4510) 
  
ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne establishing the zoning classification of MR Medium-Density Residential for land being 
annexed to the City of Cheyenne located northwest of and adjacent to the intersection of Thomas 
Road and Ridge Road.  Mr.  Cook moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. 
Segrave.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#4511) 
 
ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land 
located south of and adjacent to Rawlins Street, east of Cleveland Avenue .  Mr. Cook moved to 
approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body. (#4512)

Cheyenne establishing the zoning classification of MR Medium-Density Residential for land being 
annexed to the City of Cheyenne located south of and adjacent to Rawlins Street, east of Cleveland

carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#4513) 
 
ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne establishing the zoning classification of AG Agricultural for land being annexed to the 
City of Cheyenne located southwest of and adjacent to the intersection of Holland Court and Ridge 
Road.  Mr. Cook moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion 
carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#4514)

Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from LI Light Industrial and MR Medium -Density

to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” –

developments.  Mr. Cook advised there was no recommendation from Public Services Committee.

petitions from 20% to 50%, seconded by Mr. Cook.  Motion to amend failed.  Voting “no” – all 
members of the governing body.  Main m otion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Laybourn voting “no”. Public comments 
were made by: Jason Stephen, Bedrock Development, Dan Dorsch, Director, Habitat for Humanity 
of Laramie County, Rebecca Merchie, Elizabeth Stapel , Peggy Escamilla  and Michael White. 
Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich  and Dr. 
Rinne. (#4517) 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Creating Chapter 8.68, Camping in Public Places, of Title 
8, Health and Safety, of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, Prohibiting the 
Act of Camping on Public Property as Specified.  Mr. Cook moved to approve on second reading, 
seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with 
the exception of Mr. Johnson voting “no”.  Public comments were made by:  Del Scholfield, 
Floyd’s Truck Center, Robert McDaniels,  Trails End Homeowners Association, David Dillon, 
McCandless Truck Center, Billie Hopka, Chris Taveira and Cathy Deister, Trails End. Comments 
were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Johnson, Mr. 
Laybourn, Dr. Rinne and Mr. White. [Clerk’s note: Mr. Esquibel left the meeting after the vote on 
this item at 7:30 p.m.] 
   
ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from HI Heavy Industrial, AG Agricultural and 
County A -2 to LI Light Industrial for land located west of Burlington Trail and south of and 
adjacent to HR Ranch Road – referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Cook)

Riding Club Road and Hynds Boulevard (Postponed from June 26, 2023).  Mr. Cook advised there

– Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Roybal, Mr. Segrave and Mr. White.  Public comment was made

Dr. Rinne and Mr. Segrave.

of Cheyenne, Wyoming, requiring the promulgation of a Conflict of Interest Policy for employees 
of the City of Cheyenne as specified and making a conforming amendment to Section 2.52.010, 
Regulations and Benefits.  Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Cook moved to approve 
on third and final reading, seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members 
of the governing body. (#4521)  
 
 
 
 
 
ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Creating a new Section 15.50.070, Neglected Structure, 
of Chapter 15.50, Historic Design Guideline, of Title 15, Buildings and Construction, of the 
Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming.  Mr. Cook moved to approve on thir d and 
final reading, seconded by Mr. Johnson. Mr. Laybourn moved to postpone to September 11, 2023, 
seconded by Mr. White.  Motion to postpone carried.  Voting “yes” all members of the governing 
body. Public comments were made by: Milward Simpson , Historic Preservation Board , Kathy 
Scigliano and Maeke Ermarth.  Comments were made by the following members of the governing 
body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Roybal. 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Submitting to the qualified property owners of real 
property within the boundaries of the Cheyenne Downtown Development Authority District of 
Cheyenne, Wyoming, excluding real property used exclusively for residential purposes, at a 
Special Election on Wednesday, October 18, 2023, the following question: ‘Shall a Special 
Assessment of twenty (2 0) mills be levied upon the assessed value of real  property within the 
boundaries of the Cheyenne Downtown Development Authority District, excluding real property 
used exclusively for residential purposes, for a period of four (4) years pursuant to the provisions 
of Wyo. Stat. § 15 -9-217(b) for the purposes of (1) Landscaping or maintenance of public areas; 
(2) Planning or management of development or improvement activities; (3) Promotion of public 
events; and (4) Activities in support of business recruitment and development?’.  Mr. White moved 
to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Roybal.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body. Comment was made by the following member of the governing 
body: Mr. Laybourn. 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from Frontier Mall PUD - Planned Unit Development 
(Ordinance No. 3132) to CB - Community Business for land located at Lot 7B, Block 1, Frontier 
Mall).  Mr. Cook moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion carried.  
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Public comment was made by: Shane Hansen, 
agent for the applicant, Steil Surveying Services . Comment was made by the following member 
of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich. 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Pursuant to Section 2.2.2 Planned Development -  
Regulating Plan or Development Master Plan and Section 5.6.2 PUD - Planned Unit Development 
District of the Unified Development Code, amending Ordinance No. 4286 by modifying certain 
standards of the adopted district, Planned Unit Development (PUD), for Sweetgrass (located 
southeast of the inte rsection of College Drive and Avenue C) .  Mr. Cook moved to approve on 
second reading, seconded by Mr. Roybal. Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body. 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Creating Chapter 8.68, Limiting the use of Plastic Single 
Use Carryout Bags, of Title 8, Health and Safety, of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, 
Wyoming, regulating the use of single use plastic bags as specified.  Mr. White advised there was 
no recommendation from Finance Committee.  Mr. White moved to approve on second reading, 
seconded by Mr. Johnson. Mr. Johnson moved to amend by substitute dated August 25, 2023,  
seconded by Dr. Rinne.  Motion to amend by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body. Dr. Rinne moved to amend Section 3 by updating the effective date to July 1, 
2024, seconded by Mr. Johnson.  Motion to amend carried with all members of the governing body 
voting “yes” with the exception of Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Segrave voting “no”.  Dr. 
Rinne moved to amend Section 8.68.030 by deleting “environmental service fee” from the title 
and deleting subsections B-E, seconded by Mr. Johnson.  Motion to amend failed due to a tie vote.  
Voting “yes” – Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Johnson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Roybal and Mr. White.  Voting “no” – 
Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Cook, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Segrave. Main motion as amended 
by substitute, as amended failed. Voting “yes” – Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Johnson, Dr. Rinne and Mr. 
Roybal.  Voting “no” – Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Cook, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Segrave and Mr. White. Public 
comment was made by: Kathy Russell, Jacob Was serberger, Brian Pixley, Richard Lyle, Nancy 
Loomis, Mark Moody, John Young, Gail Young, Marilyn Burton, Dale  Steenburgen, Greater 
Cheyenne Chamber of Commerce, Evan Williams, Cathy Deister, Maeke Ermarth, Doug Powell, 
Kathy Scigliano, Darryl Orr, Adrian Crader, Kathy Selock, Steve Borin, Alan Shobin and Zachary 
Taylor.  Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, 
Mayor Collins, Mr. Cook, Mr. Esquibel, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mr. White.  
 
Following a brief recess, Mayor Collins reconvened the meeting at 7:47 p.m. 
 
ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending Section 5.8.2.h of the Unified Development 
Code (UDC), amending Manufactured Homes on Single Platted Properties or Tracts – referred to 
Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Cook) 
 
ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending Section 15.08.031, Building Permit Fees -
Exceptions for Incentivization Program, of Chapter 15.08, International Building Code Adopted, 
of Title 15, Buildings and Construction, of the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, to create 
incentives for attainable housing and historic preservation – referred to Public Services Committee. 
(Sponsors – Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Johnson and Mr. White)   
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Re-appropriating the Fiscal Year 2023 Budget of the City of Cheyenne 
according to the provisions of W.S. §§ 16- 4-112 & 16- 4-113.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#6346) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Expressing the support of the Governing Body for the establishment of 
an Urban Renewal Authority Fiduciary Fund.  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6347) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the acceptance of a Federal Emergency Management 
Agency FY 2022 Assistance of Firefighters Grant in the amount of $387,043.63 and authorizing 
the contribution of $38,704.37 from the Fifth and Sixth Penny funds in support of this program, 
for the purpose of purchasing breathable air fill stations (FEMA AFG Grant) – referred to Finance 
Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. White)

4200 Converse Avenue from perpetual public outdoor recreation use and committing to purchase 
and encumber one additional replacement property to be deed restricted for perpetual public 
outdoor recreation use pursuant to the requirements set forth in the Land and Water Conservation 
Fund Act – referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Laybourn)   
  
[CA] RESOLUTION – Approving the West Downtown Urban Renewal Plan and West 
Downtown Urban Renewal Project pursuant to Wyoming Statute § 15- 9-110 – referred to Public 
Services Committee. (Sponsors – Mr. Johnson and Mr. White)   
  
[CA] RESOLUTION – To accept and approve the federally funded Dry Creek Drainage Master 
Plan Update submitted by GLM Design Group – referred to Public Services Committee.  (Sponsor 
– Mr. Cook)   
 
[CA] Grant Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the Federal Transit Administration to 
fund Transit Operations (FTA Section 5307 Grant).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an 
amount of $2,418,763.00). (#7810) 
  
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Wilson & Company, 
Inc. for consultant services for the Pershing Blvd. and Windmill Rd. Intersection and Signal Design 
Project (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an 
amount not to exceed $180,182.00). (#7811) 
            
 Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Design Workshop, 
Inc. for the City of Cheyenne Parks and Recreation Master Plan P roject (American Rescue Plan 
Federal Recovery Funds).  Mr. White moved to approve in an amount not to exceed $274,845.00, 
seconded by Mr. Roybal.  Mr. White moved to amend by substitute dated August 21, 2023, 
seconded by Mr. Roybal.  Motion to amend by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of 
the governing body.  Main motion as amended by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – all members 
of the governing body. (#7812) 
 
Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Cheyenne Metropolitan 
Planning Organization, and TischlerBise for the Laramie County Roads Impact Fee Study (MPO 
Funds).  Mr. White advised the item was reviewed under other items for the agenda at the August 
21, 2023, Finance Committee meeting, therefore , provisions of Title 2 of City Code have been 
met.  Mr. White moved to approve in an amount not to exceed $97,840.00, seconded by Dr. 
Aldrich.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#7813) 
 
Cooperative Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the Wyoming  Department of 
Transportation for Project ARSCT N561 A02, US 30/Pershing Blvd. to Christensen Road, 
Cheyenne Streets, Laramie County (2023- 2026 Optional 1% Sales Ta x Fund and 2017 Specific 
Purpose Option Tax Fund).   Mr. White advised the item was reviewed under other items for the 
agenda at the August 21, 2023, Finance Committee meeting, therefore, provisions of Title 2 of 
City Code have been met.  Mr. White moved to approve in an amount not to exceed $2,823,800.00, 
seconded by Dr. Aldrich .  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.         
(#7814) 
 
[CA] Real Estate Purchase Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Trace G. Lewark and 
Mary J. Lewark for the purchase of real property located at 700 Gettysburg Drive, City of 
Cheyenne, consisting of approximately 189,921.6 square feet, more or less and associated 
easement documents (2021 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
[CA] Contract between the City of  Cheyenne, Office of Youth Alternatives, and Laramie 
County to provide services for juveniles appearing in the Laramie County  Circuit Court and the 
Municipal Court of the City of Cheyenne for supervised probation, diversion, and the coordination 
of drug and alcohol services (Revenue to the City) – referred to Finance Committee. 
  
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Volunteers of 
American Northern Rockies, Alcohol Receiving Center, to provide alcohol and drug detoxification 
services (General Fund) – referred to Finance Committee.   
 
[CA] Human Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and United Way of Laramie 
County to provide services to various community programs (2023- 2026 Optional 1% Sales Tax 
Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Safe Harbor to 
provide a safe and secure environment to families who have been affected by abuse (General Fund) 
– referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Ayers Associates Inc 
for the West Crow Creek Greenway Plan (MPO Funds) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Memorandum of Understanding betwee n the City of Cheyenne and Wyoming Housing 
Network, Inc. to provide financial assistance relating to the construction of affordable housing for 
the Robin’s Point Apartments Housing Project (Housing Loans Fund) – referred to Finance 
Committee. 
 
[CA] Amendment to Contract No. 7521 between the City of Cheyenne and Laramie County for 
Animal Control Services (Revenue to the City) .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an 
amount of $130,800.00). (#7521) 
 
Re-appointments of Wendy Soto and JC Manalo to the Housing and Community 
Development Advisory Council.  Dr. Aldrich moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Roybal. Motion 
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Collins 
who did not vote (mayoral appointments).   
 
Appointment of Heather Hirsch to the Mayor’s Council for People with Disabilities.  D r. 
Aldrich moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Laybourn. Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Collins who did not vote (mayoral 
appointment).   
 
There were no comments made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
There were no comments made on the Revenue Report as presented. 
 
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held on September 11, 2023 at 6:00 
p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic 
conference meeting, to receive public comments and input relating to the Federally Funded Dry 
Creek Drainage Master Plan Update. 
Announcement was made that due to City offices being closed for the Labor Day holiday 
on Monday, September 4, 2023, regularly scheduled City Council Committee meetings will 
instead be held in the Municipal Building, Room 104, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, 
and via electronic conference meetings as follows:   Finance Committee will meet Tuesday, 
September 5, 2023 at Noon and Public Services Committee will meet Wednesday, September 6, 
2023 at Noon. 
 
The following members of the governing body made comments under other business: Dr. 
Aldrich, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. White. 
 
 There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 7:58 p.m. 
   
        Submitted by, 
 
              
        Kristina F. Jones, 
        City Clerk 
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  September 2, 2023 

---

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
September 11, 2023  
  
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich , Bryan Cook, Ken Esquibel, 
Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne,  Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White .  
Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion.  There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda.  Upon request by Mr. Cook, and pursuant to support received 
by Mr. Esquibel and Mr. White, item #19 was removed from the Consent Agenda.  Upon request 
by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Mr.  White and Mr. Segrave, item #25(f) 
was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Segrave moved to approve remaining items, seconded 
by Mr. Esquibel.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on August 28, 2023.  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
               
Mayor Collins opened a public hearing to receive public comments and input relating to 
the Federally Funded Dry Creek Drainage Master Plan Update.  Public comments were made by: 
Harry LaBonde , Jack Palma, Roberta Coates, Ed Heffern, Jeff Geyer, Laramie County 
Conservation District and Steve Achter.  There being no further comments or input, and purpose 
of the hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing.  
 
ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Creating a new Section 15.50.070, Neglected Structure, 
of Chapter 15.50, Historic Design Guideline, of Title 15, Buildings and Construction, of the 
Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming .  Reporting for Public Services Co mmittee, 
Mr. Cook advised there was no recommendation from the committee.  Mr. Cook moved to approve 
on third and final reading, seconded by Mr . Johnson.  Dr. Rinne moved to amend paragraph B, 
section 12 to read: Review Committee means a group of three individuals that are nominated by 
the CHPB and approved by the City’s Governing Body.  Their purpose will be to investigate 
petitions filed with the Directo r alleging that a violation of this Chapter has occurred and to 
recommend to the CHPB if further action is necessary.  Ideally, the members of the Committee 
would have a background in Engineering, Real Estate, the Law or knowledge of Cheyenne’s 
history, seconded by Mr. Johnson.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body.  Main motion as amended failed due to a tie vote. Voting “yes” – Mr. Esquibel, 
Mr. Johnson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Roybal and Mr. White.  Voting “no” – Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, 
Mr. Cook, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Segrave.  Public comment was made by: Milward Simpson, 
Historic Preservation Board.    Comments were made by the following members of the governing 
body: Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Johnson, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mr. 
White. 
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Submitting to the qualified property owners of real 
property within the boundaries of the Cheyenne Downtown Development Authority District of

Assessment of twenty (20) mills be levied upon the assessed value of real  property within the 
boundaries of the Cheyenne Downtown Development Authority District, excluding real property 
used exclusively for residential purposes, for a period of four (4) years pursuant to the provisions

(2) Planning or management of development or improvement activities; (3) Promotion of public 
events; and (4) Activities in support of business recruitment and development?’ .  Reporting for 
Finance Committee, Mr. White moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Dr. 
Aldrich.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Comment was made 
by the  following member of the governing body: Mr. Laybourn.  During Mr. Laybourn’s 
comments, Mayor Collins noted comments weren’t germaine to the subject and were out of order. 
(#4522) 
 
ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from Frontier Mall PUD - Planned Unit Development 
(Ordinance No. 3132) to CB - Community Business for land located at Lot 7B, Block 1, Frontier 
Mall).  Mr. Cook moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Johnson.  Motion 
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#4523) 
 
ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Pursuant to Section 2.2.2 Planned Development -

District of the Unified Development Code, amending Ordinance No. 4286 by modifying certain 
standards of the adopted district, Planned Unit Development (PUD), for Sweetgrass (located

carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  Main motion as amended by substitute

the following member of the governing body: Mayor Collins. (#4524) 
 
ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending Section 5.8.2.h of the Unified Development

Roybal and Mr. Segrave.  Main motion failed. Voting “yes” – Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel, Mr.

ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending Section 15.08.031, Building Permit Fees -

[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the acceptance of a Federal Emergency Management

[CA] RESOLUTION – Supporting the conversion of a portion of Dutcher Ball Fields located at

and encumber one additional replacement property to be deed restricted for perpetual public 
outdoor recreation use pursuant to the requirements set forth in the Land and Water Conservation

 RESOLUTION – Approving the West Downtown Urban Renewal Plan and West 
Downtown Urban Renewal Project pursuant to Wyoming Statute § 15-9-110.  Mr. Cook moved to 
adopt, seconded by Mr.  Roybal.  Motion carried. Voting “y es” – all members of the governing 
body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Segrave voting “no” .  Comments 
were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Segrave. (#6350) 
  
 RESOLUTION – To accept and approve the federally funded Dry Creek Drainage Master 
Plan Update submitted by GLM Design Group .  M r. Cook moved to adopt, seconded by Mr.  
Segrave.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.   Public comments

[CA] RESOLUTION – Re-appropriating the Fiscal Year 2024 Budget of the City of Cheyenne

(Sponsor – Mr. White)  
 [CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Shining

[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for R and

[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for

Laramie County, Wyoming (located north of Lincolnway and west of Paul Smith Way) – referred

[CA] RESOLUTION – Expressing the support of the Governing Body for the designation of the

trash compactor for the City of Cheyenne Landfill (Solid Waste Fund) . Motion (per Consent

[CA] Consideration of Bid #S -4-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Built

Committee. 
 
[CA] Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Advanced Comfort Solutions 
for the purchase and installation of Fire Station Vehicle Exhaust Systems   (General Fund & 2019-
2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
No comments were made on the Revenue Report as presented. 
 
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held November 13, 2023 at 6:00 p.m. 
in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via  electronic 
conference meeting, for a bar and grill application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Wyoming 
Horse Racing LLC d/b/a Horse Palace, 1802 Dell Range Blvd. Suite 3, Cheyenne, WY.  
 
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held November 13, 2023 at 6:00 p.m. 
in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via electronic 
conference meeting, to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by 
Wyoming Statute §15-1-402 exist for the City-initiated annexation of 51 parcels of land totaling 
100.56 acres comprised of various tracts of land situate in northwest Cheyenne generally located 
north of Dell Range Boulevard and west of Powderhouse Road. 
  
The following members of the governing body made comments  under other business: Dr. 
Aldrich, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Segrave, and Mr. White. 
 
Mr. Esquibel moved to meet in executive session pursuant to Wyoming Statute §16- 4-
405(a)(iii), seconded by Mr. Roybal.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body present.  Mayor Collins announced members would meet in executive session, not open to 
the public and stated there would be no action taken by the governing body as a result of the 
executive session, and that the regular City Council meeting would officially conclude at the close 
of the executive session. The following staff members were in attendance: Stephanie Boster, City 
Attorney, Charles Bloom, Planning & Development Director, Tom Cobb, City Engineer, Eric 
Fountain, Compliance Director, Kristina F. Jones, City Clerk, and John Kopper, Fire Chief.   
 
 There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 7:42 p.m. 
 
        Submitted by, 
 
              
        Kristina F. Jones, 
        City Clerk 
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
Published: November 4, 2023, Wyoming Tribune-Eagle

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
November 13, 2023  
  
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich , Bryan Cook, Ken Esquibel, 
Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne, Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White .

received by Mr. Segrave and Mr. Esquibel, item #16 was removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon

body.

 Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and GSG Architecture, 
Inc for the Municipal Building Spatial Analysis Project (2021 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund). 
Mr. White moved to approve in an amount not to exceed $115,027.00, seconded by Mr. Roybal.

[CA] Purchase and Sale Agreement for property located at 813 West 23 rd Street for the Reed

 Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Dowdle Studios for the

Purpose Option Tax Fund Ballot)

 Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held December 21, 2023 at 6:00 p.m. 
in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via electronic 
conference meeting regarding the required sale of real property and related equipment in Swan 
Ranch Industrial Park to Granite Peak Development Limited Partne rship upon a finding of 
beneficial economic development. 
  
Announcement was made that due to the Christmas holiday schedule, the regularly 
scheduled City Council meeting on Monday, December 25, 2023, will instead be held on 
Thursday, December 21, 2023 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, 
Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting.  
 
Announcement was made that a Calcutta benefitting the Breast Cancer Initiative of 
Wyoming, will be held on January 5 – January 6, 2024 at Peppermill Bar, 1618 Stillwater Avenue, 
Cheyenne, WY. 
 
 
Mr. Segrave noted the motion to adopt the following Ordinance -  Amending Subsections 
6.6.3.b.3, 6.7.5.c, and 6.9.3.e of the Unified Development Code (UDC), changing the building 
façade design requirements for multifamily residential development, failed at the November 27, 
2023 City Council meeting.  Having voted on the prevailing side and pursuant to Chapter 2.04 of 
City Code, Mr. Segrave moved to reconsider the vote taken on the ordinance, seconded by Roybal.  
Motion to reconsider carried.  Voting “yes” - all members of the governing body.  Dr. Rinne moved 
to postpone to December 21, 2023, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion to postpone carried.  Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body.  Comments were made by the following members of 
the governing body: Dr. Rinne and Mr. Segrave. 
 
The following members of the governing body made comments under other business: Dr. 
Aldrich, Mr. Johnson, Mr. Segrave and Mr. White. 
 
Mr. Johnson moved to meet in executive session Pursuant to Wyoming Statute s §§16-4-
405(a)(iii) and 16 -4- 405(a)(vii), seconded by Mr. Esquibel. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body.  Mayor Collins announced members would meet in executive 
session, not open to the public and stated there would be no action taken by the governing body as 
a result of the executive session, and that the regular City Council meeting would officially 
conclude at the close of the executive session. The following staff members were in attendance: 
Stephanie Boster, City Attorney, Robin Lockman, City Treasurer, TJ Barttelbort, Purchasing 
Manager, Tom Cobb, City Engineer, Kylie Soden, Deputy City Clerk and Jason Sanchez, Director 
of Community Recreation and Events.  Also present: Attorney Mark Stewart.   
 
 There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 10:14 p.m. 
 
        Submitted by, 
 
              
        Kylie Soden, 
        Deputy City Clerk, CMC

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
December 21, 2023  
  
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, (via Zoom), Bryan Cook, Ken 
Esquibel, Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne, Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff 
White. Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda. Upon request by Mr. Cook, and pursuant to support received 
by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Johnson, item #20 was removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon request 
by Mr. Johnson, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Cook, item #21 was 
removed from the Consent Agenda.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve remaining items, seconded by 
Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception 
of Mayor Collins who declared a conflict due to a business affiliation with agenda item #18. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on December 11 , 2023.  Motion 
(per Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
Mayor Collins opened a public hearing regarding the required sale of real property and 
related equipment in Swan Ranch Industrial Park to Granite Peak Development Limited 
Partnership upon a finding of beneficial economic development. Public comment was made by Joe 
Stephenson, Granite Peak Development, Limited Partnership. Comment was made by the 
following member of the governing body:  Mayor Collins.  There being no further comments or 
input, and purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the hearing. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending subsection 6.7.5.b of the Unified 
Development Code (UDC), changing building façade design requirements to reduce required 
windows on urban loft multifamily residential and mixed-use residential development. Reporting 
for Public Services Committee, Mr. Cook moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded 
by Mr. Segrave.  Mr. Cook moved to postpone to January 8, 2024, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  
Motion to postpone carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  Comments were 
made by the following members of the governing body: Mayor Collins and Mr. Johnson.   
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending subsection 5.1.5 of the Unified Development 
Code (UDC), removing minimum lot area requirements for detached dwellings, semi -attached 
dwellings, attached dwellings, and multi -dwelling buildings . Mr. Cook advised there was no 
recommendation from Public Services Committee.  Mr. Cook moved to approve on third and final 
reading, seconded Mr. Johnson.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” –  all members of the governing 
body with the exception of Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Segrave voting “no” .  Public comment was 
made by Jason Stephen, Gateway Construc tion, Brenda Birkle, My Front Door, Sam Weinstein, 
Southeast Wyoming B uilders Association and Eric Adams, Gateway Construction.  Comments 
were made by the following members of the governing body:   Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. 
Laybourn, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Segrave. (#4535) 
  
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending subsection 5.1.5 of the Unified Development 
Code (UDC), removing density requirements for multi-dwelling buildings. Mr. Cook advised there 
was no recommendation from Public Services Committee. Mr. Cook moved to approve on third 
and final reading, seconded by Mr. Johnson.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body with the exception of Mr. Cook, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Segrave voting “no”.   
Public comment was made by:  Jason Stephen, Gateway Constru ction, Brenda B irkle, My Front 
Door, Ansley Mouw, Winters Griffith Architects, Sam Weinstein,  Southeast Wyoming Builders 
Association, Wendy Volk, #1 Properties and Eric Adams, Gateway Construction.  Comments were 
made by the following members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Segrave. (#4536) 
  
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending subsection 6.2.4 of the Unified Development 
Code (UDC), amending Table 6- 2, required automobile parking for multi -family development. 
Mr. Cook moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Johnson.  Motion carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Laybourn and Mr. 
Segrave voting “no”.  Public comment was made by:  Jason Stephen, Gateway Construc tion, 
Brenda B irkle, My Front Door , Ansley Mouw, Winters Griffith Architects, Sam Weinstein,  
Southeast Wyoming Builders Association, Wendy Volk, #1 Properties and Eric Adams, Gateway 
Construction.  (#4537) 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending Title 6, Animals, of the Municipal Code of 
the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, regarding the registration, control, impoundment and general 
care of animals and birds within the city.  Mr. Cook moved to approve on second reading, seconded 
by Mr. Roybal.  Mr. Cook moved to postpone to  January 8, 2024, seconded by Mr. Esquibel.  
Motion to postpone carried. Voting “yes”- all members of the governing body.   Comments were 
made by the following members of the governing body:  Mr. Johnson and Mr. Laybourn.     
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending Ordinance No. 4520 Defining the Terms and 
Conditions of Employment for Sworn Officers of the Cheyenne Police Department for Fiscal Year 
2023-2024. Reporting for Finance Committee , Mr. White moved to approve on second reading, 
seconded by Mr. Esquibel.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” - all members of the governing body.   
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, land 
located east of Polk Avenue and north of and adjacent to East Pershing Boulevard. Mr. Cook 
moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” -
all members of the governing body. 
 
 
 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne establishing the zoning classification of AR Agricultural Residential for land annexed 
to the City of Cheyenne located east of Polk Avenue and north of and adjacent to East Pershing 
Boulevard. Mr. Cook moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion 
carried. Voting “yes” - all members of the governing body.   
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from AR Agricultural Residential to LI Light 
Industrial for land located east of Polk Avenue and north of and adjacent to East Pershing 
Boulevard. Mr. Cook moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion 
carried. Voting “yes” - all members of the governing body.   
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending Subsections 6.6.3.b.3, 6.7.5.c, and 6.9.3.e of 
the Unified Development Code (UDC), changing the building façade design requirements for 
multifamily residential development (Reconsidered from December 11, 2023).  Mr. Cook moved 
to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Mr. Cook moved to amend by substitute 
dated December 18, 2023, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion to amend  by substitute  carried.  
Voting “yes” - all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Cook 
and Mr. Roybal voting “no”.  Main motion  as amended by substitute carried. Voting “yes” -  all 
members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich voting “no”. 
         
[CA] RESOLUTION – Re-appropriating the Fiscal Year 2024 Budget of the City of Cheyenne 
according to the provisions of W.S. §§16- 4-112 and 16- 4-113. Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#6376) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Designating local banks as depositories for municipal funds .  Motion 
(per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6377) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Expressing the will of the Governing Body directing the Mayor to hire a 
Special Projects Manager to assist the City of Cheyenne in managing and coordinating 6th Penny 
Tax projects and other city project priorities as directed by the Mayor.  Mr. White moved to adopt, 
seconded by Mr. Johnson.  Mr. White moved to amend by substitute dated December 13, 2023, 
seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion to amend by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” - all members of 
the governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich voting “no”.  Main motion  as amended by 
substitute carried.  Voting “yes” -  all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. 
Rinne voting “no”.  Comments were made by the following members of the Governing Body: Dr. 
Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Johnson, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Roybal, Mr. 
Segrave and Mr. White. (#6378) 
 
 RESOLUTION – In accordance with Section 2D of the second amended and restated 
Project Development and Administration Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, the 
Cheyenne-Laramie County Corporation for Economic Development and Granite Peak 
Development Limited Partnership, and pursuant to W.S. §15-1-112(b), authorizing the sale of the 
rails, ties and related rail equipment in the Swan Ranch Industrial Park to Granite Peak 
Development Limited Partnership upon determining that the sale benefits the economic 
development of the community.  Mr. White moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Roybal.  Motion 
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  Comment was made by the following 
member of the governing body: Mayor Collins.  (#6379) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing submission of the Capital Construction Loan application to 
the State Loan and Investment Board on behalf of the Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne 
for the construction of water, sewer and road infrastructure to support housing for F.E. Warren Air 
Force Base and for economic development. Mr. White moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Johnson.  
Motion carried. Voting “yes” - all members of the governing body.  Public comment was made 
by: Rob Graham, Coldwell Banker, Dale Steenbergen,  President/CEO, Greater Cheyenne 
Chamber of Commerce , Wendy Volk, #1 Properties, Brenda Birkle, My Front Door  and Sam 
Weinstein.  Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, 
Mayor Collins, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Johnson and Mr. Roybal. (#6380) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor to execute a Settlement Agreement with Rodney 
and Joyce Stone and Dean and Jayne Fertig to resolve a lawsuit regarding increased flooding 
following the development of the Thomas Heights Subdivision -- referred to Finance Committee.  
(Sponsor – Mr. White) 
 
[CA] Professional Services Contract between the City of Cheyenne and Lance & Hall, LLP for 
public defense services (General Fund). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#7884) 
 
[CA] Purchase and Sale Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Taurus Holdings, LLC 
for approximately 2.10 acres of vacant land west of Snyder Avenue at 7th Street and more 
particularly described in Exhibit A  (2023-2026 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) .  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $155,000.00). (#7885) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7775 between the City of Cheyenne and Sunrise 
Engineering for additional design services for the 7th Street Drainage and Access Improvements 
Project (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) . Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried ( in an 
amount not to exceed $13,300.00). (#7775) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7561 between the City of Cheyenne and HDR 
Engineering, Inc. for additional engineering services related to the Pedestrian Traffic Safety Study 
and HAWK System Design Project  (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) . Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $10,420.00). (#7561) 
 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7782 between the City of Cheyenne and DHM 
Design Corporation, for utility locating services for the Reed Avenue Rail Corridor Design Project 
(2017 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund) -- referred to Finance Committee.    
 
[CA] Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Meridian Rapid Defense 
Group LLC, for the purchase of an Anti -Vehicle Barrier and Trailer System for the Community 
Recreation and Events Department  (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund, 2021 Specific 
Purpose Option Tax Fund and Wyoming Department of Homeland Security).  Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $100,059.34). 
 
[CA] Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Axon Enterprise, Inc., for 
the purchase of Axon Body 4, Body Worn Video Cameras for the City of Cheyenne Police 
Department (General Fund Reserves and Future Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund Ballot) . 
Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $800,797.50). 
 
[CA] Request to extend the time period in which Wyoming Horse Racing LLC d/b/a Horse 
Palace has to become operational for an additional year for their retail license, located at 5640 
High Plains Road, Cheyenne, Wyoming -- referred to Finance Committee. 
 
Appointment of Anthony Laird and Darrell Hibbens to the Planning Commission; and 
Mark Moody to the Board of Adjustment.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve, seconded by Dr. Aldrich.  
Motion carried. Voting “yes” - all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor 
Collins who did not vote (mayoral appointments). 
 
Reappointments of James W. Hearne to the City/County Joint Powers Board; Darin Westby 
to the Cheyenne Frontier Days Joint Powers Board;  Donald Pierson to the Police Civil Service 
Commission; Mark C. Hardee to the Fire Civil Service Commission ; Joe Patterson and Chandler 
Carroll to the Contractor Licensing Board; David Benner, Amber Conwell and Elizabeth Bales to 
the Cheyenne  Historic Preservation Board ; Kristian Richardson and Jared Dixon to the Mayor’s 
Council for People with Disabilities ; Gabriel Herrera and William Casey to the Building Code 
Board of Appeals; Dustin Brown and Curtis Clabaugh to the Board of Adjustment; Pete Laybourn 
to the Downtown Development Board; and Bryan Thomas to the  Planning Commission. Mayor 
Collins announced Mr. Laybourn requested his name be withdrawn for reappointment to the 
Downtown Development  Board.  Mr. White moved t o approve  the reappointments with the 
exception of Mr. Laybourn’s reappointment, seconded by Mr. Esquibel.  Motion carried. Voting 
“yes” - all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Johnson voting “no” and 
Mayor Collins who did not vote (mayoral appointments). 
 
No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
No comments were made on the Revenue Report as presented. 
 
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing  to be held January 8, 2024 at 6:00 p.m. in 
City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via electronic conference 
meeting to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute 
§ 15- 1-402 exist for about 9.39 acres of land at 5419 Ridge road (located northeast of the 
intersection of Douglas St. and Ridge Rd.) 
 
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing  to be held January 8, 2024 at 6:00 p.m. in 
City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via electronic conference 
meeting to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute 
§ 15- 1-402 exist for about 29.61 acres of land east of Converse Avenue and south of Storey 
Boulevard.    
 
Announcement was made that a Calcutta benefitting the Make-A-Wish, Wyoming, will be 
held February 2 – February 3, 2024 at the Red Lion Hotel and Conference Center, 204 W. Fox 
Farm Road.      
 
Announcement was made that due to the New Years Day holiday on Monday, January 1, 
2024, regularly scheduled City Council Committee meetings will instead be held as follows:  
Finance Committee will meet at Noon on Tuesday, January 2, 2024 and Public Services 
Committee will meet at Noon on Wednesday, January 3, 2024.  Both meetings will be held at 2101 
O’Neil Avenue, Room 104 and via electronic conference meeting.        
 
The following member of the governing body made comment  under other business: Mr. 
Laybourn.   
 
Mr. Johnson moved to meet in executive session Pursuant to Wyoming Statute s §16-4- 
405(a)(vii), seconded by  Mr. Esquibel.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body.  Mayor Collins announced members would meet in executive session, not open 
to the public and stated there would be no action taken by the governing body as a result of the 
executive session, and that the regular City Council meeting would officially conclude at the close 
of the executive session. The following staff members were in attendance:  Stefanie Boster, City 
Attorney; Charles Bloom, Planning & Development Director; Kris Jones, City Clerk; Seth Lloyd, 
Planning & Development; Brenda Moureaux, Deputy City Treasurer  and Jason Sanchez, 
Community Recreation and Events Director.      
 
 There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 8:35 p.m. 
 
        Submitted by, 
 
              
         Kristina F. Jones, 
        City Clerk 
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.

  December 29, 2023

at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Bryan Cook (arriving at 6:01 
p.m.), Ken Esquibel , Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne, Scott Roybal , Tom 
Segrave and Jeff White. Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to 
be routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no 
separate discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support 
by two other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered 
in its normal sequence on the agenda ). Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support  
received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Johnson, item #24 was removed from the Consent Agenda.  Upon 
request by Dr. Aldrich, and pursuant to support received by Mr. Johnson and Mr. Segrave, item 
#29(a) was removed from the Consent Agenda.   Mr. Roybal moved to approve remaining items, 
seconded by Dr. Aldrich.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on December 21, 2023.  Motion 
(per Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 Expression of appreciation was made to Richard Johnson as President of the City Council 
for 2023. 
 
 Election of city council president for 2024. Dr. Rinne moved to nominate and elect Mr. 
Esquibel as city council president, seconded by Dr. Aldrich . Dr. Aldrich moved to cease 
nominations, seconded by Mr. White .  Motion to cease nominations carried.  Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body.  Motion to elect Mr. Esquibel as city council president carried.  
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
 Election of city council vice-president for 2024. Mr. Roybal moved to nominate and elect 
Dr. Rinne as  city council vice -president, seconded by Mr. Cook. Mr. Esquibel moved to cease 
nominations, seconded by Dr. Aldrich.  Motion to cease nominations carried.  Voting “yes” – all

OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE

March 25, 2024  
  
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Bryan Cook, Ken Esquibel, 
Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne, Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White . 
Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be

normal sequence on the agenda). Mr. Segrave moved to approve, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion 
carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.

been met, Mayor Collins closed the hearing and referred the applications to Finance Committee.

southwest of the I-25 and I-80 Interchange adjacent to Roundtop Rd. Mr. Roybal moved to approve

seconded by Mr. Roybal. Motion Approved. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body.  
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented.
