acceptance of cash-in-lieu for public improvements including a turn lane, as required by the UDC 
and Traffic Impact Study for the development. Dr. Aldrich moved to approve in an amount not to 
exceed $70,500.00, seconded by Mr. White. Dr. Aldrich moved to amend by substitute dated May 
6, 2024, seconded by Mr. Roybal.  Motion to amend by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body.  Main motion as amended by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – 
all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Cook voting “no”.  Comments were 
made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Cook and 
Mr. Esquibel. (#7964) 
  
 
 Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Univerus, Inc., for the 
Sanitation Rerouting and Optimization Project (Solid Waste Fund).  Dr. Aldrich moved to approve 
in an amount not to exceed $142,676.00, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – 
all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Laybourn voting “no”.  Comments 
were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Cook, Mr. Johnson, 
Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Roybal and Mr. White. (#7965)  
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Landmark Aquatics, 
for the Johnson Pool Evaluation and Design Project (2021 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund)  – 
referred to Finance Committee.      
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and TPT Trails, LLC for 
the Belvoir Ranch, Phase 2 Design Build Trail Project  (Belvoir Recreation Fund)  – referred to 
Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #2 to Contract #7775 between the City of Cheyenne and Sunrise 
Engineering for additional engineering services for the 7 th Street Drainage and Access 
Improvements Project (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried (in an amount not to exceed $6,500.00). (#7775)    
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7897 between the City of Cheyenne and Richardson 
Construction, Inc. for the Gymnastics Facility Project (2019- 2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund).  
Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $74,292.50). (#7897) 
 
[CA] Renewal of Contract #7535 between the City of Cheyenne and Blue Cross Blue Shield of 
Wyoming for Third Party Administrator Services and Group Health Insurance benefits for City 
employees (Self Insurance Fund) – referred to Finance Committee.       
 
[CA] Renewal of Contract #6837 between the City of Cheyenne and Delta Dental for Group 
Dental Insurance benefits for City employees  (Various City Funds)  – referred to Finance 
Committee.         
 
[CA] Renewal of Contract #7523 between the City of Cheyenne and VSP Vision Insurance 
benefits for City employees (Various City Funds) – referred to Finance Committee.         
 
[CA] Renewal of Contract #7536 between the City of Cheyenne and Granular Insurance 
Company for Stop Loss Insurance for City employees (Self Insurance Fund) – referred to Finance 
Committee.       
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S-12-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and JTL 
Group Inc. d/b/a Knife River, for the 2024 City Overlay #1 Project (2021 Specific Purpose Option 
Tax Fund).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (accepted the bid in an amount not to exceed 
$2,192,669.75). (#7966) 
 
 
                            
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S-13-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Simon 
Contractors, for the 2024 City Overlay #2 Project  (2021 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund.  
Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (accepted the bid in an amount not to exceed $1,518,379.60). 
(#7967) 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S -15-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and 
Asphalt Preservation, LLC, for the 2024 Surface Seal Project #2 (2021 Specific Purpose Option 
Tax Fund).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (accepted the bid in an amount not to exceed 
$2,084,128.00). (#7968) 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S -10-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and 
Reiman Corp for the HAWK Signals Construction Project  (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax 
Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S-20-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Simon 
Contractors for the Public Works Improvements Project (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund, 
Solid Waste Fund, & Fleet Maintenance Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S-21-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Spire 
Building Group for the Municipal Building Restroom Renovations Project (2021 Specific Purpose 
Option Tax Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
                               
 [CA] Consideration of Bid #S -22-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and 
Richardson Construction, Inc. for the Hitching Post Storm Sewer and Paul Smith Way Project  
(2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Request to amend a previously approved outdoor seating area for consumption by adding 
an additional area relating to City of Cheyenne Bar & Grill liquor license held by Paris West 
Restaurant and Bar, located at 1719 Carey Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming  – referred to Finance 
Committee. 
 
 Urban Renewal Authority 2023 Annual Report. Mr. Esquibel moved to acknowledge 
receipt, seconded by Mr. Johnson. Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body.  Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Mr. Johnson. 
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
Announcement was made that due to the Memorial Day holiday on Monday, May 27, 2024, 
the regularly scheduled City Council meeting will instead be held on Tuesday, May 28, 2024.  The 
meeting will be held at 2101 O’Neil Avenue in City Council Chambers and via electronic 
conference meeting at 6:00 p.m.  
 
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held May 28, 2024 at 6:00 p.m. in City 
Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting, 
to hear public comment regarding the City’s intent to apply for a 2024 Wyoming Business Council 
Business Ready Community Grant and Loan Program for a Community Readiness Project for 
essential infrastructure at the Precision Industrial Park. 
Public comment was made by the following under Other Business: Ed Galavotti. 
 
The following members of the governing body made comments under other business:  Dr. 
Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Johnson and Mr. White. 
 
Mr. Esquibel moved to meet in executive session Pursuant to Wyoming Statutes §16- 4- 
405(a)(iii), seconded by Mr. Roybal. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body.  Mayor Collins announced members would meet in executive session, not open to the public 
and stated there would be no action taken by the governing body as a result of the executive 
session, and that the regular City Council meeting would officially conclude at the close of the 
executive session. The following staff members  were in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief 
of Staff;  Stefanie Boster, City Attorney; John Brodie, Deputy City Attorney; Charles Bloom, 
Planning & Development Director; Seth Lloyd, Planning and Development  and Kris Jones, City 
Clerk. [Clerk’s note: Mr. Segrave was absent for Executive Session] 
 
 There being no further business to come before the  governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 8:06 p.m. 
 
 
        Submitted by, 
 
              
         Kristina F. Jones, 
        City Clerk 
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  May 22, 2024

MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2024-05-28 | CLIP_ID: 955 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 955

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
May 28, 2024  
  
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Bryan Cook, Ken Esquibel, 
Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne (arriving at 6:02 p.m.), Scott Roybal, and Jeff 
White. Absent: Tom Segrave.  Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was 
recited. 
 
 Expression of Appreciation of the 2023- 2024 Mayor’s Youth Council and State of the 
Youth Address was made. 
 
Consent Agenda.  (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be 
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate 
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two 
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda).  Mr. Johnson declared a conflict of interest  due to items related 
to his employment.  Upon request by Dr. Aldrich, and pursuant to support received by Mr. Johnson 
and Dr. Rinne, item #33(c) was removed from the Consent Agenda.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve 
remaining items, seconded by Mr. Esquibel.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body present with the exception of Mr. Johnson who did not vote.  
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on May 13, 2024.  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing regarding the City’s intent to apply for a 2024 
Wyoming Business Council Business Ready Community Grant and Loan Program for a 
Community Readiness Project for essential infrastructure at the Precision Industrial Park.   There 
being no comments or input and purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins 
closed the public hearing. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending Sections 1.4.3 Defined Terms and 5.8.8 
Accessory Buildings of the Unified Development Code, clarifying Detached Buildings. Reporting 
for Public Services Committee, Mr. Roybal moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded 
by Mr. White.  Mr. Roybal moved to amend by substitute dated May 21, 2024, seconded by Dr. 
Rinne. Motion to amend by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body 
present with the exception of Dr. Aldrich  voting “no”. Main motion as amended by substitute 
carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present.  Comments were made by the 
following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich and Mayor Collins. (#4567) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending Ordinance No. 4519 amending the Official 
Zoning Map of the City of Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from HI Heavy Industrial, 
AG Agricultural, and County A-2 to LI Light Industrial for land located west of Burlington Trail 
and south of and adjacent to HR Ranch Road.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve on thir d and final 
reading, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body present. (#4568) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending Subsections 6.5.4.b.3 Incentives / Bonus, 
6.5.4.b.4 Creative Sign Program, and 6.5.8.j Billboards of the Unified Development Code, to 
restructure sign incentives and bonuses by modifying allowances for signs near interstate 
highways, al lowances for shared signs, eliminating the Creative Sign Program, and clarifying 
applicability of certain billboard allowances .  Mr. Roybal moved to approve on thir d and final 
reading, seconded by Mr. White.  Mr. Roybal moved to amend by substitute dated May 21, 2024, 
seconded by Mr. Johnson.  Motion to amend by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – all members of 
the governing body present.  Main m otion as amended by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” –  all 
members of the governing body present. (#4569) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending Section 5.1.5 of the Unified Development 
Code to allow for up to three stories for detached dwellings, semi-attached dwellings, and attached 
dwellings.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve on third and final  reading, seconded by Mr. Johnson.  
Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. Public comment was 
made by: Brenda Birkle, Affordable Housing Task Force and Brandon Swain. (#4570)   
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending and updating the Solid Waste Fee Schedule 
in accordance with Section 8.44.010 of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, 
and repealing Ordinance No. 4503. Reporting for  Finance Committee , Dr. Aldrich moved to 
approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr . White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” –  all 
members of the governing body present with the exception of Dr. Aldrich voting “no”. (#4571)  
    
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending Sections 10.82.030 and 10.82.040 of the 
Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, modifying the term of Dockless Vehicle 
licenses, specifying an effective date and making other conforming amendments .  Dr. Aldrich 
moved to approve on thir d and final reading, seconded by Mr . White.  Motion carried.  Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body present.  (#4572) 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Approving and establishing revised water and sewer 
rates, tap and system development fees, administrative fees, service charges and penalties, and 
septic and commercial waste dump rates, as recommended by the Board of Public Utilities .  Dr. 
Aldrich moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr . Roybal.  Motion carried. Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of Dr. Aldrich and Mr. 
White voting “no”.  Public comment was made by: Brenda Birkle, Affordable Housing Task Force.  
Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich.  
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending Chapter 5.78, Towing and Wrecker Recovery 
Operations, of Title 5, Business Licenses and Regulations, of the Municipal Code of the City of 
Cheyenne, Wyoming, modifying provisions governing towing and wrecker recovery operation 
licensure and the Police Department’s towing and wrecker recovery operation rotation list .  Mr. 
Roybal moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body present. Public comment was made by: Dave Rose, 
Big Al’s Towing.  Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. 
Aldrich and Mr. White. 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Appropriating moneys for the City of Cheyenne, 
Wyoming for the various purposes in conducting the municipal government of said City and fixing 
the amount of general and special taxes as part of the revenue required to meet the said 
appropriation, all for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2024 and ending June 30, 2025.  Reporting 
for Committee of the Whole, Mr. Esquibel moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. 
Roybal.  Mr. Esquibel moved to amend by substitute dated May 23, 2024 (by increasing the City 
Council Department’s Ward I Discretionary Account by $11,666.67, the Ward II Discretionary 
Account by $11,666.67 and the Ward III Discretionary Account by $11,666.66 and by decreasing 
the Miscellaneous Department’s Insurance and Bonding line item by $35,000.00) , seconded by 
Mr. Roybal.  Motion to amend carried.  V oting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. 
Dr. Rinne moved to amend by increasing the Mayor’s salary to $125,000.  Motion died due to lack 
of a second.  Main motion as amended carried.  V oting “yes” – all members of the governing body 
present with the exception of Mr. Cook voting “no”. Public comment was made by: Erin LeBlanc, 
Director, Laramie County Senior Services.   Comments were made by the following members of 
the governing body: Dr. Rinne and Mr. Roybal. 
 
 ORDINANCE –1st READING – Defining the Terms and Conditions of employment for 
sworn officers of the Cheyenne Police Department for Fiscal Year 2024- 2025, repealing and 
replacing Ordinance Nos. 4520 and 4539 –  referred to Finance Committee. (SPONSOR – MR. 
WHITE) 
 
 ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending Sections 1.4.3 Defined Terms and 2.2.6 
Temporary Use Approval of the Unified Development Code, adding a minimum of fourteen days 
– referred to Public Services Committee. (SPONSOR – MR. ROYBAL)           
 
 ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending Section 1.4.4.c Service Uses, Table 5- 1 
Zoning District Uses, Section 5.7.4 Child Care Uses, and Table 6 -2 Required Parking of the 
Unified Development Code, changing Child Care Requirements  – referred to Public Services 
Committee. (SPONSOR – MR. ROYBAL) 
 
 ORDINANCE –1st READING – Creating Section 10.24.190, Critical Traffic Control 
Areas; Creation and Administration; Enhanced Penalties, of the Municipal Code of the City of 
Cheyenne, Wyoming, authorizing the designation of Critical Traffic Control Areas and authorizing 
enhanced penalties as specified  – referred to Public Services Committee.  (SPONSORS – DR. 
ALDRICH, MR. COOK, MR. ESQUIBEL, MR. JOHNSON, MR. ROYBAL, MR. SEGRAVE 
AND MR. WHITE)           
 
 RESOLUTION – Adopting the fee schedule setting the approved towing service rates for 
towing charges related to calls for service by the Cheyenne Police Department made pursuant to 
the tow rotation list.  Mr. Roybal moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body present .  Public comment was made by: Dave Rose, 
Big Al’s Towing and Jerry Hargraves, Wrecker’s Towing.  Comments were made by the following 
members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Cook, Mr. Johnson, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Roybal. 
(#6403) 
 RESOLUTION – Expressing the support of the Governing Body for the submission of an 
application by the Cheyenne Transit Program to the Wyoming Department of Transportation for 
grant funding under the Wyoming Rural Public Transit Program .  Dr. Aldrich  moved to adopt, 
seconded by Mr. White.  Dr. Aldrich moved to amend by substitute dated May 20, 2024, seconded 
by Mr. White.  Motion to amend by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body present.  Main motion as amended by substitute carried.  Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body present with exception of Mr. Cook voting “no”. (#6404)  
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Supporting the submission of an application to the Wyoming Business 
Council under the Wyoming Business Ready Community Grant and Loan Program for an 
Enhancement Grant in support of the development of the Precision Industrial Park.  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. (#6405) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for 
Cheyenne Business Parkway, Thirteenth Filing, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming 
(located west of Christensen Road and south of and adjacent to Campstool Road) .  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. (#6406) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for 
Centennial Heritage, 3 rd Filing, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located east of 
Savannah Drive and south and north of Raleigh Drive) .  Mr. Roybal  moved to adopt with staff 
conditions #1 & 2, seconded by Dr. Rinne .  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body present. (#6407) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Approving sanitary sewer service, by Outside User Agreement, for 
Laramie County, for the property known as the Archer Complex (south of the I -80 and Archer 
Parkway Interchange).  Mr. Roybal moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present. Public comment was made by: Molly 
Bennett, Laramie County Public Works and Ben Hornok.  Comments were made by the following 
members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich and Mr. White. (#6408)   
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Approving the budget of the Cheyenne Regional Airport Board for the 
for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2024 and ending June 30, 2025.  Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried. (#6409) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Approving the budget of the Cheyenne Downtown Development 
Authority for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2024 and ending June 30, 2025.  Dr. Aldrich moved 
to adopt, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body present. Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Mayor 
Collins, Mr. Johnson and Mr. Laybourn. (#6410) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the City of Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities to discharge 
uncollectible debts pursuant to Wyoming Statute 16- 4-502 – referred to Finance Committee.  
(SPONSOR – DR. RINNE)  
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Supporting the adoption of a Vision Zero Policy to eliminate fatalities 
and serious injuries that are a result of crashes on city streets within the City of Cheyenne by 2040 
– referred to Public Services Committee.  (SPONSOR – DR. ALDRICH)  
 
 Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Landmark Aquatics, 
for the Johnson Pool Evaluation and Design Project (2021 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund) .  
Dr. Aldrich advised there was no recommendation from Finance Committee.  Dr. Aldrich moved 
to approve in an amount not to exceed $236,957.00.  Motion died due to lack of a second.  
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and TPT Trails, LLC for 
the Belvoir Ranch, Phase 2 Design Build Trail Project  (Belvoir Recreation Fund) .  Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $219,672.93). (#7975) 
 
[CA] Grant Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Transit Division, and the U.S. 
Department of Transportation for a Federal Transit Administration (FTA) Section 5307 Transit 
Capital Grant for the replacement of transit vehicles over the next three-year period (FTA Section 
5307 Grant) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Cheyenne Metropolitan 
Planning Organization (MPO) and Quandel Consultants, Inc., for the Passenger Rail Station Site 
Selection Study (MPO Funds, County Funds and 2021 Specific Purpose Option Tax) – referred to 
Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and The Design Studio, 
Inc. (TDSi), for the Johnson Pool Evaluation and Design Project  (2021 Specific Purpose Option 
Tax Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Just Be You, Inc. d/b/a 
Star Playgrounds, for the Saddle Ridge Playground Design and Installation Project (Development 
Impact Fees) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Purchase and Sale Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Section 20 LLC for land 
located at the northeast corner of Powderhouse Road and East Carlson Street  (Public Safety 
Infrastructure Fees) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and William H. Smith and 
Associates (WHS), for design services for the Cheyenne - Three Alleyway Project (2021 Specific 
Purpose Option Tax) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Cheyenne, Cheyenne Police 
Department, and Laramie County School District No. 1 for the School Resource Officers Program 
– referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Renewal of Contract #7535 between the City of Cheyenne and Blue Cross Blue Shield of 
Wyoming for Third Party Administrator Services and Group Health Insurance benefits for City 
employees (Self Insurance Fund).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#7535)       
 
[CA] Renewal of Contract #6837 between the City of Cheyenne and Delta Dental for Group 
Dental Insurance benefits for City employees (Various City Funds).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#6837) 
 
[CA] Renewal of Contract #7523 between the City of Cheyenne and VSP Vision Insurance 
benefits for City employees (Various City Funds).  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#7523)         
 
[CA] Renewal of Contract #7536 between the City of Cheyenne and Granular Insurance 
Company for Stop Loss Insurance for City employees (Self Insurance Fund).  Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried. (#7536) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7769 between the City of Cheyenne and Terracon 
Consultants, Inc., for landfill leachate system maintenance services to extend the contract for 2 
years (Solid Waste Fund) – referred to Finance Committee.          
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7760 between the City of Cheyenne and Miller & 
Sons Construction Inc. for the 2023 Miscellaneous Concrete Project for additional concrete curb, 
gutter, sidewalk and valley pans  (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund)  – referred to Finance 
Committee.           
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S -10-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and 
Reiman Corp for the HAWK Signals Construction Project (2019- 2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax 
Fund).  Motion (per Consent Agenda)  carried (accepted the bid in an amount not to exceed 
$831,294.75). (#7976) 
 
 Consideration of Bid #S-20-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Simon 
Contractors for the Public Works Improvements Project (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund, 
Solid Waste Fund, & Fleet Maintenance Fund).  Dr. Aldrich moved to accept the bid in an amount 
not to exceed $2,377,017.25, seconded by Mr. Johnson.  Dr. Aldrich moved to amend to include 
funding the amount of $124,140.50 from General Fund Reserves for maintenance repairs to the 
Municipal Building, seconded by Mr.  Roybal.  Motion to amend carried.  Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body present.  Main motion as amended carried.  Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body present with the exception of Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. 
White voting “no”.  Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. 
Rinne and Mr. White. (#7977)  
 
 Consideration of Bid #S-21-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Spire 
Building Group for the Municipal Building Restroom Renovations Project (2021 Specific Purpose 
Option Tax Fund) . Dr. Aldrich moved to approve in an amount not to exceed $625,850.00, 
seconded by Dr. Rinne .  Motion failed.  Voting “yes” – Mr. Esquibel and Mr. Roybal.  Voting 
“no” – Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Cook, Mr. Johnson, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne and Mr. White.  Comments 
were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. 
Esquibel, Mr. Johnson, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Roybal and Mr. White.  
 
 
                               
 [CA] Consideration of Bid #S -22-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and 
Richardson Construction, Inc. for the Hitching Post Storm Sewer and Paul Smith Way Project  
(2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) .  Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount 
not to exceed $1,693,498.45). (#7978) 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #E -17-24 for the Cheyenne Junior League Bleachers Replacement 
(equipment only) Project (General Fund) – referred to Finance Committee.       
                               
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S-14-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and S & 
S Builders, LLC, for the 2024 Dell Range Concrete Repair for Overlay Project  (2023-2026 
Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund and 2021 Specific Purpose Option Tax Fund) – referred to Finance 
Committee. 
            
[CA] Consideration of Bid #S -16-24 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and 
Asphalt Preservation, LLC, for the 2024 Crack Seal #1 Project (2023-2026 Optional 1% Sales Tax 
Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
                               
[CA] Consideration of Bid E-19-24 for one (1) new sliding axle transportation trailer for the City 
of Cheyenne Street & Alley Division  (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund)  – referred to 
Finance Committee.        
                            
[CA] Consideration of Bid #E-20-24 for one (1) new 2024-2025, 19,500 GVWR, cab & chassis 
with 45 foot aerial device body for the City of Cheyenne Traffic Division (2019-2022 Optional 
1% Sales Tax Fund) – referred to Finance Committee.  
                               
[CA] Request to amend a previously approved outdoor seating area for consumption by adding 
an additional area relating to City of Cheyenne Bar & Grill liquor license held by Paris West 
Restaurant and Bar, located at 1719 Carey Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming.  Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried. 
 
[CA] Request to extend the time period in which Cheyenne Regional Airport Board d/b/a Cloud 
Nine Restaurant & Bar has to become operational for an additional year for their retail license, 
located at 300 East 8th Avenue, Cheyenne, Wyoming – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
 Appointment of Elisabeth DeGrenier to the Historic Preservation Board and Christopher 
Mickey to the Cheyenne Housing Authority Board. Dr. Aldrich moved to approve, seconded by 
Mr. Roybal.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present with the 
exception of Mayor Collins who did not vote (Mayoral appointments). 
  
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
 Comment was made by the following member of the governing body related to the 
Revenue Report: Mr. Johnson.  
 
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held June 10, 2024 at 6:00 p.m. in City 
Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting, 
for proposed budgets for the City of Cheyenne and Board of Public Utilities for Fiscal Year 2025.   
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held June 10, 2024 at 6:00 p.m. in City

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
August 12, 2024 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in special session on this date beginning 
at 7:01 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting, for the purpose of 
collective labor bargaining with the Cheyenne Professional Firefighters, International Association 
of Firefighters, Local No. 279.  Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS 
– Dr. Michelle Aldrich,  Ken Esquibel, Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne  (via 
Zoom), Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White.  Absent: Bryan Cook.  Also  present: Kylie 
Soden, Deputy City Clerk, Amber Ash, Chief of Staff, Stefanie Boster, City Attorney, John Brodie, 
Deputy City Attorney, Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief John Kopper, Cheyenne Fire 
Rescue.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
   
Mayor Collins advised the special session was for the purpose of re-negotiating the existing 
contract labor agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the Fire Union. He briefly provided 
details relating to the proposed Ground Rules for the special session and the Ground Rules were 
agreed upon and signed by the City and Union. Vincent McQueeney , spokesperson for the 
Cheyenne Professional Fire fighters, International Association of Fire fighters, Local No. 279, 
expressed appreciation to the City for their continued collaboration in working with the Union to 
address and update the contract. Mayor Collins advised the only sections that would be opened for 
re-negotiation are Section 2 – Definitions, Section 4 – Terms of Agreement, Section 13 – 
Management Rights, Section 15 – Department Staffing, Section 21 – Classification of 
Employment and Basic Wages and Section 27 – Sick Leave.  Mayor Collins provided information 
on the City’s and Union’s requested changes for each section of the contract which include: Section 
2 – Definitions – acceptable fire-training academy, Cadre/Training Instructor, Ladder Company 
and Squad/Support Company; Section 4 – Terms of Agreement – update term date; Section 13 – 
Management Rights – additional management right to address organizational risk; Section 15 – 
Staffing – update department staffing level to 100, increase how many firefighters are assigned to 
each shift to 29, remove Front Range Fire Academy, increase staffing of Suppression, Community 
Risk Reduction and Support and Administration divisions to 98; Section 21 – Classification of 
Employment and Basic Wages – update to reflect current compensation program, table updated to 
reflect Cost -of-Living Adjustment and Section 27 – Sick Leave – update to reflect proper 
conversion requirements outlined in Section 24 for sick leave for daytime personnel.  The City and 
Union announced acceptance of the proposal .  Mayor Collins noted the revised contract would 
come before the governing body at the next City Council meeting.    
 
  There bein g no fur ther business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 7:13 p.m.  
 
 
 
 
   
       Submitted by, 
        
        
        
       Kylie Soden, Deputy City Clerk  
 
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  Wednesday, August 21, 2024

 Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held November 12, 2024 at 6:00 p.m.

meeting, for disposal of real property and land exchange between the City of Cheyenne and Black 
Hills Energy (properties generally located at 108 W. 18th Street and the 1300 block of W. 24th 
Street).           
 
 Public comment was made by the following under Other Business: Brandon Swain. 
 
The following member of the governing body commented under Other Business: Mr. 
Johnson.  
 
 There being no further business to come before the  governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 7:25 p.m. 
 
        Submitted by, 
 
              
        Kylie Soden, 
        Deputy City Clerk

MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2024-11-12 | CLIP_ID: 983 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 983

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
November 12, 2024  
  
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Bryan Cook (arriving at 6:03 
p.m.), Ken Esquibel (via Zoom), Richard Johnson, Pete Laybourn, Dr. Mark Rinne (via Zoom), 
Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White. Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk. The pledge of 
allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be 
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate 
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two 
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda.  Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received 
by Dr. Aldrich  and Mr . Cook, items  #29(e), 29(f) and 29(g)  were removed from the Consent 
Agenda. Mr. Segrave moved to approve remaining items, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on October 28, 2024. Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened  a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation 
conditions required by Wyoming Statute § 15- 1-402 exist for about 640 acres of land situate in 
portions of Sections 4 and 5, T13N, R67W, 6th P.M., Laramie County, Wyoming (also known as 
North Range Business Park; located northwest of the I -80 and Roundtop Road Interchange). 
Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich. There being no 
further comment or input and the purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed 
the public hearing. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened  a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation 
conditions required by Wyoming Statute § 15- 1-402 exist for the City- initiated annexation of 38 
parcels of land totaling 26.67 acres comprised of various tracts of land situate in northeast 
Cheyenne generally located north of Bevans Street, west of College Drive and south of Dell Range 
Boulevard. Comment was made by the following member of the governing body Dr. Aldrich. 
There being no further comment or input and the purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor 
Collins closed the public hearing. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened  a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation 
conditions required by Wyoming Statute § 15- 1-402 exist for the City- initiated annexation of 26 
parcels of land totaling 38.37 acres comprised of various tracts of land situate in northeast 
Cheyenne generally located east of Ridge Road, west of Whitney Road and along Dell Range 
Boulevard. Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, 
Mr. Cook, Mr. Johnson  and Mr. Laybourn. There being no further comment or input and the 
purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for disposal of real property and land exchange 
between the City of Cheyenne and Black Hills Energy (properties generally located at the 800 
block of  W. 18th Street and the 1300 block of W. 24th Street). Comment w as made by the 
following member of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich. There being no further comment or input 
and the purpose of the hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne adding the Urban Use Overlay District to land located north of East 21st Street and east 
of and adjacent to Warren Avenue. Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Roybal advised 
there was no recommendation from the committee. Mr. Roybal moved to approve on third and 
final reading, seconded by Mr. Johnson. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body with the exception of Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Segrave voting “no”. Public comment 
was made by: Elizabeth Valverde-Bartlett.  Comments were made by the following members of 
the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Johnson, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Segrave. (#4591) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Authorizing the Contractor Licensing Board to license 
and otherwise regulate portable fire extinguisher, hose station equipment and hood system cleaning 
and maintenance professionals, making conforming amendments, and repealing obsolete 
provisions of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming. Reporting for Finance 
Committee, Dr. Aldrich moved to approve on third and final  reading, seconded by Mr. White. 
Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Cook 
and Mr. Johnson voting “no”.  Comment was made by the fol lowing member of the governing 
body: Mr. Cook. (#4592) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, tracts of 
land situate in portions of Sections 4 and 5, T13N, R67W, 6th P.M., Laramie County, Wyoming 
(also known as ‘North Range Business Park’, located northwest of the I -80 and Roundtop Road 
interchange) – referred to Public Services Committee.  (Sponsor – Mr. Roybal)

Cheyenne establishing the zoning classification of LI Light Industrial and BP Business Park for 
tracts of land being annexed to the City situate in portions of Sections 4 and 5, T13N, R67W, 6th 
P.M., Laramie County, Wyoming (also known as ‘North Range Business Park’, located northwest 
of the I-80 and Roundtop Road interchange) – referred to Public Services Committee.  (Sponsor – 
Mr. Roybal)

Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from AG Agricultural and HI Heavy Industrial to AG 
Agricultural for land located south of Campstool Rd and north of Interstate 80 – referred to Public 
Services Committee.  (Sponsor – Mr. Roybal)    
 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, various 
tracts of land completely surrounded by current City limits situate in northeast Cheyenne generally 
located north of Bevans Street, west of College Drive and south of Dell Range Boulevard – referred 
to Public Services Committee.  (Sponsor – Mr. Roybal)

Cheyenne establishing the zoning classification of MR - Medium-Density Residential, HR - High 
Density Residential, and CB -  Community Business for land annexed to the City of Cheyenne 
generally located north of Bevans Street, west of College Drive, and south of Dell Range 
Boulevard – referred to Public Services Committee.  (Sponsor – Mr. Roybal) 
  
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, various 
tracts of land completely surrounded by current City limits situate in northeast Cheyenne generally 
located east of Ridge Road, west of Whitney Road and along Dell Range Boulevard – referred to 
Public Services Committee.  (Sponsor – Mr. Roybal)

annexed to the City of Cheyenne generally located east of Ridge Road, west of Whitney Road and 
along Dell Range Boulevard – referred to Public Services Committee.  (Sponsor – Mr. Roybal) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne changing the zoning classification from P Public and MUR Mixed- Use Residential to 
MUB Mixed-Use Business for land located northeast of the intersection of Morrie Avenue and 
East Lincolnway – referred to Public Services Committee.  (Sponsor – Mr. Roybal) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Amending Section 8.60.080, Non- Compliant Vehicles 
as a Nuisance, of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, declaring oversized 
vehicles as a nuisance, providing for their regulation, clarifying provisions and making conforming 
amendments – referred to Committee of the Whole.  (Sponsors – Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Johnson) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Creating Chapter 13.32, Stormwater Runoff 
Management System, of Title 13, Public Services, of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, 
Wyoming, establishing the Stormwater Runoff Management System, imposing a user fee for 
necessary funding and repealing obsolete provisions  – referred to Committee  of the Whole .  
(Sponsor – Mr. Johnson) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Specifying the monthly Stormwater Runoff 
Management System User Fee in accordance with Section 13.32.050 of the Municipal Code of the 
City of Cheyenne, Wyoming – referred to Committee of the Whole.  (Sponsor – Mr. Johnson) 
 
[CA]  RESOLUTION – Acknowledging receipt of the Rotary Park Master Plan Report . Motion 
(per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6436) 
 
[CA]  RESOLUTION – Expressing the intent of the Governing Body, repealing and replacing 
Resolution No. 6127 governing the creation and administration of the Innovation and Entrepreneur 
Advisory Council. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6437) 
 
  RESOLUTION – Acknowledging receipt of a petition by the City of Cheyenne Planning

Emphasis with frontage on the east side of Warren Avenue between 21st and 22nd Streets, and

Mr. Johnson, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Roybal.  Voting “no” – Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Laybourn, 
Mr. Segrave and Mr. White. Comments were made by the following members of the governing 
body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Johnson, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Segrave. 
 
 RESOLUTION – Directing City staff to research and develop a plan to initiate the process 
to pave the road on Birch Place between Charles Street and Cheyenne Street and install curb, gutter 
and sidewalks . Mr. Roybal advised there was no recommendation from Public Services 
Committee. Mr. Roybal moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Johnson. Motion failed. Voting “no” – 
all members of the governing body. Comments were made by the following members of the 
governing body: Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Johnson. 
 
 RESOLUTION – Directing City staff to research and develop a plan to initiate the process 
to pave the road on Ridge Road between Hillcrest Road and Stevens Drive and install curb, gutter 
and sidewalks . Mr. Roybal advised there was no recommendation from Public Services 
Committee. Mr. Roybal moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Johnson. Motion failed. Voting “no” – 
all members of the governing body. Comments were made by the following members of the 
governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins and Mr. Johnson. 
 
[CA]  RESOLUTION – Authorizing the City Treasurer to discharge uncollectible debts pursuant 
to Wyoming Statute § 16-4-502 – referred to Finance Committee.  (Sponsor – Dr. Aldrich) 
 
[CA]  RESOLUTION – Certifying Planning Commission action amending the Future Land Use

Commercial for property generally located northeast of the intersection of Morrie Avenue and East 
Lincolnway – referred to Public Services Committee.  (Sponsor – Mr. Roybal) 
 
[CA]  RESOLUTION – Directing City staff to evaluate and determine an effective drainage plan 
for the intersection of Bevans Street and Wills Road and the adjacent areas  – referred to Public 
Services Committee.  (Sponsor – Mr. Johnson) 
 
[CA]  RESOLUTION – By the Governing Body designating a Paid On -Street Parking District 
for Downtown Cheyenne in accordance with Section 10.60.015 of the Municipal Code of the City 
of Cheyenne, Wyoming – referred to Finance Committee.  (Sponsor – Mr. Johnson) 
  
 
  Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Metropolitan Planning 
Organization (MPO), and Kimley- Horn and Associates, Inc., for an update of the MPO Long-
Range Metropolitan Transportation Plan (MTP) (MPO Fund). Dr. Aldrich moved to approve in an 
amount not to exceed $199,841.82, seconded by Mr. White . Motion carried . Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Cook voting “no” . Comments were 
made by the following members of the governing body: Mayor Collins and Mr. Johnson. (#8079) 
 
[CA]  Grant of Utility Easement between the City of Cheyenne and the Cheyenne Board of Public 
Utilities on city owned property situated in the S½ of Section 35, Township 14 North, Range 66 
West of the 6th P.M., Laramie County. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#8080) 
 
[CA]  Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Cheyenne and the National Forest 
Foundation to establish roles and responsibilities as a subrecipient of the US Endowment for 
Forestry and Communities Grant . Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to 
exceed $110,000.00). (#8081) 
 
[CA]  Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Cheyenne and the World Resources 
Institute to establish roles and responsibilities as a subrecipient of the US Endowment for Forestry

  Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Safe Harbor to provide a safe and secure

Executive Director , Safe Harbor.   Comments were made by the following members of the 
governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Cook and Mr. Laybourn. (#8083) 
 
  Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and The Cheyenne Housing Authority to provide

exceed $100,000.00, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body.  Public comment  was made by: Erin LeBlanc, Director, Senior Services. 
Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mr. 
Laybourn, Mr. Roybal and Mr. White. (#8084)

executive session. The following staff members were in attendance: Kris Jones, City Clerk; Amber 
Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; Stefanie Boster, City Attorney; Tom Cobb , City Engineer; Craig 
LaVoy, Public Works Deputy Director; Jean Anderson- Shrednik, Greenway and Parks Planner;

body: Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Segrave.

The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting.  Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Bryan Cook, Ken Esquibel , 
Richard Johnson, Dr. Mark Rinne , Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White. Absent: Pete 
Laybourn. Also present: Kris Jones, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited.

routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate

other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Motion 
carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body present with the exception of Mayor 
Collins who declared a conflict due to a business affiliation on agenda item #18.

Consent Agenda) carried.

comment was made by: Jason Stephen, Gateway Construction, Brandon Swain, and Dan Dorsch, 
Executive Director, Habitat for Humanity  of Laramie County.  Comments were made by the

(#4604)

the Governing Body any outstanding debt owed the City by any City Board, Council or 
Commission Member.  Reporting for Finance Committee, Dr. Aldrich moved to approve on third 
and final reading, seconded by Mr. Johnson.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the

the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, expanding the general prohibition on

amendments and repealing obsolete provisions.  Mr. Roybal moved to approve on third and final

MEETING: First Regular Meeting | DATE: 2025-01-06 | CLIP_ID: 991 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 991

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
            
January 6, 2025 
 
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne assembled for its First Regular Meeting for 
2025 on this date in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting. Prior to the meeting 
being officially convened The Honorable Justice Kate Fox, Wyoming Supreme Court, 
administered the oath of office to Mayor Patrick Collins and to the following newly elected and 
re-elected members of City Council: Pete Laybourn and Jeff White, Ward I; Dr. Kathy Emmons  
and Tom Segrave, Ward II, and Dr. Michelle Aldrich and Mark Moody, Ward III. Welcoming 
comments were made by Mayor Collins. 
 
 Mayor Collins officially called the First Regular Meeting of the governing body to order 
at 10:48 a.m. Those present were: MAYOR –  Patrick Collins ; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. 
Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark 
Rinne, Scott Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White.  Also present was Kylie  Soden, Deputy City 
Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
 Approval of appointment of City Officials (pursuant to Title 2 of the Code of the City of 
Cheyenne) as follows: Charles W. Bloom  Planning & Development Director, Bradley M. 
Bowen Assistant City Treasurer (Board of Public Utilities), John A. Brodie City Attorney, Thomas 
D. Cobb City Engineer, Mark Francisco Chief of Cheyenne Police Department,  Ronnald J. 
Jeffrey Juvenile Court Judge, John B. Kopper Chief of Cheyenne Fire Rescue Department,  Robin 
L. Lockman City Treasurer, Vicki Nemecek Director of Public Works, Jason M. Sanchez Director 
of Community Recreation & Events, David E. Singleton Senior Municipal Court Judge, Kylie 
Soden City Clerk/Assistant City Treasurer . Mr. Esquibel moved to approve the appointees “en 
masse”, seconded by Mr. White .  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” -  all members of the governing 
body with the exception of Mayor Collins who did not vote (mayoral appointments).  Following 
announcement of the vote, Honorable Justice Kate Fox, Wyoming Supreme Court, administered 
the oath of appointed office to the City Officials. Comments were made by the following members 
of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich. 
 
 Election of City Council President for 2025.  Mayor Collins  stated that, pursuant to City 
Code, the mayor conducts the election for Council President but does not cast a vote.  Mr. Roybal 
moved to nominate and elect Dr. Rinne  as City Council President for 20 25, seconded by Mr. 
Segrave.  Motion carried. Voting “yes” - all members of the governing body with the exception of 
Mayor Collins who did not vote. Comments were made by the following members of the governing 
body: Dr. Aldrich. 
 
 Election of City Council Vice President for 2025.  Dr. Rinne moved to nominate and elect 
Mr. Roybal as City Council Vice President for 20 25, seconded by Mr. Esquibel. Motion carried.  
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Collins  who did 
not vote.  
 
 There being no further business previously noted for the First Regular Meeting and purpose 
of the meeting have been met, the meeting was officially adjourned at 10:55 a.m. 
 
       Submitted by, 
 
 
       Kylie Soden, 
       City Clerk 
 
 This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
   
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  January 11, 2025

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
February 24, 2025 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in special session on this date beginning 
at 7:35 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting, for the purpose of 
collective labor bargaining with the Cheyenne Professional Firefighters, International Association 
of Firefighters, Local No. 279.  Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS 
– Dr. Michelle Aldrich,  Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Scott 
Roybal, Tom Segrave and Jeff White.  Absent: Dr. Mark Rinne.  Also present: Kylie Soden, City 
Clerk, Amber Ash, Chief of Staff, John Brodie, City Attorney, Robin Lockman, City Treasurer  
and Chief John Kopper and Deputy Chief Andrew Dykshorn, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. The pledge 
of allegiance was recited. 
 
Mayor Collins provided opening comments  and noted the importance of the labor 
management discussions that occur leading up to negotiations. He provided meeting room location 
information that would be used for the purpose of caucusing if needed. The proposed Ground Rules 
were agreed upon and signed by the City and Union. [Clerk’s note: City’s Spokespersons we re 
Mayor Patrick Collins, City Attorney John Brodie and City Council Vice President Scott Roybal.  
The Union’s Spokespersons were Neil Durante, Vincent McQueeney and Chris Thoms .]  Mayor 
Collins and Vincent McQueeney, Spokesperson for the Cheyenne Professional Firefighters, 
International Association of Firefighters, Local No. 279, expressed mutual appreciation for their 
continued collaboration in working together on the Collective Labor Agreement. 
   
Mayor Collins and Union Spokesperson McQueeney reviewed the proposed agreement 
which included changes to the following: Section 2 – Definitions; Section 4 – Term of Agreement; 
Section 13 – Management Rights; Section 15 – Department Staffing; Section 21 – Classification 
of Employment and Basic Wages; Section 22 – Overtime;  Section 23 – Working in a Highter Job 
Rank; Section 24 – Conversion of Benefit Hours; Section 25 – Wellness/Fitness Program; Section 
27 – Sick Leave and Section 42 – Longevity Pay. Mayor Collins and Mr. McQueeney announced 
acceptance of the proposed agreement as written.   
 
  There bein g no fur ther business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 8:04 p.m.  
 
       Submitted by, 
        
        
       Kylie Soden, Deputy City Clerk  
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  March 5, 2025

Emmons.

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
June 9, 2025  
  
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: MAYOR 
– Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich (via Zoom), Dr. Kathy Emmons, 
Ken Esquibel (via Zoom) , Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne , Scott Roybal, Tom 
Segrave and Jeff White.  Also present: Kylie Soden , City Clerk.  The pledge of allegiance was 
recited. 
 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be 
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate 
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two 
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda. Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received 
by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody, item #24(a) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Segrave 
moved to approve the remaining items, seconded by Mr. Roybal. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – 
all members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on May 2 7, 2025. Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation 
conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15-1-402 exist for about 199.67 acres of land generally 
located east of South Greeley Highway and north of Chalk Bluff Road. Public comment was made 
by: Mark Christensen, AVI PC , agent for the applicant . Comments were made by the following 
members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Roybal . There being no further comments 
or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public 
hearing. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for proposed budgets for the City of Cheyenne and 
Board of Public Utilities for Fiscal Year 2026. There being no comments or input and the purpose 
of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing. 
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Appropriating moneys for the City of Cheyenne, 
Wyoming, for the various purposes in conducting the municipal government of said City and fixing 
the amount of general and special taxes as part of the revenue required to meet the said 
appropriation, all for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2025, and ending June 30, 2026. Reporting 
for the Committee of the Whole, Dr. Rinne moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded 
by Mr. White . Dr. Rinne moved to amend by substitute dated June 5, 2025, seconded by Mr. 
Roybal. Motion to amend by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
Main motion as amended carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the 
exception of Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Moody voting “no”. Public comment was made 
2 
 
by: Erin LeBlanc and Katie Brady, Laramie County Senior Services. Comments were made by the 
following members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. 
Moody. The following is a summary of the proposed budget, including the aforementioned 
amendments: General Fund, $74,517,876; Weed and Pest, $801,700; Youth Alternatives Grants, 
$919,234; Recreation Programs, $2,656,270, Community Development Block Grant, $660,183; 
Law Enforcement Grants, $267,441; Miscellaneous Federal Grants, $1,125,070; Transportation 
Planning, $1,805,225; Transit, $6,023,629; Juvenile Justice, $280,726; Youth Alternatives 
Mentoring, $73,794; Development Impact Fees, $1,531,100; One Percent Sales Tax, $13,878,876; 
Specific Purpose Option Tax, $595,554; Youth A ctivities, $19,195; Golf Facilities, $570,700; 
Fleet Maintenance, $7,090,211; Solid Waste Management, $21,513,486; Civic Center, 
$2,369,999; Ice & Events Center, $970,215; Surface Water Mitigation, $5,983,757; Perpetual 
Care, $16,400; Self -Insurance $11,203,838; Total City, $154,874,481; Water Enterprise, 
$31,851,815; Sewer Enterprise, $16,920,270; Total Appropriation, $203,646,566. (#4624) 
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Approving and establishing revised water and sewer 
rates, tap and system development fees, administrative fees, service charges and penalties, and 
septic and commercial waste dump rates, as recommended by the Board of Public Utilities . 
Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Laybourn moved to approve  on third and final reading, 
seconded by Mr. Roybal. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with 
the exception of Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody voting “no”. Comments were made by the following 
members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich and Dr. Rinne. (#4625) 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending portions of the Unified Development Code, 
modifying provisions related to Park Impact Fees, including the timing of fee payment and 
permitted uses of such fees, and making conforming amendments thereto. Reporting for Public 
Services Committee, Mr. Segrave moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. White . 
Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending portions of the Unified Development Code 
regarding signage, to increase allowances for window signs and further clarifying prohibited signs. 
Mr. Segrave moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. White . Dr. Rinne moved to 
amend Section 3, Pedestrian Signs, bullet point three to read “Window Signs shall be allowed in 
any window. Window signs sha ll be counted toward the allowed wall sign area. If 100% of the 
window area is to be covered, it must utilize  a material that allows light to penetrate in to the 
building”, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion to amend carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich voting “no”. Main motion as amended carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Comments were made by the following 
members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins and Dr. Rinne.

tracts of land completely surrounded by current city limits situate in northeast Cheyenne generally 
located north of Dell Range Boulevard, east and west of Ridge Road and south of Storey 
Boulevard. Mr. Segrave moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Dr. Emmons. Motion 
carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich and 
Mr. Moody voting “no”. Public comment was made by:  Daniel Singh. Comments were made by 
3 
 
the following members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. 
Esquibel, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Segrave.

 Contract between the City of Cheyenne and the Wyoming Game and Fish Commission by

OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
December 8, 2025  
 
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers  and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: 
MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich (via Zoom), Dr. Kathy 
Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne (via Zoom, joining at 6:02 
p.m.), Tom Segrave (via Zoom), Jeff White and Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City 
Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited.

routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate 
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two 
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda. Upon request by Mr. Moody, and pursuant to support received by 
Mr. Esquibel and Mr. Laybourn, item #22(a) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. White 
moved to approve the remaining items, seconded by Mr. Esquibel. Motion carried. Voting “yes” 
– all members of the governing body.

(per Consent Agenda) carried.

application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Cheyenne GS, LLC d/b/a Hi Market Cheyenne, 
215 E. Lincolnway, Cheyenne, WY (license currently held by Scooters Scoreboard, LLC d/b/a 
Scooters Scoreboard Bar). Public comment was made by: Sukhpreet Bajwa, Hi Market Cheyenne. 
Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Mr. Esquibel, Dr. Rinne 
and Mr. Wolfe. There being no further  comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing

Committee.

west of Parsons Place. Reporting for Public Services Committee, Dr. Emmons moved to approve

the governing body. Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Mr. 
Moody. (#4650)

Cheyenne, establishing the zoning classifications of: MR – Medium-Density Residential; MUB –

generally located south of Laramie Street, east of T-Bird Drive, north of East Lincolnway and US 
30, and west of Parsons Place. Dr. Emmons moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded 
by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#4651)

Moody. (#4652)

carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Comment was made by the following 
member of the governing body: Mr. Moody. (#8296)

Environmental and Demolition Services, for the High Plains Arboretum – Greenhouse and Lath 
House Demolition and Abatement (WY State Parks and Cultural Resources – Arboretum Grant). 
Mr. Laybourn moved to accept the bid in an amount not to exceed $148,175.00, seconded by Mr.

by the following member of the governing body: Mayor Collins. 
 
[CA] Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Motorola Solutions for ten 
(10) Motorola Mobile Radios for the Cheyenne Police Department (2023-2026 Optional 1% Sales 
Tax Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Consideration to Purchase between the City of Cheyenne and Axon Enterprise, Inc. for ten 
(10) In-Car Camera Systems for the Cheyenne Police Department (2023-2026 Optional 1% Sales 
Tax Fund) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing pursuant to Wyoming Statute §16-4-404(b) 
to be held December 10, 2025 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, 
Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting to discuss and gather public input regarding 
proposed 6th Penny projects.  
 
Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held December 22, 2025 at 6:00 p.m.

meeting for amendments to the City’s 2025- 2027 Consolidated Plan and 2025 Program Year 
Annual Action Pla n for the Housing & Community Development Division’s Community 
Development Block Grant Program.  
  
Announcement was made that a Calcutta benefitting Make-A-Wish Wyoming will be held 
January 30 - January 31, 2026 at Red Lion Hotel and Conference Center, 204 W. Fox Farm Rd., 
Cheyenne, WY (10% of proceeds go to the charity). 
 
Public comment was made by the following under Other Business: Jason Sanchez, Director 
of Community Recreation & Events.  
 
The following members of the governing body made comments under Other Business : 
Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel and Mr. White. 
 
Mr. Laybourn moved to meet in Executive Session pursuant to Wyoming Statute §16- 4-
405(a)(vii), seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body. Mayor Collins announced members would meet in executive session, not open to the public 
and stated there would be no action taken by the governing body as a result of the executive 
session, and that the regular City Council meeting would officially conclude at the close of the 
executive session. The following staff members wer e in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief 
of Staff; David Hopkinson, Deputy City Attorney;  Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Kylie 
Soden, City Clerk. 
 
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 7:12 p.m.

December 22, 2025, seconded by Mr. Esquibel. Motion to amend by substitute carried. Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body present. Main motion as amended by substitute carried.

[00:00:09] Good afternoon. Oh, that's loud. I'm sorry. Good afternoon and thank you for joining us today for this important discussion on data center development.
[00:00:16] My name is Tom Crave and I serve as the president of the Cheyenne City Council. Over the past several months, there has been significant interest in data center development within our community.
[00:00:28] The purpose of today's panel is to provide factual information about data center development, its opportunities,
[00:00:34] challenges, infrastructure requirements,
[00:00:37] economic impacts, and potential effects on our community. Our goal is to help
[00:00:42] inform the public conversation by
[00:00:45] bringing together individuals with firsthand knowledge and expertise.

[00:01:06] Collins served three terms on the Cheyenne City Council and was elected as
[00:01:11] council president four times. Collins
[00:01:14] previously served on the boards of the Greater Cheyenne Chamber of Commerce and Prevent Child Abuse Wyoming.
[00:01:20] Our next panelist is Charles Bloom, AICP. He is the director of planning and
[00:01:24] development for the city of Cheyenne, Wyoming, a role he has held since 2018.
[00:01:31] Charles has over two decades of public sector planning experience relating to the development, review, policy development, comprehensive planning, and
[00:01:39] co-development with almost 21 of those years being in southeast Wyoming. He is
[00:01:45] also president of the American Planning Association's Western Central Chapter.

[00:01:56] leads the business attraction expansion
[00:01:59] and community marketing efforts. Betsy
[00:02:02] has more than 20 years of economic development leadership experience and earned her certified economic developer
[00:02:08] designation in 2020.
[00:02:11] Betsy has extensive experience working with largecale industrial and technology
[00:02:16] projects including data center development where she has coordinated the site selection, infrastructure planning, utility partnerships, and the
[00:02:25] management of offsite improvements.

[00:02:36] brings extensive experience in water and
[00:02:39] wastewater system design and operation,
[00:02:43] supported by his degree in civil engineering from the University of Wyoming and 13 years of prior experience
[00:02:49] working as a consultant on water and wastewater.
