MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2026-01-12 | CLIP_ID: 1050 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 1050

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
January 12, 2026 
 
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers  and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: 
MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, 
Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne (via Zoom), Tom Segrave, Jeff White 
and Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be 
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate 
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two 
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda. Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received 
by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody, item #22 (a) was removed from the Consent Agenda. Mr. Esquibel 
moved to approve remaining items, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on December 22, 2025. Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 Election of C ity Council President for 2026. Mayor Collins stated that, pursuant to City 
Code, the mayor conducts the election for Council President but does not cast a vote. Mr. Esquibel 
moved to nominate and elect Mr. Segrave as City Council President, seconded by Mr. White. Dr. 
Aldrich moved to cease nominations, seconded by Mr. W olfe. Motion to cease nominations 
carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Motion  to elect Mr. Segrave as City 
Council President carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception 
of Mayor Collins who did not vote.  
 
Election of City Council Vice-President for 2026 . Mayor Collins stated that, pursuant to 
City Code, the mayor conducts the election for Council Vice- President but does not cast a vote.  
Dr. Emmons moved to nominate and elect Mr. Laybourn as City Council Vice-President, seconded 
by Mr. Moody. Dr. Aldrich moved to cease nominations, seconded by Mr. White. Motion to cease 
nominations carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Motion to elect Mr. 
Laybourn as City Council Vice-President carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body with the exception of Mayor Collins who did not vote. 
 
Mayor Collins opened a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation 
conditions required by Wyoming Statute § 15- 1-402 exist for the City- initiated annexation of 26 
parcels of land totaling roughly 279.98 acres comprised of various tracts of land situate in north 
Cheyenne generally located south of Storey Boulevard, east of Powderhouse Road, north of Dell 
Range Boulevard, and west of Ridge Road. There being no comments or input and the purpose of 
the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing. 
Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for a transfer of ownership of retail liquor license 
application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for Ace’s Range LLC d/b/a Ace’s Range, 1505 
Pioneer Ave., Cheyenne, WY (license currently held by F & G Corporation d/b/a The Green Door). 
Public comment was made by: Ben Trautwein, The Green Door, JB Kunz, Ace’s Range and April 
Brimmer Kunz, Ace’s Range. Comments were made by the following members of the governing 
body: Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel and Mr. Wolfe. There being no further comments or input and the 
purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing and 
referred the application to Finance Committee. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing for a transfer of ownership of retail liquor license 
application filed with the City Clerk’s Office Westby Edge LLC d/b/a Westby Edge Brewing, 714 
W. 20th St., Cheyenne, WY (license currently held by Scooters Scoreboard Inc.). Public comment 
was made by: Teri Cassidy, representative for Scooters Scoreboard Bar and Darin Westby, Westby 
Edge Brewing. Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. 
Aldrich and Mayor Collins . There being no further comments or input and the purpose of the 
public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed the public hearing and referred the 
application to Finance Committee. 
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Defining the terms and conditions of employment for 
sworn officers of the Cheyenne Police Department for January 2026 until the end of the Fiscal 
Year 2026. Reporting for Finance Committee, Mr. Laybourn moved to approve on third and final 
reading, seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body. (#4655) 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Creating Chapter 1.28, Administrative Inspection 
Warrants, establishing authority for their issuance, and amending the Municipal Code of the City 
of Cheyenne, Wyoming, to authorize certain city officials, as specified, to apply for administrative 
inspection warrants. Reporting for Public Services Committee, Mr. Segrave moved to approve on 
second reading, seconded by Dr. Emmons. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Moody and Dr. Rinne voting “no”.  During 
comments made by Mr. Wolfe, Mr. Moody raised a point of order that comments were off subject 
with the agenda topic, with Mayor Collins concurring with the point of order. Public comment was 
made by: Exie Brown, Gary Pugh, Kathy Scigliano, Ka di Bradfield, John Frank, Dee Drierden , 
Patricia McCoy, Steve Olson, Clarence Fisher, Erin Edwards, Steve Melia, Colin Crossman, John 
Thomas, Lee Filer, Alan Sheldon, Jon Puls, Sam McGinnis, Caleb Wilkins, Charles Miller,  
Stephen Jacobsen and Marren Stalp . Comments were made by the following members of the 
governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. 
Moody, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe. 
 
 Following a brief recess, Mayor Collins reconvened the meeting at 8:08 p.m.  
 
 ORDINANCE –1st READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, various 
tracts of land completely surrounded by current City limits situate in eastern Cheyenne, generally 
located south of Storey Boulevard, east of Powderhouse Road, north of Dell Range Boulevard, 
and west of Ridge Road – referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Emmons) 
 
 ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, establishing the zoning classifications of AG – Agricultural, and MR – Medium-
Density Residential, for land annexed to the City of Cheyenne generally located south of Storey 
Boulevard, east of Powderhouse Road, north of Dell Range Boulevard, and west of Ridge Road – 
referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Emmons) 
 
 ORDINANCE –1st READING – Amending 5.7.3 Accessory Dwelling Units of the 
Cheyenne Unified Development Code to remove owner -occupancy and adjust parking 
requirements for Accessory Dwellings, and making conforming amendments to the definitions of 
an Accessory Dwelling and Semi -Attached Dwelling under 1.4.4 Descriptions of Uses of Land 
and Buildings – referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Moody) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Approving a sponsorship by Bison Beverage for Cheyenne Frontier Days 
events occurring July 17 through July 26, 2026, July 23 through August 1, 2027, and July 21  
through July 30, 2028. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6506) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Adopting the amended 2025- 2027 City of Cheyenne Comprehensive 
Consolidated Plan and the amended 2025 Annual Action Plan, as prepared by the Cheyenne 
Housing and Community Development Office, and setting the public comment period and public 
hearings for the plans. Mr. Laybourn moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Moody voting “no”. 
Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Mayor Collins and Mr. 
Moody. (#6507) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Re-appropriating the Fiscal Year 2026 Budget of the City of Cheyenne 
According to the Provisions of W.S. §§ 16- 4-112 & 16-4-113 – referred to Finance Committee. 
(Sponsor – Mr. Esquibel) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION –  Establishing the City of Cheyenne’s prioritized list of projects proposed 
for potential inclusion on the One Percent (1%) Specific Purpose Sales and Use Tax Ballot 
proposition to be submitted to the qualified electors of Laramie County at the Primary Election on 
August 18, 2026 – referred to Committee of the Whole. (Sponsor – Mr. Segrave) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION –  Authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Cheyenne 
Business Parkway, 15 th Filing, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming, located east of 
Echostar Drive and south of and adjacent to Campstool Road – referred to Public Services 
Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Emmons) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Certifying compliance with Wyoming Statute § 15 -1-402 for the City-
initiated annexation of various tracts of land completely surrounded by current City limits situate 
in western and southern Cheyenne generally located east of I -25, south of the intersection of 
Westland Road and Missile Drive, north of West and East Allison Road and east of and adjacent 
to North College Drive – referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Emmons) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the submission of an application by the City of Cheyenne 
for state funding for the Office of State Lands and Investments Unmet Housing Grant  – referred 
to Finance Committee. (Sponsors – Dr. Rinne & Mr. Segrave) 
 
[CA] Preliminary Plat for Dry Creek Vista, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming 
located northeast of the intersection of Frank Court and Rock Springs Street  – referred to Public 
Services Committee. 
 
  Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and RingCentral, LLC for providing cloud based 
enterprise telecom services for all City departments and divisions. Mr. Laybourn moved to approve 
in an amount not to exceed $65,000.00, seconded by Mr. Moody. Mr. Laybourn moved to amend 
the total dollar amount of the contract to $324,750.58 over 36 months, seconded by Mr. Moody. 
Motion to amend carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Main motion as 
amended carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Public comment was made 
by: Charles Miller. Comment w as made by the following member of the governing body: Dr. 
Aldrich. (#8303) 
 
[CA] Human Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and United Way of Laramie 
County to provide funding to community agencies and monitor performance of community 
programs – referred to Finance Committee. (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Cheyenne Metropolitan  
Planning Organization and Stantec Consulting Services Inc. for the East Allison Road Corridor 
Study – referred to Finance Committee. (MPO Funds) 
 
[CA]  Consideration of Bid #S -7-26 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Pole 
Mountain Electric, Inc., for the Cheyenne Dunbar Field Light Installation project  (2021 Specific 
Purpose Option Tax Fund, Development Impact Fees and Rec Mill Grant) . Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $317,000.00). (#8304) 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #E -11-26 for Microsoft Data Center Product Licensing and Virtual 
Infrastructure for the City of Cheyenne Information Technology Division – referred to Finance 
Committee. (General Fund) 
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
 Announcement was made that due to the Martin Luther King Jr. Holiday on Monday, 
January 19, 2026, the regularly scheduled City Council Committee meetings will instead be held 
in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference 
meeting as follows: Public Services Committee will meet Tuesday, January 20, 2026 at Noon and 
Finance Committee will meet Wednesday, January 21, 2026 at Noon. 
 
 Announcement was made of a Special Meeting to be held January 23, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. 
in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference 
meeting to consider the transfer of ownership of retail liquor license application filed with the City 
Clerk’s Office for Westby Edge LLC d/b/a Westby Edge Brewing, 714 W. 20th St., Cheyenne, 
WY (license currently held by Scooters Scoreboard Inc.).  
 Announcement was made that a Committee of the Whole meeting will be held on 
Wednesday, January 14, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, 
Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting. 
 
The following members of the governing body made comments under Other Business: Dr. 
Aldrich and Mr. Moody. 
 
Mr. Segrave moved to meet in Executive Session pursuant to Wyoming Statute §16- 4- 
405(a)(vii), seconded by Mr. Laybourn. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body. Mayor Collins announced members would meet in executive session, not open to 
the public and stated there would be no action taken by the governing body as a result of the 
executive session, and that the regular City Council meeting would officially conclude at the close 
of the executive session. The following staff members were in att endance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s 
Chief of Staff; John Brodie , City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer ; Eric Fountain, 
Director of Compliance; Jason Sanchez, Director of Community Recreation & Events; Charles 
Bloom, Director of Planning and Development, Jean Anderson- Shrednik, Parks and Greenway 
Planner and Kylie Soden, City Clerk. 
 
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 8:52 p.m. 
 
 
        Submitted by, 
 
              
        Kylie Soden, 
        City Clerk 
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  January 21, 2026

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
January 26, 2026 
 
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers  and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: 
MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, 
Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne , Tom Segrave , Jeff White  and 
Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be 
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate 
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two 
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda. Upon request by Dr. Aldrich, and pursuant to support received by 
Mr. Esquibel and Mr. Moody, item #11 was removed from the Consent Agenda. Dr. Aldrich  
moved to approve  remaining items, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on January 12, 2026. Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Creating Chapter 1.28, Administrative Inspection 
Warrants, establishing authority for their issuance, and amending the Municipal Code of the City 
of Cheyenne, Wyoming, to authorize certain city officials, as specified, to apply for administrative 
inspection warrants. Reporting for Public Services Committee, Dr. Rinne  moved to approve on 
third and final  reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave . Dr. Rinne moved to postpone to February 9, 
2026, seconded by Mr. White . Motion to postpone carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body. Public comment was made by: Gary Pugh, Ann Lucas, Kathy Scigliano, Patricia 
McCoy, Peter Seekell, Abe Mendez,  Lee Filer, Colin Crossman, Tamara Trujillo, Jacob 
Wasserberger, Charles Miller, Stephen Jacobsen and Phillip Bowling. Comments were made by 
the following members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. 
Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Wolfe.  
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, various 
tracts of land completely surrounded by current City limits situate in eastern Cheyenne, generally 
located south of Storey Boulevard, east of Powderhouse Road, north of Dell Range Boulevard, 
and west of Ridge Road. Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave. 
Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Comments were made by the 
following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody. 
 
 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, establishing the zoning classifications of AG – Agricultural, and MR – Medium-
Density Residential, for land annexed to the City of Cheyenne generally located south of Storey 
Boulevard, east of Powderhouse Road, north of Dell Range Boulevard, and west of Ridge Road. 
Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
 ORDINANCE –2nd READING – Amending 5.7.3 Accessory Dwelling Units of the 
Cheyenne Unified Development Code to remove owner -occupancy and adjust parking 
requirements for Accessory Dwellings, and making conforming amendments to the definitions of 
an Accessory Dwelling and Semi -Attached Dwelling under 1.4.4 Descriptions of Uses of Land 
and Buildings. Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Dr. Emmons. Motion 
carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. R inne and 
Mr. Segrave voting “no” . Public comment was made by: Dan Dorsch, Executive Director of 
Habitat for Humanity of Laramie County. Comments were made by the following members of the 
governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody and Dr. Rinne. 
 
 ORDINANCE –1st READING – Creating Chapter 8.72, Private Displays on Public 
Property, to prohibit the unauthorized use of public property for specified private displays  – 
referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsors – Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Re-appropriating the Fiscal Year 2026 Budget of the City of Cheyenne 
According to the Provisions of W.S. §§ 16-4-112 & 16-4-113. Reporting for Finance Committee, 
Mr. Esquibel moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members 
of the governing body. Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Dr. 
Aldrich. (#6508) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Establishing the City of Cheyenne’s prioritized list of projects proposed 
for potential inclusion on the One Percent (1%) Specific Purpose Sales and Use Tax Ballot 
proposition to be submitted to the qualified electors of Laramie County at the Primary Election on 
August 18, 2026. Reporting for Committee of the Whole, Mr. Segrave moved to adopt, seconded 
by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Comments were 
made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Moody, 
Dr. Rinne and Mr. White. (#6509) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to sign a Final Plat for Cheyenne 
Business Parkway, 15 th Filing, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming, located east of 
Echostar Drive and south of and adjacent to Campstool Road. Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#6510) 
 
 RESOLUTION –  Certifying compliance with Wyoming Statute § 15- 1-402 for the City-
initiated annexation of various tracts of land completely surrounded by current City limits situate 
in western and southern Cheyenne generally located east of I -25, south of the intersection of 
Westland Road and Missile Drive, north of West and East Allison Road and east of and adjacent 
to North College Drive . Dr. Rinne advised there was no recommendation from Public Service s 
Committee. Dr. Rinne moved to adopt, seconded by Dr. Emmons. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – 
all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Moody voting “no”. Comments were 
made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Dr. Emmons and Mr. Moody. 
(#6511) 
 
 RESOLUTION –  Authorizing the submission of an application by the City of Cheyenne 
for state funding for the Office of State Lands and Investments Unmet Housing Grant . Mr. 
Esquibel moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. White. Mr. Esquibel moved to amend the total amount 
to $500,000.00, seconded by Mr. White. Motion to amend carried. Voting “yes” – all members of 
the governing body. Main motion as amended carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body. Public comment was made by: Dan Dorsch, Executive Director of Habitat for 
Humanity of Laramie County and Shea Sparks, Vice President of Community Services for Magic 
City. Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor 
Collins, Mr. Moody and Mr. Segrave. (#6512) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing the submission of an application by the City of Cheyenne 
for State funding through the Office of State Lands and Investments for a Rodeo Grounds 
Pedestrian Transportation Infrastructure Grant, and authorizing the execution and submittal of all 
necessary documents in support of the applica tion. Mr. Esquibel advised that the item was 
reviewed under “Other Items for the Agenda” at the January 21, 2026, Finance Committee 
meeting, therefore, provisions of Title 2 of City Code have been met. Mr. Esquibel moved to adopt, 
seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Public 
comment was made by: Tom Hirsig , Chief Executive Officer of Cheyenne Frontier Days . 
Comments were made by the following members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mayor 
Collins, Mr. Moody and Dr. Rinne. (#6513) 
 
 Preliminary Plat for Dry Creek Vista, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming 
located northeast of the intersection of Frank Court and Rock Springs Street. Dr. Rinne moved to 
acknowledge receipt with staff conditions #2 and #3, seconded by Mr. Segrave . Motion carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Comment was made by the following member 
of the governing body: Mr. Moody. 
 
[CA] Human Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and United Way of Laramie 
County to provide funding to community agencies and monitor performance of community 
programs (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an 
amount not to exceed $100,000.00). (#8306) 
 
[CA] Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne, Cheyenne Metropolitan  
Planning Organization and Stantec Consulting Services Inc. for the East Allison Road Corridor 
Study (MPO Funds) . Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed 
$199,514.44). (#8307) 
 
[CA]  Lease Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the Girl Scouts of Montana and 
Wyoming, for 45.93 acres of city- owned real property located near the former Roundtop Water 
Treatment Facility to be used for the purposes of conducting activities consistent with the By-Laws 
and Articles of Incorporation of the Girl Scouts of Montana and Wyoming – referred to Finance 
Committee. (Revenue to the City) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #8111 between the City of Cheyenne, Office of 
Youth Alternatives, and the Laramie County Community Juvenile Services Joint Powers Board 
for a Juvenile Diversion Coordinator to provide diversion related services to increase the potential 
contract dollar amount – referred to Finance Committee. (Revenue to the City) 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #E -11-26 for Microsoft Data Center Product Licensing and Virtual 
Infrastructure for the City of Cheyenne Information Technology Division (General Fund). Motion 
(per Consent Agenda) carried (accepted bid from Hypertec USA Inc. in an amount not to exceed 
$239,577.88). 
 
[CA]  Consideration of Bid #S -8-26 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and  
Fencetrak, Inc. d/b/a Full Tilt Services, for the Dry Creek Restoration Project. Phase 1: 
Meadowland, Holmes, and Henderson Ditches project  – referred to Finance Committee. (2023-
2026 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) 
 
[CA]  Consideration of Bid #S -10-26 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and 
Mechanical Systems, Inc., for the North Cheyenne Community Park Drainage Improvement 
project – referred to Finance Committee. (Development Impact Fees) 
 
[CA]  Consideration of Bid #S-11-26 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Miller 
and Sons Construction, Inc., for the Parsley Boulevard Greenway Connectors project – referred to 
Finance Committee. (2021 Specific Purpose Tax Fund) 
 
[CA]  Application for a transfer of ownership of retail liquor license application filed with the 
City Clerk’s Office for Ace’s Range LLC d/b/a Ace’s Range, 1505 Pioneer Ave., Cheyenne, WY 
(license currently held by F & G Corporation d/b/a The Green Door).  Motion (per Consent 
Agenda) carried. 
 
 Appointment of Mike Beitz to the Laramie County Community Juvenile Services Joint 
Powers Board and Christina Ruffatti to the Mayor’s Council for People with Disabilities. Dr. 
Aldrich moved to approve, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members 
of the governing body present with the exception of Mayor Collins who did not vote (mayoral 
appointments).  
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented. 
 
 No comments were made on the Revenue Report as presented. 
 
 Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held February 9, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in 
City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY and via electronic conference 
meeting, to determine whether compliance of annexation conditions required by Wyoming Statute 
§15-1-402 exist for the City-initiated annexation of 16 parcels of land totaling roughly 49.4 acres 
comprised of various tracts of land situate in western and southern Cheyenne generally located 
east of I -25, south of the intersection of Westlan d Rd. and Missile Dr., north of West and East 
Allison Rd. and east of and adjacent to North College Dr. 
 
 
The following members of the governing body made comments under Other Business: Dr. 
Aldrich and Mr. White. 
 
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 7:47 p.m. 
 
 
        Submitted by, 
 
              
        Kylie Soden, 
        City Clerk 
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  February 4, 2026

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
February 9, 2026 
 
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers  and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: 
MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich (via Zoom), Dr. Kathy 
Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne (via Zoom), Tom Segrave, 
Jeff White and Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance 
was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be 
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate 
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two 
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda). Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received 
by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody, items #21(a) and #21(c) were removed from the Consent Agenda. 
Mr. White moved to approve remaining items, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on January 26, 2026. Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Special Meeting of the Governing Body on January 23, 2026. Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing to determine whether compliance of annexation 
conditions required by Wyoming Statute §15- 1-402 exist for the City- initiated annexation of 16 
parcels of land totaling roughly 49.4 acres comprised of various tracts of land situate in western 
and southern Cheyenne generally located east of I -25, south of the intersection of Westland Rd. 
and Missile Dr., north of West and East Allison Rd. and east of and adjacent to North College Dr. 
Public comment s were made by:  David Kni seley, Tomm ie Kniseley, Chelsea McCort, Sheriff 
Brian Kozak, Tam ara Trujillo, Richard Kniseley, Kathy S cigliano, Patricia McCoy, Donn

Kim Stevens, Tat iana M., Charles Miller and Erin Edwards . Comments were made by the 
following members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. 
Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe . There being no further 
comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed 
the public hearing.  
 
 Following a brief recess, Mayor Collins reconvened the meeting at 8:16 p.m. 
 
 ORDINANCE –3rd READING – Creating Chapter 1.28, Administrative Inspection 
Warrants, establishing authority for their issuance, and amending the Municipal Code of the City 
of Cheyenne, Wyoming, to authorize certain city officials, as specified, to apply for administrative 
inspection warrants. Reporting for Public Services Committee, Dr. Emmons moved to approve on 
third and final  reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Dr. Emmons moved to amend by substitute 
dated February 5 , 2026 , seconded by Mr. Segrave. Dr. Aldrich moved to amend  section 
1.28.020(b)(2) to replace the first “or” with “and” to read “There is probable cause to believe that 
a condition of nonconformity, violation or other circumstance requiring corrective action exists 
with respect to the designated property and  that causes an immediate risk to public health or 
safety”, seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion to amend  failed. Voting “no” – all members of the 
governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody voting “yes”. Dr. Aldrich moved 
to amend section 1.28.020(b)(3)  to remove “determine, discover or ”, seconded by Mr. Moody. 
Motion to amend carried. Voting “yes” Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody, Dr. 
Rinne and Mr. White. Voting “no” - Dr. Emmons, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Segrave and Mr. Wolfe. Mr. 
Moody moved to amend section 1.28.020(b)(1) to add “For the purpose of this ordinance, area is 
defined as any large open space in a single commercial or abandoned property, and includes 
gathering areas, open office space, parking areas, and the exterior environment of the single parcel 
within which the single commercial or abandoned property resides”, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Mr. 
Wolfe raised a point of order  regarding Mr. Moody’s proposed amendment , stating that verbal 
amendments are not an efficient way to approach amendments. Mayor Collins responded that, 
under Robert’s Rules of Order, verbal amendments are permitted; however, as a courtesy, 
providing amendments in writing would be beneficial in the future. Motion to amend failed. Voting 
“no” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody voting 
“yes”. Motion to amend by substitute, as amended carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body. Main motion as amend ed by substitute, as amended carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody and Dr. Rinne 
voting “no”. Public comment was made by: Patricia McCoy, Exie Brown, Kathy Scigliano, Bailey 
Turner, Mr. Matthews, Gary Chadwick, Charles Miller, Steven Love, Tamara Trujillo, Al an 
Sheldon and Kristen Turner . Comments were made by the following members of the governing 
body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne  and Mr. 
Wolfe. (#4656)

exceed $121,606.00). (#8315) 
 
  Consideration of Bid #S-11-26 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Miller 
and Sons Construction, Inc., for the Parsley Boulevard Greenway Connectors project (2021 
Specific Purpose Tax Fund) . Mr. Esquibel moved to accept  the bid in an amount not to exceed  
$228,970.80, seconded by Mr. White . Motion carried. Voting “yes” –  all members of the 
governing body.  Comment was made by the following member of the governing body:  Mr. 
Laybourn. (#8316) 
 
[CA]  Consideration of Bid #S-9-26 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Aztec 
Construction Co., Inc., for the Kiwanis Park Trail and Constructed Wetlands project (2017 Specific 
Purpose Tax Fund & Wyoming Department of Environmental Quality Grant)  – referred to Finance 
Committee.  
 
[CA]  Consideration of Bid #E-8-26 for furnishing One (1) New 52K GVWR Truck with Trash 
Loader and Dump Body for the Forestry Division (One Time State Distribution Funds) – referred 
to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA]  Consideration of Bid #E -12-26 for furnishing One (1) New Recycling Vacuum & High 
Pressure Water Jet Truck 66K GVWR for the Street and Alley Division (2019-2022 Optional 1% 
Sales Tax Fund) – referred to Finance Committee.  
 
 Appointment of Rebecca Ogletree to the Community Action of Laramie County Board. Dr. 
Aldrich moved to approve, seconded by Mr. Esquibel. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members 
of the governing body with the exception of Mayor Collins who did not vote (mayoral 
appointments). 
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented.  
 Announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held Monday, February 23, 2026 at 
6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Ave., Cheyenne, Wyoming, and via electronic 
conference meeting, for renewal applications for existing City liquor licenses (retail, restaurant, 
limited retail, resort, bar and grill licenses, microbrewery, satellite distillery, special malt beverage 
and winery permits) filed with the City Clerk’s Office.  
  
 Announcement was made that due to the President’s Day Holiday on Monday, February 
16, 2026, the regularly scheduled City Council Committee meetings will instead be held in City 
Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference meeting 
as follows: Public Services Committee will meet Tuesday, February 17, 2026 at Noon and Finance 
Committee will meet Wednesday, February 18, 2026 at Noon. 
 
Public comment was made by the following under Other Business:  Mary Whalen, Jim 
Chiro and Charles Miller. 
 
The following members of the governing body made comments under Other Business: Dr. 
Aldrich and Mr. Esquibel. 
 
Mr. Segrave moved to meet in Executive Session pursuant to Wyoming Statute §16- 4- 
405(a), seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body. Mayor Collins announced members would meet in executive session, not open to the public 
and stated there would be no action taken by the governing body as a result of the executive 
session, and that the regular City Council meeting would officially conclude at the close of the 
executive session. The following staff members were in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief 
of Staff; John Brodie, City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer; Tom Cobb, City Engineer; 
Chief Andrew Dykshorn and Deputy Chief Don Wood, Cheyenne Fire Rescue and Kylie Soden, 
City Clerk. 
 
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 11:41 p.m. 
 
 
        Submitted by, 
 
              
        Kylie Soden, 
        City Clerk

MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2026-02-23 | CLIP_ID: 1066 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 1066

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
February 23, 2026 
 
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers  and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: 
MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, 
Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne, Tom Segrave (via Zoom), Jeff White 
and Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be 
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate 
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two 
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda). Upon request by Mr. Esquibel, and pursuant to support received 
by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody, items #19(a) and #19(b) were removed from the Consent Agenda.  
Upon request by Mr. Moody, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. White, item 
#14 was removed from the Consent Agenda.  Dr. Aldrich  moved to approve  remaining items , 
seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on February 9, 2026. Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 Mayor Collins opened a public hearing  for renewal applications for existing City liquor 
licenses (retail, restaurant, limited retail, resort, bar and grill licenses, microbrewery, satellite 
distillery, special malt beverage and winery permits) filed with the City Clerk’s Office. Public 
comments were made by: A.K. Wallace and Cameron Brown, Cheba Hut. There being no further 
comments or input and the purpose of the public hearing having been met, Mayor Collins closed 
the public hearing and referred the applications to the Finance Committee.  
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Creating Chapter 8.72, Private Displays on Public 
Property, to prohibit the unauthorized use of public property for specified private displays . 
Reporting for Public Services Committee,  Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second reading, 
seconded by Dr. Aldrich . Dr. Aldrich moved to amend by substitute dated February 13, 2026, 
seconded by Mr. Moody . During comments made by Dr. Emmons regarding the substitute, Dr. 
Aldrich raised a point of order that comments were off subject.  Mayor Collins responded that the 
comments were germane to the substitute. Motion to amend by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – 
all members of the governing body with the exception of Dr. Emmons  voting “no”. Main motion 
as amended by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the 
exception of Dr. Emmons and Dr. Rinne voting “no”. Public comments were made by: Cheryl 
Gerrish and Steven Love. Comments were made by the following members of the governing body: 
Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Wolfe. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for certain land located north of Prairie Avenue, east 
of Powderhouse Road, west of Rue Terre, and south of Storey Boulevard from AG – Agricultural 
to NR -3 – Neighborhood Residential High Density. Dr. Rinne moved to approve on second 
reading, seconded by Mr. Esquibel. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body. Public comment was made by:  Andrew Schafer, R eal Estate Equities D evelopment 
Company. Comment was made by the following member of the governing body: Mayor Collins.  
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located southeast of the intersection of South 
Greeley Highway and East Dayshia Lane from AG – Agricultural to BP – Business Park. Dr. Rinne 
moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, various 
tracts of land completely surrounded by current City limits situate in western and southern 
Cheyenne, generally located east of I-25, south of the intersection of Westland Road and Missile 
Drive, north of West and East Allison Road, and east of and adjacent to North College Drive. Dr. 
Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by D r. Aldrich. Dr. Aldrich moved to 
postpone to March 9, 2026, seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion to postpone failed. Voting “yes” – 
Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody and Mr. White. Voting “no” – Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, 
Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mr. Wolfe. Mr. Moody moved to amend by removing 
Parcel 4  and the southern portion of P arcel 7 , seconded by Dr. Aldrich.  During comments  
regarding the amendment, Mayor Collins ruled David Kniseley out of order. Mr. Esquibel moved 
to divide the question to consider Parcel 4 and the southern portion of Parcel 7 separately, seconded 
by Dr. Aldrich. Dr. Rinne raised  a point of order regarding the motion to divide the question, 
stating it was not divisible. Mayor Collins ruled the motion  was in order. Motion to divide the 
question failed. Voting “yes” – Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody and Mr. White. Voting “no” 
– Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mr. Wolfe.  
 
 Following a brief recess, Mayor Collins reconvened the meeting at 7:40 p.m. 
 
 Mr. Moody, with concurrence by Dr. Aldrich as the second to the motion, moved by 
friendly amendment to remove Parcels 4 and 7 in their entirety. Motion to amend failed. Voting 
“no” all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Esquibel and Mr. Moody voting 
“yes”.  Main motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception 
of Mr. Esquibel and Mr. Moody voting “no”. Public comments were made by: David Kniseley, 
WYFresh, Donald Crerar, Steven Love, Brian Pixley, Richard Knis eley, Micah Sutton, Chelsea 
McCort, Alan Sheldon and Tommy Kniseley, WYFresh . Comments were made by the following 
members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. 
Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, establishing the zoning classifications of AG – Agricultural, MR – Medium-Density 
Residential, CB – Community Business, and LI – Light Industrial, for land annexed to the City of 
Cheyenne generally located east of I -25, south of the intersection of Westland Road and Missile 
Drive, north of West and East Allison Road, and east of and adjacent to North College Drive. Dr. 
Rinne moved to approve on second reading, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion carried. Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
 ORDINANCE –1st READING – Repealing and replacing Ordinance No. 4603, specifying 
the monthly Stormwater Runoff Management System user fee in accordance with Section 
13.32.050 of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, and providing a revised 
effective date – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsors – Dr. A ldrich, D r. E mmons, M r. 
Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Expressing the support of the Governing Body for the inclusion of 
Laramie County Property ID Number 14663133500500 in the Downtown Development District . 
Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6514) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to sign a final plat for Village 
Cooperative, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located north of Prairie Avenue, east 
of Powderhouse Road, west of Rue Terre, and south of Storey Boulevard) . Dr. Rinne moved to 
adopt, seconded by Mr. Wolfe. Dr. Rinne moved to postpone to March 9, 2026, seconded by Mr. 
Wolfe. Motion to postpone carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Comment 
was made by the following member of the governing body: Mayor Collins. 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Directing the deposit of proceeds from the sale of certain real property 
into the City’s Real Property Revolving Fund – referred to Finance Committee . (Sponsor – Mr. 
Esquibel) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the submission of an Americorps Seniors Foster 
Grandparent Program application to Americorps on behalf of the Governing Body of the City of 
Cheyenne for a three-year continuation of funding for the Youth Alternatives Foster Grandparent 
Program and related support items – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Esquibel) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities to execute a grant 
agreement with the Wyoming Office of Homeland Security for Federal Emergency Management 
Agency Rehabilitation of High Hazard Potential Dams funding and to authorize the Dire ctor of 
the Board to execute all related documents  – referred to Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Rinne) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – In support of the Professional Rodeo Cowboy Association (PRCA) and 
Professional Rodeo Hall of Fame and Museum of the American Cowboy  – referred to Finance 
Committee. (Sponsors– Dr. Aldrich, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. 
Rinne, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe) 
 
  Professional Services Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and TDSi for professional 
design services for the repurposing of the Historic Pumphouse (General Fund Reserves). Reporting 
for Finance Committee, Mr. Esquibel moved to approve in an amount not to exceed $198,903.00, 
seconded by Mr. White. Mr. Wolfe moved to amend by substitute dated February 20, 2026, 
seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion to amend by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – all members of 
the governing body. Main motion as amended by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – all members 
of the governing body.  Public comments were made by:  Maren Kallas, Historic Cheyenne Inc., 
Milward Simpson and Randy Byers, TDSi. Comment s were made by the following member s of 
the governing body: Mayor Collins, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne and Mr. Wolfe. (#8317) 
 
  Utility Easement Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Microsoft Corporation for 
grant of perpetual right-of-way and temporary easement for underground fiber lines  (Revenue to 
the City). Mr. Esquibel moved to approve in an amount of $10.00, seconded by Mr. White . Mr. 
Esquibel moved to amend in the amount of $1,265.00, seconded by Mr. White. Motion to amend 
carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Main motion as amended carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Moody voting “no”. 
(#8318) 
 
[CA]  Contract Modification #3 to Contract #7977 between the City of Cheyenne and Simon 
Contractors for the Public Works Improvements project (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund, 
Fleet Maintenance Fund & Solid Waste Fund). Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount 
not to exceed $266,406.49). (#7977) 
 
[CA]  Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7821 between the City of Cheyenne and United 
Way of Laramie County to provide funding to community agencies and monitor performance of 
community programs (2019-2022 Optional 1% Sales Tax Fund) . Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#7821) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7322 between the City of Cheyenne and Sweetgrass 
Homeowners Association and the Sweetgrass Commercial Owners Association to outline 
responsibilities for both construction and maintenance of the Greater Cheyenne Greenway as well 
as enhanced landscaping constructed within tracts of land owned by the City and for areas within 
the public right-of-way within Sweetgrass, 1st and 2nd Filings – referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA]  Consideration of Bid #S-9-26 for an Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and Aztec 
Construction Co., Inc., for the Kiwanis Park Trail and Constructed Wetlands project (2017 Specific 
Purpose Tax Fund & Wyoming Department of Environmental Quality Grant) . Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried (in an amount not to exceed $487,560.00). (#8319) 
 
[CA]  Consideration of Bid #E-8-26 for furnishing One (1) New 52K GVWR Truck with Trash 
Loader and Dump Body for the Forestry Division (One Time State Distribution Funds) . Motion 
(per Consent Agenda) carried (accepted bid from Floyd’s Truck Center Inc. in an amount not to 
exceed $253,260.00). 
 
[CA]  Consideration of Bid #E -12-26 for furnishing One (1) New Recycling Vacuum & High 
Pressure Water Jet Truck 66K GVWR for the Street and Alley Division (2019-2022 Optional 1% 
Sales Tax Fund). Motion (per Consent Agenda)  carried (accepted bid from Kaiser Premier in an 
amount not to exceed $848,639.00).  
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #E -13-26 for the Lease of One (1) New In Stock 40 Yard Front 
Loader Refuse Collection Truck for the City of Cheyenne Sanitation Division (Solid Waste Fund 
& WARM Insurance Proceeds) – referred to Finance Committee. 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented.  
   
 No comments were made on the Revenue Report as presented. 
  
Public comment was made by the following under Other Business: Ted Hanlon. 
 
The following members of the governing body made comments under Other Business: Dr. 
Aldrich, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody and Mr. Wolfe.   
 
Mr. Laybourn moved to meet in Executive Session pursuant to Wyoming Statute §16- 4- 
405(a), seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body. Mayor Collins announced members would meet in executive session, not open to the public 
and stated there would be no action taken by the governing body as a result of the executive 
session, and that the regular City Council meeting would officially conclude at the close of the 
executive session. The following staff members were in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief 
of Staff; John Brodie, City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasur er; Kylie Soden, City Clerk;  
Chief Andrew Dykshorn,  Deputy Chief Don Wood, and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, 
Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. 
 
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 9:46 p.m. 
 
 
        Submitted by, 
 
              
        Kylie Soden, 
        City Clerk 
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  March 6, 2026

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
February 23, 2026 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in special session on this date beginning 
at 5:30 p.m. in Council Chambers and via electronic conference meeting, for the purpose of 
collective labor bargaining with the Cheyenne Professional Firefighters, International Association 
of Firefighters, Local No. 279.  Present were: MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS 
– Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark 
Rinne, Tom Segrave (via Zoom), Jeff White and Lawrence Wolfe .  Also present: Kylie Soden, 
City Clerk , Amber Ash, Chief of Staff, John Brodie, City Attorney, Robin Lockman, City 
Treasurer and Chief Andrew Dykshorn, Deputy Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of 
Administrative Services, Glenn Rodgers,  Cheyenne Fire Rescue . The pledge of allegiance was 
recited. 
 
Mayor Collins provided opening remarks and emphasized the importance of the labor -
management discussions that take place in advance of formal negotiations. The proposed Ground 
Rules were reviewed, agreed upon, and signed by both the City and the Union. [Clerk’s Note: The 
City’s spokespersons are Mayor Patrick Collins, City Attorney John Brodie, and Chief of Staff 
Amber Ash. The Union’s spokespersons are Union President Chris Thoms, Union Vice President 
Jason Lindsay, and Union Grievance Representative James Lewis.]  
 
Mayor  Collins announced that additional negotiation meetings will be scheduled in the 
coming weeks to review City and Union proposals. 
   
  There bein g no fur ther business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 5:33 p.m.  
 
 
       Submitted by, 
        
        
       Kylie Soden, City Clerk  
 
 
This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request.

  March 6, 2026

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
 
Office of City Clerk 
 
March 5, 2026 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne convened in a special meeting on this date 
beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers for the purpose of collective labor bargaining 
with the Cheyenne Professional Fire Fighters, International Association of Fire Fighters, Local 
No. 279.  Present were:  MAYOR – Patrick Collins; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Mr. Esquibel, Mr. 
Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Mr. Segrave (via Zoom), Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe. Absent:  Dr. Aldrich, 
Dr. Emmons and Dr. Rinne . Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk; John Brodie, City Attorney; 
Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief Andrew Dykshorn 
and Deputy Chief Don Wood, Cheyenne Fire Rescue.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
      
 Mayor Collins advised he would entertain a motion to go into executive session.  Pursuant 
to Wyoming State Statute §16 -4-405(a)(x), Mr. Wolfe moved to meet in executive session, 
seconded by Mr. Esquibel.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body 
present. The following staff members were in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; 
John Brodie, City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer; Kylie Soden, City Clerk  and Chief 
Andrew Dykshorn and Deputy Chief Don Wood, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. [City Clerk note: audio 
and video recording of the special meeting was stopped; Executive Session convened at 6:05 p.m. 
in the Mayor’s conference room] 
 
Following closure of the executive session, Mayor Collins reconvened the special meeting 
at 6:40 p.m.  
 
Chris Thoms, President, Local #279, expressed appreciation for the labor -management 
meetings that take place in advance of contract negotiation meetings. He stated the Union’s 
primary goal is to address firefighter wages and presented wage comparisons for firefighter 
positions in Wyoming, Colorado, Montana, and South Dakota. Mr. Thoms indicated it is the 
Union’s position that Cheyenne firefighter compensati on falls behind regional standards. Upon a 
request for clarification on the jurisdictions used for wag e comparisons , Mr. Thoms provided 
additional information and stated that Cheyenne competes with departments along the Front 
Range. Mayor Collins stated that Wyoming communities are the most appropriate peer 
comparisons and noted the City has not experienced significant recruitment or retention issues in 
recent years. Mr. Thoms indicated the Union’s analysis includes both starting and top -out wages 
and that Cheyenne falls behind some communities in top-out compensation. 
 
Discussion continued regarding differences in municipal funding structures, statewide 
compensation averages, top-out wages, identification of appropriate peer communities with similar 
tax structures and populations, and the number of applicants for entry-level firefighter positions.

MEETING: City Council Meeting | DATE: 2026-03-09 | CLIP_ID: 1071 | SOURCE: cheyenne.granicus.com MinutesViewer clip 1071

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
Office of City Clerk 
 
March 9, 2026 
 
The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne met in regular session on this date beginning 
at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers  and via electronic conference meeting. Present were: 
MAYOR – Patrick Collins, COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Michelle Aldrich, Dr. Kathy Emmons, 
Ken Esquibel, Pete Laybourn, Mark Moody, Dr. Mark Rinne , Tom Segrave , Jeff White  and 
Lawrence Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk. The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
 
Consent Agenda. (All agenda items listed with the designation of [CA] are considered to be 
routine items by the governing body and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate 
discussion on these items unless a member of the governing body so requests and support by two 
other members is received.  Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered in its 
normal sequence on the agenda ). Upon request by Dr. Aldrich, and pursuant to support received 
by Mr. Moody and Mr. White, items #18, #20 and #22 were removed from the Consent Agenda. 
Upon request by Mr. Laybourn, and pursuant to support received by Dr. Aldrich and Mr. Moody, 
item #21 was removed from the Consent Agenda. Upon request by Dr. Aldrich, and pursuant to 
support received by Mr. Moody and Mr. Esquibel, item #26 (a) was  removed from the Consent 
Agenda. Mr. Segrave moved to approve remaining items, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
 
Dr. Rinne moved to suspend the rules to change the order of the agenda to bring forward 
agenda item #22 (Resolution regarding support of the Professional Rodeo Cowboy Association) 
for action immediately prior to agenda item #7, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. Voting 
“yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Laybourn voting “no.” 
 
[CA] Minutes from Regular Meeting of the Governing Body on February 23, 2026. Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
[CA] Minutes from Special Meeting of the Governing Body on February 23, 2026. Motion (per 
Consent Agenda) carried. 
 
 RESOLUTION – In support of the Professional Rodeo Cowboy Association (PRCA) and 
Professional Rodeo Hall of Fame and Museum of the American Cowboy. Reporting for Finance 
Committee, Mr. Esquibel moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” 
– all members of the governing body. Public comments were made by: Katharine Wilkinson, 
Betsey Hale, Cheyenne LEADS and Don Odom. Comments were made by the following members 
of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody and Mr. White . 
(#6515) 
 
 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Creating Chapter 8.72, Private Displays on Public 
Property, to prohibit the unauthorized use of public property for specified private displays . 
Reporting for Public Services Committee,  Dr. Emmons  moved to approve on third and final  
reading, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion failed. Voting “no” – all members of the governing body 
with the exception of Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. White  voting “yes”. Public comments 
were made by: Kathy Scigliano, Steven Love and Chelsea McCort. Comments were made by the 
following members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Laybourn and Mr. 
Wolfe. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for certain land located north of Prairie Avenue, east 
of Powderhouse Road, west of Rue Terre, and south of Storey Boulevard from AG – Agricultural 
to NR-3 – Neighborhood Residential High Density. Dr. Emmons moved to approve on third and 
final reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave . Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body. (#4660) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located southeast of the intersection of South 
Greeley Highway and East Dayshia Lane from AG – Agricultural to BP – Business Park. Dr. 
Emmons moved to approve on third and final reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#4661) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Annexing to the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, various 
tracts of land completely surrounded by current City limits situate in western and southern 
Cheyenne, generally located east of I-25, south of the intersection of Westland Road and Missile 
Drive, north of West and East Allison Road, and east of and adjacent to North College Drive. Dr. 
Emmons moved to approve on third and final  reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave.  Following a 
brief recess, Mayor Collins reconvened the meeting at 9: 00 p.m. Mr. Moody moved to amend by 
substitute dated March 2, 2026, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion to amend failed due to a tie vote. 
Voting “yes” – Dr. Aldrich, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Moody, Mr. Wolfe, and Mr. White. Voting “no” – 
Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Laybourn, Dr Rinne  and Mr. Segrave. Dr. Aldrich moved to 
divide the question to remove Parcel #4 and the agricultural portion of Parcel #7, seconded by Mr. 
White. Motion to divide the question failed  due to a tie vote . Voting “yes” – Dr. Aldrich, Mr. 
Esquibel, Mr. Moody, Mr. Wolfe, and Mr. White. Voting “no” – Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. 
Laybourn, Dr Rinne and Mr. Segrave. Mr. Moody moved to amend the effective date to March 10, 
2027, seconded by Dr. Aldrich. Motion to amend failed. Voting “no” – all members of the 
governing body. Dr. Aldrich moved to amend with a postponement date certain of June 8, 2026, 
seconded by Mr. Moody. Mr. White moved to amend the amendment with a postponement date 
certain of November 9, 2026, seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion to amend the amendment carried. 
Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Motion to postpone by amended postponement 
date certain of November 9, 2026 carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. 
Public comments were made by: Tommie Kniseley, WY Fresh Farm, Michael Jordan, Roxy Havel, 
Laura Lee, Patricia McCoy, Scott Boersma, Kathy Scigliano, Becky Boersma, Jacob 
Wasserburger, Gary  Pugh, Don Odom, Denel Pugh, Exie Brown, Tatyana Machemer , Brian 
Pixley, Verena Booth, Donald Crerar, Colleen Shassetz, Gary Brown, Ann Lucas, Steve Johnson, 
Richard Lyle, Daniel Singh, Jerry Ditto, Steve Melia, Chelsea McCort, Carol Atkinson, Hannah 
Fields, Steven Love, Glenn Connor, Betty Keetley, Gay Woodhouse, Tam ara Trujillo, Cody 
Smith, David Kniseley, Wade Blunn, Richard Kniseley, Micah Sutton, Gerry (no last name given), 
Dakota Titus, Johnnie Kniseley, Jordan Wisdorf, Ken Williams, Eric Henderson, Sarah Morgan, 
Bobbie Ecker-Mauthe, Charles Miller, Anna Blessing, Joee Pavlica, Lucky Buffalo Farmstand, 
Adrian Crader, Ronald Stringer, Ann Domah, and Pattie Thomas . During comments made by 
Charles Miller, Mr. Wolfe raised a point of order that commen ts were off subject. Mayor Collins 
responded that comments weren’t germane to the subject. Comments were made by the following 
members of the governing body:  Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. 
Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White and Mr. Wolfe. 
 
 Following a brief recess, Mayor Collins reconvened the meeting at 11:05 p.m. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 3rd READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, establishing the zoning classifications of AG – Agricultural, MR – Medium-Density 
Residential, CB – Community Business, and LI – Light Industrial, for land annexed to the City of 
Cheyenne generally located east of I -25, south of the intersection of Westland Road and Missile 
Drive, north of West and East Allison Road, and east of and adjacent to North College Drive. Dr. 
Emmons moved to approve on third and final  reading, seconded by Mr. Segrave . Dr. Aldrich 
moved to postpone with a date certain of November 9, 2026, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion to 
postpone carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Public comments were made 
by: David Kniseley. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 2nd READING – Repealing and replacing Ordinance No. 4603, specifying 
the monthly Stormwater Runoff Management System user fee in accordance with Section 
13.32.050 of the Municipal Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, and providing a revised 
effective date. Mr. Esquibel moved to approve on second  reading, seconded by Mr. White. Mr. 
Esquibel moved to amend by substitute dated February 25, 2026, seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion 
to amend by substitute carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with th e 
exception of Mr. Laybourn and Mr. Wolfe voting “no”. Main motion as amended by substitute  
carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body with the exception of Mr. Laybourn 
and Mr. Wolfe voting “no”. Public comment was made by: Steven Love. Comments were made 
by the following members of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich, Mayor Collins, Dr. Emmons, Mr. 
Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Dr. Rinne, Mr. Segrave and Mr. Wolfe. 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of  
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located north of West College Drive and 
east of South Parsley Boulevard from PUD Harmony Valley Planned Unit Development to NR -3 
Neighborhood Residential - High Density – referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. 
Emmons) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located south of West Allison Road, west 
of Walterscheid Boulevard, and north of Grand Harmony Boulevard from PUD Harmony Valley 
Planned Unit Development to NR-3 Neighborhood Residential - High Density – referred to Public 
Services Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Emmons) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located north of Allison Road and west of 
Walterscheid Boulevard from AG Agriculture to NR-3  Neighborhood Residential -  High Density 
– referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Emmons) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Amending the Official Zoning Map of the City of 
Cheyenne, changing the zoning classification for land located northwest of the intersection of East 
29th Street and Central Avenue from MR – Medium-Density Residential to NR-2 – Neighborhood 
Residential Medium-Density – referred to Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Emmons) 
 
 ORDINANCE – 1st READING – Vacating Frank Court and a small segment of a 
previously vacated alley, north of Rock Springs Street, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, 
Wyoming (located east of North College Drive and north of Rock Springs Street)  – referred to 
Public Services Committee. (Sponsor – Dr. Emmons) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Mayor and City Clerk to sign a final plat for Village 
Cooperative, City of Cheyenne, Laramie County, Wyoming (located north of Prairie Avenue, east 
of Powderhouse Road, west of Rue Terre, and south of Storey Boulevard). Dr. Emmons moved to 
adopt with staff recommendations, seconded by Mr. Segrave. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all 
members of the governing body. (#6516) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Directing the deposit of proceeds from the sale of certain real property 
into the City’s Real Property Revolving Fund. Motion (per Consent Agenda) carried. (#6517) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing the submission of an Americorps Seniors Foster 
Grandparent Program application to Americorps  on behalf of the Governing Body of the City of 
Cheyenne for a three-year continuation of funding for the Youth Alternatives Foster Grandparent 
Program and related support items. Mr. Esquibel moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. Moody. Motion 
carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Comment was made by the following 
member of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich. (#6518) 
 
 RESOLUTION – Authorizing the Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities to execute a grant 
agreement with the Wyoming Office of Homeland Security for Federal Emergency Management 
Agency Rehabilitation of High Hazard Potential Dams funding and to authorize the Dire ctor of 
the Board to execute all related documents. Mr. Esquibel moved to adopt, seconded by Mr. White. 
Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. (#6519) 
 
[CA] RESOLUTION – Authorizing the City of Cheyenne to approve and submit the Wyoming 
Division of Victim Services Funding Application for State Fiscal Years 2027 and 2028 – referred 
to Finance Committee. (Sponsor – Mr. Esquibel) 
 
 
 
 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #7322 between the City of Cheyenne and Sweetgrass 
Homeowners Association and the Sweetgrass Commercial Owners Association to outline 
responsibilities for both construction and maintenance of the Greater Cheyenne Greenway as well 
as enhanced landscaping constructed within tracts of land owned by the City and for areas within 
the public right -of-way within Sweetgrass, 1 st and 2 nd Filings. Motion (per Consent Agenda) 
carried. (#7322) 
 
[CA] Contract Modification #1 to Contract #8267 between the City of Cheyenne and Plan One 
Architects for the Municipal Building Renovation Design project (General Fund Reserves)  – 
referred to Finance Committee. 
 
[CA] Consideration of Bid #E -13-26 for the Lease of One (1) New In Stock 40 Yard Front 
Loader Refuse Collection Truck for the City of Cheyenne Sanitation Division (Solid Waste Fund 
& WARM Insurance Proceeds) . Motion (per consent agenda) carried ( accepted bid from Elliot 
Equipment Company in an amount not to exceed $409,388.96).  
 
 Renewal applications for existing City liquor licenses (retail, restaurant, limited retail,  
resort, bar and grill licenses, microbrewery, satellite distillery, special malt beverage and winery 
permits) filed with the City Clerk’s Office.  Mr. Esquibel moved to approve, seconded by Mr. 
White. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body. Public comment was 
made by: B ryan ‘Alf’ Grzegorczyk, Alf’s Pub and Cameron Brown, Cheba Hut. Comment was 
made by the following member of the governing body: Dr. Aldrich. 
 
 No comments were made on the Voucher Report as presented.  
 
An announcement was made of a Public Hearing to be held March 23, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. 
in City Council Chambers, 2101 O’Neil Avenue, Cheyenne, WY, and via electronic conference 
meeting, for a bar & grill liquor license application filed with the City Clerk’s Office for 
Mongolian Bar & Grill, d/b/a Mongolian Bar & Grill, 1637 Stillwater Ave. Ste. C, Cheyenne, WY.  
 
Public comment was made by the following under Other Business: Ted Hanlon and Charles 
Miller. 
 
The following members of the governing body made comments under Other Business: Dr. 
Aldrich and Mr. Moody.   
 
Mr. Segrave moved to meet in Executive Session pursuant to Wyoming Statute §16- 4- 
405(a), seconded by Mr. Esquibel. Motion carried. Voting “yes” – all members of the governing 
body. Mayor Collins announced members would meet in executive session, not open to the public 
and stated there would be no action taken by the governing body as a result of the executive 
session, and that the regular City Council meeting would officially conclude at the close of the 
executive session. The following staff members were in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief 
of Staff; John Brodie, City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer;  and Kylie Soden, City 
Clerk.  
 
There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 12:14 a.m.      
        Submitted by, 
 
              
        Kylie Soden,

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
 
Office of City Clerk 
 
March 12, 2026 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne convened in a special meeting on this date 
beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers for the purpose of collective labor bargaining 
with the Cheyenne Professional Fire Fighters, International Association of Fire Fighters, Local 
No. 279.  Present were:  MAYOR – Patrick Collins; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Aldrich, Dr. 
Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Mr. Segrave, Mr. White  and Mr. Wolfe . 
Absent: Dr. Rinne. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk; John Brodie, City Attorney;  Amber 
Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff;  Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief Andrew Dykshorn , 
Deputy Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne 
Fire Rescue.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
      
 Mayor Collins advised he would entertain a motion to go into executive session.  Pursuant 
to Wyoming State Statute §16 -4-405(a)(x), Mr.  Segrave moved to meet in executive session, 
seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the governing body 
present. The following staff members were in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s Chief of Staff; 
John Brodie, City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer; Kylie Soden, City Clerk  and Chief 
Andrew Dykshorn, Deputy Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn 
Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire Rescue.  [City Clerk note: audio and video  recording of the special 
meeting was stopped; Executive Session convened at 6:04 p.m. in the City Council office] 
 
Following closure of the executive session, Mayor Collins reconvened the special meeting 
at 6:33 p.m.  
 
Chris Thoms, President of Local #279, expressed appreciation for the Governing Body’s 
support and positive relationship with the Union. He briefly reviewed the Union’s request, noting 
that no wage increase was requested last year and emphasiz ed the need to remain competitive 
within the regional market. Mayor Collins thanked the Union for its constructive relationship with 
the City and acknowledged their concerns. He noted the importance of identifying an appropriate 
peer group for compensation comparisons and provided an overview of benefits offered in 
Cheyenne compared to other Wyoming communities, including retirement , wages and specialty 
and longevity pay. Mayor Collins stated that, in many cases, Cheyenne’s compensation is more 
favorable and noted that working in other states can involve  a higher cost of living due to factors 
including income and property taxes. He also provided a brief overview of the City’s proposal.  
Mr. Thoms requested a recess at 6:43 p.m., and Union members vacated chambers to the H R 
conference room to caucus. 
 
Mayor Collins reconvened the special session at 7:11 p.m., at which time it was agreed to 
adjourn until the next meeting. 
 
 There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 7:12 p.m. 
 
 
      Submitted by, 
 
 
       Kylie Soden, 
       City Clerk 
 
 This notice is available in alternative, accessible formats upon request. 
 
Published: Wyoming Tribune-Eagle 
  March 18, 2026

RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS FOR THE GOVERNING BODY 
OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE 
 
Office of City Clerk 
 
March 16, 2026 
 
 The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne convened in a special meeting on this date 
beginning at 6:00 p.m. in City Council Chambers for the purpose of collective labor bargaining 
with the Cheyenne Professional Fire Fighters, International Association of Fire Fighters, Local 
No. 279.  Present were:  MAYOR – Patrick Collins; COUNCIL MEMBERS – Dr. Aldrich, Dr. 
Emmons, Mr. Esquibel, Mr. Laybourn, Mr. Moody, Mr. Segrave and Mr. White. Absent: Dr. Rinne 
and Mr. Wolfe. Also present: Kylie Soden, City Clerk; John Brodie, City Attorney; Amber Ash, 
Mayor’s Chief of Staff;  Robin Lockman, City Treasurer and Chief Andrew Dykshorn, Deputy 
Chief Don Wood  and Deputy Chief of Administrative Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire 
Rescue.  The pledge of allegiance was recited. 
      
Chris Thoms, President of Local #279, emphasized the Union’s priority of maintaining fair 
market wages and noted that peer departments, including those along the Front Range, provide 
relevant comparisons. Jason Lindsay, Vice President of Local #279, presented pension and salary 
comparisons for firefighters in Wyoming, Colorado, and Montana. Discussion included specialty 
pay, Cheyenne’s economic growth,  and cost-of-living data sourced from bestplaces.net.  Mr. 
Thoms presented a counter proposal which included updates to Section 19 – Inclement Weather 
and Section 21 – Classification of Employment and Basic Wages. Additional discussion included 
recruitment efforts, attrition history, firefighter candidate pools, appropriate peer comparisons, the 
importance of aligning recurring revenues with recurring expenses, as well as the City’s use of 
reserves. 
 
Pursuant to Wyoming State Statute §16 -4-405(a)(x), Mr.  Segrave moved to meet in 
executive session, seconded by Mr. White.  Motion carried.  Voting “yes” – all members of the 
governing body present. The following staff members were in attendance: Amber Ash, Mayor’s 
Chief of Staff; John Brodie, City Attorney; Robin Lockman, City Treasurer; Kylie Soden, City 
Clerk and Chief Andrew Dykshorn, Deputy Chief Don Wood and Deputy Chief of Administrative 
Services, Glenn Rodgers, Cheyenne Fire Rescue. [City Clerk note: audio and video recording of 
the special meeting was stopped; Executive Session convened at 6:41 p.m. in the City Council 
office] 
 
Following closure of the executive session, Mayor Collins reconvened the special meeting 
at 7:06 p.m. and discussion continued regarding wage comparisons, specialty pay, and appropriate 
peer groups, including how comparable communities structure and fund compensation.  Mayor 
Collins expressed the belief that the City’s firefighters are not underpaid. Discussion also included 
cost-of-living comparisons among certain Wyoming communities, paramedic compensation and 
training considerations, and ongoing challenges in reaching an agreement on wage comparisons 
and the identification of appropriate peer groups. The City reiterated its standing offer related to 
wage increases. The Union requested adjournme nt to review rank average amounts provided by 
the City. 
 
 There being no further business to come before the governing body, the meeting was 
officially adjourned at 7:35 p.m.
